The riff on the a in différance as all of those things is something that we can only pick up if we understand language as writing, because in speech these modes of difference don’t register.

“Différence”（带e）其实就是索绪尔的语言系统，一个将差异理解为空间性的系统：也就是说，当我们站在它面前时，它就像一个自助餐，任我们取用。Différance引入了延宕的概念，并提醒我们，差异——也就是说，我们对差异的理解，我们协商差异的方式——并非实际发生在空间中；它是在时间中发生的。当我感知差异时，我是在时间上感知它。我并不将符号之间的关系理解为一种同时性。如果我想用科学的方法确定它，我当然希望如此，但在实际的——正如乔伊斯所说——意识流中，我是在时间上理解差异的。我延宕差异。我展开差异。我不断地协商差异，而在这个过程中，我需要Différance的概念。

Différence (with an e) is simply the Saussurian linguistic system, a system of differences understood as spatial: that is to say, understood as available to us as a kind of smorgasbord as we stand in front of it. Différance introduces the idea ofdeferral and reminds us that difference–that is to say, our understanding of difference, our means of negotiating difference–is not something that’s actually done in space; it’s done in time. When I perceive a difference, I perceive it temporally. I do not understand the relation among signs as a simultaneity. I want to, if I want to pin it down scientifically, but in the actual–as Joyce would say–stream of consciousness, I understand difference temporally. I defer difference. I unfold. I successively negotiate difference, and in doing that I need the concept of différance.

好的。关于德里达的关键思想，我想谈几点。下次我会提到。我还会回顾一下笔记，看看能否进一步阐述这些棘手的术语及其与德里达语言理解的关系。这样，周二的介绍仍然会围绕德里达展开，之后我们会转而探讨德曼。

All right. There a couple of things that I want to say about the key moves of Derrida. I will mention those next time. I will also look over my notes and see what I might say further about these troublesome terms and their relation to Derrida’s understanding of language so that Tuesday our introduction will still have to do with Derrida and then we’ll move into thinking about de Man.

第十一讲 - 解构二

Lecture 11 - Deconstruction II

第一章 德里达和列维-斯特劳斯

Chapter 1. Derrida and Levi-Strauss

保罗·弗莱教授：在讨论德曼之前，我想先再多谈谈德里达。我知道我接下来要放弃一个对我来说颇为有趣的部分——或许你们并不这么认为——那就是对德里达文章第926页右栏最后一句非凡语句的阐释。我读给你们听，只是为了让你们思考一下。我想建议你们，如果你们还没有确定论文主题，不妨考虑一下这个主题。你们可能觉得它不太合适；但假设你们对德里达的这最后一句话很感兴趣，想看看它是如何呼应贯穿全文的主题，如何将文章带回到起点，以及仔细考察它的隐喻——它反思了自身的隐喻——我想你们可能会觉得很有意思。这段文字是：

Professor Paul Fry: I’d like to start with a little more discussion of Derrida before we turn to de Man. I know already that I’m going to forego what for me is a kind of pleasure—perhaps it wouldn’t be for you–which is an explication of the last extraordinary sentence in Derrida’s essay on page 926 in the right-hand column. I’m going to read it to you just so you can reflect on it. What I’d like to do is suggest to you that if you still haven’t determined on a paper topic, you might very well consider this one. You may not find it congenial; but supposing that you are intrigued by Derrida to account for this last sentence, to show how it picks up motifs generated throughout the essay, how it returns the essay to its beginning, and to consider very carefully its metaphors–it reflects on its own metaphors–I think you might find intriguing. The passage is:

这里有一个问题，姑且称之为历史性的问题，我们今天只是略窥一斑：构思、形成、孕育、分娩。我承认，我使用这些词语时，目光投向了生育之事——但也投向了那些人，他们（我并不排除自己属于其中一员）面对那尚未命名之物视而不见，而这物正在宣告自身，并且只能以非物种的形态，以无形、无声、幼小而又恐怖的怪物形态，在每次新生命即将诞生之际，如此宣告。好了，这就是我想说的一句话，正如我所说，我没有时间详细解释，但我推荐你把它作为论文选题，如果你还在寻找选题的话。

Here there is a sort of question, call it historical, of which we are only glimpsing today, the conception, the formation, the gestation, the labor. I employ these words, I admit, with a glance toward the business of childbearing–but also with a glance toward those who, in a company from which I do not exclude myself, turn their eyes away in the face of the as yet unnamable, which is proclaiming itself and which can do so, as is necessary whenever a birth is in the offing, only under the species of the non-species in the formless, mute, infant, and terrifying form of monstrosity. Well, there is a sentence for you and, as I say, I don’t have time to explicate it but I commend it to you as a possible paper topic if you’re still in need of one.

现在我想回到德里达和列维-斯特劳斯之间的关系。我上次提到过，虽然这篇文章在某些方面确实像是对列维-斯特劳斯的批判，但无论是否承认，它在很大程度上都建立在列维-斯特劳斯的肩膀之上；然而，与此同时，在利用列维-斯特劳斯的同时，德里达也找到了一种与原文保持距离的方法。例如，在第924页到925页，他引用了列维-斯特劳斯为马塞尔·莫斯关于语言的诞生、事件或出现这一主题的著作所作的导言。从表面上看，他引用的列维-斯特劳斯的这段话似乎与德里达本人对语言的出现或诞生所持的保留和犹豫的态度如出一辙。列维-斯特劳斯写道：

Now I do want to go back to the relationship between Derrida and Levi-Strauss. I suggested last time that while in some ways the essay really seems to stage itself as a critique of Levi-Strauss, to a remarkable degree, confessed or unconfessed, it stands on the shoulders of Levi-Strauss; at the same time, however, having made use of Levi-Strauss finding a means of distancing himself from the source text. Take, for example, page 924 over onto 925 when he quotes from Levi-Strauss’ introduction to the work of Marcel Mauss on the subject of the birth, event, or emergence of language. What he quotes from Levi-Strauss would seem, on the face of it, to have exactly the same kinds of reservation and hesitation about the emergence or birth of language that Derrida himself has. Levi-Strauss writes:

无论语言在动物生命尺度上出现的时机和环境如何，它都只能一蹴而就。事物不可能逐步赋予意义。在经历了一场并非社会科学范畴，而是生物学和心理学范畴的转变之后，事物从无意义的阶段跃升至万物皆有意义的阶段。换句话说，砰！语言突然就出现了。符号系统也随之诞生，而在此之前，甚至就在昨天或一分钟前，语言还不存在。也就是说，不存在这样一种观念：我突然看到某样东西，然后说，“哦，它有意义”，接着我又看到另一样东西，然后说，“哦，它有意义”，最终，瞧，语言就出现了——因为列维-斯特劳斯认为，意义这一概念的出现，瞬间就赋予了万物意义。换句话说，语言并非逐渐产生的。你拥有的，就像火山喷发的熔岩一样，是一种断裂。你拥有某种东西，它突然出现在其他事物之中：某种潜藏在这些事物之中的东西，尽管它们本身并不具备这种东西，直到你赋予它们它，那就是赋予意义的东西——语言。

Whatever may have been the moment and the circumstances of its appearance in the scale of animal life, language could only have been born in one fell swoop. Things could not have set about signifying progressively. Following a transformation the study of which is not the concern of the social sciences but rather of biology and psychology, a crossing over came about from a stage where nothing had a meaning to another where everything possessed it. In other words, bam! All of a sudden you had language. You had a semiotic system, whereas before, yesterday, or a minute ago you had no language at all. In other words, there’s no notion that somehow or another suddenly I looked at something and said, “Oh, that has a meaning,” and then somehow or another I looked at something else and said, “Oh, that has a meaning,” and in the long run, lo and behold, I had language–because the bringing into existence of the very thought of meaning, Levi-Strauss wants to argue, instantly confers meaning on everything. In other words, you don’t have a gradual emergence of language. You have, like lava emerging from a volcano, a rupture. You have something which suddenly appears amid other things: something which is latent in those things, although they don’t in themselves have it until you confer it on them, namely that which confers meaning–language.

这就是列维-斯特劳斯的论点，德里达对此很感兴趣，因为他意识到这与他自己在谈论事件、诞生、涌现等等问题上的犹豫不决有着相似之处。同时，他以批判的口吻指出，如果假设昨天没有语言，事物只是无意义地存在，而今天有了语言——事物因为有了我们称之为语言的符号系统而具有意义——那么这意味着文化必然是在自然之后才出现的。自然曾经存在；现在有了文化，这与旧意义上的事件或诞生非常相似。事实上，一旦我们拥有了文化——列维-斯特劳斯尤其在他那本名为《忧郁的热带》的著名著作中表达了这种感受——一旦我们拥有了文化，我们就开始对自然产生强烈的怀旧之情；但是，德里达说：“这种怀旧之情除了我们怀旧的对象正是由于这种怀旧而产生的这一事实之外，还能是什么呢？”换句话说，如果没有文化来思考自然，自然就不存在。自然本身就是一个毫无意义的概念，就像自然本身缺乏意义一样，文化也只有在文化出现后才会出现，然后文化会说：“哦，其实并没有那么多自然，但我很不高兴，因为在我出现之前，自然是存在的。”对吧？

So this is Levi-Strauss’ argument, and Derrida is interested in it because he recognizes its affinity with his own hesitation in talking about events, births, emergence and so on. At the same time, he points out by way of criticism that to suppose that yesterday there was no language, there were just things as they are without meaning, and that today there is language–that things have meaning as a result of there now being in place that semiotic system we call language–he points out that this means that culture somehow or another must come after nature. There was nature; now there is culture, which is very much like an event or birth in the older sense. In fact, as soon as we have culture–Levi-Strauss expresses this feeling especially in a famous book called Tristes Tropiques–as soon as we have culture, we begin to feel overwhelming nostalgia for nature; but, says, Derrida, “What is this nostalgia other than the fact that the very thing we’re nostalgic for comes into existence as a result of the nostalgia?” In other words, there is no nature unless you have culture to think it. Nature is a meaningless concept just like the lack of meaning within nature, where there’s no culture until culture comes along and says, “Oh, not so much there is nature, but I’m terribly unhappy because before I came along, there was nature.” Right?

这就是民族志学者的怀旧或遗憾，他们会说：“如今，由于可怕的欧洲中心主义，由于研究这些事物的欧洲人可怕的民族中心主义，我们不再拥有野性的思维。”也就是说，我们不再拥有那种在自然、在自然环境中蓬勃发展的思维。你可以看到，这种论点对环境主义和民族志都有影响。这是一个引人入胜的论点，但关键在于：即使是这种批评——它实际上是对列维-斯特劳斯的批评，因为他说：“哦，列维-斯特劳斯，你关于语言的论述非常有趣，但你忘记了，这意味着你自己也认为自然先于文化，尽管文化创造了自然。”

This is the nostalgia or regret of the ethnographer who says, “Now as a result of this terrible Eurocentrism, as a result of the terrible ethnocentrism of the Europeans studying these things, we no longer have a savage mind.” That is to say, we no longer have the kind of mind which flourishes in nature, in a natural environment. You can see ramifications of arguments of this sort for environmentalism as well as for ethnography. It’s a fascinating argument, but the bottom line is this. Even this critique, and it is a critique of Levi-Strauss because he’s saying, “Oh, Levi-Strauss, that’s very interesting what you say about language, but you’ve forgotten that this means that you yourself must think nature preceded culture even though culture brings nature into being.”

但这种针对列维-斯特劳斯的批评，他其实也能在列维-斯特劳斯本人身上找到，而且也确实在其他场合找到过。列维-斯特劳斯的名著《生与熟》本身就体现了这种批评。你说“生”是什么意思？“嗯，有人坐在田里吃胡萝卜。那就是生的，”你可能会说，但等等：这个“生”的概念到底是什么？你不可能在“熟”的概念出现之前就理解“生”的概念。我坐在田里，吃着我的胡萝卜。我把它举起来，说：“这是生的？太荒谬了。‘生’和什么相对？”对吧？所以，在某种意义上，没有“熟”的存在，就没有“生”的概念。“熟”创造了“生”，正如文化创造了自然一样。

But this very critique leveled against Levi-Strauss, he could have found in Levi-Strauss and does find it on other occasions. Levi-Strauss’ famous book, The Raw and the Cooked, essentially stages this critique in and of itself. What do you mean, “raw”? “Well, somebody’s sitting in a field eating a carrot. That’s raw,” you say, but wait a minute: what is this notion of “raw”? You can’t have a notion of “raw” until you have the notion of “cooked.” I sit in my field. I’m eating my carrot. I hold it up and I say, “This is raw? It’s ridiculous. ‘Raw’ as opposed to what?” Right? So there can be no “raw” without, in a certain sense, the prior existence of “cooked.” “Cooked” brings “raw” into being in exactly the way culture brings nature into being.

现在让我们稍作停顿，思考一下这个问题。我们意识到，这种基本的思维方式——仔细想想，其实从我们开始阅读这门课程以来，我们就一直在遇到这种思维方式——与其说是二元对立的颠倒，不如说是质疑它们如何能够彼此分离地存在。换句话说，批判一种事物状态的起源是否源于或继发于另一种事物状态，这种批判的过程本质上——我很抱歉这样简化，但我真的看不出这样说有什么歪曲之处——就是在问：“先有鸡还是先有蛋？”对吧？这实际上是在宣告我们用二元论来理解的事物之间存在绝对的相互依存关系，而我们在思考它们时，却又不知不觉地认为其中一种事物是另一种事物的因果关系。

Now to pause over this for a moment, we realize that sort of this basic move–a move that, when you start to think about it, we’ve been encountering ever since we started reading in this course of readings–is not so much the inversion of binaries as the calling into question of how they can exist apart from each other. In other words, the question of criticizing the origin of one state of things out of or after another state of things, the process of criticizing that is basically–and I’m sorry to be so reductive about it but I really can’t see the distortion in saying this–is basically saying, “Which came first, the chicken or the egg?” Right? It is a declaration of absolute interdependency among the things that we understand in binary terms but that we take somehow one to be causative of the other when we think about them.

这其实是解构主义的基本步骤，但任何学习哲学和文学理论的人都会反复遇到这一步骤，从黑格尔一直到我们课程后续会遇到的后解构主义思想家——其中最突出的或许是性别理论家朱迪斯·巴特勒。你会在巴特勒的论述中反复遇到这个观点。这就像在问：“如果没有‘同性恋’这个概念，又怎么可能有‘异性恋’这个概念呢？”对吧？这些概念的绝对相互依存性，再次成为她论证和理解事物的核心。显然，我们之后还会回到这一点。

This is really the basic move of deconstruction, but it’s a move which anyone who studies philosophy as well as literary theory will encounter again and again and again, all the way from Hegel right on through the post-deconstructive thinkers we encounter for the rest of our syllabus–perhaps preeminently among them the gender theorist Judith Butler. Again and again and again you will encounter this idea in Butler. It’s a question of saying, “How on earth would you ever have the concept ‘heterosexual’ if you didn’t have the concept ‘homosexual’ in place?” Right? The absolute interdependency of these concepts is, again, central to her argument and to her understanding of things. Obviously, we’ll be returning to that in the long run.

第二章 写作与演讲

Chapter 2. Writing and Speech

那么，我想就德里达关于书写和言语——写作（writing）和言语（speech）的区分——再稍作停留。这种区分并非意在反直觉地暗示，与我们通常的认知相反，书写先于言语——完全不是。他并非认为我们本末倒置。他只是坚持认为，我们不能将书写理解为衍生品。我们不能说书写是相对于言语而产生的，其目的是为了复制、模仿或转录言语。书写和言语是相互依存、相互关联的现象，它们各自发挥着不同的作用。

Now I want to pause a little bit more, then, in this regard over Derrida’s distinction between writing and speech–writing,ecriture. This is a distinction which is not meant sort of counter-intuitively to suggest that somehow or another, as opposed to what we usually think, writing precedes speech–not at all. He’s not saying that we’ve got it backwards. He’s just insisting that we cannot understand writing to be derivative. We cannot say writing came into being belatedly with respect to speech in order to reproduce, imitate, or transcribe speech. Writing and speech are interdependent and interrelated phenomena which do different things.

上次我们谈到了“différance”（差）。我们说过，带e的“deference”和带a的“différance”之间的区别无法通过发音来区分。这种区别，或者说“différance”，恰恰是在书写中产生的，也只有在书写中，我们才能突然领悟到“différance”作为“diff”和“deferral”（延宕）的双重本质。我想稍作停顿——这将会引出德曼的观点——先讲一个有趣的法语例子，英语中没有类似的例子，但我认为它非常具有启发性，值得我们停下来仔细探讨一下[在黑板上写下“est/et”]。你们还记得上次吗？这里确实存在一个细微的发音差异，就像“deference”和“différance”之间也存在细微的发音差异一样，但这种差异并不大。它不容易被唤起和理解，但在书写中却显而易见。首先，在法语单词 est（发音为 ay）中，“s”表示“意义”，但发音时这个“s”会被省略。est 是“是”的意思，而 et 的发音也与“和”相同。这两个词恰好用法语表达了德里达试图描述的“补充性”的双重含义。“是”在这里指的是隐喻意义上的“是”——“这是那个，A 是 B”，这里将其理解为一种隐喻——它是一种补充，使整体得以完善。它是一种通过“A 是 B”这一宣告来完善整体的手段。

Last time we spoke about différance. We said that the difference between deference with an e and différance with an acan’t be voiced. It’s a difference, or différance, that comes into being precisely in writing, and it’s only in writing that we suddenly grasp the twofold nature of différance as difference and deferral. I’d like to pause a little bit–this will be my segue to de Man–over an interesting example in French which we don’t have in English but is, I think, so instructive that it’s worth pausing over [writes on chalkboard “est/et”]. You remember last time–and there is a slight voicing difference here just as there is also a slight voicing difference: deference, différance, but it’s not a big voicing difference. It’s not something that’s easy to evoke and get across, whereas in writing it’s perfectly obvious. For one thing, the s in est, which means “signification,” [laughs] is dropped out of this word when you say it, est [pron. ay], the word for is–which is also the pronunciation for et, the word for and. Now these two words precisely express in French what Derrida is trying to describe as the double meaning of supplementarity. Is in the sense of the metaphor–“This is that, A is B,” understood as a metaphor–is a supplement that completes a whole. It’s a means of completing a whole through the declaration that A is B.

但“is”还有另一种含义，并非修辞意义上的，因为隐喻可以说是修辞的核心，修辞意义上的“is”指的是“A是B”——顺便说一句，我们非常清楚A不是B。A怎么可能是B呢？A就是A。事实上，A是否是A本身就是一个问题，但它肯定不是B，对吧？这一点我们很清楚。在语法意义上，隐喻本身并不存在任何神秘之处。在语法意义上，这个词是谓词的手段或原则，通过它，我们才能表达一件事是另一件事：例如，母马是马的雌性。请注意，修辞意义上的“is”和语法意义上的“is”之间的关系，本质上就是雅各布森所说的“诗性功能”和“元语言功能”之间的关系。正如你在德曼的著作中看到的那样，这个词的修辞意义（声称具有隐喻性）与这个词的语法意义（不作此主张，而仅仅是在句子中建立谓词）之间存在着不可调和的张力。

But is has another sense which is not a rhetorical sense, because metaphor is sort of the heart of rhetoric, the rhetorical sense A is B–when, by the way, we know perfectly well that A is not B. How can A be B? A is only A. In fact, it’s even a question whether A is A, but it’s certainly not B, right? This much we know. In the grammatical sense there is no sort of mystification about the metaphor. In the grammatical sense, this word is the means or principal of predication whereby we say one thing is another thing: the mare is the female of the horse, for example. Notice that the relationship between the rhetorical is and the grammatical is is basically the relationship between what Jakobson calls the “poetic function” and the “metalingual function.” As you’ll see in de Man, there is an irreducible tension between the rhetorical sense of this word, which claims metaphoricity, and the grammatical sense of this word, which makes no such claim but is simply the establishment of predication in a sentence.

现在，几乎与“est”同音的“et”或“est”，强化了补充的概念，并非指对需要补充才能完整的事物的完成——即隐喻中意义的实现——而是指对已完成之物的添加。这种在“and”或“et”表达中，同位语式的、语法式的、持续的意义添加，归根结底，非常类似于雅各布森所说的“转喻”：也就是说，事物的连续添加，并不声称是隐喻性的，就像语法谓词一样。因此，我认为，仅仅通过观察这两个发音相似的词语就能建立起的张力或差异体系，为我们提供了一种象征或范例，来阐释德里达所说的“补充性”，以及德曼所说的修辞与语法之间不可化约的张力、差异和冲突。这就是我们今天要讨论的关于德曼的主要内容。

Now the word est or et, which is almost like est, reinforces the idea of the supplement, not as the completion of something that needs it to be complete–the fulfillment of meaning in a metaphor–but rather “supplement” in the sense of adding on to something that’s already complete. The appositional, sort of grammatical, perpetual addition of meaning in the expression and or et is after all very much like what Jakobson calls “metonymic”: that is to say, the contiguous adding on of things, making no claim to be metaphorical just like grammatical predication. So the tension or the system of differences that can be established simply by looking at these two similarly voiced words, I think, gives us a kind of emblem or paradigm for what Derrida calls “supplementarity” and what de Man calls the irreducible tension between, difference between, and conflict between rhetoric and grammar. That is the main topic of what we have to say about de Man today.

第三章 保罗·德曼与纳粹主义

Chapter 3. Paul de Man and Nazism

上次我略微提到了德里达和德曼，以及一位名叫J·希利斯·米勒的学者，还有与他们交往密切的学者——杰弗里·哈特曼和哈罗德·布鲁姆——在20世纪70年代和80年代初耶鲁大学的鼎盛时期，他们共同组成了所谓的“耶鲁学派”。这一时期在学术界备受推崇，但在学术界内外却饱受争议。然而，这却是文学学术思想史上一个特殊且引人注目的时期，也是文学学术思想对远超文学本身的更广泛领域产生独特影响的时期。它开始渗透到其他学科，并在那段时期展现出蓬勃的活力。

Now last time I said a little bit about the presence of Derrida and de Man together, together with a scholar named J. Hillis Miller, and scholars who associated themselves with them–Geoffrey Hartman and Harold Bloom–in a kind of period of flourishing in the seventies and early eighties at Yale called abroad “the Yale school,” subject to much admiration in the academy and much vilification both within and outside the academy. But this was a moment of particular and headlined notoriety in the history of academic thinking about literature, and a moment in which academic thinking about literature had a peculiar influence on topics much broader than literature. It began to infiltrate other disciplines and was in general a high-spirited horse for that certain period of time.

后来，米勒在八十年代去了欧文，德里达也去了那里。1983年，保罗·德曼去世，解构主义运动的主体力量开始让位于其他兴趣、倾向和潮流，无论是在耶鲁大学还是其他地方。德曼去世后不久，关于德曼出现了一个惊人的发现——你的编辑在《符号学与修辞学》的斜体序言中提到过——这个发现本身就令人震惊，使人再也无法用同样的方式解读德曼，但我不得不说，这恰恰是解构主义的敌人所期待的（笑）。事实是，德曼年轻时仍居住在比利时，他是比利时一位杰出的社会主义政治家的侄子。他曾为一家纳粹资助的比利时报纸撰写了一系列带有反犹倾向的文章，其中几篇是公开的反犹文章，或者至少在某种程度上带有种族中心主义的欧洲视角，主张将犹太人排除在欧洲的知识生活之外等等。这些文章被收集起来，作为保罗·德曼的战时新闻作品出版，引发了巨大的轩然大波，其程度堪比海德格尔与纳粹政府关系的揭露——后者从未被完全压制，但随着更多细节的披露，其影响反而愈演愈烈。在20世纪80年代末，读过德曼作品的人、没读过但反对他作品的人，以及那些竭力捍卫他的作品、试图维护其遗产以及解构主义遗产的人之间，展开了一场激烈的公开辩论。

Then Miller eventually in the eighties went to Irvine, Derrida followed him there, and in 1983 Paul de Man died, and the main force of the movement began to give way to other interests and other tendencies and trends both here at Yale and elsewhere. Then shortly after de Man’s, death there was a revelation–which is mentioned by your editor in the italicized preface to “Semiology and Rhetoric”–about de Man which was horrible in itself and made it impossible ever to read de Man in quite the same way again, but which was also, I have to say, precisely what the enemies of deconstruction were [laughs] waiting for. That was the fact that in his youth, de Man, still living in Belgium, the nephew of a distinguished socialist politician in Belgium, wrote for a Nazi-sponsored Belgian newspaper a series of articles anti-Semitic in tendency, a couple of them openly anti-Semitic or at least sort of racially Eurocentric in ways, that argued for the exclusion of Jews from the intellectual life of Europe and so on. These papers were gathered and published as Paul de Man’s wartime journalism, and there was a tremendous furor about them similar to the revelations, which had never been completely repressed but grew in magnitude as more and more was known about them–the revelations about Heidegger’s association with the Nazi government. In the late eighties, there was a furious public argumentation back and forth among those who had read de Man, those who hadn’t who were opposed to his work, and those who scrambled in one way or another to attempt to defend it to preserve his legacy and also the legacy of deconstruction.

现在这一切都有据可查，我想有必要稍作停顿。德曼的一篇文章——也收录在他那本名为《阅读的寓言》的书中（你今天读的那篇《符号学与修辞学》的文章也出自该书）——是那些真正读过德曼文章的人经常争论的一篇文章，名为《被盗的丝带》。这篇文章与卢梭《忏悔录》中的一段情节有关：卢梭偷了一条丝带，想把它送给一位他心仪的女仆。当有人问他是谁偷的，或者他是否知道是谁偷的时，他脱口而出她的名字：玛丽昂。德曼说这其实并非指控——事实上，这只是脱口而出的一句毫无意义的话——他认为根本不可能坦白，不存在任何能够肯定或否定罪责或责任的主观性：换句话说，很多事情，毋庸置疑，都引起了公众的关注。公众或许并不太在意他写过这些文章，而是在意他此后的职业生涯中从未承认过此事；换句话说，他隐瞒了过去。没人真的相信他仍然抱有这些同情，但关键问题是，他为什么不坦白？为什么不坦白？当然，人们把《被盗的丝带》解读为他用一种寓言的方式暗示自己不可能坦白，因为没有人能够坦白，不存在人类的主观性，等等等等。

Now all of this is a matter of record and I suppose needs to be paused over a little bit. One of the texts of de Man–also in the book called Allegories of Reading where you’ll find also a version of the essay “Semiology and Rhetoric” that you read for today–one of the essays that those who had actually read de Man actually argued about in a persistent fashion is called “The Purloined Ribbon.” It has to do with the passage in Rousseau’s Confessions where Rousseau has stolen a ribbon in order to give it to a serving maid to whom he felt attraction, and then when he was asked who had done it, or did he know anything about who had done it, he blurted out her name, Marion. De Man says this really wasn’t an accusation–in fact, this was just a meaningless word blurted out–that there is no possibility really of confession, that there is no real subjectivity that can affirm or deny guilt or responsibility: in other words, a lot of things that, needless to say, attracted the attention of a public that wasn’t perhaps so much concerned that he had written these articles but that he had never for the rest of his career admitted having done so; in other words, that he had suppressed a past. Nobody really believed he still had these sympathies, but the whole question was, why didn’t he fess up? Why didn’t he come clean? Of course, they took “The Purloined Ribbon” to be his sort of allegorical way of suggesting that he couldn’t possibly confess because nobody can confess, there’s no human subjectivity, etc., etc., etc.

正如我所说，这篇文章引发了相当大的争议，就像海德格尔一样，由于我们现在所了解的，很难再用同样的方式解读德曼。不过，我也要指出——我认为参与这场争论的人大多都承认这一点，尽管有些人走得更远——德曼或解构主义中都不存在任何隐晦的右翼主义。对于解构主义所谓的“不可判定性”（即我们无法对任何事物形成有理有据的观点），有两种可能的应对方式。对此有两种可能的应对方式，一种是积极的，一种是消极的。消极的应对方式认为，不可判定性会在理智和意识中打开一个空洞，狂热和暴政可以趁虚而入。换句话说，如果存在一种经过深思熟虑且论证巧妙的反对意见的方式——不妨称之为“解构”——那么，在缺乏有理有据、论证充分的意见的情况下，就会出现一个真空地带，狂热和暴政便可趁虚而入。这就是对不可判定性的负面回应，当然，我们许多人可能都持有这种观点。

So, as I say, there was a considerable controversy swirling around this article, and just as is the case with Heidegger, it has been very difficult to read de Man in the same way again as a result of what we now know. Let me just say though also that–and I think this was largely confessed by the people engaged in the controversy although some people did go farther–there is no cryptically encoded rightism either in de Man or in deconstruction. There are two possible ways of reacting to what deconstruction calls “undecidability,” that is to say the impossibility of our really being able to form a grounded opinion about anything. There are two possible ways of reacting to this, one positive and one negative. The negative way is to say that undecidability opens a void in the intellect and in consciousness into which fanaticism and tyranny can rush. In other words, if there is a sort of considered and skillfully argued resistance to opinion–call that “deconstruction”–then in the absence of decently grounded, decently argued opinion, you get this void into which fanaticism and tyranny can rush. That’s the negative response to undecidability, and it’s of course, a view that many of us may entertain.

然而，对不可判定性的积极回应是这样的：不可判定性是一种对所有观点本身持续不断的警惕审视，其目的正是为了抵制和反抗那些最恶劣、最顽固的观点：狂热和暴政的观点。换句话说，你可以对怀疑论采取两种截然不同的看法：[笑] 一种看法是，怀疑论坚持观点缺乏基础，这本身就是一种对任何挑战它的观点的被动默许；另一方面，你也可以认为，如果没有怀疑论，每个人都容易过度执着于某种观点，而这恰恰是怀疑论应该抵制的。这并非我在课程中第一次停下来思考这样一个十字路口：你不可能同时选择两条路[笑]，但显然，做出决定非常非常困难。虽然人们不愿承认，但最终选择哪条路可能取决于个人的性格。

The positive reaction, however, to undecidability is this: undecidability is a perpetually vigilant scrutiny of all opinion as such, precisely in order to withstand and to resist those most egregious and incorrigible opinions of all: the opinions of fanaticism and tyranny. In other words, you can take two views in effect of skepticism: [laughs] the one that it is, in its insistence on a lack of foundation for opinion, a kind of passive acquiescence in whatever rises up in its face; and on the other hand, you can argue that without skepticism, everybody is vulnerable to excessive commitment to opinion, which is precisely the thing that skepticism is supposed to resist. Now this isn’t the first time in this course that I’ve paused over a moment at a crossroads where you can’t possibly take both paths [laughs] but where it is obviously very, very difficult to make up one’s mind. More than one can say or care to admit, it may ultimately be a matter of temperament which path one chooses to take.

第四章 德曼与德里达的相似之处

Chapter 4. Similarities Between De Man and Derrida

好的。总之，既然我们谈到了解构主义，在深入探讨德曼之前，我想先说明一点，如果可以的话，还有另一种不批评解构主义的方式。人们普遍认为，解构主义否认文本之外任何现实的存在。德里达曾说过一句名言：“文本之外什么都没有”，对吧？当然，他的意思是，除了文本之外什么都没有。也就是说，我们生活的整个组织、结构和本质——包括我们知道文本就是一切的历史——我们的生活就是文本化的生活。这就是他的意思。他并不是说文本就在这里，文本包含了所有重要的东西，除此之外什么都不存在。他的意思是，从某种意义上说，“除了文本之外什么也没有”，因为我们通常认为的自发生活的一切，实际上都是通过我们在本课程中已经详细讨论过的方式进行媒介化的，我们将通过我们的知识进一步讨论，而我们的知识是文本性的，对吗？

All right. Now in any case, while we’re on the subject of deconstruction in general and before we get into de Man, let me just say that there is one other way, if I may, not to criticize deconstruction. It’s always supposed popularly that deconstruction denies the existence of any reality outside a text. Derrida famously, notoriously, said “there is nothing outside the text,” right? What he meant by that, of course, is that there’s nothing but text. That is to say, the entire tissue, structure, and nature of our lives–including history, which we know textually is all there is–our lives are textual lives. That’s what he meant. He didn’t mean to say the text is here, the text contains everything that matters, and nothing else exists anyway. What he meant to say is that there is “nothing but text” in the sense that absolutely everything we ordinarily take to be just our kind of spontaneously lived existence is, in fact, mediated in the ways we’ve already discussed at length in this course, and we’ll discuss more by our knowledge and that our knowledge is textual, right?

他的意思就是这样，但正如我所说，这一点被广泛误解了。德曼在你表格上的第四段中再次反驳了这种流行的假设，他说：

That’s what he meant but, as I say, it’s widely misunderstood, and de Man in the fourth passage on your sheet returns to the attack against this popular supposition and says:

在真正的符号学以及其他以语言学为导向的理论中，语言的指称功能（注意这里引用了雅各布森）并未被否定。恰恰相反。（换句话说，这并非像约翰逊博士反驳的那位唯心主义者那样，他踢了一块石头，然后痛苦地跳开，说道：“我这样反驳它。”没有人会否认石头的存在，对吧？事实并非如此。现实存在，现实就是现实本身，而指称功能在语言中始终发挥作用，试图与现实相联系。）问题在于语言对自然或现象认知的权威性。（也就是说，我们能否借助语言这一工具来认识事物是什么——不是事物存在，而是事物是什么？德曼接着提出了一个极具挑战性的观点：）我们所谓的意识形态，恰恰是混淆了语言现实与自然现实，混淆了指称与现象学。换句话说，意识形态无非就是相信语言，我的语言——我用语言所说的话和我所想的话——表达的是真理。这就是我所持的立场，这与说外面的世界不存在完全是两回事——两者毫无关系。

In genuine semiology as well as in other linguistically oriented theories, the referential [and notice the citation of Jakobson here] function of language is not being denied. Far from it. [In other words, it’s not a question of the idealist who was refuted by Dr. Johnson who kicked a stone and leaped away in terrible pain saying, “I refute it thus.” Nobody denies the existence of the stone, right? That is not at all the case. Reality is there, reality is what it is, and the referential function is perpetually in play in language, trying to hook on to that reality.] What is in question is its authority for natural or phenomenal cognition. [That is to say, can we know what things are–not that things are but what things are using the instrument of language? De Man goes on to say very challengingly:] What we call ideology is precisely the confusion of linguistic with natural reality, of reference with phenomenalism. [In other words, ideology is nothing other than the belief that language, my language–what I say and what I think in language–speaks true.] That’s the position taken up, not at all the same thing as saying what’s out there doesn’t exist–nothing to do with that.

好的。德曼早期的学术生涯受到了影响——我指的不是他撰写这些文章的早期阶段，而是他第一本书《盲目与洞察》中收录的那些文章。他的早期学术生涯主要受到法国知识分子思想的影响，尤其是让-保罗·萨特的《存在与虚无》。《盲目与洞察》的论证与其说是德曼后来对语言学的关注，不如说是他将萨特和存在主义融合进一种文学理论的过程。这些文本，特别是题为《批评与危机》的文章——也就是我在你们的资料上引用的第一篇——最好从这个角度来解读；但很快，德曼就接受并吸收了索绪尔在语言学和结构主义方面的影响，他的词汇也从此呈现出这些特征。今天这篇文章中我们需要探讨的词汇，部分来源于雅各布森对隐喻和转喻之间关系的理解，我们稍后会对此进行更详细的讨论。

All right. Now de Man’s early career was influenced–I’m not speaking of the very early career in which he wrote these articles, but the early career involving the essays which were collected in his first book, Blindness and Insight. His early career is mainly influenced by French intellectualism, in particular Jean-Paul Sartre’s Being and Nothingness, and the argument of Blindness and Insight is largely to be understood not so much in terms of de Man’s later preoccupations with linguistics as with the negotiation of Sartre and existentialism into a kind of literary theory. The texts, in particular the text called “Criticism and Crisis”–the first one that I quote on your sheet–can best be read in those terms; but soon enough, de Man did accept and embrace the influence of Saussure in linguistics and structuralism, and his vocabulary henceforth took these forms. The vocabulary that we have to wrestle with for today’s essay is taken in part from Jakobson’s understanding of the relationship between metaphor and metonymy, and we will have more to say about that.

但与此同时，既然我们承认德里达和德曼都受到了同一种语言学思维的影响，那么或许可以借此机会谈谈他们之间的异同。同样地，他们都认为思考开端非常困难，但与此同时，人们必须找到某种方法，某种原始结构主义的方法来理解，在某个特定时刻之前——也就是说，在某个共时性切面之前——事物与之后某个时刻的状态有所不同。所以，在你表格上的第二段文字中（我稍后会再提到），我们发现德曼说：“可以说，文学理论是在……”——这是德曼对这一事件的解读，他同意德里达的观点：“当然，上帝诞生了；人诞生了；意识诞生了。这些都很好，但它们只是形而上学中的中心能指。语言则有所不同。”对吧？

But in the meantime it’s probably on this occasion, once we accept them both as having come under the influence of the same form of linguistic thinking, to say a little bit about the similarities and differences that exist between Derrida and de Man. Now similarly, they both take for granted that it is very difficult to think about beginnings, but at the same time, one has to have some way, some proto-structuralist way, of understanding that before a certain moment–that is to say, before a certain synchronic cross-section–things were different from the way they were in some successive moment. So in the second passage on your sheet to which I’ll return in the end, we find de Man saying, “Literary theory can be said to come into being when”–that is de Man’s version of the event, and he agrees with Derrida in saying, “Well, sure God came into being; man came into being; consciousness came into being. That’s all very well, but they’re just head signifiers in metaphysics. There’s something different about language.” Right?

德里达和德曼都认为，语言的产生与其他事物的产生方式截然不同。他们指出，语言并不试图独立于自身之外。它无法独立于自身之外，也无法构成自身。它始终被自身的系统性所包裹，因此它本身就是一个中心。我们必须避免过度执着于语言作为中心的观念，但至少它并非那种独立于自身之外的中心，也并非那种仅仅因为其是某种遥远、隐秘、非人格化的、疏远的原因而存在的中心。语言以一种其他事物所不具备的方式，被自身所包裹。此外，我认为，德里达和德曼都强调这些二元关系是相互依存、相互影响的，这与我一直在德里达的论述有相似之处。

What both Derrida and de Man say about the difference when one thinks of language coming into being, from thinking about all those other things coming into being, is that language does not purport to stand outside of itself. It cannot stand outside of itself. It cannot constitute itself. It is perpetually caught up in its own systematic nature so that it’s a center. We have to resist excessive commitment to this idea of it being a center, but it is at least not a center which somehow stands outside of itself and is a center only in the sense that it is some remote, hidden, impersonal, distant cause. Language is caught up in itself in a way that all of these other moments were not. Then also, I think that you can see the similarity to Derrida and de Man’s way of insisting on these binary relations as interdependent and mutual, comparable to the sort of thing that I’ve been talking about in Derrida.

以第 891 页和 892 页为例，特别是第 891 页最底部到第 892 页的部分。德曼说：

Take page 891 and 892 for example, the very bottom of 891 over to 892. De Man says:

不难看出，这种表面上以真理之名对批评家兼哲学家的推崇，实际上是对诗人作为真理主要来源的推崇……他的意思并非像弗洛伊德那样，说“诗人先于我出现，诗人在我之前就知道我所知道的一切”。他完全不是这个意思。他的意思体现在他接下来的论述中。

It is easy enough to see that this apparent glorification of the critic-philosopher in the name of truth is in fact a glorification of the poet as the primary source of this truth… Now he does not mean, as Freud, for example, meant in saying, “The poets came before me and the poets knew everything I knew before I knew it.” He does not mean that at all. What he means is what he says in the following clauses.

如果真理是对某种谬误的系统性特征的认识，那么它就完全依赖于这种谬误的先在存在。换句话说，真理源于谬误。谬误并非偏离真理，对吗？谬误并非对事物进行诗意的阐释，也并非像柏拉图所认为的那样，以某种方式破坏哲学家所认定的真理的完整性。相反，正确理解的哲学，正是在充分认识一种预先存在的谬误之后才产生的。这正是德曼想要思考文学与其他言语形式之间关系的方式。

[I]f truth is the recognition of the systematic character of a certain kind of error, then it would be fully dependent on the prior existence of this error. In other words, truth arises out of error. Error is not a deviance from truth. Right? Error is not a poetic elaboration on things which somehow, as it does in Plato’s view, undermines the integrity of that truth identified by philosophers. On the contrary, philosophy properly understood is what comes into being when one has achieved full recognition of a preexisting error. That is the way in which de Man wants to think about the relationship precisely between literature and other forms of speech.

第五章 德曼与德里达：差异

Chapter 5. De Man and Derrida: Differences

说到这里，我想立刻谈谈我与德里达的不同之处。正如我所说，德里达相信存在一种无缝衔接的话语网络，或者说话语性。我们被话语所包围。没错，我们可以暂时地、启发式地谈论某种话语形式与另一种话语形式之间的区别——文学、法律、神学、科学等等——但所有这些都很容易被瓦解，并被揭穿其作为真正独立完整性的存在。德曼并不认同这种观点。相反，德曼认为存在一种“文学性”。在这方面，他比德里达更始终如一地追随雅各布森。他反复强调，重要的是要坚持文学与其他话语形式之间的区别。

In saying that, I want to move immediately to the differences with Derrida. Derrida, as I said, believes in a kind of seamless web of discourse or discursivity. We are awash in discourse. Yes, we can provisionally or heuristically speak of one form of discourse as opposed to another–literature, law, theology, science and so on–but it is all easily undermined and demystified as something that has real independent integrity. De Man does not believe this. De Man thinks, on the contrary, that there is such a thing as literariness. He follows Jakobson much more consistently in this regard than Derrida does. Again and again he says that the important thing is to insist on the difference between literature and other forms of discourse.

我可以引用很多段落来佐证这一点。让我快速读几段，在第883页，大约在左侧栏三分之二的位置，他在那里听起来很像一位俄国形式主义者，谈论文学，尤其是其他话语形式所独有的东西。他说：

There are all kinds of passages I could elicit in support of this. Let me just quickly read a few, page 883, about two thirds of the way down the left-hand column, where he’s sounds very much like a Russian formalist talking about the what literature, in particular, has exclusively that other forms of discourse don’t have. He says:

……文学不能仅仅被视为一个明确的指称意义单元，可以被解码而不留下任何痕迹。其编码异常醒目、复杂且神秘；它本身就吸引了过多的关注，而这种关注必须发展成一种严谨的方法。对编码本身的专注是不可避免的，文学必然会孕育出其自身的形式主义。由于时间关系，我将略过一些原本打算读给你们听的段落，这些段落旨在强化德曼关于文学与其他话语形式区别的论点。剩下的问题是：文学与其他话语形式的区别究竟在哪里？嗯，它揭示了其他自以为指涉事物的话语形式所无法察觉的错误。文学深知自身的虚构性。最终，我们得出这样的结论：如果我们要思考文学，我们就应该想到虚构的东西：不是基于某种事物的东西，而是虚构的东西。

… [L]iterature cannot merely be received as a definite unit of referential meaning that can be decoded without leaving a residue. The code is unusually conspicuous, complex, and enigmatic; it attracts an inordinate amount of attention to itself, and this attention has to acquire the rigor of a method. The structural moment of concentration on the code for its own sake cannot be avoided, and literature necessarily breeds its own formalism. In the interest of time, I’m going to skip over a few other passages that I was going to read to you in reinforcement of this insistence, on de Man’s part, that literature differs from other forms of discourse, the remaining question being: literature differs from other forms of discourse how? Well, it is the disclosure of error that other forms of discourse supposing themselves to refer to things remain unaware of. Literature knows itself to be fictive. Ultimately, we reach the conclusion that if we’re to think of literature, we’re to think of something that is made up: not something that is based on something but something that is made up.

在第一段中，批评界对语言的论述——符号与意义永远不可能重合——恰恰是我们称之为“文学”的语言中理所当然的。文学不同于日常语言，它始于对这种认知的超越。它是唯一一种摆脱了直接表达谬误的知识形式——换句话说，它摆脱了“当我说‘下雨了’时，我指的是气象学家，我说的就是‘下雨了’”这种谬误。文学作品在表达“下雨了”时，并非在向窗外眺望，对吧？这的确完全正确。作者或许确实在向窗外眺望（笑），但我们所接触到的文学作品，作为文本本身，并非在向窗外眺望。文本又怎能向窗外眺望呢？当文学作品表达“下雨了”时，它另有所图，正如我们所说：

In the first passage, the statement about language by criticism, that sign and meaning can never coincide, is what is precisely taken for granted in the kind of language we call “literary.” Literature, unlike everyday language, begins on the far side of this knowledge. It is the only form of knowledge free from the fallacy of unmediated expression–in other words, free from the fallacy that when I say “It is raining,” I mean I’m a meteorologist and I mean it is raining. Literature, when it says “It is raining,” is not looking out of the window, right? This is after all perfectly true. The author may have been looking out of the window, [laughs] but literature, as we encounter it and as a text, is not looking out of the window. How can a text look out of the window? When literature says “It is raining,” it’s got something else, as one might say, in view:

德曼继续说道，我们所有人都明白这一点，尽管我们以一种误导性的方式，即一厢情愿地断言相反的情况，但当我们称文学为虚构作品时，我们对文学本质的预知便会浮现出来。正因如此，在你那份摘自斯特凡诺·罗索访谈的资料的最后一段中，德曼才愿意大胆地将自己的作品与他挚友雅克·德里达的作品区分开来。他说：

All of us [de Man continues] know this although we know it in the misleading way of a wishful assertion of the opposite, yet the truth emerges in the foreknowledge we possess of the true nature of literature when we refer to it as fiction. This is why in the last passage on your sheet from the interview with Stefano Rosso, de Man is willing to venture on a categorical distinction between his own work and that of his very close friend, Jacques Derrida. He says:

我倾向于赋予文本（他指的是文学文本）一种内在的权威，我认为这种权威比德里达赋予它们的要强。从某种复杂的角度来看，我会坚持认为文本会自我解构（换句话说，文学是对自身指涉性的永恒否定），它是自我解构的，而不是被哲学干预所解构（就像雅克·德里达所做的那样——也就是说，雅克·德里达从外部用他那把精细的大锤砸向每一种可以想象的表达形式——而不是被文本之外的哲学干预所解构）。以上就是我对德曼和德里达之间异同的一些看法。

I have a tendency to put upon texts [and he means literary texts] an inherent authority which is stronger, I think, than Derrida is willing to put on them. In a complicated way, I would hold to the statement that the text deconstructs itself [In other words, literature is the perpetual denial of its referentiality], is self-deconstructive rather than being deconstructed by a philosophical intervention [that which Jacques Derrida does–that is to say, Jacques Derrida bringing his sort of delicate sledgehammer down on every conceivable form of utterance from the outside–right–rather than being deconstructed by a philosophical intervention from outside the text]. So those are some remarks then on the differences and the similarities between de Man and Derrida.

第六章 例子：《一家子》、叶芝和普鲁斯特

Chapter 6. Examples: “All in the Family,” Yeats, and Proust

从历史角度来看，《符号学与修辞学》的出现接近《结构、符号与游戏》所开启的时期的尾声。也就是说，它发表于《阅读的寓言》一书中，我们可以将其创作时间追溯到20世纪80年代初。虽然它最初于1979年以文章的形式发表，但这同时也接近德里达文章所开启的繁荣时期的尾声，其他一些因素开始变得至关重要。甚至在德曼去世以及他的过往被揭露之前，就已经有很多人挥舞着拳头，质问道：“历史呢？现实呢？”我已经指出，这种回应在很多方面都显得天真，但它仍然根深蒂固。在这种回应的氛围中，德曼在第883页左栏顶部写道：

Now “Semiology and Rhetoric” historically comes near the end of the period that “Structure, Sign, and Play” inaugurates. That is to say, it is published in Allegories of Reading and is a text which we can date from the early 1980s. Well, it was published originally as an article in 1979, but this is also near the end of a period of flourishing that Derrida’s essay inaugurates, and other things have begun to become crucial. Even before the death of de Man and the revelations about his past, there were a lot of people sort of shaking their fists and saying, “What about history? What about reality?” I’ve already suggested that in a variety of ways this is a response that can be naïve but it is still very much in the air. De Man says in this atmosphere of response–at the top of page 883, the left-hand column, he says:

我们仿佛认为，文学形式的问题已经彻底解决，结构分析的技巧也已臻于完美，现在我们可以“超越形式主义”，去探讨真正让我们感兴趣的问题，最终收获之前对技巧的美学专注所带来的成果，而正是这些技巧为我们迈出这一决定性一步做好了准备。显然，我想你现在应该明白，他想表达的是，如果我们真的迈出这一步，超越形式主义，我们就忘记了俄国形式主义者的一条基本原则：即形式与内容之间没有区别——换句话说，我们实际上无法超越形式主义，认为我们可以超越形式主义的想法仅仅是程序上的错误。当然，这正是本文所要阐述的立场。本文的任务是否定互补性——即使在像热拉尔·热奈特、托多罗夫、巴特等人那样严谨的修辞分析中，也存在相互加强的情况，而作者认为这些人已经从雅各布森的严谨性退步了——否定在修辞分析中，话语的修辞和语法方面可以被认为是相互勾结、连续或合作的。

We speak as if, with the problems of literary form resolved once and forever and with techniques of structural analysis refined to near-perfection, we could now move “beyond formalism” toward the questions that really interest us and reap, at last, the fruits of the aesthetic concentration on techniques that prepared us for this decisive step. Obviously, I think by this time you can realize what he’s saying is if we make this move, if we move beyond formalism, we have forgotten the cardinal rule of the Russian formalists: namely, that there’s no distinction between form and content–in other words, that we in effect can’t move beyond formalism and that it is simply a procedurally mistaken notion that we can. That’s the position, of course, pursued in this essay. The task of the essay is to deny the complementarity–the mutual reinforcement even in rigorous rhetorical analysis like that of Gerard Genette, Todorov, Barthes and others, all of whom he says have regressed from the rigor of Jakobson–to deny that in rhetorical analysis rhetorical and grammatical aspects of discourse can be considered collusive, continuous, or cooperative with each other.

我已经指出了即使单独考虑这个术语本身也会出现的问题。顺便说一句，我其实是借鉴了雅克·德里达的一篇文章，嗯……（笑）（笑）——总之，就是那篇文章，（笑）现在你永远不会知道我的出处了。（笑）无论如何，德里达在这篇文章中（笑）（笑）竭力论证语法不能还原为修辞，修辞也不能还原为语法。所以，当我们按照我的建议思考这些问题时，我们已经引入了德曼反复强调的观点。他说：“哎呀，这理论太复杂了。我完全搞不懂，所以我最好还是实际一点，给你们举些例子来说明我的意思。”于是他拿起《一家子》，讲起了阿奇被伊迪丝解释保龄球鞋鞋带系在鞋帮上和系在鞋帮下的区别时，阿奇恼火不已的那段情节——这源于阿奇问他：“有什么区别？”换句话说，阿奇问了一个反问句。“我不在乎区别是什么”就是这个反问句的含义。正如德曼所说，伊迪丝的阅读理解力极其简单，她把这个反问句误解成了语法问题：“有什么区别？我很好奇。”然后她开始解释说，一种是鞋带系在鞋帮上，另一种是鞋带系在鞋帮下。阿奇当然受不了，因为对他来说，反问句就是反问句，这显而易见。

Now I’ve already suggested the problems that arise when you consider this term even in and of itself. I’m actually ripping off, by the way, an essay of Jacques Derrida’s called, hm [laughs] [laughter]– anyway, it’s that essay and [laughter] now you’ll never know my source. [laughter] In any case, Derrida, too, in this essay which [laughs] [laughter] is at pains to argue that you can’t reduce grammar to rhetoric or rhetoric to grammar. So as we think about these things as I suggest, we’ve already introduced what de Man drives home to us. He says, “Boy, this is complicated theory. I’m in over my head, so I better just get practical and give you some examples of what I mean.” So he takes up “All in the Family” and talks about the moment in which Archie becomes exasperated when Edith begins to tell him that the difference between bowling shoes laced over and bowling shoes laced under–this in response to Archie’s question, “What’s the difference?” In other words, Archie has asked a rhetorical question. “I don’t care what the difference is” is the meaning of the rhetorical question. Edith, a reader of sublime simplicity, as de Man says, misinterprets the rhetorical question as a grammatical question: “What is the difference? I’m curious to know.” Then she proceeds to explain that there’s lacing over, on the one hand, and lacing under, on the other hand. Archie, of course, can’t stand this because for him it’s perfectly clear that a rhetorical question is a rhetorical question.

德曼的观点是，一个问题既是修辞性的又是语法性的，二者不可相互简化。两种解读都是成立的。他随后引用叶芝的诗作《在学童之间》，使论点更加复杂化，但并未改变原有的论证。这首诗的结尾——你还记得吗？——运用了一系列隐喻，试图（至少表面上是试图）将对立的事物融合起来，最终得出结论：“我们如何区分舞者和舞蹈？”又是一个问题，对吧？现在，这个修辞性问题完成了对这首诗的通常解读。而这个修辞性问题的答案是：我们无法区分舞者和舞蹈。它们在构成艺术作品的综合性、象征性的瞬间中融为一体，而之前所有的隐喻都指向这种胜利般的统一感，这种象征性的统一感，正是艺术作品的本质——顺便一提，这种统一感包含着作者与文本的统一、主体与作品的统一，以及所有那些正如我们所见，许多文学理论试图瓦解的事物的统一。我们如何区分舞者和舞蹈呢？

De Man’s point is a question is both rhetorical and grammatical, and the one cannot be reduced to the other. Both readings are available. He complicates, without changing the argument, by then referring to Yeats’ poem “Among Schoolchildren,” which culminates you remember–it has a whole series of metaphors of attempting, seeming at least to attempt, the synthesis of opposites concluding: “how can we can tell the dancer from the dance?” Another question, right? Now the rhetorical question completes the usual reading of the poem. The answer to the rhetorical question is that we can’t tell the difference between the dancer and the dance. They are unified in a synthetic, symbolizing, symbolic moment that constitutes the work of art, and all the preceding metaphors lead up to this triumphant sense of unity, of symbolic unity, as the essence of the work of art–a unity which, by the way, entails among other things the unity of author and text: the unity of agent and production, the unity of all of those things which, as we’ve seen, much literary theory is interested in collapsing. How can we tell the dancer from the dance?

德曼说：“等等，这其实也是个语法问题。”如果你停下来，把它当成一个语法问题来思考，你就会想：“哎呀，这真是个好问题，不是吗？[笑]因为，世界上最容易的事情当然是区分舞者和舞蹈。[笑]我就是舞者，这是我跳的舞，[笑]显然它们不是一回事，”对吧？这诗句真是胡说八道。简直荒谬至极。而且，即使你那严谨的、某种象征性的解读坚持认为它应该消失，它仍然具有语法意义，对吧？然后，恰巧是叶芝研究专家的德曼（他发表过关于叶芝的论文，对叶芝的作品了如指掌）开始从叶芝的全部作品中引证，以证明叶芝完全了解并意识到这些语法差异，而且诗中蕴含的某种反讽使其免于被这种象征性的神秘化。他提出了一个完全合理的论点，即这个问题是语法性的，而非修辞性的。他并没有声称——他也向我们指出了这一点——他的解释才是正确的。这根本不是他的重点。他只是声称，这种解释是存在的，并且可以从我们所谓的“证据”中推导出来，就像基于反问句的象征性解释是存在的，并且可以从证据中推导出来一样——而且这两种观点是不可分割的。传统学生在研究文学作品的修辞和语法效果时，往往想当然地认为修辞和语法之间的关系是可以调和的，但事实并非如此。

Well, de Man says, “Wait a minute though. This is also a grammatical question.” If you stop and think of it as a grammatical question, you say to yourself, “Gee, that’s a very [laughs] good question, isn’t it, because, of course, the easiest thing in the world is to tell the dancer from the dance. [laughs] I am the dancer and this is the dance I am doing and [laughter] obviously they’re not the same thing,” right? What nonsense poetry speaks. It’s perfectly ridiculous. There is also a grammatical sense which won’t go away just because your rigorous, sort of symbolic interpretation insists that it should go away, right? Then de Man, who happens to be a Yeats scholar–he published a dissertation on Yeats and really knows his Yeats–starts adducing examples from all over the canon of Yeats to the effect that Yeats is perfectly knowing and self-conscious about these grammatical differences, and that there is a measure of irony in the poem that saves it from this sort of symbolizing mystification. He makes a perfectly plausible argument to the effect that the question is grammatical rather than rhetorical. He’s not claiming–and he points this out to us–that his explication is the true one. That’s not his point at all. He’s claiming only that it is available and can be adduced from what we call “evidence” in the same way that the symbolic interpretation, based on the rhetorical question, is available and can be adduced from evidence–and that these two viewpoints are irreducible. They cannot be reconciled as traditional students of the relationship between rhetoric and grammar in studying the rhetorical and grammatical effects of literature take for granted.

这就是他的论点。这是一种内讧，因为他谈论的是两个实际上关系非常密切的盟友。他说他们做得很好，但他们忘记了一件小事：修辞和语法无法调和。每个句子都是一个谓词，如果每个句子都是谓词，那么它也具有隐喻的结构；而句子中的隐喻和谓词总是相互矛盾的。隐喻就是我们所说的诗意的谎言。人人都知道A不是B。另一方面，谓词通常是为了指称而存在的。它是一种真理主张——对吧？——但如果修辞和语法同时存在于一个句子中，那么句子的真理主张和它的谎言就永远相互冲突。仅仅把这句话当作句子来看，撇开我们对意图的任何推断——我们非常清楚伊迪丝的意图和阿奇·邦克的意图。这并不是说我们对他们所说的话的意思感到困惑。只是还有其他可能的解释，而由于他们的想法并不一致，这两种解释就痛苦地、无法调和地相互冲突，对吧？

That’s his argument. It’s a kind of infighting because he’s talking about two people who are actually very close allies. He’s saying they’re doing great work but they forget this one little thing: you cannot reconcile rhetoric and grammar. Every sentence is a predication, and if every sentence is a predication, it also has the structure of a metaphor; and the metaphor in a sentence and the predication in a sentence are always going to be at odds. A metaphor is what we call a poetic lie. Everybody knows A is not B. A predication, on the other hand, usually goes forward in the service of referentiality. It’s a truth claim of some kind–right?–but if rhetoricity and grammaticality coexist in any sentence, the sentence’s truth claim and its lie are perpetually at odds with each other. Just taking the sentence as a sentence, irrespective of any kind of inference we might make about intentions–we know perfectly well what Edith intends and what Archie Bunker intends. It’s not as if we’re confused about the meaning of what they’re saying. It’s just that other meanings are available, and since they’re not on the same page, those two other meanings coexist painfully and irreducibly at odds, right?

但有些情况——假设阿奇·邦克是阿凯·德邦克。假设阿奇·邦克是雅克·德里达，而雅克·德里达走过来问：“什么是差异？”对吧？[笑声] 那将是完全不同的情况，不是吗？因为你根本不知道这个问题是修辞性的还是语法性的，对吧？在这种情况下，不可能援引意图，因为德里达的复杂性恰恰在于提出关于未知的问题，无法表达差异与差异之间的差异，也不知道阿奇是对的还是伊迪丝是对的。

But there are cases–suppose Archie Bunker were Arkay Debunker. Suppose Archie Bunker were Jacques Derrida, and Jacques Derrida came along and said, “What is the différance?” Right? [laughter] That would be an entirely different matter, wouldn’t it, because you would have absolutely no idea whether the question was rhetorical or grammatical, right? There it wouldn’t be possible to invoke an intention because the whole complication of Derrida is precisely to raise the question about not knowing, not being able to voice the différance between difference and différance and not knowing whether Archie is right or whether Edith is right.

我没时间读普鲁斯特，但那段精彩的文字解读得非常精彩——记得他在文章开头就巧妙地铺垫了这段文字，他提到普鲁斯特笔下的祖母总是把马塞尔赶到花园里，因为她受不了他沉浸在阅读中的内心世界。后来，德曼引用了这段精彩的文字，马塞尔在文中谈到，他如何将外部世界带入内心，因为他在阅读过程中始终意识到外面发生的一切，最终，在他沉浸于阅读的奇妙时刻，内外之间失去了界限。换句话说，这里运用了一种隐喻，一种对内外关系的修辞理解，但语法分析表明，这段文字的整体结构是叠加式的——也就是说，不断添加内容——它在使论点复杂化和强化的同时，并没有强调同一性，也没有强调隐喻所依赖的根本同一性。所以他称之为转喻。

Proust I don’t have time for, but it’s a marvelous reading of that wonderful passage in which–remember that he’s set it up at the beginning of the essay with a kind of wonderful, cunning sort of sense of structure by talking about the grandmother in Proust who’s always driving Marcel out into the garden because she can’t stand the interiority of his reading. Well, later on in the essay de Man quotes this wonderful passage in which Marcel talks about the way in which he brought the outside inside as he was perpetually conscious of everything that was going on out there during the process of his reading, so that ultimately in the charmed moment of his reading, there was no difference between inside and outside. In other words, a metaphor, a rhetorical understanding of the relationship between inside and outside has been accomplished, but then grammatical analysis shows that the whole structure of the passage is additive–that is, adding things on–and is complicating and reinforcing an argument without insisting on identity, on the underlying identity on which metaphor depends; so he calls this metonymic.

顺便说一句，关于将修辞手法——转喻——与语法在组合层面上的运用混为一谈所造成的奇怪混乱，我也要留给你们的章节来讨论。这部分就留给你们的章节吧。与此同时，他说道：“不，不，不。我猜这段文字终究不是修辞。它一定是转喻——但是等等！它是用一个声音说的。毕竟，有一个美妙的、统摄一切的声音。这就是我所说的，”德曼说道，“语法的修辞化，对吧——但是等等！那个声音不是作者的声音。那个声音是一个说话者的声音。那个声音是马塞尔在施展他那奇妙的隐喻魔法，但我们知道，作者正在以最费力、最精心的方式，煞费苦心地将这一切组合起来，以一种叠加的方式创造出一些根本不是修辞的东西；它是语法性的。这是一位伟大的作家在组合长句，所以等等。它终究一定是修辞的语法化，”关键在于，解释的蠕虫一直在转动。明白了吗？它不会随意地在任何地方戛然而止，因为修辞和语法是不可化约的。我们必须始终认为它们彼此不相容。好了，就此打住——或许还会补充一两句话——但恐怕到了周四，我们将不得不略显尴尬地转向弗洛伊德和彼得·布鲁克斯；我真希望中间能有个周末。到时候见。

By the way, I’m going to leave also to your sections the strange confusion that ensues in taking a rhetorical device, metonymy, and making it synonymous with grammar on the axis of combination. I leave that to your sections. In the meantime he says, “No, no, no then. I guess this passage isn’t rhetorical after all. It must be metonymic–but wait! It is spoken by a voice. There is this wonderful overarching voice that unifies everything after all. This is what I call,” says de Man, “the rhetoricization of grammar, right–but wait! That voice is not the author. That voice is a speaker. That voice is Marcel performing his wonderful sort of metaphoric magic, but we know that the author is painstakingly putting this together in the most laborious kind of composed way, making something up in an additive way that’s not rhetorical at all; it’s grammatical. This is a supreme writer putting together long sentences and so wait a minute. It must be, after all, a grammaticization of rhetoric,” the whole point of which is that the worm of interpretation keeps turning. All right? It doesn’t arbitrarily stop anywhere because rhetoric and grammar remain irreducible. We have to keep thinking of them as being uncooperative with each other. Okay, have to stop there–might add a word or two–but on Thursday we turn, I’m afraid with a certain awkwardness; I wish there were an intervening weekend, to Freud and Peter Brooks. In the meantime, we’ll see you then.

第十二讲——弗洛伊德与小说

Lecture 12 - Freud and Fiction

第一章 布鲁克斯对雅各布森和德曼的感激之情

Chapter 1. Brooks’s Debt to Jakobson and de Man

保罗·弗莱教授：嗯，今天显然是我们课程的一个分水岭或过渡日。你们记得，我们一开始强调的是语言。然后我们承诺会转向心理学方面的内容，最后是文学的社会和文化决定因素。到目前为止，我们一直致力于探讨这样一种观点：思想和言语是由语言构成的，或者换句话说，是由语言产生的；思想和言语必须被理解为与其语言环境密不可分——这里的语言有时被广义地理解为一种结构或符号系统。

Professor Paul Fry: Well, now today is obviously a kind of watershed or transition in our syllabus. You remember we began with an emphasis on language. We then promised to move to an emphasis on psychological matters, and finally social and cultural determinants of literature. So far we have immersed ourselves in notions to the effect that thought and speech are constituted by language or, to put it another way, brought into being by language and that thought and speech have to be understood as inseparable from their linguistic milieu–language here being understood sometimes broadly as a structure or a semiotic system.

显然，我们从以语言为主导的关于言语、话语和文学的观念，过渡到以心理学为主导的关于话语和文学的思考方式，这条路走得相当顺畅，因为前两位作者虽然借鉴了弗洛伊德的理论，并在一定程度上从精神分析的角度理解他们的研究，但他们使用的词汇对我们来说却极其熟悉。也就是说，他们确实认为，我们现在所关注的意识媒介——心灵，以及意识与无意识之间的关系——无论它是什么，都可以用我们从语言思维和语言学中借鉴的术语来理解。拉康曾说过一句名言（下周你会读到），“无意识的结构就像一种语言”，而布鲁克斯显然也同意这一点。你翻开布鲁克斯的著作，或许会发现自己与他截然不同——我不知道你们对弗洛伊德的著作有多熟悉。我们会简单谈谈《超越快乐原则》，这本书对我们的研究至关重要；但显然撇开弗洛伊德的影响和借鉴的思想不谈，你会发现布鲁克斯的写作内容对你来说相当熟悉。

Now obviously our transition from language-determined ideas about speech, discourse, and literature to psychologically determined ways of thinking about discourse and literature has a rather smooth road to follow because the first two authors who borrow from Freud and understand their project to a degree in psychoanalytic terms are nevertheless using what is now for us an extremely familiar vocabulary. That is to say, they really do suppose that the medium of consciousness to which we now turn–the psyche, the relationship between consciousness and the unconscious–they really do suppose that this entity, whatever it may be, can be understood in terms that we take usefully from verbal thought and from linguistics. Lacan famously said, as you’ll find next week, “The unconscious is structured like a language,” and Brooks plainly does agree. You open Brooks and you find yourself really apart perhaps–I don’t know how well all of you are acquainted with the texts of Freud. We’ll say a little bit about Beyond the Pleasure Principle,which is the crucial text for our purposes; but plainly apart from the influence of and the ideas borrowed from Freud, you’ll find Brooks writing on what for you is pretty familiar turf.

例如，他一开始就借用俄国形式主义的区分来解释小说在情节和故事之间的本质区别。我觉得我最终还是不得不承认，俄语中表示情节和故事这两个概念的词分别是“syuzhet”和“fabula”，因为布鲁克斯反复使用这两个词。我已经解释过，我不好意思使用那些我完全不理解其含义的词（笑），除非我在读的书里看到它们的含义，而这些书也是你们在读的。总之（笑），既然布鲁克斯一直在用这些词，我也只能克服这种尴尬，至少偶尔自己也用用。顺便说一句，如果你试图在英语里找到它们的同源词，你会发现它们有点反直觉，因为你会觉得“syuzhet”应该是“主题”，换句话说，它更接近形式主义者在英语里所说的“故事”。另一方面，你可能会认为 fabula 可能类似于“情节”或“虚构”，但事实并非如此。恰恰相反。Syuzhet 是情节，是故事的构建方式，而 fabula 是构成 syuzhet 的主题或素材。

For example, he begins by borrowing the Russian formalist distinction in trying to explain what fiction is between plot and story. I feel that I do ultimately have to cave in and admit to you that the Russian words for these concepts, plot and story, are syuzhet and fabula respectively, because Brooks keeps using these terms again and again. I’ve explained my embarrassment about using terms that I really have no absolutely no idea [laughs] of the meaning of except that I’m told what the meaning of them is in the books that I am reading, which are the same books that you’re reading. In [laughs] any case, since Brooks does constantly use these terms, I have to overcome embarrassment and at least at times use them myself. They’re a little counterintuitive, by the way, if you try to find cognates for them in English because you’d think that syuzhet would be “subject matter,” in other words something much closer to what the formalists mean in English by “story.” On the other hand, you’d think that fabula might well be something like “plot” or “fiction,” but it is not. It’s just the opposite. Syuzhet is the plot, the way in which a story is constructed, and the fabula is the subject matter or material out of which the syuzhet is made.

好的。除了运用情节与故事之间的关系之外，我们还发现布鲁克斯使用了我们现在读过雅各布森和德曼的作品后非常熟悉的术语：“隐喻”和“转喻”。显然，现代文学理论倾向于将所有修辞手法简化为这两个术语。必要时，他们会稍作调整，援引其他术语，但文学理论通常理解的修辞学的基本区别在于隐喻和转喻之间的区别。隐喻统一、综合、融合，而转喻则通过一种可识别的邻近性手法将一个事物置于另一个事物旁边，但它并不声称或试图统一或确立同一性——简而言之，它并不坚持A就是B。正如我所说，这两个术语被简化地理解为修辞学的核心主题，并被现代理论以这种方式所挪用。

All right. In addition to the use of the relationship between plot and story, we also find Brooks using terms that are now, having read Jakobson and de Man, very familiar to us: the terms “metaphor” and “metonymy.” There’s plainly a tendency in modern literary theory to reduce all the tropes of rhetoric to just these two terms. When needed, they back up a little bit and invoke other terms, but the basic distinction in rhetoric, as literary theory tends to understand it, is the distinction between metaphor–which unifies, synthesizes, and brings together–and metonymy, which puts one thing next to another by a recognizable gesture toward contiguity but which nevertheless does not make any claim or pretension to unify or establish identity–to insist, in short, that A is B. These two terms, as I say, are understood reductively but usefully to be the essential topics of rhetoric and appropriated by modern theory in that way.

正如我所说，布鲁克斯随后以我们应当熟悉的方式运用了这些术语。我们在阅读雅各布森和德曼的著作时已经充分接触过它们。因此，尽管布鲁克斯的论证框架是精神分析的，并且他主要引用的是弗洛伊德的《超越快乐原则》一书，但他的文章《弗洛伊德的宏大计划》中仍然存在着一种语言的语言。

Now Brooks then uses these terms in ways that should be familiar to us, as I say. We have now been amply exposed to them in reading Jakobson and de Man. So there is a language of language in Brooks’ essay, “Freud’s Masterplot,” despite the fact that the framework for his argument is psychoanalytic and that he is drawing primarily on the text of Freud’s Beyond the Pleasure Principle.

第二章 布鲁克斯对弗洛伊德的借鉴

Chapter 2. Brooks’s Debt to Freud

那么，布鲁克斯从弗洛伊德那里汲取了什么？弗洛伊德的哪些方面吸引了他？顺便一提，他是一位杰出的弗洛伊德研究学者，对弗洛伊德了如指掌，事实上，他对弗洛伊德的方方面面都感兴趣。但就本文以及本文所属的著作《情节阅读》（Reading for the Plot）而言，为了构建这一论点，他尤其从弗洛伊德那里汲取的是结构的概念：弗洛伊德对拉康的预见——拉康本人当然也认为弗洛伊德预见了他——无意识的结构如同语言一般。就虚构情节的创作而言，就虚构的本质而言（这正是布鲁克斯感兴趣的），这意味着什么呢？亚里士多德告诉我们，情节有开头、中间和结尾。“废话！”我们当然会这样回应，但与此同时，我们却无法理解这看似简单的论断中蕴含的某种神秘。当然，开头是必不可少的——它必须有个开头。我们假设，除非我们讨论的是《天方夜谭》，否则它必然有个结尾。但与此同时，我们不妨问问自己，它为什么会有中间部分？中间部分相对于开头和结尾的作用是什么？正如布鲁克斯引述的，亚里士多德为什么说情节应该有一定的长度？为什么它不能更短？为什么它不能更长？换句话说，这些部分之间有什么关系？尤其是中间部分，它如何向我们揭示开头和结尾之间必然的联系：并非任何开头或结尾，而是一个能够引发某种逻辑的开头，以及一个能够以某种方式（无论是悲剧还是喜剧）令人满意地解决这种逻辑的结尾？这一切是如何运作的？布鲁克斯认为，他可以用精神分析的术语来理解这一切，我们将尝试解释。

So what does he take from Freud? What interests Brooks about Freud? He is, by the way, a distinguished Freudian scholar who knows everything about Freud and is interested, in fact, by every aspect of Freud, but for the purpose of constructing the argument here and in the book to which this essay belongs, the book called Reading for the Plot–for the purposes of constructing that argument, what he takes in particular from Freud is the idea of structure: the idea that, insofar as we can imagine Freud anticipating Lacan–Lacan himself certainly believed that Freud anticipated him–the idea that the unconscious is structured like a language. In terms of creating fictional plots, in terms of the nature of fiction, which is what interests Brooks–well, what does this mean? Aristotle tells us that a plot has a beginning, a middle and an end. “Duh!” of course, is our response, and yet at the same time we can’t understand a degree of mystery in even so seemingly simple a pronouncement. A beginning, of course–well, it has to have a beginning. We assume that unless we’re dealing with Scheherazade, it has to have an end, but at the same time we might well ask ourselves, why does it have a middle? What is the function of the middle with respect to a beginning and an end? Why does Aristotle say, as Brooks quotes him, that a plot should have a certain magnitude? Why shouldn’t it be shorter? Why shouldn’t it be longer? In other words, what is the relation of these parts, and what in particular does the middle have to do with revealing to us the necessary connectedness of the beginning and the end: not just any beginning or any end but a beginning which precipitates a kind of logic, and an end which in some way, whether tragically or comically, satisfactorily resolves that logic? How does all this work? Brooks believes that he can understand it, as we’ll try to explain, in psychoanalytic terms.

所以，他从弗洛伊德那里得到了这一点，而且正如我之前提到的，他还得到了方法论上的理念，即可以用弗洛伊德的区分来思考文本的运作机制——不是在《超越快乐原则》中，而是在《梦的解析》中，也就是你今天作业中读到的摘自该书的关于梦境运作的段落。弗洛伊德在那里论证，梦境运作的两个核心机制是凝缩和置换。凝缩提取梦境的基本符号，并将它们提炼成一种过度决定的统一体，这样，如果研究梦境运作，就能看到梦中所表达的潜在愿望或欲望以特定的符号统一体的形式显现出来。

So this he gets from Freud, and he also gets, as I’ve already suggested, the methodological idea that one can think of the machinations of a text in terms of the distinction that Freud makes–not in Beyond the Pleasure Principle, but in The Interpretation of Dreams in the passages that you read for today’s assignment taken from that book, The Interpretation of Dreams, about the dream work. It’s there that Freud argues that really the central two mechanisms of the dream work are condensation and displacement. Condensation takes the essential symbols of the dream and distills them into a kind of over-determined unity so that if one studies the dream work one can see the underlying wish or desire expressed in the dream manifest in a particular symbolic unity.

这就是梦境凝结的方式，但与此同时，梦境也在进行着截然不同的另一种活动，这被称为移置。梦境的本质象征——也就是说，梦境试图展现其渴望之物的方式——并非直接表达，而是被移置到有时晦涩相关的概念、符号、意象或活动中，而解梦者，也就是试图解读梦境的人，需要抵达并理解这些概念、符号、意象或活动。因此，移置是一种理解上的延迟或迂回，而凝结则是一种理解上的提炼。弗洛伊德在他1905年出版的著作中研究梦境时，注意到一个非凡之处——梦境运作方式的非凡之处在于，这些效应似乎存在某种共存或同时性。梦境运作同时凝结和移置着它试图以某种方式展现的渴望对象。

That’s the way in which the dream condenses, but at the same time the dream is doing something very, very different, and it’s called displacement. There the essential symbols of the dream–that is to say, the way in which the dream is attempting to manifest that which it desires, are not expressed in themselves, but are rather displaced on to sometimes obscurely related ideas or symbols, images, or activities that the interpreter, that the person trying to decode the dream, needs to arrive at and to understand. So displacement is a kind of delay or detour of understanding, and condensation, on the other hand, is a kind of distillation of understanding. The extraordinary thing that Freud remarks on as he studies dreams in this book–published in 1905, by the way–the extraordinary thing about the way in which dreams work is that there seems to be a kind of coexistence or simultaneity of these effects. The dream work simultaneously condenses and displaces that which it is somehow or another struggling to make manifest as its object of desire.

首先注意到凝缩与置换、隐喻与转喻之间可能存在联系的人有很多，其中最著名的是雅克·拉康，布鲁克斯曾引用拉康的观点：日常话语，包括我们所说的话、梦境以及我们与分析师的对话，都可以被理解为通过这两种修辞手法运作。换句话说，凝缩本质上是隐喻，而置换本质上是转喻。正如我们从德里达那里了解到的，转喻是意义的延迟或永恒的延异。隐喻则是将试图表达自身的论述汇聚成一个身份认同的陈述。正如布鲁克斯在他的文章中所论述的，我们在小说中再次看到，隐喻和转喻这两种修辞倾向并存——当然，你也能从中听出对德曼的隐晦批判——它们或许能够和谐运作，或许不能；或许能够最终达成统一，或许不能；但它们确实以某种方式共存，使我们能够理解虚构叙事的展开，如同梦境的解构过程。因此，布鲁克斯对弗洛伊德的这两个要素很感兴趣，并且他主要也是从弗洛伊德那里借鉴的。

Now the first person to notice that there might be–there are a variety of people who noticed that there might be a connection between condensation and displacement and metaphor and metonymy, most notably Jacques Lacan whom Brooks quotes to this effect: that the work in everyday discourse, in what we say but also in our dreams and in what we tell our analyst, can be understood as operating through the medium of these two tropes. Condensation, in other words, is metaphorical in its nature, and displacement is metonymic in its nature. Metonymy is the delay or perpetual, as we gathered also from Derrida, différance of signification. Metaphor is the bringing together in a statement of identity of the discourse that’s attempting to articulate itself. Again we see in fiction, as Brooks argues in his essay, that these two rhetorical tendencies, the metaphorical and metonymic, coexist–and of course you can hear the implicit critique of de Man in the background–and may or may not work in harmony, may or may not conduce to an ultimate unity, but nevertheless do coexist in such a way that we can understand the unraveling of a fictional narrative as being like the processes we see at work in the unraveling of dreams. So it’s these two elements that Brooks is interested in in Freud and that he primarily does take from Freud.

第三章：布鲁克斯与弗洛伊德的决裂

Chapter 3: Brooks’s Departure from Freud

这意味着，布鲁克斯与我们可能出于本能而刻板印象所认为的传统精神分析批评家截然不同。布鲁克斯并非四处寻找俄狄浦斯情结和阳具象征。正如我希望你能看到的，布鲁克斯感兴趣的是弗洛伊德文本中截然不同的方面，他在第1171页右栏文章结尾处也明确指出了这一点：

Now this means, among other things, that Brooks is not anything like what we may spontaneously caricature perhaps as a traditional psychoanalytic critic. Brooks is not going around looking for Oedipus complexes and phallic symbols. Brooks is, as I hope you can see, interested in very different aspects of the Freudian text, and he says as much at the end of essay on page 1171 in the right-hand column where he says:

……对文本本身的精神分析批评可以不沦为（正如他所说，“这就是我正在做的”）——通常情况下——对文本的心理发生（作者的无意识）、文学反应的动力（读者的无意识）或人物的隐秘动机（假设他们也存在“无意识”）的研究。换句话说，布鲁克斯对发展一套作者理论或人物理论并不感兴趣。

… [T]here can be psychoanalytic criticism of the text itself that does not become [“This is what I’m doing,” he says]–as has usually been the case–a study of the psychogenesis of the text (the author’s unconscious), the dynamics of literary response (the reader’s unconscious), or the occult motivations of the characters (postulating an “unconscious” for them). In other words, Brooks is not interested in developing a theory of the author or a theory of character.

现在，我认为他并非有意否定弗洛伊德批评。他只是想告诉我们，他的做法与弗洛伊德批评有所不同。顺便提一下，虽然这门课程不深入探讨传统的弗洛伊德批评，但它确实非常有趣：例如，弗洛伊德的弟子欧内斯特·琼斯就曾撰写过一篇影响深远的莎士比亚《哈姆雷特》研究，他在文中指出哈姆雷特有俄狄浦斯情结。想想这部剧，你会发现琼斯的观点很有道理；事实上，在莎士比亚戏剧的舞台和电影史上，劳伦斯·奥利弗爵士正是在欧内斯特·琼斯的影响下扮演了哈姆雷特——你可能也知道这一点。在奥利弗的《哈姆雷特》中，他与格特鲁德的关系清晰地展现了他的俄狄浦斯情结。再次强调，确实有一些文学作品直接受到了弗洛伊德的影响。例如，人们会想到D·H·劳伦斯的《儿子与情人》，其中的主人公保罗·莫雷尔患有无法克服的俄狄浦斯情结，而情节的困难和复杂性正是此类。

Now I don’t think he really means to be dismissive of Freudian criticism. I think he’s really just telling us that he’s doing something different from that. I would remind you in passing that although we don’t pause over traditional Freudian criticism in this course, it can indeed be extremely interesting: just for example, Freud’s disciple, Ernest Jones, wrote an influential study of Shakespeare’s Hamlet in which he showed famously that Hamlet has an Oedipus complex. Think about the play. You’ll see that there’s a good deal in what Jones is saying; and in fact, famously in the history of the staging and filming of Shakespeare–as you probably know, Sir Laurence Olivier took the role of Hamlet under the influence of Ernest Jones. In the Olivier production of Hamlet, let’s just say made it painfully clear in his relations with Gertrude that he had an Oedipus complex. Again, there were actual sort of literary texts written directly under the influence of Freud. One thinks of D. H. Lawrence’s Sons and Lovers, for example, in which the central character, Paul Morel, is crippled by an Oedipus complex that he can’t master and the difficulties and complications of the plot are of this kind.

临近当下，我们将在本课程中研究一位重要的文学理论家——哈罗德·布鲁姆。他的理论文本发展历程始于《影响的焦虑》，这是一部关于作者的理论——也就是说，它基于后世诗人与其前辈之间的关系，也就是父子关系。因此，其中存在某种模式——当然，我正是运用这种模式来论证列维-斯特劳斯对俄狄浦斯神话的解读暴露了他与弗洛伊德相关的俄狄浦斯情结。显然，带有此类倾向的弗洛伊德式批评十分普遍，时至今日依然存在，我们不能简单地将其视为文学思考发展或文学思考可能性的推动因素而予以忽视或轻视。

Moving closer to the present, an important figure in literary theory whom we’ll be studying in this course, Harold Bloom, can be understood to be developing in his theories of theoretical text, beginning with The Anxiety of Influence, a theory of the author–that is to say, a theory that is based on the relationship between belated poets and their precursors, which is to say a relationship between sons and fathers. So there is a certain pattern in–and of course, I invoke this pattern in arguing that Levi-Strauss’ version of the Oedipus myth betrays his Oedipus complex in relation to Freud. Plainly, Freudian criticism with these sorts of preoccupations is widespread, continues sometimes to appear, and cannot simply be discounted or ignored as an influence in the development of thinking about literature or of the possibilities of thinking about literature.

但布鲁克斯作品中奇特之处，或许也并非那么奇特——或者说有趣之处——在于，尽管文本并非旨在向我们讲述作者或人物的任何信息（尽管人物在小说中至关重要，而这正是布鲁克斯主要探讨的主题），但文本本身却如同作者或人物一般，在许多方面都鲜活生动。也就是说，文本的存在是为了表达欲望，推动并展现某种欲望。这的确令人深思，尤其当布鲁克斯甚至明确表示他心中怀有某种特定的欲望时。换句话说，文本的结构，或者说文本的功能，都以某种方式满足了人们对减少兴奋的渴望：也就是说，这种渴望可以与性方面的快乐原则联系起来，也可以与弗洛伊德在《超越快乐原则》中提出的死亡愿望联系起来——我稍后会再谈到死亡愿望，它指的是减少兴奋，最终达到死亡的状态。通过这些方式——至于这些方式是否以及在多大程度上是相互关联的，还有待观察——布鲁克斯认为，文本中呈现的结构、延迟、繁复的描写或对结局的延宕，都包含着一种我一直在谈论的共存关系，这种共存关系存在于通过减少兴奋的欲望、兴奋本身以及减少兴奋这三者之间。

But the odd thing, or maybe not so odd–the interesting thing, that is, in Brooks’ work is that although the text is not there to tell us something about its author or to tell us something about its characters, even though character is important in fiction and that’s what Brooks is primarily talking about–although it’s not there to do those things it is nevertheless, like an author or a character, in many ways alive. That is to say, the text is there to express desire, to put in motion, and to make manifest desire or a desire. That is a rather odd thing to think about, especially when Brooks goes so far as to say that he has a particular desire in mind. The text, in other words, the structure of the text, or the way in which the text functions is to fulfill in some way or another a desire for reduced excitation: that is to say, the desire which can be associated with the pleasure principle in sexual terms and can be associated with the idea of the death wish that Freud develops in Beyond the Pleasure Principle that I’ll be coming back to as the reduction of excitation that would consist in being dead. In these ways–and it remains to see whether, or to what extent, these ways are cooperative–Brooks understands the structure, the delay, the arabesque, or postponement of the end one finds in the text to involve a kind of coexistence of the sort that I have been talking about between relations to the possibility through desire of reducing excitation, being excited, and reducing excitation.

显然，梦境和故事不仅表达了这种渴望，它们也延缓了这种渴望的到来。我相信我们都曾有过这样的经历：醒来后——顺便说一句，这是一种体验，一种错觉；它并非真实存在——感觉自己整晚都在做着同样的梦：换句话说，我们仿佛被困在一个永无止境的梦境困境中，一遍又一遍地重复，直至彻底的厌倦。我们做的很多梦既不令人兴奋，也不令人兴奋，只是单纯的乏味。无论它们最终可能带来怎样的兴奋，醒来后我们都会觉得它们持续得太久了。或许，小说在这方面确实优于梦境：它的艺术，它的结构，恰恰在于将这种延缓延长到恰到好处的程度，既不会过分拖延，也不会过度延长。

Now obviously both dreams and stories don’t just express this desire; they also delay it. I’m sure we have all had the experience of waking up–it’s an experience, by the way, which is an illusion; it hasn’t really been the case–and thinking that we have been dreaming the same damn thing all night long: in other words, that we have just been interminably stuck in a dream predicament which repeats itself again and again and again to the point of absolute total tedium. Many of the dreams we have are neither exciting nor the reverse but simply tedious. Whatever excitement they may have entailed in the long run, we feel as we wake up that they go on too long. Perhaps fiction does have this superiority over the dream work: that its art, that its structure, is precisely the protraction of delay to a desired degree but not unduly beyond that degree.

但小说的中间部分不仅仅包含这些拖延的过程。更重要的是，它们似乎——这也是布鲁克斯引用弗洛伊德这篇特定文本的原因之一——还具有一种奇特的倾向，即重温那些令人不快的事物。也就是说，小说的中间部分并非总是引人入胜。我们热爱阅读，而且我们读的每一本书都让人欲罢不能，这当然是好事；但事实上，我们对阅读的迷恋并非仅仅是一种娱乐。实际上，我们在小说中读到的很多内容都明显令人不快。即使翻页时，我们也会感到不适。一种说法是，尤其是在布鲁克斯特别感兴趣的十九世纪现实主义作品中，所有这些人物都在疯狂地做出错误的选择。他们爱上了不该爱的人。他们陷入了无法自拔的困境，因为他们不够成熟，因为他们考虑不周，也因为命运的阴影笼罩着他们，使他们无法做出更好的选择——无论如何，即使是最伟大、最激动人心的虚构作品中那些构成中间部分的经历，如果从某种程度上抽离出来思考，往往也令人不快。换句话说，为什么要回到那些不有趣的事情，回到那些没有快乐的地方？这又与快乐原则有什么关系呢？

But it’s not just that the middles of fiction involve these processes of delay. It’s that they seem also–and this is one of the reasons Brooks does have recourse to this particular text of Freud–they also have the curious tendency to revisit unpleasurable things. That is to say, it’s not that–the middles of fiction are exciting. We love to read and everything we read is a page turner, all to the good; but the fact is our fascination with reading isn’t simply a fascination that takes the form of having fun. In fact, so much of what we read in fiction is distinctly unpleasurable. We wince away from it even as we turn the page. One way to put it, especially in nineteenth-century realism which particularly interests Brooks, is all these characters are just madly making bad object choices. They’re falling in love with the wrong person. They’re getting stuck in sticky situations that they can’t extract themselves from because they’re not mature enough, because they haven’t thought things through, and because fate looms over the possibility of making a better choice–however the case may be, the experiences that constitute the middles even of the greatest and the most exciting fiction do have a tendency, if one thinks about them from a certain remove, to be unpleasurable. Why, in other words, return to what isn’t fun, to where it isn’t pleasure, and what can this possibly have to do with the pleasure principle?

第四章 弗洛伊德的《超越快乐原则》

Chapter 4. Freud’s Beyond the Pleasure Principle

这正是弗洛伊德在《超越快乐原则》一书中提出的问题，该书开篇便探讨了创伤受害者。它写于第一次世界大战末期，你应该明白，它并非孤立地反映了当时欧洲作家们的关注点。几乎与《超越快乐原则》同时期的，是英国涌现的一系列小说，部分原因在于战争结束后，心理学家们公布了关于战争创伤受害者的研究成果。你们大多数人都读过弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫的《达洛维夫人》，应该意识到，她在《达洛维夫人》中对塞普蒂默斯·史密斯的刻画，正是对一位遭受创伤的战争受害者的写照。与她同时代的丽贝卡·韦斯特也是一位作家，她创作了许多小说，其中一部名为《士兵归来》，其主人公也是一位遭受创伤的战争受害者。因此，这是那个时代的一个主题，而弗洛伊德的《超越快乐原则》也对这一主题有所贡献。布鲁克斯本人喜欢把《超越快乐原则》的文本本身称为一个宏大的情节——换句话说，它具有某种虚构的性格特征。我认为，出于我之前提到的原因，将它与《士兵归来》或《达洛维夫人》一起阅读会非常有启发意义。

Now that’s precisely the question that Freud asked himself in Beyond the Pleasure Principle, a text which begins with a consideration of trauma victims. It’s written at the end of the First World War, and you should understand this text as not isolated in the preoccupation of writers in Europe. Almost contemporary with Beyond the Pleasure Principle are novels written in England partly as a result of the making public of findings of psychologists about traumatic war victims as the war came to its conclusion. Most of you have read Virginia’s Woolf’s Mrs. Dalloway, and you should recognize that her treatment of Septimus Smith in Mrs. Dalloway is a treatment of a traumatized war victim. Rebecca West, a contemporary and an acquaintance of hers who wrote a good many novels, wrote one in particular called The Return of the Soldier,the protagonist of which is also a traumatized war victim. So it was a theme of the period and Freud’s Beyond the Pleasure Principle contributes to this theme. Brooks himself likes to refer to the text of Beyond the Pleasure Principle as itself a master plot–in other words as having a certain fictive character. It would be, I think, extremely instructive to read it alongside The Return of the Soldier or Mrs. Dalloway for the reasons I’ve mentioned.

好的。 总之，弗洛伊德开篇说道：“我诊室里遇到的这些创伤受害者，奇怪的是，他们在描述梦境，甚至在各种神经质的重复行为中，似乎都在强迫性地重复导致他们陷入困境的创伤经历。换句话说，他们并不回避它，也没有严格意义上的压抑它，而是不断地强迫性地重温它。这是为什么呢？这怎么可能是我在1919年之前一直认为存在的唯一一种驱力的表现呢？这种驱力，我们可以以某种方式与快乐联系起来——显然，与快乐原则有关；与一种隐含的社会生物学理解有关，即生命的延续完全是为了性繁殖，而与此相关的直接驱力的转移或抑制，则表现为渴望成功、渴望自我提升、渴望在情感上变得更加复杂等等。所有这些都可以与快乐原则联系起来。这又是如何解释的呢？”任何想要重返创伤事件的冲动，是否符合或能够用快乐原则来解释？

Okay. So anyway, Freud begins by saying, “The weird thing about these trauma victims whom I have had in my office is that in describing their dreams and even in their various forms of neurotic repetitive behavior, they seem compulsively to repeat the traumatic experience that has put them in the very predicament that brought them to me. In other words, they don’t shy away from it. They don’t in any strict sense repress it. They keep compulsively going back to it. Why is that? How can that possibly be a manifestation of the only kind of drives I had ever thought existed up until the year 1919, namely drives that we can associate in one way or another with pleasure–with the pleasure principle, obviously; with a sort of implicit sociobiological understanding that the protraction of life is all about sexual reproduction and that the displacement or inhibition of the direct drives associated with that take the form of the desire to succeed, the desire to improve oneself, and the desire to become more complex emotionally and all the rest of it? All of this we can associate with the pleasure principle. How does this compulsion to return to the traumatic event in any way correspond to or submit itself to explanation in terms of the pleasure principle?”

于是，他举了自己家庭生活中的一个例子：他的小孙子汉斯站在婴儿床里，把系着线轴的绳子扔出床外，喊着“Fort！”（意思是“在外面，不在那儿”），然后又把线轴拉回来，喊着“Da！”（意思是“又在那儿了”）。“Fort！Da！”小汉斯到底为什么要这么做呢？弗洛伊德很快就明白，小汉斯这样做是为了表达他对母亲离开房间方式的不满；换句话说，他的母亲并不总是在他身边。那么，这种游戏有什么意义呢？他把母亲“拴”在绳子上了，对吧？没错，她会离开——我们必须明白这一点：我们知道母亲会离开，但你猜怎么着？我可以把她拉回来，她又回来了。正如弗洛伊德所说，布鲁克斯也赞同他的观点，这就是我们通过重复创伤事件而获得的掌控感。所以，也许应该这样想，但这不能仅仅是掌握了某种技能，因为没有什么能消除或削弱这样一个事实：其中一部分驱动力似乎是为了回到创伤中——也就是说，不断地把其中涉及的不幸和创伤的本质摆在我们面前。

So then he turns to an example in his own home life, his little grandson, little Hans, standing in his crib throwing a spool tied to a string out of the crib saying, “Fort!” meaning “away, not there,” and then reeling it back in and saying, “Da!” meaning “there it is again”: “Fort! Da!” Why on earth is little Hans doing this? Well, Freud pretty quickly figures out that what little Hans is doing is finding a way of expressing his frustration about the way in which his mother leaves the room; in other words, his mother is not always there for him. So what is this play accomplishing? He’s got her on a string, right? Sure, she goes away–we have to understand this: we know our mother goes away, but guess what?
