Then as time passes, this idea of mimesis, the imitation of nature, gradually becomes transformed so that by the time you get to the Silver Age of Roman literature, a high-water mark of elegance in the Latin language, you have rhetorical theorists like Quintilian and Cicero and others talking not about mimesis but about–in Latin, of course–imitatio, seemingly the same idea. They are still talking about imitation, but the strange thing that’s happened is now they’re not talking about the imitation of nature anymore. They’re talking about the imitation of literary models: in other words, the imitation of language, the way in which we can establish canons by thinking about the relationship of particular poets and other writers with a tradition of literary expression from which they emerge. So this then, imitatio, becomes a language-based theory of influence arising seemingly spontaneously out of a nature-based theory of influence.

现在请看你纸上摘自亚历山大·蒲柏《论批评》的第一段文字。他在这里谈论的是维吉尔。论点是，荷马一定是模仿了自然。毕竟，当时没有文学范式可供模仿，所以如果荷马模仿了什么，那一定是自然。好吧，荷马模仿了自然，但后来维吉尔出现了——顺便一提，就在同一时期，修辞理论正在将模仿重新定义为对语言范式的模仿——维吉尔出现了，他说：“我要写一部属于我自己的民族史诗，你知道吗，我就坐下来写。”但随后他开始研究荷马；这就是蒲柏在准备写下你纸上的那两行诗时的想法。然后他开始写作，但随后他又重读了荷马。起初他感到很糟糕，因为他意识到荷马已经把一切都说完了。史诗只有两部，《伊利亚特》和《奥德赛》。已经没有什么可写的了。荷马已经把整个河岸都描绘得淋漓尽致，维吉尔也陷入了困境。他还能做什么呢？

Now take a look at the first passage on your sheet from Alexander’s Pope’s “Essay on Criticism.” He’s talking about Virgil here. Homer, the argument is, has to have imitated nature. After all, there were no literary models to imitate, so if Homer imitated anything it must have been nature. Well, fine. Homer imitated nature, but then along comes Virgil–in this same period, by the way, when rhetorical theories were redefining imitation as the imitation of verbal models–along comes Virgil and he says, “I’m going to write my own national epic and you know what, I’ll just sit down and write it.” But then he starts looking at Homer; this is all what Pope is thinking as he prepares to write the couplet that’s on your sheet. Then he starts to write, but then he rereads Homer. At first he feels terrible because he realized that Homer has said it all. There are two poems, The Iliad and The Odyssey. There’s nothing left to say. Homer has covered the entire waterfront, and so Virgil is sort of stuck. What is he going to do?

既然他无法再模仿自然（因为荷马已经做到了这一点），那么他能做的就是模仿荷马。结果是，他最终领悟到了一种境界，蒲柏用这首对句概括了这种境界：

Well, what he can do, if he can’t imitate nature anymore because Homer has done that, is he can imitate Homer. The result is that he comes to a sort of realization that Pope epitomizes in this couplet:

但是，当他仔细审视每一部分时，他发现自己[也就是说，荷马作品的每一部分，以及他自己创作史诗时的每一部分]

But when t’ examine ev’ry part he came [that is to say, every part of Homer’s compositions, every part of his own composition as he undertook to write his own epic]

他发现，自然与荷马是同一回事。

Nature and Homer were, he found, the same.

所以，这里逐渐出现了这样一种观点：模仿自然和模仿艺术——模仿世间万物、世间人物和语言——是同一过程的组成部分，密不可分。要做其中之一，就必然会做另一个。这就是我所说的，我们仍在努力摆脱语素生成论（笑）模式，转向心理生成论模式。即使在最传统的关于影响如何运作的论述中，比如蒲柏的理论，我们仍然试图区分自然和艺术，而且发现很难做到这一点。在蒲柏之后五十年，塞缪尔·约翰逊仍然说：“没有什么能取悦大众，或者长久取悦大众，唯有对普遍自然的再现。”他关于再现和普遍自然的观念，在艺术模仿世间万物和艺术模仿现有文学典范并从中汲取灵感这两种感觉之间摇摆不定。因此，模仿的概念本身就存在某种崩溃。模仿自然的概念和模仿艺术的概念之间存在一种崩溃，仔细想想，这或许是一种令人惊讶的崩溃。

So here you have emerging the idea that to imitate nature and to imitate art–to imitate the things of the world, the people of the world, and to imitate language–is part and parcel of the same process. To do one you necessarily and perforce do the other. That’s what I mean by saying that we’re still struggling to get away from the logogenetic [laughs] model to the psychogenetic model. Even in the most traditional expressions of how influence works, like Pope’s, we are still concerned to distinguish, and find it very difficult to distinguish, between nature and art. When Samuel Johnson, fifty years after Pope, is still saying, “Nothing can please many, or please long, but just representations of general nature,” he is in this idea of representations and in the idea of general nature teetering between a sense that it’s things in the world that art imitates and it is existing literary models that art imitates and from which art takes its cue. So there’s a kind of collapse then in the idea of imitation. There’s a kind of a collapse, a surprising collapse perhaps when you think about it, between the notion of the imitation of nature and the notion of the imitation of art.

第三章 布鲁姆“误读”艾略特

Chapter 3. Bloom “Misreads” Eliot

现在，如果我们再来看今天读过的两篇文章，它们都是关于影响的理论，就会发现T·S·艾略特对于这两种模仿之间的关系也有些含糊不清。在艾略特看来，融入传统、与之互动的个人才能必须应对他所谓的“欧洲的思维”（第539页，左栏）。我将朗读一段较长的文字，因为这是艾略特观点最易于理解的概括之一：

Now if we turn then to the two texts that you’ve read for today, both of which are theories of influence, you can see that T. S. Eliot, too, is a little bit unclear as to the relationship of these two sorts of imitation. For Eliot the individual talent that inserts itself into, that engages with, tradition has to cope with what Eliot calls “the mind of Europe,” page 539, left-hand column. I’ll read a fairly extensive passage because this is one of the most accessible summaries of what Eliot has to say:

这位诗人一定非常清楚一个显而易见的事实：艺术本身永远不会进步，但艺术的素材却永远不会一成不变。他一定也明白，欧洲的思想——他自己国家的思想——这种思想他最终会明白，远比他个人的思想重要得多……我先停一下，因为布鲁姆的风格似乎与此截然相反，因为布鲁姆，这位浪漫主义者，关注的是个人的内心世界，关注的是个体思想如何与所有其他争夺关注的思想抗争，最终超越它们，使它们实际上被抹去，而迟来的自我才能最终确立自身，凌驾于所有先前的自我之上。这种抗争——我用“似乎”这个词，因为我还要在此多加探讨——在艾略特的作品中似乎并不存在。艾略特似乎崇尚自我谦逊，认为欧洲的集体思想比个人思想更为重要，如果一个人要以个人才能为传统做出贡献，那么这种贡献必须源于对万物极其敏锐的感知，不是努力追求某种成就，而是保持一种超然物外的状态。换句话说，这似乎是一种截然不同的视角。

[The poet] must be quite aware of the obvious fact that art never improves, but that the material of art is never quite the same. He must be aware that the mind of Europe–the mind of his own country–a mind which he learns in time to be much more important than his own private mind… Let me just stop there and say this seems as much unlike Bloom as it can possibly be because Bloom, the Romantic, is all about one’s own private mind, the struggle of the individual mind to define itself over against all of those minds jostling for attention that precede it to over them to the point where they are, in effect, effaced, and the belated ego can finally establish itself as prior to all preceding egos. This sort of struggle seems–and I say “seems” because I’m going to be lingering over this for a while–seems to be absent from Eliot. Eliot seems to be all about self-effacement, about the recognition that the mind of Europe is more important than one’s own mind, and that if one is to contribute anything as an individual talent to tradition, that contribution has to be a matter of the most acutely sensitive awareness of everything, not that one is struggling to be but that one is not. It seems, in other words, like a very different perspective.

继续这段文字：

To continue the passage:

……[欧洲的思维]是一种不断变化的思维，这种变化是一种发展，它不会抛弃任何沿途的事物，也不会让莎士比亚、荷马，甚至是马格德林岩画的作者的作品过时。这种发展，或许是精炼，也肯定是复杂化，从艺术家的角度来看，并非任何意义上的进步。换言之，传统与个人才能之间的关系，是一种融入浩瀚的文学、哲学及其他各种表达形式的关系，这种关系不断变化，却从未真正蜕变，也绝不能被理解为迈向某个伟大目标的宏伟征程或进步，因为没有任何事物会真正消失，也没有任何根本性的创新能够真正出现。

… [The mind of Europe is] a mind which changes, and that this change is a development which abandons nothing en route which does not superannuate either Shakespeare or Homer, or the rock drawing of the Magdalenian draftsman. That this development, refinement perhaps, complication certainly, is not, from the point of view of the artist any improvement. In other words, the relationship between tradition and the individual talent is a relationship of entering into a vast matrix of literary, philosophical, and other sorts of expression that changes and yet never really transforms itself and certainly can’t be understood as a grand march or progress toward some great goal, because nothing is ever lost and nothing radically innovative can ever really be introduced.

我希望你们正在思考和反思这段话，它与我们之前讨论过的许多内容息息相关：伽达默尔认为，传统完全依赖于对连续性的认知，依赖于与过去进行中途对话的意愿，依赖于一种融合的视野，在这种视野中，过去与现在能够以一种真实的方式彼此对话；而从另一个角度来看，这种观点，或者也可能是俄国形式主义的达尔文式观点，认为任何文学文本的主导元素和隐性元素始终存在于任何时间。只不过它们倾向于在一种持续的振荡中相互转换位置。因此，根据这类历史理论，所有文学的可能性，所有表达的可能性，始终都在那里，而一个人进入这片广阔的表达可能性海洋的过程始终是一个微妙的过程，绝不能像浪漫主义传统所强调的那样，被视为展现或体现某种原创天才。所以这基本上是艾略特的观点，而布鲁姆的观点显然与此不同。

I hope you are thinking and reflecting on a passage of this kind about a good deal that we’ve passed through already: Gadamer’s sense of tradition as something which depends absolutely on the awareness of continuity, on the willingness to meet the past halfway, to enter into a merger of horizons in which the past and the present can speak in an authentic way to each other; and that in other ways this idea, or possibly also the Russian formalist idea in its Darwinian sense, that the dominant and the recessive elements of any literary text are always present at any time. It’s just that they tend perpetually in a kind of oscillation to be changing places with each other. So the whole gamut of literary possibility, of expressive possibility, is, according to theories of history of this kind, is always already there, and one’s own entry into this vast sea of expressive possibility is always a subtle thing that certainly can’t in any way be seen to showcase or to manifest any sort of original genius as the Romantic tradition might want to insist on it. So this is basically the perspective of Eliot and one from which certainly you know Bloom would obviously seem to be diverging.

现在我想论证的是，艾略特和布鲁姆之间实际上存在着大量的延续性，而布鲁姆的[笑]“影响的焦虑”——顺便说一句，我从未和哈罗德讨论过这个问题。你们当中有些人可能会参加他的研讨会，至于是否要和他讨论这个问题，就由你们自己决定了。正如我所说，这由你们自己决定，但我认为可以提出一个强有力的论点，而且我已经把它写成文章，哈罗德也看到了，那就是布鲁姆误读了T·S·艾略特，而且是严重误读：也就是说——这就是严重误读的逻辑——T·S·艾略特已经把布鲁姆想说的都说完了。我确实相信这一点，[笑]尽管从表面上看，他们的视角截然不同，比如传统与浪漫等等。我不想在这个论点上深入探讨，以免被认为过于执着，但我想顺便提几点，因为我认为这完美地诠释了“影响的焦虑”是如何运作的。布鲁姆一直否认“个人才能中的传统”的影响。他承认受到某些影响，但这些影响来自爱默生、尼采、伟大的浪漫主义诗人等等。正如我所说，他强烈否认艾略特的影响，然而，当我们阅读艾略特的作品时——我现在要花些时间研究艾略特——在我看来，至少在框架和暗示层面，布鲁姆的思想已经完全融入其中。毕竟，这正是布鲁姆对先驱作家和后继作家之间关系的全部论述：所以这并不令人惊讶，不是吗？

Now I want to argue that actually there is a tremendous amount of continuity between Eliot and Bloom, and that Bloom’s [laughs] Anxiety of Influence–I’ve never discussed this with Harold, by the way. Those of you who may be taking his seminars, I leave it up to you whether you want to take this up with him. As I say, I leave that up to you, but I think a strong argument can be made, and I have made it in print so Harold has seen it, that Bloom misreads and is a strong misreader of T. S. Eliot: which is to say–such is the logic of strong misreading–that T. S. Eliot said everything Bloom has to say already. I do believe this, [laughs] despite this extraordinary appearance of total difference in perspective, the traditional versus the Romantic and so on. I don’t want to go into detail in this argument for fear of being considered obsessive, but I’d like to make a few points about it in passing, because I think it’s such a perfect exemplification of how The Anxiety of Influence works. Bloom has always denied the influence of “Tradition in the Individual Talent.” He acknowledges influences, but they are Emerson, Nietzsche, the great Romantic poets, and so on. He has, as I say, vehemently denied the influence of Eliot, yet as one reads Eliot–and I’m going to spend some time with Eliot now–it seems to me that at least in skeletal form, in suggestion, Bloom is all there already, which is, after all, all Bloom ever says about the relationship between a precursor and a belated writer: so it can’t be surprising, can it?

好的。首先，对布鲁姆来说，展现新事物如何重构旧事物至关重要：也就是说，是对先导文本的挪用，而这并非一个概念性的文本，尽管它——这也是布鲁姆这一时期写作中一个有点反直觉的地方。他坚持认为存在一个特定的先导文本。《丁登寺》的先导文本是《利西达斯》。别跟我提其他的（笑）先导文本。就是《利西达斯》，他论证了这一点，但后世文本与先导文本之间的关系如此特殊，以至于我们再也无法用同样的视角解读先导文本。换句话说，对先导文本的强烈误读如此强大，以至于它本身也成为了我们强烈的误读。读完《丁登寺》之后，我们就无法再用同样的视角去思考《利西达斯》了。

All right. Now first of all, it’s very important to Bloom to show the way in which the new reconstitutes the old: that is to say, the appropriation of the precursor text, which is not a notional text although it–and that’s one of the things that’s sort of counterintuitive about Bloom’s writing in this period. He insists that there is a particular precursor text. The precursor text for “Tintern Abbey” is “Lycidas.” Don’t tell me about other [laughs] precursor texts. It’s “Lycidas,” and he shows how this is the case, but the relationship between the belated text and the precursor text is such that we can never read the precursor text the same way again. The strong misreading of the precursor text is so powerful, in other words, that it becomes our strong misreading. We just can’t think about “Lycidas” in the same way on this view after we’ve read “Tintern Abbey.”

如果这听起来有悖常理，不妨想想一些例子。最明显的例子就是博尔赫斯那篇著名的文章《皮埃尔·梅纳尔，堂吉诃德的作者》。我想你们当中很多人都读过这篇文章，但它的内容其实很简单——它讲述的是一位法国人在十九世纪末用西班牙语写了一篇文章，而这篇文章的内容竟然一字不差地照搬了塞万提斯的《堂吉诃德》，只不过它不是塞万提斯的《堂吉诃德》，而是皮埃尔·梅纳尔的《堂吉诃德》。想想这其中的区别。这是一个十九世纪末的法国人用西班牙语写作的故事。这相当了不起，远比塞万提斯仅仅用自己的母语写作更令人印象深刻，而且这完全是另一种历史视角。塞万提斯自认为对所处的历史时期——骑士精神的消亡等等——略带讽刺意味，但想想看，几个世纪后，你用如今的知识去书写那个历史时期，又能从中获得怎样的讽刺呢？在十九世纪末用另一种语言写出《堂吉诃德》，这简直是惊人的壮举，完全是另一种境界！你还能用同样的眼光去读塞万提斯的《堂吉诃德》吗？这听起来是不是很天真？

If this seems counterintuitive, just think about certain examples that might come to mind. The most obvious example is the famous text by Borges called “Pierre Menard, Author of Don Quixote.” I imagine a number of you know that text, but what it consists in basically is–it’s a kind of an anecdote about a Frenchman writing, as I recall, in the end of the nineteenth century in Spanish a text, and his text is as it turns out verbatim, word for word, Cervantes’ Don Quixote, only it’s not Cervantes’ Don Quixote; it’s Pierre Menard’s Don Quixote. Think how different it is. This is a Frenchman at the end of the nineteenth century writing in Spanish. That’s pretty impressive, much more impressive than Cervantes merely writing in his own language, and it’s a completely different historical perspective. Whereas Cervantes thinks he’s being a little bit ironic about his own historical moment–the death of chivalry and all that–think about how ironic you can be about that historical moment writing several centuries later with everything that you know now. What a tour de force to be able to write Don Quixote at the end of the nineteenth century in another language, a whole new ball game! How can you ever read Cervantes’ Don Quixote in the same way? It seems naïve, right?

但这并非故事的重点。故事的重点实际上是贬低皮埃尔·梅纳尔，但你可以将其视为一种强烈的误读理论。皮埃尔·梅纳尔以为自己在做一些新的事情，对吧？事实上，他根本没有做什么新的事情。他之所以认为自己在做一些新的事情，恰恰是他对前文的误读——顺便说一句，你甚至不必读过前文——但这种误读本身就具有某种力量，它仿佛渗透到我们对前文的理解中，使我们无法再用同样的眼光去解读它。

Now that’s not the point of the story. The point of the story is actually to belittle Pierre Menard, but you can see this as a theory of strong misreading. Pierre Menard thinks he’s doing something new, right? The fact is, he’s not doing anything new at all. His belief that he’s doing something new is precisely his misreading of the precursor text–and by the way, you don’t have to have read the precursor text–but that misreading, after all, is something in its very power which, as it were, infiltrates our own understanding of the precursor text, making it impossible for us to read it the same way again.

想想乔伊斯的《尤利西斯》。我们都知道，《尤利西斯》和维吉尔的《埃涅阿斯纪》一样，都是以《奥德赛》为基础创作的，它可以说是对《奥德赛》的重新演绎；但它似乎用错了角度来看待《奥德赛》。它将原诗中所有英雄主义的元素都拉低到对现代社会日常生活琐碎的描述中。换句话说，它在沿袭《奥德赛》的过程中，恰恰暗含着对《奥德赛》英雄神话的解构。那么，读过《尤利西斯》之后，我们又该如何用同样的眼光去解读《奥德赛》呢？

Think of Joyce’s Ulysses. We all know that Ulysses, like Virgil’s Aeneid, is based on The Odyssey and that it, as it were, recycles The Odyssey; but it seems to be looking at The Odyssey through the wrong end of a telescope. It’s dragging all the sort of heroic dimension of the poem down into a kind of nitty-gritty account of everyday life in recent society. In other words, it implicitly, precisely in following The Odyssey debunks the heroic myth of The Odyssey. How can we read, in other words, The Odyssey in the same way again after we’ve read Ulysses?

现在必须指出，布鲁姆也会这么说，《尤利西斯》并非对《奥德赛》的严重误读，因为它完全清楚自己的意图。它非常清楚自己对《奥德赛》文本的解读，因此这是一种有意为之的误读，但它也有其自身的价值。它与布鲁姆的理论并不完全相同，但它与布鲁姆的理论以及艾略特关于个人才能与传统之间关系的观点都存在共通之处：它重构了传统。它不仅仅是提供了一些新颖的东西，它还让我们以一种不同的方式看待传统本身。请翻到第538页，右侧栏大约在中间位置：

Now it has to be said, and Bloom would say this, Ulysses is not a strong misreading of The Odyssey because it’s perfectly conscious of what it’s doing. It knows exactly what it’s doing with respect to the text of The Odyssey, so it’s a deliberate misreading which has other virtues. It’s not quite the same thing, but what it does have in common with Bloom’s theory and what it has in common also with Eliot’s idea about the relationship between the individual talent and tradition is that it reconstitutes tradition. It doesn’t just provide something novel. It makes us see tradition itself in a different way. Turn to page 538, the right-hand column about halfway down:

艾略特说，现有的纪念碑彼此之间构成了一种理想的秩序，而新的（真正意义上的）艺术作品的出现改变了这种秩序。在新的作品出现之前，现有的秩序是完整的；为了使秩序在新事物出现之后得以延续，整个现有的秩序必须发生改变，哪怕只是细微的改变。我们无法再以同样的方式看待它，因此，这是一种传统与个人才能之间动态的、相互影响的关系：强大的先驱者和迟来的诗人，在每种情况下，这种关系都在相互转化。这种转化的基础，或者说原则，在于迟来的诗人对先驱的强烈误读，这种误读同时又强调了迟来的诗人的自我中心：我正在做一些新的事情；我正在去往从未有人去过的地方。我这样做如此有力，以至于一方面，人们不禁要问，在我之前是否真的有人这样做过；另一方面，随着对这种关系的深入思考，人们最终会发现，强大的先驱者似乎已经把迟来的诗人想要表达的一切都说完了，对吗？因此，布鲁姆的文学史理论，他的文学史编纂学，同时重视创新和保守主义，或者说传统。与倾向于保守或传统的伽达默尔，以及倾向于创新的伊瑟尔或俄国形式主义者不同，布鲁姆的观点同时认可了传统作为绝对连续的事物，以及传统作为不断被重塑或至少被重新思考的事物。我必须指出，这与T·S·艾略特的观点非常相似。

The existing monuments [says Eliot] form an ideal order among themselves which is modified by the introduction of the new (the really new) work of art among them. The existing order is complete before the new work arrives; for order to persist after the supervention of novelty, the whole existing order must be, if ever so slightly, altered. We can’t quite see it the same way again, so it’s a dynamic, mutual relationship between tradition and the individual talent: the strong precursor and the belated poet, in each case, which is mutually transforming. The basis, the principle of transformation, is the belated poet’s strong misreading of the precursor which simultaneously asserts the egoistic priority of the belated poet: I’m doing something new; I’m going where no one has ever gone before. I’m doing so so powerfully that it’s a question of whether there actually was anybody before, on the one hand, and the strong precursor who turns out, as one reflects more and more and more about the relationship, to have said everything the belated poet says already, right? So simultaneously, Bloom’s theory of literary history, his literary historiography, places a premium on innovation and on conservatism, or tradition, simultaneously. Unlike Gadamer, leaning toward the conservative or traditional, and Iser or the Russian formalists, who lean toward the innovative, the Bloomian idea simultaneously countenances the idea of tradition as something absolutely continuous and also of tradition as something which is constantly being remade or at least rethought. That, I have to tell you, is very similar to T. S. Eliot’s position.

现在再次引用艾略特在第539页左下角的那句著名格言：

So now again the famous aphorism of Eliot on page 539, the left-hand column at the bottom:

有人说：“逝去的作家与我们疏远，是因为我们比他们知道得更多。” 的确如此，他们就是我们所知道的。我觉得这说得挺好。T·S·艾略特的著名格言也可以理解为布鲁姆以他自己的方式表达的意思。过去是我们知道的，但我们却意识不到自己知道。换句话说，当我写这首迟来的诗时，我写的是过去，但我并不认为自己是在写过去。相反，我认为自己在做一些新的事情。在第一个暂定比例（clinamen）中，我偏离了过去：我向外向下偏转，我找到了属于自己的空间，就像卢克莱修的原子一样。如果没有偏转——卢克莱修说所有的原子都会落到同一个地方——那将是不好的，所以它们都偏转，这样才能落到各自的位置。嗯，这就是迟来的诗人对他与先驱者之间关系的理解。他似乎在偏离前辈诗人的路线，但实际上并非如此。[笑] 再说一遍——我们稍后会再谈到这一点——他并没有偏离。他实际上落在同一条线上，但这种偏离的力量，这种修辞上的姿态，如此强大，以至于我们确实感到被带入了另一个世界。我们再次同时感受到了新诗人作品中的创新和必要的保守主义，或者说是传承的一面。

Someone said: “The dead writers are remote from us because we know so much than they did.” Precisely, and they are that which we know. Rather good, I think. The famous aphorism of T.S. Eliot can also be understood as something that Bloom, in his own way, might very well say. The past is what we know, but we’re not aware of knowing it. In other words, I write the past when I write my belated poem, but I don’t think I’m doing it. I think instead that I’m doing something new. In the first provisionary ratio, clinamen, I am swerving from the past: I swerve out and down, I find my own space like a Lucretian atom. If it weren’t for swerving–and Lucretius says all the atoms would fall in the same place–that wouldn’t be good, so they all swerve so they can all fall in their own place. Well, that is the belated poet’s sense of what he’s doing in relation to the precursor. He’s swerving out and down from the precursor poet, but of course he’s not. [laughs] Again–and we’ll come back to this–he’s not. He’s actually falling in the same place, but the strength of that swerve, the rhetorical gesture of the swerve, is so powerful that we do feel transported. Once again we feel both at once, the innovation and the necessary conservatism, or preservational aspect, of the new poet’s composition.

好的。所以我认为，正如我所说，艾略特的格言也很大程度上预示了布鲁姆关于诗人之间竞争的观点。最后，艾略特著名的强调——当然，没有什么比这更不显得阴郁了——强调诗人的非人格化，强调摆脱人格的愿望：他在第541页右栏第二部分末尾写道：“当然，只有那些拥有人格和情感的人才知道想要摆脱这些东西意味着什么”——换句话说，实际上就是进入一个艺术的世界，放弃那种认为重要的只是我个人心理痛苦的感觉；相反地，进入欧洲的思想世界；认识到任何个人思想的完全微不足道，当然也包括我自己的；并将自己作为诗人、艺术家和创造者（如果还能保留这个词的话）沉浸于比自身无限广阔的事物之中。

All right. So I think, as I say, that Eliot’s aphorism, too, very much anticipates Bloom’s view of the agonistic struggle among poets. Then finally Eliot’s famous emphasis–and of course, nothing could seem to be less gloomy than this–Eliot’s famous emphasis on the poet’s impersonality, on the wish to escape personality: he says, in the right-hand column, page 541, end of section two, “But, of course, only those who have personality and emotions know what it means to want to escape from these things”–in other words, to enter a world of art, in effect, to abandon the sense that what’s important is my personal psychological agony; to enter, by contrast, the mind of Europe; to recognize the complete insignificance of any individual mind, certainly my own; and to immerse oneself as a poet, as an artist, and as a creator, if one can still retain this term, in that which is infinitely more vast than one is oneself.

第四章 文学史：早已写就的“强诗”

Chapter 4. Literary History: the Always Already Written “Strong Poem”

嗯，这听起来不太像布鲁姆的风格，但请看第1160页右侧栏，布鲁姆的第五个修正比例——苦行（askesis）。[笑] 他谈到的是后世诗人，或者说迟来的诗人，为了给自己找到空间而做的事情。我该如何让自己与众不同呢？你可能会觉得答案是让自己比任何人都更强大。华莱士·史蒂文斯有一首很棒的诗叫《兔子是幽灵之王》，诗中的兔子膨胀得如此巨大，以至于几乎淹没了一切。我一直认为这就是布鲁姆所说的迟来的诗人，但如果你把苦行（askesis）视为一个真正的修正比例，那么最终达到同样目的的，却是截然不同的事情。

Well, that doesn’t sound very Bloomian, but look on page 1160, the right-hand column, at Bloom’s fifth revisionary ratio, askesis. [laughs] He’s talking about what the later poet, the belated poet, does in order to find space for himself. What can I do in order to make myself different from other people? Well, you’d think the answer would be make yourself bigger than anybody. Wallace Stevens has a wonderful poem called “Rabbit as King of the Ghosts,” and the rabbit swells up to become so big that it just kind of overwhelms everything. I always think of this as Bloom’s belated poet, but if you have askesis as one of the authentic revisionary ratios, something very different is happening to this same end.

在定义进行到大约一半的时候，也就是第五个定义——顺便一提，哈罗德从未为此道歉过使用男性代词。他的意思是，诗人通常被赋予男性性别，但当然，任何女性都可以成为诗人。我们稍后会再讨论这类区别。例如，他认为艾米莉·狄金森是一位杰出的诗人。显然，这是布鲁姆作品中一个颇具争议的方面，但他毫不掩饰地使用了男性代词。当然，他的理论深受俄狄浦斯情结的影响，而正如弗洛伊德一直受到批评的那样，除非像拉康和拉康主义女性主义者那样将其投射到象征领域，否则俄狄浦斯情结无疑是一种男性主义思想。如果人类最根本的代际冲突发生在父子之间，那么显然[笑]就会出现问题，而且在布鲁姆的修辞中，在他的词汇中，男性俄狄浦斯情结仍然是核心。

About halfway through the definition, definition five–and by the way, the masculine pronoun is something that Harold has never apologized for. What he means is that a poet is gendered masculine but that, of course, any woman can be a poet. We’ll come back to distinctions of that sort later. He does think of Emily Dickinson, for example, as a strong poet. Obviously, that’s a controversial aspect of Bloom’s work, but he uses the masculine prologue unapologetically. Of course, his theory is very much caught up in the idea of Oedipal conflict which, as Freud is always being criticized for, is, unless you project it into the realm of the symbolic as Lacan and feminist Lacanians do, undoubtedly a masculist idea. If the essential generational conflict of human beings is between father and son, well, obviously [laughs] problems can be seen to arise from that, and in Bloom’s rhetoric, in his vocabulary, the masculist Oedipal conflict is still central.

总之，回到关于自我消融这一点，在试图为自己作为创新者找到一席之地的过程中——这种消融，在我看来，又一次将布鲁姆推回了他试图强烈误读的艾略特的立场。他说：“（诗人）放弃了一部分自身的人性天赋和想象力。”换句话说，他限制了自己；他缩小了自己；他让自己变得不如他本可以成为的那样，当然，是为了超越他已经成为的。他放弃了一部分自身的人性天赋和想象力，以便将自己与他人（包括先驱者）区分开来。因此，在苦行（askesis）中——顺便一提，在虚己（kenosis）中也是如此——对于这些针对先驱者的强烈误读行为而言，存在着一种自我缩减或自我消融。换句话说，这不仅仅是兔子作为幽灵之王的问题。这并非是极度膨胀的自我占据了所有空间的问题。事情远比这复杂，而正因为如此，它才更像艾略特的风格。

In any case, returning to this point about the effacement of the self, in the very act of trying to find a place for oneself as an innovator–an effacement which, however, once again seems to me to catapult Bloom back into the position of Eliot that he is trying to misread strongly. He says, “[The poet] yields up part of his own human and imaginative endowment.” In other words, he curtails himself; he shrinks himself; he makes himself less than he might have been, of course, in order to be more than he has been. He yields up part of his own human and imaginative endowment so as to separate himself from others including the precursor. So in askesis–and also in kenosis, by the way–there is a self-shrinking or self-effacement on the part of these particular moves of strong misreading with respect to the precursor. It’s not, in other words, just a question of the rabbit as king of the ghosts. It’s not a question of a massive ego swelling to the point where it fills all space. It is more complicated than that, and in being more complicated it is frankly more Eliot-like.

好的。那么，让我们更直接地谈谈布鲁姆。他的创作生涯始于诗人之间关系的斗争。在他早期的作品——雪莱的《神话的创造》、布莱克的《启示录》和《幻象公司》——中，斗争的理念被清晰地体现为他所谓的“新教主义”。换句话说，他认为他所谈论的传统兴起于宗教改革时期，正如我在诠释学简史中所述，那时每个人都突然意识到自己拥有属于自己的圣经，拥有属于自己的与上帝的关系：换句话说，那时人类的个性开始显现，当然，许多人也称之为资产阶级的兴起。在那一刻，“新教主义”的理念——正如杜雷尔笔下的一个人物所说，“我对此表示抗议”——应运而生，以至于每位诗人在某种意义上都对以往的文学模式采取了一种对抗的姿态。这一点从布鲁姆创作生涯的伊始就贯穿于他的作品之中。 “新教徒”一词逐渐被“修正主义者”所取代，而“修正主义者”一词又成为他在《幻象公司》等作品中的主要用词，最终演变为误读的概念。这位迟来的人物的抗议，是通过对先例文本进行改造，从而找到自身原创性的方式而实现的。这是一种俄狄浦斯式的挣扎。

All right. So turning then more directly to Bloom, his career begins–it has always involved a sense of struggle in the relationship among poets. In his earliest work–Shelley’s Mythmaking, Blake’s Apocalypse, and The Visionary Company–the idea of struggle was embodied plainly as what he called Protestantism. In other words, he saw the tradition he was talking about arising in relation to the Reformation, that time when, as I said in my thumbnail history of hermeneutics, everybody suddenly realized he had his own Bible and his own relationship with God: in other words, that time when human individuality emerges, which is also, of course, called by many others the emergence of the bourgeoisie. In that moment, the idea of Protestantism–purely in the sense, as a character in Durrell says, “that I protest”–emerges so that each poet takes, in some sense, an adversary stance toward previous literary models. This is present in Bloom’s work from the beginning of his career. The word “Protestant” gradually gives way to the word “revisionary,” and then that’s the word that he uses primarily in The Visionary Company, for example, and then finally becomes the notion of misreading. The protest of the belated figure is the protest which takes the form of transfiguring the precursor text in such a way that one can find oneself to be original. It is an Oedipal struggle.

这种俄狄浦斯情结的挣扎，很大程度上是无意识的，布鲁姆对此并不陌生。我们快速浏览一下表格上的接下来三段文字。朗基努斯，这位作者的真实身份我们尚无法确定，但他的《论崇高》一书——一部极其引人入胜的作品——我们得以阅读——我这里有两段摘录。第一段是：

Now this idea of Oedipal struggle, which is largely unconscious, is not new to Bloom, just quickly to review the next three passages on your sheet. Longinus, the author whose actual identity we cannot quite determine but whose On the Sublime, an extraordinarily interesting text, is available to us to read–I’ve got two passages from him. The first is:

仿佛本能地（这就是崇高时刻），我们的灵魂被真正的崇高所提升。（好吧，这倒是人人都会这么说。）它骄傲地飞翔，充满喜悦和炫耀（而这正是令人惊讶之处），仿佛它自己创造了它所听到的。换句话说，有一种被他者占有的感觉，同时在心理上也被体验为占有他者，对吗？它借我之口说话。它让我像个小孩子一样兴奋。他们正在看电视，有人打出了全垒打，小男孩就像这样（做手势），以为自己打出了全垒打。他完全沉浸在成为英雄的幻想中，对吧？当我们对未曾说过的话做出反应时，也是如此，以至于在某个时刻，我们觉得自己已经说了。这是一种相互占有。它占有了我们，引发了我们认为自己拥有它的心理反应。在我看来，朗吉努斯的话很有见地，而且对布鲁姆的立场产生了重要影响。

As if instinctively [this is in the moment of the sublime] our soul is uplifted by the true sublime. [Fine. That’s what you would expect anybody to say.] It takes a proud flight and is filled with joy and vaunting [and this is where the surprise comes] as though it had itself produced what it has heard. In other words, there’s a kind of possession by the other that takes place which is simultaneously experienced psychologically as possession of the other, right? It is speaking through me. It’s making me very excited like a little kid. They’re watching TV, somebody hits a home run, and the little kid goes like this [gestures] and thinks he thought he hit the home run. He’s completely into the fantasy of being that hero, right? It’s the same thing with the response to something that we haven’t said, such that in a certain moment we think we have said it. It’s a mutual possession. It possesses us, causing the psychological reaction that we think of ourselves as possessing it. It seems to me that there is real insight in what Longinus is saying and that it has an important influence on Bloom’s position.

朗吉努斯的另一段话——顺便说一句，我认为朗吉努斯在这里说的绝对正确：柏拉图不断地贬低荷马，然而，要证明荷马的伟大壮举乃至比喻如何塑造柏拉图的思想，却易如反掌。这是一个引人入胜的话题，在我看来，朗吉努斯再次一针见血地指出：“如果柏拉图没有全心全意地与荷马争夺主导地位，他的哲学理论就不会如此臻于完美。”他甚至用布鲁姆式的思维方式来思考，即即使内心深处知道自己是第二，仍然渴望成为第一——他甚至为了争夺主导地位而奋斗，或许过于热衷于争论，仿佛与荷马决一死战，但无论如何，他都从这场较量中获益；正如他所说，“这种斗争对凡人来说是有益的。”

Another passage from Longinus–and by the way, I think what Longinus says here is absolutely true: Plato is constantly abusing Homer, and yet nothing can be easier than to show the ways in which the great Homeric actions and even tropes help shape Platonic thought. It’s a fascinating topic and Longinus, it seems to me, again is exactly right about it: “There would not have been so fine a bloom of perfection on Plato’s philosophical doctrines unless he had with all his heart and mind struggled with Homer for primacy.” He even thinks in Bloomian terms of that of wanting to be first even though in some part of your mind you know you’re second–he even struggles for primacy, showing perhaps too much love of contention and breaking a lance with him, as it were, but deriving some profit from the contest nonetheless; for as he says, “This strife is good for mortals.”

快速举一个更常见的例子，出自圣伯夫的著名文章《何谓经典？》，这篇文章探讨的是影响力。关于“何谓经典？”的文章由来已久，艾略特在1944年就写过一篇佳作，这些文章对影响力理论的发展史做出了重要贡献。圣伯夫写道：

Quickly, a more commonplace example taking from Sainte-Beuve, a famous essay of his called “What is a Classic?”–which is all about influence. There’s a tradition of essays called “What is a Classic?” Eliot wrote a great one in 1944, and these are very much a contribution to the history of the theory of influence. So Sainte-Beuve writes:

歌德说得没错，拜伦虽然才华横溢，诗风奔放，却害怕莎士比亚在人物塑造和实现方面比自己更胜一筹（的确，拜伦总是贬低莎士比亚）。他本想否认这一点。莎士比亚那种超脱于自我之外的境界令他感到恼火（这是歌德的说法）。他觉得，一旦靠近莎士比亚，自己就永远无法自在地展现自我。他从未否认过蒲柏，因为他并不畏惧蒲柏。他知道蒲柏（你知道蒲柏的身材有多矮）不过是他身旁的一堵矮墙。换句话说，他选择了一个他自认为比自己更优秀的人作为自己的文学榜样——顺便说一句，这并非事实，但他确实认为自己比亚历山大·蒲柏更胜一筹——并且他始终否认莎士比亚对他写作的强大影响，不断地与莎士比亚、对莎士比亚的崇拜、对《哈姆雷特》的过度喜爱等等争论不休。他似乎一直在否认莎士比亚对他有任何影响或权力。换句话说，他选择了一个较弱的先驱者，而不是一个强大的先驱者。所有这些都是布鲁姆在其心理动力学理论阐述过程中贯穿始终的主题。

Goethe spoke the truth when he remarked that Byron, great by the flow and source of poetry, feared that Shakespeare was more powerful than himself [it’s true, Byron was always abusing Shakespeare] in the creation and realization of his characters. He would have liked to deny it. The elevation so free from [this is Goethe talking] egoism irritated him. He felt when near it that he could never display himself at ease. He never denied Pope because he did not fear him. He knew that Pope was [and you know how short Pope was] only a low wall by his side. So in other words, he chose as his literary model somebody he knew he was better than– not true, by the way, but he thought he was better than Alexander Pope, and he perpetually denied a very, very powerful influence on his writing, quarreling constantly with Shakespeare and bardolatry and excessive love of Hamlet and all the rest of it. He’s constantly sort of denying any influence or power over himself on the part of Shakespeare. He chooses, in other words, for his precursor a weak precursor instead of a strong precursor. All of this is a continuous theme in the psychodynamic of Bloom’s theory as he elaborates it.

因此，除了词汇和哲学思想的广度之外，布鲁姆论证的复杂之处在于我一开始就提到的：传统的“影响”概念，即艺术与自然的问题，试图弄清影响危机究竟是关乎人对自然的取向、人模仿自然的能力以及人获取自然的能力，还是关乎文字本身——布鲁姆似乎更倾向于后者——关乎人与文本的关系。但请注意第1157页，布鲁姆其实并不想说这仅仅关乎文本。他并不想说这完全与被理解为作者的强大先驱有关。在某种意义上，自然本身也是一种文本，因此布鲁姆在第1157页右栏底部写道：

So what complicates Bloom’s argument, apart from the vocabulary and the philosophical range of thought, is what I began with: the traditional idea of influence as an art-nature problem, trying to figure out, in fact, whether the crisis of influence is the sense of one’s orientation to nature, one’s ability to imitate nature and have nature available to one, or whether it’s word oriented, which it seems to be more in Bloom: the sense of one’s relationship with text. But notice on page 1157 that Bloom really doesn’t want to say it’s just about text. He doesn’t really want to say that it has exclusively to do with the strong precursor understood, as it were, as an author. There is in some sense a text of nature as well, so that Bloom says, bottom of 1157, right-hand column:

……弗洛伊德的弟子奥托·兰克对艺术家与艺术的斗争，以及这种斗争与艺术家与自然的对立斗争之间的关系，有着更深刻的认识。换句话说，自然即死亡。如果作者不能在坚持自然优先性的论断中保持自我，他最终将以死亡的形式回归自然。等着瞧他们试图转录这句话时的反应吧。

… Freud’s disciple, Otto Rank, show[s] a greater awareness of the artist’s fight against art, and of the relation of this struggle to the artist’s antithetical battle against nature. In other words, nature is death. Nature is that into which–should he not sustain himself in the triumph of his assertion of priority nature–the author will fall back in the form of death. Wait until they try to transcribe that sentence.

好吧。嗯，不过你（笑）明白我的意思。这是一个很有意思的问题，布鲁姆想要强调的是，迟来的诗人所面临的部分困境，其实是对永生的追求。作为先行者，意味着你认为自己终将落败，意味着你将永生，意味着你并不属于我们称之为历史的那种不断展开、不可阻挡的序列；相反，你是一种超越历史的存在，一种力量，一种天才，或者一种超凡脱俗的权力。这既包含了布鲁姆所说的“对抗时间的谎言”，意味着你抗拒死亡，也意味着你坚持认为你的所作所为没有开端，没有优先性，也没有起源；你是第一个存在的。

Okay. Well, but you [laughter] got what I mean. This is an interesting problem, and Bloom wants to insist that part of the struggle of the belated poet is a struggle for immortality. Part of what it means to come first and to know nothing ever having been there before you is also to suppose that you are going to be last, that you’re going to be immortal, that you really do not belong in an unfolding, inexorable sequence of the sort that we call history; but that you are rather something, a force, a genius, or a power that transcends history. This entails as much the “lie against time,” as Bloom calls it, holding off death as it does, insisting on there having been no beginning, no priority, and no genesis in what you do; you were there first.

好的。为了快速说明这一点，我们来看你纸上的第五段和第六段。在布鲁姆看来，华兹华斯是一位对弥尔顿作品理解有深刻误解且姗姗来迟的诗人。他写了一首类似纲领性或承诺性的诗——实际上写于1800年，直到1814年才作为他名为《远足》的诗的序言发表——他为《隐士》写了一篇计划书，而《远足》一度被认为是《隐士》的一部分。他在诗中写道：“我对写《失乐园》不感兴趣。《失乐园》对我来说是过去的事情。它太古老了。谁会在乎弥尔顿在乎的那些东西：‘所有的力量，所有恐惧，无论是单独出现还是成群结队，无论是耶和华的雷霆，还是天使的合唱，以及帝王的宝座，我都毫不畏惧地走过。’” 《失乐园》？那不过是玩弄玩具兵罢了。与我即将要做的事相比，那根本不算什么：“无论是混沌，还是厄瑞玻斯最黑暗的深渊，亦或是梦境所挖掘出的盲目空虚，都无法孕育出我们审视内心、审视人类内心时所感受到的那种恐惧和敬畏——人类的内心，我的栖身之所，也是我歌声的主域。” 我说的不是上帝，不是天堂，不是地狱，也不是天堂之战，更不是任何神话传说或古代英雄事迹。

All right. To illustrate this very quickly, let’s look at passages five and six on your sheet. Wordsworth, the particularly important strong misreader and belated poet with respect to Milton, in Bloom’s view: Wordsworth writes in a kind of programmatic or promissory poem–written actually in 1800 and not published until 1814 as part of the preface to a poem of his called “The Excursion”–he wrote a prospectus to “The Recluse,” that’s what at one time “The Excursion” was supposed to be part of, and he says: “I am not interested in writing Paradise Lost. Paradise Lost for me is a thing of the past. It’s just archaic. Who would care about the things Milton cares about: ‘all strength, all terror, single or in bands that ever was put forth in personal form, Jehovah with his thunder and the choir of shouting angels and the imperial thrones, I pass them unalarmed.’ Paradise Lost, that’s just playing with toy soldiers. That’s nothing compared with what I myself am going to do: ‘not chaos, not the darkest pit of lowest Erebus nor aught of blinder vacancy scooped out by help of dreams can breed such fear and awe as fall upon us often when we look into our minds, into the mind of man, my haunt and the main region of my song.’ I’m not talking about God. I’m not talking about heaven. I’m not talking about hell. I’m not talking about war in heaven. I’m not talking about anything mythological or archaically heroic.

“我说的就是这个。我说的是人的心灵。我主要说的是我的心灵，但我的心灵也是你的心灵。心灵是普遍存在的，谈论心灵，我并不会重蹈自然的覆辙。我的关注点不在于天上的神灵，也不在于华莱士·史蒂文斯所说的那些‘超验的、星光璀璨的垃圾’，不在于我的前辈们，那些人陈旧的迷信。我对那些都不感兴趣，对其他的也不感兴趣。我对自然不感兴趣。我对那些如果我把自己简化成自然就会被埋葬的东西不感兴趣。我感兴趣的是意识，是心灵。换句话说，”华兹华斯说，“我的关注点完全是心理层面的。”

“I’m talking about this. I’m talking about the mind of man. I’m talking primarily about my mind, but my mind is your mind. Mind is universal, and in talking about mind I’m not falling back into the pit of nature. I’m keeping my focus not on the sky gods, not on the”transcendent, starry junk,” as Wallace Stevens called it, of my precursors, all those people with their outworn superstitions. I’m not interested in any of that, but I’m not interested in any of this either. I’m not interested in nature. I’m not interested in that in which I would be buried if I reduced myself to that. I am interested in consciousness, the psyche. In other words, my focus is,” Wordsworth says, “altogether psychological.”

好吧。我对《失乐园》没兴趣。那太古老了。那么，看看第五段：布鲁姆坚持认为，撒旦的三句话——与其说是弥尔顿的，不如说是布莱克和雪莱的。与其说是弥尔顿是华兹华斯的有力先驱，不如说是撒旦的，对吧？[笑] 正是弥尔顿笔下的撒旦说：“心灵自有其境，它能将地狱化为天堂，也能将天堂化为地狱。” 好吧。我的天。[笑] 我猜撒旦在写《隐士》的序言，不是吗？因为华兹华斯在《隐士》的序言里也是这么说的。“我不知道，”撒旦说，“我何时不像现在这样。” 这就是那位迟来的诗人常说的，“我先于一切而来。”在诗的另一处，撒旦对他的部下说：“你们知道吗？上帝一直说他创造了你们。你们还记得自己被创造吗？我不记得自己被创造过。我一直都在那里。”对吧？实际上，这就是他再次说的话，也是他在这一段中重复的话：“最终，我就是地狱。”当然，这话说起来让人很不舒服，但同时，这不正是兔子作为鬼王的象征吗？无论你扔给我什么，我都已经是它了。对吧？因为“我歌声的主要栖息之处和唯一领域是心灵”，指的是我自己的心灵。

All right. No interest in Paradise Lost. That’s just archaic. Well, look at passage five: three statements by Satan which Bloom insists–it’s not so much Milton, because Bloom follows Blake and Shelley in this. It’s not so much Milton who is the strong precursor of Wordsworth. It’s actually Satan, right? [laughs] It’s Milton’s Satan who says, “The mind is its own place and in itself can make a heaven of hell, a hell of heaven.” Okay. Gee whiz. [laughs] I guess Satan is writing the prospectus to “The Recluse,” isn’t he, because that’s what Wordsworth is saying in the prospectus to “The Recluse.” “I know no time,” says Satan, “when I was not as now.” That’s what the belated poet always says, “I came first.” Elsewhere in the poem Satan tells his troops, “You know what. God keeps saying he created you. Do you remember being created? I don’t remember being created. I’ve always been there.” Right? That is, in effect, what he says again, what he repeats in this passage, “Finally, myself am hell.” Well, that’s, of course, rather an uncomfortable thing to say, but at the same time it’s the rabbit as king of the ghosts, isn’t it? It is whatever you can throw at me, I’m it already. Right? Because “the main haunt and sole region of my song is the mind,” is my own mind.

好吧。所以，撒旦在《失乐园》里已经把华兹华斯在《隐士》的引言里能说的一切都说完了。他对《失乐园》的解读完全错误，以至于他以为自己在创作全新的作品，而实际上却恰恰揭示了，伟大的先驱诗人早已写出了后继诗人能写的一切。换句话说，在所有这样的时刻，在所有涉及影响焦虑的时刻，保守与创新之间的张力，或者说动态，都始终存在。

All right. So Satan has already said in Paradise Lost everything Wordsworth can possibly say in the prospectus to “The Recluse.” He has strongly misread Paradise Lost such that he thinks he’s doing something completely new, while revealing precisely that the strong precursor poet has always already written what the successor poet can write. The tension, the dynamic in other words, between conservation and innovation is intact in all such moments, in all the moments, that involve the anxiety of influence.

第五章 拉康和布鲁姆论玩具卡车托尼

Chapter 5. Lacan and Bloom on Tony the Toy Truck

很抱歉我时间有限。请给我一两分钟，因为我们得好好谈谈拖车托尼。很明显，在拉康看来，拖车托尼的故事讲述的是托尼最终选择了小客体a，没错：小汽车邦比，一个不完美但却乐于助人的朋友——“这才叫朋友”；而欲望对象，尼托、斯皮迪——哇，它们可是汽车啊。这些欲望对象表面上看是不恰当的选择。美国自我心理学家会这么说，但用布努埃尔式的说法，它们是模糊的欲望对象，它们在路上行驶，对托尼来说，作为客体关系根本就不存在。所以，尼托和斯皮迪是“大他者”——对吧？——而邦比则是小客体a。

I’m sorry I have so little time for this. Give me a minute or two because we have to honor Tony the Tow Truck, and it’s rather obvious that for Lacan, Tony the Tow Truck is a text in which Tony settles for the objet petit a, right: little Bumpy the Car, an imperfect being but a helpful one and a friend–“that’s what I call a friend”; whereas the objects of desire, Neato, Speedy–whoa, those are cars. The objects of desire are improper object choices on the face of it. That’s what an American ego psychologist would say, but they are, in a more Bunuelesque way of putting it, obscure objects of desire as they motor on down the road which are simply unavailable to Tony as object relations at all. So Neato and Speedy are the big other–right?–and Bumpy is the object petit a.

好了。现在很明显，哈罗德·布鲁姆认为《拖车托尼》是对《小火车头的故事》的严重误读。这一点显而易见，因为在《小火车头的故事》中，邦比才是英雄。而误读之处在于，托尼成了需要邦比帮助的英雄。换句话说，按照故事的民间传说意义，邦比成了帮助者而非英雄。但我们最终可以看到，故事的核心叙事模式——弱者通过坚持不懈的努力最终必然会增强强者的力量——是关于强者和弱者的关系。无论是《小火车头的故事》还是《拖车托尼》，都讲述了强者和弱者的关系，强者必须在某种程度上被弱者补充或取代，才能真正实现自我价值。在邦比出现之后，我们再也无法用同样的眼光看待拖车托尼这个角色了。然而，邦比正是《小火车头》中的英雄，而托尼在本作中却占据了这一主角位置。因此，这种关系再次呈现出一种对抗性，英雄主义的焦点从一个角色转移到了另一个角色身上。与此同时——任何给孩子读过这两个故事的人都能看出——托尼以一种《小火车头》完全预料到的方式重写了这个故事。

All right. Now it’s just perfectly obvious that for Harold Bloom, Tony the Tow Truck is a strong misreading of The Little Engine that Could. It’s perfectly clear because Bumpy is the hero of The Little Engine that Could. The misreading involves making Tony the hero who needs the help of Bumpy. In other words, Bumpy, in the folkloric sense of the story, becomes the helper and not the hero, but we can see, after all, that the essential narrative model–the model of the small turning out through perseverance and energy to necessarily reinforce the strength of the strong–is about the strong and the weak. Both The Little Engine that Could and Tony the Tow Truck are about the strong and the weak, that the strong must in some sense or another be supplemented or supplanted by the weak if the strong is fully to self-realize. We can’t ever read Tony the Tow Truck, the character, Tony, quite the same way again after the appearance of Bumpy, and yet Bumpy is nothing other than the hero of The Little Engine that Could, a subject position that has been appropriated by Tony in this text. So the relationship is again an agonistic one involving the transposition of heroism from one character-focus to another while at the same time–as anybody can recognize who has read both stories to their kids–simply rewriting the story in a way that The Little Engine that Could completely anticipates.

好了，就先说到这儿吧。周二我们将继续深入拉康的理论领域，学习德勒兹、加塔利和斯拉沃热·齐泽克。

All right. So much then for that. We’ll be returning to more Lacanian pastures on Tuesday when we study Deleuze and Guattari and Slavoj Žižek.

第十五讲——后现代心理

Lecture 15 - The Postmodern Psyche

第一章 齐泽克、德勒兹与政治

Chapter 1. Žižek, Deleuze, and the Political

保罗·弗莱教授：所以今天我们仍然聚焦于个体意识。“为什么？”你可能会问。嗯，我们可以把文本或电影的心理发生过程看作是某种符号模式的场所或模型，这在齐泽克的作品中尤为明显，在某种程度上在德勒兹的作品中也有体现。因此，与周四的阅读材料不同，我们仍然可以把今天的阅读理解为课程大纲中心理学重点的一部分。这实际上是我们对心理学重点的告别，之所以这样安排，是因为今天的作者们暗示了其中蕴含的政治意义。也就是说，我们应该以某种方式理解他们关于心理运作方式的论证具有政治含义。

Professor Paul Fry: So today we’re still focused on individual consciousness. “Why?” you might ask. Well, we can speak of the psychogenesis of the text or film as the site or model for symbolic patterning of one sort or another, perhaps in the case certainly of Žižek, to some extent also of Deleuze. Therefore we can still understand today’s readings, unlike Thursday’s readings, as belonging to the psychological emphasis in our syllabus. This is actually our farewell to the psychological emphasis, and it is so arranged because there are intimations in today’s authors that there are political stakes. That is to say, in one way or another we are to understand their argument about the way in which the psyche functions as having political implications.

在我看来，齐泽克在你文章结尾处对《哭泣的游戏》的精彩解读尤其引人入胜。他实际上是在说：“瞧，这不仅仅是对爱尔兰共和革命责任的一种推卸。士兵并非只是放弃了他在革命活动中的角色；他在私生活中——也就是说，在他意识的情欲维度中——发现了内心革命的必要性。他必然以一种与理解自身与新兴的爱尔兰共和政权之间关系所需的思维颠覆同样激进且密切相似的方式颠覆了自己的思维。因此，”齐泽克实际上是在说，“与‘大他者’最终悲剧性的遭遇所带来的意识剧变，具有政治意义。”

Žižek is fascinating, it seems to me, in his brilliant reading of The Crying Game at the very end of your essay, in the moment when he says in effect, “Look. This isn’t just a kind of abdication from responsibility for the Irish Republican Revolution. The soldier has not merely walked away from his role in revolutionary activity; he has discovered in his private life–that is to say, in the erotic dimension of his consciousness–the need for revolution from within. He has necessarily disrupted his own thinking in ways equally radical to and closely parallel to the disruption of thinking that’s required to understand one’s relationship with the emerging Republican status of Ireland. And so,” says Žižek in effect, “there are political implications for the upheaval in consciousness that an ultimately tragic encounter with the Big Other entails.

关于齐泽克，我还想顺便提一下——我想你们的编辑在斜体字的前言中也略有提及——这种对晦涩难懂甚至超越世俗的欲望对象的迷恋，既关乎个人，也关乎社会心理，其中蕴含着诱惑，政治上的诱惑。就宗教而言，齐泽克的作品中对宗教表现出一种或许令人惊讶或反直觉的友好态度，因为信仰或对信仰的追求，归根结底，确实是一种努力，试图与自己渴望却又无法拥有的事物建立某种有意义的联系。同样地——在某些时刻，他坦言自己的政治思想存在某种不稳定性，尽管他总体上属于左翼，并且在某种程度上需要被理解为马克思的追随者——但他仍然认识到，在政治中，对宏大理念的迷恋既令人兴奋，也可能蕴含着潜在的危险。当然，它也可能是一种进步的集体主义形式。另一方面，它也可能是一种助长法西斯主义兴起的宏大理念。齐泽克也承认这一点——公众认同某种几乎或完全无法接近的“他者”，无论是作为一种政治理念还是作为一位魅力型政治领袖，最终都可能带来令人眩晕的危险可能性。

I should say in passing also about Žižek that –and your editor, I think, goes into this a little bit in the italicized preface–that there are temptations, political temptations, entailed in this fascination with an obscure or even perhaps transcendent object of desire for the individual, but also for the social psyche. In religious terms, there is a perhaps surprising or counterintuitive friendliness toward religion in Žižek’s work on the grounds that faith or the struggle for faith, after, all does constitute an effort to enter into some kind of meaningful relationship with that which one desires yet at the same time can’t have. By the same token–and this is where, in certain moments, he confesses to a kind of instability in his political thinking, even though he is by and large on the left and partly needs to be understood as a disciple of Marx–nevertheless, he recognizes that in politics there is a kind of excitement but also, perhaps, potential danger in fascination with a big idea. It could be, of course, some form of progressive collectivity. It could, on the other hand, be the kind of big idea that countenances the rise of fascism. Žižek acknowledges this– that public identification with a kind of almost, or completely, inaccessible otherness, either as a political idea or as a charismatic political leader, can, after all, open up a vertigo of dangerous possibilities.

我特意使用“眩晕”这个词，因为我稍后会再谈到希区柯克的电影《迷魂记》，但与此同时，德勒兹的思想显然也带有政治意味。当然，在《千高原》的第一章中，德勒兹向我们呈现了一种思想实验，既是向读者推荐的——看看你是否能以这种全新的、激进的创新方式思考——也是通过本章的风格、组织和结构，为这种思考方式提供了一个范例。因此，在进行思想实验的过程中，德勒兹再次在思想上进行了一场你或许可以称之为“内在革命”的变革，但其在政治上的意义，正如齐泽克所言，仍然有些模糊不清。也就是说，这种根茎式的思维模式——我们稍后会再谈到这种思维模式——它彻底去中心化，并倾向于认同某种意义上的群众集体运动，显然可以逐步走向民主：也就是说，它超越了我们现有的社会和文化等级制度所能容纳的民主范畴。但与此同时，它也可能再次走向法西斯主义，因为法西斯文化的组织，尽管仍然是一种自上而下的安排，并在群众动员过程中融入了狂热，但这种动员本身却是根茎式的。

I use the word “vertigo” advisedly because I’m going to be coming back to Hitchcock’s Vertigo in just a minute, but in the meantime there are also obviously political stakes in Deleuze. Deleuze, of course, presents to us in this first chapter of his book, A Thousand Plateaus, he presents to us a kind of thought experiment, both as something recommended to the reader–see if you can think in this new, radically innovative way–but also providing a model for thinking of this kind in the style and organization and composition of the chapter itself. So in making a thought experiment, once again, Deleuze has to perform in thought what you might call a revolution from within, but the implications once again in politics, as indeed also for Žižek, are somewhat ambiguous. That is to say, the rhizomatic mode of thinking–and we’ll come back to the rhizomatic mode of thinking as we go along–which is radically de-centering and which lends itself to identification with, as it were, the mass movement of collectivity, can plainly be progressively democratic: that is to say, democratic beyond even what our social and cultural hierarchies accommodate. But at the same time it can once again be fascistic, because the organization of fascistic culture, while nevertheless a kind of top-down arrangement with a fervor involved as the mass is mobilized, nevertheless is, in this mobilization, rhizomatic.

德勒兹谨慎地指出，根茎，以及根茎式思维，正如他反复强调的那样，既有利也有弊。[笑] 老鼠是根茎。马唐草也是根茎。换句话说，所有以这种方式组织自身的事物都是根茎式的；不过，正如我稍后会更仔细地解释的那样，其中很多在德勒兹看来是有益的。顺便说一句，我提到“德勒兹”的方式和提到“温萨特”的方式一样。加塔利是一位重要的同事和盟友。他们合著了许多书籍，包括我稍后会提到的一本。他们也各自独立创作，但“德勒兹”——仅仅因为他的作品更为丰富，而且人们在某种程度上觉得他在这项工作中更为核心——是“德勒兹和加塔利”的代称。所以我会提到“德勒兹”，但我并非有意轻视加塔利。无论如何，我们会更仔细地考察德勒兹的根茎理论，但与此同时，就其政治含义而言——当我们开始思考这类人物时，我们离政治层面也越来越近——他们两人都承认，这种含义在某种程度上是模糊的。换句话说，他们引入了新的思考可能性，而且正如我们将看到的，他们彼此之间截然不同。他们引入了新的思考可能性，但他们也坦诚地承认，他们并不完全清楚这些可能性会走向何方——也就是说，成功进入他们任何一人的思想世界会带来哪些影响或后果。

Deleuze is careful to point out that rhizomes are, and rhizomatic thinking is, as he says repeatedly, both for the best andworst. [laughs] Rats are rhizomes. Crabgrass is a rhizome. In other words, everything which organizes itself in this fashion is rhizomatic; much of it, though, as I’ll be coming back to try to explain with a little more care, is for the good in Deleuze’s view. By the way, I say “Deleuze” in the same way I said “Wimsatt.” Guattari is an important colleague and ally. They wrote many books together including one that I’ll mention later. They also wrote things separately, but “Deleuze,” simply because his oeuvre is more ample and people feel somehow or another that he’s more central to this work, is a synecdoche for “Deleuze and Guattari.” So I’ll be saying “Deleuze,” but I don’t mean to slight Guattari. In any case, so we’ll be examining the Deleuzian rhizome a little bit more closely, but in the meantime, as to its political implications–and we are moving closer to the political as we begin to think about figures of this kind–they’re really on the admission of both of them somewhat ambiguous. In other words, they’re introducing new possibilities of thought and they’re very different from each other, as we’ll see. They’re introducing new possibilities of thought, but they are candid enough to admit that they don’t quite know where these possibilities are going–that is, what the implications or consequences of successfully entering the thought world of either one of them might be.

第二章 什么是后现代主义？

Chapter 2. What Is Postmodernism?

好的。没错，他们的观点确实截然不同。你可能会问：“我们为什么要把这两篇文章放在一起读？” 它们的重叠之处并不完全清晰。我稍后会解释，但就目前而言，它们探讨的内容确实大相径庭。正如我所说，德勒兹关注的是一种思想实验，这种实验与去中心化思维有关，摆脱了树状或类似树木的思维模式——我们稍后会详细讨论这一点；另一方面，齐泽克遵循拉康对“现成的客体”（即唾手可得的客体，你可以随意拥有）和“欲望的客体”（即意义链中永远超越或遥不可及之物）的区分，在发展这一理念并思考“欲望的客体”及其各种形式时，他提出了一个奇特的思想，即“污点”（blot）——叙事形式中的元素，我们叙事能力组织方式中的元素，它实际上无法被叙述，也无法赋予意义。当然，这种意义是具体的、特定的意义，可以与可触及的客体联系起来。因此，正如我们将看到的，齐泽克在其文章中试图阐述的核心思想与“大他者”和“污点”之间的关系密切相关。

All right. So yes, they certainly have very different ideas. I wouldn’t blame you for saying, “Why on earth are we reading these two texts together?” The overlap isn’t altogether clear. I’m going to suggest what it is in a minute, but in the meantime they are certainly on about very different things. Deleuze is concerned with, as I say, introducing a kind of thought experiment which has to do with the de-centering of thought, getting away from the tree or arboresque model of thought–we’ll have more to say about that; and Žižek, on the other hand, following Lacan’s distinction between the object, ready to hand, that you can have if you want, and the object of desire which–such is the chain of signification–is perpetually something that exceeds or outdistances our grasp–in developing this idea, and thinking about what the object of desire, in all of its manifold forms, might be, he develops this curious idea, which is at the center of his thinking, of the blot–the element in narrative form, the element in the way in which our storytelling capacities are organized, which really can’t be narrated, which really can’t lend itself to meaning. That sort of meaning is, of course, concrete, specific meaning, that which can be tied down to an accessible object. So the central idea that Žižek is attempting to develop in his essay has to do with this notion of the relationship between the Big Other and the blot, as we’ll see.

所以，这些观点乍一看截然不同，正如我所说，你肯定会好奇它们之间究竟存在哪些重叠之处。不过，我想当你阅读这两篇文章略显轻快、节奏紧凑的文风时，你会发现它们在某种情绪、立场或批判理论取向上是共通的。换句话说，它们似乎属于同一时期。尽管它们的观点看似迥异——也就是说，它们试图表达的基本理念截然不同——但如果仅仅从文风来看，你或许会觉得这两篇文章出自同一人之手。实际上，我认为这种说法并不完全正确，但同时，这两篇文章的文风都给人一种高能量、略带亢奋的感觉，这或许会让你停下来思考：那么，这究竟属于哪个时期呢？

So these strike one as being extremely different ideas, and as I say I wouldn’t blame you for wondering just what overlap there can be. Well, at the same time I would think that as you read the somewhat bouncy and frantic prose of both of these texts, you did see that they had a kind of mood, stance, or orientation toward the critical and theoretical project in common. They seem, in other words, to be of the same moment. Even though their ideas seem to be so very different–that is, the basic ideas they’re trying to get across seem to be so very different–you could perhaps imagine these two texts as being written, if it was just a question of considering their style, by the same person. Actually, I think that’s not quite true, but at the same time the kind of high-energy, too-caffeinated feeling that you get from the prose of both is something that might give you pause and make you wonder: well, just what moment does this belong to?

答案很重要，某种程度上也显而易见。我相信你们都准备好告诉我它属于哪个时期了。它属于后现代主义。这两个例子恰恰体现了过去二三十年来我们接触到的最难以捉摸的概念——喜欢它的人会说它灵活多变（笑），不喜欢它的人会说它晦涩难懂。我认为，如果我们稍作停顿，仅仅围绕“后现代主义”这个概念展开讨论，就能更好地理解这两篇文章。也许这正是你们想通过这门课学习的内容之一，所以我只是尽力提供一些帮助。（笑）

The answer is important and, in a way, obvious. I’m sure all of you are ready to tell me what moment it belongs to. It belongs to Postmodernism. These are two exemplars of what is by far the most slippery–if one likes it, one wants to say versatile, [laughs] and if one doesn’t like it, one wants to say murky–concepts to which we have been exposed in the last twenty or thirty years. I think that, in a way, we can bring both essays into focus as a pair a little bit if we pause somewhat, simply over the concept “Postmodernism.” Maybe that’s one of the things you wanted to learn in taking a course like this, so I’m just providing a service. [laughter]

那么，后现代主义究竟是什么？我想我们对它在艺术表达中的含义有所了解。我们已经接触过足够多的例子。或许我们甚至上过一些课程，在这些课程中，后现代主义在艺术形式和表达的语境下被提及。艺术表达中的后现代主义——尤其是在视觉艺术领域，但我认为这同样适用于叙事和诗歌中的某些运动——是一种对过去的折衷主义取向。在某种意义上，它是一种回归过去；它向现代主义倾向于认为已经过时并被弃置一旁的传统和历史表达方式敞开了文本的可能性；因此，正如我所说，在艺术表达中，后现代主义是对艺术和文学史所提供的各种可能性的折衷回归；在建筑领域，许多例子都非常出色，但遗憾的是，也有许多例子令人不忍直视。你知道吗，十五到二十年前，每个商业街、每个购物中心都重新装修了，或者——该怎么说呢？——翻新了。每个购物中心都翻新了，他们是怎么翻新的呢？它们以前都是平的。在那之前，它们有点像密斯·凡·德·罗的风格，有点像六十年代的现代主义风格。它们就那样平淡无奇地矗立在那里，于是翻新者来了，在购物中心上加装了小山墙，这样购物中心里的每个小商店都有了自己的山墙，这就是后现代主义。最糟糕的情况发生在郊区住宅，也是打着一种盲目、毫无品味的回归新古典主义和其他一些传统风格的旗号，进行着类似的改造。

So Postmodernism. What is Postmodernism? I think we know what it is in artistic expression. We have encountered enough examples of it. We have, perhaps, even taken courses in which, in the context of artistic form and expression, it has come up. Postmodernism in artistic expression–particularly in the visual arts, but I think this is true of certain movements in both narrative and poetry as well–postmodernism is an eclectic orientation to the past. In a certain sense, it’s a return to the past; it’s an opening up of textual possibility to traditions and historical moments of expression which Modernism had tended to suppose obsolete and to have set aside; so that in artistic expression, as I say, Postmodernism is an eclectic return to possibilities thrown up by the history of art and literature; in architecture, many examples are quite extraordinary and many, unfortunately, are also hideous. You know that there was a certain point fifteen or twenty years ago when every strip mall, every shopping mall, was redecorated or–what’s the word I want?–renovated. Every shopping mall was renovated, and how did they renovate it? They’d been flat. They’d been sort of Mies van der Rohe, sort of sixties-modern before then. They just sat there flat, and so the renovators came along and put little gables on the shopping mall so that each little shop in the mall now has a gable, and this is postmodern. The most awful things were done with suburban houses, also in the name of a kind of blind, completely tasteless return to the neoclassical and certain other aspects of tradition.

所以，后现代主义在郊区文化中表现得相当糟糕，但与此同时，它也催生了大量有趣的绘画作品。突然之间，纽约的艺术圈不再局限于单一流派，而这正是它的标志。它不再仅仅局限于某种抽象艺术，也不再仅仅是所有人都认同的回归现实主义。它是各种元素的混合体。艺术家们总是对自己在艺术史上的地位无比执着，但这并非仅仅是艺术家群体为了在艺术史上找到一个固定的位置而聚集在一起。而是每个艺术家都以一种近乎无政府主义的独立性，摆脱其他艺术家的束缚，以各自的方式诠释艺术史。因此，纽约、柏林、洛杉矶等地的艺术圈，不再具有某种特定的特征。后现代主义的本质就在于它走向了全球，它受到无数的影响和来源，而艺术家们对于如何融合和组合这些来源却鲜有共识；因此，就艺术表达而言，后现代主义时期——换句话说，后现代主义之后——呈现出一种医学症状，我特意这样说，后现代主义时期在艺术表达中呈现出一种两极分化的状态。

So the postmodern in what you might call suburban culture has been pretty awful, but at the same time it has entailed a great deal of interesting work in painting. All of a sudden, the New York scene isn’t just one school, and that’s the sign of it. It’s not just a certain kind of abstraction. It’s not just a wholesale return, agreed on by everyone, to Realism. It’s a mixture of everything. Artists are always just completely obsessed with their place in art history, but it’s not just groups of artists together wanting to identify a certain place for themselves in art history. It’s every artist in a kind of anarchic independence from the thinking of other artists coming to terms with art history in his or her own way so that the scene–the art scenes of New York and Berlin and Los Angeles and so on–the scene isn’t something that you can identify as having a certain character anymore. It’s postmodern precisely in that it’s gone global, it has a million influences and sources, and there is very little agreement among artists about how to amalgamate and put these sources together; so that in terms of artistic expression, the postmodern moment–after Modernism, in other words–the postmodern moment presents itself, and I put it deliberately, as a medical symptom, the bipolar way the postmodern moment presents itself in artistic expression.

第三章 后现代主义、怀疑与愿景

Chapter 3. Postmodernism, Doubt, and Vision

从哲学角度来看，后现代主义不仅可以理解为对知识基础的怀疑，或者说是对我们在本课程中或多或少一直在讨论的那种普遍存在的怀疑的怀疑，而且尤其可以理解为对部分与整体之间关系的怀疑。换句话说，我的腿显然是我身体的一部分，而它同时又与我的脚构成一个整体，我能确定这一点吗？我又如何能以某种稳定的方式知道什么是部分，什么是整体呢？举一个更有趣的例子——这出自维特根斯坦的《哲学研究》——法国国旗，它被称为三色旗，对吧？三色旗由白、蓝、红三色条组成。如果我顺序错了，请见谅。事实上，我几乎可以肯定我见过这种颜色，[笑声]，但这三条色带彼此关联，显然是国旗的组成部分，它们具有一定的象征意义。也就是说，每种颜色都代表着某种东西，并融入到对国旗象征意义的理解中。但同时，红、白、蓝——抱歉——是的，红、白、蓝并不局限于这块布料。那条白色的小色带显然是白色的一部分。它本身并不能被简单地理解。这些色带也是其他事物的一部分；而且，如果你在不了解自己所见的情况下观察这面三色旗，你怎么能说它是整体的一部分呢？你会说，“嗯，它们只是部分而已”，或者“它们本身就是完整的整体，只是碰巧被放在一起了”。同样地，如果你看到三色旗中白色的部分，然后说“白色”，那么显然，相对于“白色”这个宽泛的普世概念而言，一面小旗子只不过是与“白色”这一概念的一种转喻关系。但简而言之，为了以另一种方式具体阐述部分与整体之间这种复杂的关系，我们为什么对我们所看到的如此确信呢？

Now philosophically, Postmodernism can be understood as doubt not just about the grounds of knowledge or the widespread sorts of doubt which we have been talking about more or less continuously in this course, but as doubt in particular about the relationship between or among parts and wholes. In other words, can I be sure that my leg is part of my body when plainly it is at the same time a whole with respect to my foot? How is it that I know in any stable way what a part or a whole is? To take a more interesting example–this is in Wittgenstein’s Philosophical Investigations–there is the flag, the French flag, which is called the tricolor, right? Now the tricolor is made up of three strips of color: white, blue, and red. I’m sorry if I’ve gotten the order wrong. In fact, I am almost positive that I have, [laughter] but there are those three strips of color existing in relation to each other, and plainly those three strips of color are parts of the flag, and they have a certain symbolic value. That is to say, each color represents something and enters into the symbolic understanding of what the flag is. But at the same time red, white, and blue–sorry–yes, red, white, and blue aren’t confined to this piece of cloth. The little strip of white is obviously part of whiteness. It can’t be understood simply in and of itelf. These strips of color are parts of other things as well; and what’s more, if you look at the tricolor without knowing what you’re looking at, how can you say that it’s the part of a whole? You say, “Well, they’re just parts,” or “They’re wholes unto themselves which somebody happens to have laid side by side.” By the same token, if you look at the part of the tricolor which is white and you say, “White,” well, obviously with respect to the vast universalizing concept “white,” a little flag is simply a kind of metonymic relationship with that sense of white. But, in short, to concretize this idea of the problematic relationship between part and whole in a different way, why are we so confident about what we see?

我相信你们大多数人都知道，哲学思考往往受到视觉隐喻的束缚。我们假定自己理解现实，因为——或许我们在谈论这个问题时并没有完全意识到这种隐喻的运用——我们说我们能看到它；但你是如何看到它的呢？你之所以能看到它，是因为眼睛的透镜或聚焦能力，这种能力对你所见之物的本质施加了某种控制。如果你看得太近，就只能看到点。如果你看着某样东西然后闭上眼睛，那也变成了一幅巨大的视网膜画作，就像马克·托比的画作一样。它与你所看到的事物有关联，但同时又是截然不同的东西。如果你离物体太远，它们就会消融。你原本以为的物体会融入一个更广阔、更宏大的空间，这个空间似乎具有另一种客观的本质。如果你坐在喷气式飞机上向下看，你看到的景象当然看起来有形状和结构，但如果你站在地面上，尽可能地观察同一片区域，你看到的景象却截然不同。你看到的只是不同的东西。如果你意识到我们在感知世界时所受到的“聚焦的束缚”，你就能明白这种持续的消解和重新聚焦，使得物体不断地以新的方式呈现。

As most of you know, I’m sure, philosophical thinking tends to be tyrannized by metaphors of vision. We assume that we understand reality because–not altogether as consciously metaphorically in speaking about this as perhaps we might be–we say that we can see it; but how do you see it? You see it because of the lensing or focusing capacities of the eye, which exercise a certain tyranny over the nature of what you see. If you look too closely at something, all you can see is dots. If you look at something and close your eyes, that, too, becomes a kind of vast retinal Mark Tobey painting. It has a relation to what you see but is at the same time something very different. And if you get too far away from objects, they dissolve. What you thought was an object dissolves into a much vaster, greater space which seems to have another objective nature. If you’re in a jet and you’re looking down, what you’re seeing certainly looks like it has form and structure, but the form and structure is not at all what you’re seeing if you’re standing on the ground looking at exactly the same, shall we say, square footage insofar as you can. You’re simply seeing different things, and if you recognize what might be called the tyranny of focus in the way in which we orient ourselves to the world, you can see this perpetual dissolve and refocus constituting objects perpetually in new ways.

科学史上也存在这种情况。亚原子粒子之间的关系有时会彻底颠覆，你原本认为的基本单元，实际上却包含着另一个基本单元，而它本身也是这个基本单元的一部分。我指的是直线加速器黄金时代发生的事情，当时实验数据似乎揭示了各种各样对既定基本概念的惊人颠覆；因此，从科学到最主观的视觉理解方式，所有这些方式都可能对部分与整体的关系产生质疑。什么是整体？我们如何定义统一性？我们是否应该执着于将现实的本质视为一系列统一体的集合？显然，德勒兹对此极为不满。他不想与统一性有任何瓜葛。他的思想实验的全部意义就在于打破事物的中心地位，使人们无法再谈论单元、整体或孤立实体。德勒兹关注的是实体的存在、融合、分离、重聚以及运动（如果它们还能被称为实体的话）。

This happens, too, in the history of science. The relationship between subatomic particles sometimes turns itself inside out, and the particle that you thought was the fundamental unit turns out, in fact, to have within it a fundamental unit of which it is a part. I’m just referring to what happened during the golden age of the linear accelerator when all sorts of remarkable sorts of inversions of what’s taken to be fundamental seemed to be made available by the experimental data; so that in all of these ways, ranging from scientific to the most subjectively visual ways of understanding the world, there are possibilities of doubt that can be raised about part-whole relations. What is a whole? How do we define a unity? Should we be preoccupied with the nature of reality as a set of unities? Obviously, Deleuze is extremely upset about this. He doesn’t want anything to do with unity. The whole function of his thought experiment is the de-centering of things such that one can no longer talk about units or wholes or isolated entities. It’s the being together, merging together, flying apart, reuniting, and kinesis or movement of entities, if they can even be called entities, that Deleuze is concerned with.

第四章 非人化

Chapter 4. Dehumanization

后现代主义的另一个方面，特别是后现代哲学家让-弗朗索瓦·利奥塔所说的“非人性”，或者说是人类非人化的过程。选择这个词有点奇怪，因为它并非反人道主义，而是一种全新的思考人类的方式。你会注意到，德勒兹谈到了“无器官的身体”——不仅在这段摘录中，而且在他的所有著作中都反复提及，这也是为什么他在这里对此解释甚少的原因。这或许会让你感到困惑，但它暗示着，正如德勒兹所说，我们是机械的，而非有机的。如果以中心为中心的思维的问题在于它将一切都视为树木，视为一棵树，那么这个问题就源于这样一个事实：树木在其象征意义上被理解为具有器官。树根是肌肉和循环系统；花朵本质上是生殖器官；树冠或树荫象征着树木伸向天空的思维，象征着树木的心理。同样地，如果我们把自己的身体比作树木，我们就会认为身体的某些部分具有认知能力，而另一些部分则具有自主性，能够做事。如果是这样，那么我们就会认为以生殖器或基因为中心的身体观才是生产力的体现。

Now another aspect of the postmodern is what the postmodern philosopher Jean-François Lyotard, in particular, has called “the inhuman” or the process of the dehumanization of the human. Now this is a weird term to choose because it’s not at all anti-humanistic. It’s really a new way of thinking about the human. Deleuze, you’ll notice, talks–not just here in this excerpt, but repeatedly throughout his work, which is why he has so little to say about it here that’s explanatory–about “bodies without organs.” That might have brought you up short, but what it suggests is that we are, as Deleuze would put it, machinic rather than organic. If the problem with centered thought is that it thinks of everything as arboreal, as a tree, that problem has to do with the fact that a tree is understood in its symbolic extensions to have organs. The roots are muscles and circulation; the blossoms are genital in nature; the crown or canopy of leaves is the mind of the tree reaching up to the sky, the mentality of the tree. By the same token, if we think of our own bodies as arboreal, we think of certain parts of those bodies as cognitive, other parts of those bodies as having agency, as doing things. If that’s the case, then we think of a centered and ultimately genital or genetic understanding of the body as being productive.

德勒兹想要理解身体，将其视为一种互动性、一种多态性、一种反常性的存在。他想要理解身体无处不在又无处可寻，一个存在于其他身体之中却又无处可寻的身体。为了实现这一点，身体与其他事物的互动必须摒弃主体性，也摒弃“我思故我在；世界因我思而生”的认知意图模式，摒弃所有这些因素。换言之，后现代的非人化并非否定人的重要性，而是以一种激进的方式重新思考人与其他身体和事物之间的关系。

Deleuze wants to understand the body as being interactive, as being polymorphous perverse, among other things. He wants to understand it as being everywhere and nowhere, an un-situated body among other bodies. In order for this to happen, its interface with other things has to be without agency and also without cognitive intention on the model of “I think, therefore I am; the world comes into being because I think,” without any of this in play. In other words, the dehumanization of the postmodern has to do not at all with denying the importance of the human but with this radical way of rethinking the human among other bodies and things.

显然，这种强调包含着一种融入他者性的过程，一种主体与客体之间的连续性，在这种连续性中，最终，内在的、构成我真实自我或不可或缺的本质，与外在的事物之间的差异变得完全渗透和可互换。十九世纪末的作家兼美学哲学家沃尔特·佩特在其名著《文艺复兴》的结尾，对此做了精彩的阐述：他实际上是说，“我们太习惯于认为自己身处其中，而其他一切都在彼岸，并且，不知何故，我们对外部一切事物的视角是一种拯救性的隔离，使我们能够保持客观性。”然后，佩特说道（大意如此）：“这怎么可能呢？因为我们和外部世界是由相同的物质构成的。换句话说，我们也是分子结构的。我们内在的东西‘能使铁生锈，也能使玉米成熟’（他的原话）。我们对自身的内在感受与我们不断接触的外部世界之间存在着一种连续性。”

Plainly, this emphasis involves a kind of dissolving into otherness, a continuity between subject and object in which the difference, ultimately, between what is inside me, what is authentic or integral to my being me, and what’s outside me become completely permeable and interchangeable. The late nineteenth-century author and aesthetic philosopher Walter Pater, in the conclusion to a famous book of his called The Renaissance, had a wonderful way of putting this: he said in effect, “We are too used to thinking that we’re in here and everything else is out there and that, somehow or another, our perspective on everything out there is a kind of saving isolation enabling our power of objectivity.” Then Pater says, paraphrased, “How can this be, because we’re made up of the same things that are out there? We, too, are molecular, in other words. What is in us ‘rusts iron and ripens corn’ [his words]. There is a continuousness between the inside feeling we have about ourselves and the exteriority with which we are constantly coming in contact.”

当然，德勒兹和加塔利用他们自己激动而跳跃的方式来表达这些概念，但我们夸大意识与其环境的隔离性并非什么新观点。这种根茎式的、去中心化的思维方式旨在关注内外之间的渗透性。现在，你可以说，德勒兹感兴趣的是——如果你回到我们讨论形式主义者时所采用的坐标系，从索绪尔到结构主义，再到解构主义——如果你回到这些坐标系，你可以说，德勒兹感兴趣的，就像我们读过的许多其他人一样，是将垂直轴虚拟化，甚至消除垂直轴：换句话说，是将构成水平轴上一切展开事物的树的中心、树梢或树冠——无论是语言，还是像语言一样结构的无意识，或是其他任何事物。你也可以说，德勒兹的计划也是对这条垂直轴的解构或虚拟化。

Deleuze and Guattari, of course, have their own excited, jumpy way of putting these things, but it’s not really a new idea that we exaggerate the isolation of consciousness from its surroundings. There is a permeability of inside and outside that this kind of rhizomic, or de-centered, thinking is meant to focus on. Now you could say that what Deleuze is interested in–if you go back to our coordinates that we kept when we were talking about the formalists, Saussure through structuralism, through deconstruction–if you go back to those coordinates, you could say that what Deleuze is interested in, like so many others we’ve read, is a rendering virtual, or possibly even eliminating, of the vertical axis: in other words, of that center or head or crown of the tree which constitutes everything that unfolds on the horizontal axis–be it language, be it the unconscious structured like a language, be it whatever it might be. You could say that the project of Deleuze, too, is the undoing or rendering virtual of this vertical axis.

第五章 德勒兹、瓜塔里和拉康

Chapter 5. Deleuze, Guattari, and Lacan

某种程度上，我认为这是对的，但横轴又是什么呢？德勒兹与解构主义的关系正是在这里变得有些棘手，也是我们能够真正看到差异的地方。我将在这一点上把他与拉康进行比较，但我想先指出一点，稍后我会提到，他与拉康也存在分歧。你们记得，在拉康的《文字的能动性》一文中，他不仅将组合轴描述为一系列同心圆，每个同心圆又由更小的同心圆组成。他不仅仅谈到这一点。他还谈到，语言中想象或欲望的组合力量就像五线谱一样运作，因此符号的组织，就其彼此间的邻近性而言，可以是旋律性的，也可以是和声性的；但无论如何，你不能仅仅把组合轴看作是一条完整的线性线。它具有不同种类的维度。

Well, in a way, I think that’s true, but then what is the horizontal axis? That is where the relation of Deleuze to, let’s say, deconstruction becomes a little problematic and where we can actually see a difference. I’m going to compare him in this one respect with Lacan, but I want to hasten to point out, as I will in a minute, a divergence from Lacan as well. You remember that in Lacan’s “Agency of the Letter” essay, he doesn’t just talk about the axis of combination as a series of concentric circles, each one of which is made up of little concentric circles. He doesn’t just talk about that. He also talks about the way in which the combinatory powers of the imaginary in language, or desire in language, take place is like a musical staff, so that the organization of signs, in their contiguity with each other, can be either melodic or harmonic; but in any case, you can’t just think of the axis of combination as a complete linearity. It has dimensionality of different kinds.

这就是德勒兹和加塔利引入“高原”概念的原因。你摘录的那本书名为《千高原》。最终，“高原”的概念对他们来说甚至比“根茎”的概念更为重要，但当他们引入“高原”的概念时，他们所做的其实是完全相同的。他们是在说：“我们从一个符号群跳到另一个符号群，并非所有的符号群都是线性且统一的。”这或许就是它与解构主义的区别所在。德勒兹和加塔利感兴趣的是他们所谓的“编码的多样性”。他们感兴趣的是，当我思考时，我并非仅仅用语言思考，并非仅仅用图像思考，也并非仅仅用音乐思考，而是在各种编码之间跳跃，从而使实际的思维过程呈现出这种折衷主义的特征。

That’s why Deleuze and Guattari introduce the concept of plateau. The book in which your excerpt appears is called A Thousand Plateaus. Ultimately, the concept of plateau is even more important to them than the concept of rhizome, but when they introduce the concept of plateau they’re doing exactly the same thing. They are saying, “We jump from sign cluster to sign cluster and not all sign clusters are linear and uniform.” This is where there is perhaps a difference from deconstruction. Deleuze and Guattari are interested in “multiplicity of coding,” as they put it. They’re interested in the way in which when I think, I’m not just thinking in language, I’m not just thinking pictorially, and I’m not just thinking musically, but I am leaping around among codes so that the actual thought process is eclectic in this way.

可以说，拉康其实也预见到了这一点。你还记得在拉康的《能动性》一文中，他提醒我们——他自认为是弗洛伊德的真正继承者——弗洛伊德在《梦的解析》开篇就说过，梦的解码就像解谜谜语——谜语是一种文字游戏，它并非完全由词语构成，而是由一些特殊的音节或图像组成，例如，“我‘爱’纽约”。“我‘爱’纽约”就是一个谜语。在弗洛伊德看来，梦的运作始终如同一个谜语。因此，可以说拉康已经为德勒兹引入了一种可能性：存在一种多重编码，需要从多个层面进行解码，才能使其有意义。

Now you could say that this is something actually anticipated also by Lacan. You remember also in the “Agency” essay that Lacan reminds us, true inheritor of Freud which he takes himself to be, that at the beginning of The Interpretation of Dreams, Freud said that the decoding of the dream work is like figuring out the puzzle of a rebus–a rebus being one of those trick sentences which are made up not exclusively of words but of the odd syllable or of pictures: for example, “I ‘heart’ New York.” “I ‘heart’ New York” is a rebus. The dream work functions constantly, in Freud’s view, as a rebus. So you could say that Lacan already introduces for Deleuze the possibility of thinking of a multiple coding that needs to be decoded on a variety of plateaus if it’s going to make any sense.

德勒兹与我们一直在阅读的所有人物之间的关系确实相当复杂。他的前作《千高原》名为《反俄狄浦斯》，书中对弗洛伊德——他总是称弗洛伊德为“将军”——这一观点进行了持续而系统的批判，即弗洛伊德认为我们整个精神生活完全被俄狄浦斯情结所浸透和支配。德勒兹运用他去中心化的思维方式，即根茎理论，试图从多个角度揭示这种对特定问题的关注最终会造成多么大的局限，以及对精神分析遗产的损害——这是德勒兹对弗洛伊德的批判，并非我的。你可能会认为，仅凭我刚才描述的原因，德勒兹就应该与拉康更为接近。然而，拉康也曾说过——在你那本复印中心的读本第34页最底部，右侧栏——“……精神分析的命运与语言学的命运紧密相连，这并不令人惊讶……”现在，我们无法确定——我认为这是有意为之——德勒兹说这句话时指的是弗洛伊德还是拉康，因为是拉康声称弗洛伊德说过这句话：换句话说，《梦的解析》是我们发现无意识的结构如同语言的文本；但与此同时，后世却将拉康对语言学的关注视为对弗洛伊德的一次大规模的、或许并不恰当的修正，认为这是截然不同的事情。因此，有趣的是，德勒兹似乎相当含糊地认为弗洛伊德和拉康密不可分。他之所以能做到这一点，是因为他感兴趣的是一种语言思考方式，而就他而言，没有任何语言学能够成功地容纳这种方式。换句话说，他一直在谈论乔姆斯基。在某种程度上，乔姆斯基似乎是你文章中的反派。但我认为，这在某种程度上只是回避谈论索绪尔的一种方式，因为你不想得罪那些结构主义者；因为索绪尔的问题也在于，他的思想中存在某种专制或类似树木般的倾向，即专注于二元对立——也就是说，将能指和所指之间的关系视为固定不变的、僵化的，缺乏德里达所谓的“自由发挥”，因此，也存在某种专制。

Now Deleuze’s relationship with all the figures we have been reading is rather problematic, really. The book precedingA Thousand Plateaus was called Anti-Oedipus, and it is a continuous systematic attack on–he always calls Freud “the General”–the idea that Freud feels that the whole of our psychic lives is completely saturated and dominated by the Oedipus complex. Deleuze with his idea of de-centered thinking, of the rhizome, sets out to show in a variety of ways how limiting and how unfortunate for the legacy of psychoanalysis this kind of focus on a particular issue turns out to be–this is Deleuze’s critique of Freud, not mine. You would think that Deleuze, then, would be a lot closer to Lacan just for the reasons that I have just described, but Lacan, too–at the very bottom of page 034 in your copy center reader, on the right-hand column–he says: “…[I]t is not surprising that psychoanalysis tied its fate to that of linguistics…” Now it’s impossible to say– I think quite by design–it’s impossible to say whether Deleuze is referring to Freud or Lacan in saying that, because it’s Lacan who claims that Freud said it: in other words, that The Interpretation of Dreams is the text in which we discover that the unconscious is structured like a language; but at the same time, posterity has taken Lacan’s focus on linguistics to be a massive, perhaps inappropriate revision of Freud and to be a very different matter. So it’s interesting that Deleuze quite ambiguously seems to suppose that Freud and Lacan are part and parcel of each other. The reason he can do that is that he is interested in a form of thinking about language which no linguistics has successfully accommodated, as far as he’s concerned. In other words, he keeps talking about Chomsky. Chomsky seems to be, in a way, the villain of your essay. But I think, in a way, that’s just a way of evading talking about Saussure, because you wouldn’t want to get in trouble with all those structuralists; because the problem with Saussure, too, is that there is a certain tyranny or arboresque tendency in Saussurean thinking to be focused on the binary–that is, the relationship between the signified and signifier as fixed, as inflexible, and as lacking in what Derrida would call “free play” and therefore, too ,a kind of tyranny.

第六章 根茎

Chapter 6. The Rhizome

那么，我们快速地谈谈根茎。我们如何识别根茎呢？无论德勒兹的文章给你带来多少困惑，我想从长远来看，你大概会对根茎的概念有相当清晰的认识。但如果还有任何疑虑，不妨想想流感。德勒兹称之为“根茎型流感”。这种流感是从其他人那里传染的，是疾病的传播。就像我们在期中考试前后都感染流感一样，这种疾病的传播就是根茎型的。这完美地诠释了——再举一个德勒兹的例子——黄蜂和兰花之间的关系。黄蜂就像病毒一样，在花朵间飞来飞去，然后传播开来，最终引发流感。与之相对的是遗传性疾病——也就是说，这种疾病潜伏在我们体内，因为我们天生就容易患上它，它根植于我们的基因之中。德勒兹将这种现象与树状结构联系起来。它源于起源。它是我们内在的因果关系，或是我们背后的原因，而非凭空出现、任意且不可预测地降临于我们身上的东西——或许这与廷亚诺夫对“变化”和“进化”的区分也有几分相似。树状结构是进化的；根茎则是变化。实体间张力的相互作用——老鼠互相翻滚、洞穴迷宫、马唐草蔓延——所有这些都带有某种随机性和不可预测性。根茎蕴含着在所有可想象的点上都存在的连接力量，而这种力量却没有任何可预测性。

So, very quickly, on the rhizome. How do we know a rhizome when we see it? Whatever frustrations Deleuze’s essay puts in your path, I think probably in the long run you’re pretty clear on what a rhizome is, but if there is any lingering doubt just think about the flu. There is what Deleuze calls “rhizomatic flu.” That’s something we get from other people, the circulation of disease. As we all come down with it around midterm period, the circulation of disease is rhizomatic. It’s a perfect example of–to use another instance from Deleuze–the relationship between the wasp and the orchid. The wasp, like the virus, sort of flits about from blossom to blossom, descends, and then constitutes the flu. By contrast there is hereditary disease–that is, that which is lurking in us because we’re programmed for it, we’re hard-wired for it, and it is genetically in our nature. This Deleuze associates with the arboresque. It comes from an origin. It is something that is a cause within us or a cause standing behind us, as opposed to something coming out of left field in an arbitrary and unpredictable fashion and descending on us–perhaps this is also not unlike Tynjanov’s distinction between modification and evolution. The arboresque evolves; the rhizomatic is modification. The give and take of tensions among entities–the rats tumbling over each other, the maze of the burrow, the spreading of crabgrass–all of this has a kind of randomness and unpredictability. The power of linkage at all conceivable points without any predictability–all of this is entailed in the rhizomatic.

至于究竟是什么受到了攻击——再次强调，围绕这些事物的价值体系并非绝对，德勒兹并没有断言“树状结构是坏的，根茎状结构是好的”。他的观点已经非常接近了，但他承认，正如我所说，根茎状结构存在风险——不过，在此我顺便提一点——因为我没时间谈论齐泽克了——关于树状结构，我只想顺便提一点。实际上，在你的文章开头几页，就出现了两种树状结构。一种是他所谓的“根书”，即传统的经典著作，它向读者呈现一个主题：“我将要写某某，而且我会系统地、分章节地写，每次只写一件事。”这就是根书。另一种是他所谓的“束书”，这种书由复杂的分支根系构成，但仍然包含着一个主根。这正是他在你的文章中将之与现代主义联系起来的。他实际上是说：“分册书就像乔伊斯的《尤利西斯》。它包罗万象，应有尽有。它看起来完全是根茎状的，但实际上，它是由一个单一的、聚焦的作者意识所控制、统一和连贯的，因此它并非真正意义上的根茎状；它是一本分册书。”而现在，《千高原》将会是一本根茎状的书。所以，在这个概念中，你不仅有两种类型的书，而是三种。

Now as to what’s being attacked–and again, the value system surrounding these things is not absolute, Deleuze is not going so far as to say “arboresque bad, rhizomatic good.” He’s coming pretty close to it, but he acknowledges the perils, as I say, of the rhizomatic–but in the meantime just one point in passing–because I’m running out of time to talk about Žižek–just one point in passing about the arboresque. There are actually, in the first pages of your essay, two forms of it. One is what he calls the “root book,” the traditional classical book which presents to you a theme: “I am going to write about so-and-so, and I’m going to do so systematically, one thing at a time in a series of chapters.” That’s the root book.
