保罗·弗莱教授：今天我们要探讨一种文学批评方法，它从七十年代末到八十年代风靡一时，被称为新历史主义。它的定义方式我稍后会谈到，而且正如我所说，它在世界各地都非常普遍。它很可能起源于加州大学伯克利分校，部分原因是斯蒂芬·格林布拉特的推动，你们今天读到的正是他的一篇短文。格林布拉特等人创办了一份期刊，至今仍是文学研究领域最重要、最具影响力的期刊之一，名为《表象》（Representations），它一直是新历史主义思想的传播平台。这场运动最初主要关注早期现代时期，也就是所谓的“文艺复兴”时期。实际上，正是新历史主义用“早期现代”一词取代了“文艺复兴”一词。

Professor Paul Fry: So today we turn to a mode of doing literary criticism which was extraordinarily widespread beginning in the late seventies and into the eighties, called the New Historicism. It was definable in ways that I’ll turn to in a minute and, as I say, prevalent to a remarkable degree everywhere. It began probably at the University of California at Berkeley under the auspices, in part, of Stephen Greenblatt, whose brief essay you’ve read for today. Greenblatt and others founded a journal, still one of the most important and influential journals in the field of literary study, calledRepresentations–always has been and still is an organ for New Historicist thought. It’s a movement which began primarily preoccupied with the Early Modern period, the so-called “Renaissance.” The New Historicism is, in effect, responsible for the replacement of the term “Renaissance” with the term “Early Modern.”

然而，它的影响很快就扩展到了其他领域，有些领域受到的影响可能更大。我认为，或许值得专门讲一堂课来解释为什么某些领域似乎比其他领域更容易接受新历史主义的研究方法（但我并不打算这样做）。我认为可以公平地说，除了早期现代时期之外，受新历史主义影响最大的三个领域是十八世纪、英国浪漫主义以及从殖民时代晚期到共和时期的美国研究。那个时代——印刷文化的兴起、公共领域作为影响媒介的出现以及知识在美国的传播——已经从新历史主义的视角得到了非常富有成效的研究。因此，这些领域是受这种方法影响最直接的。当我们讨论杰罗姆·麦克甘的文章时，你就会明白它是如何影响浪漫主义研究的。

Its influence, however, quickly did extend to other fields, some fields perhaps more than others. It would be, I think, probably worth a lecture that I’m not going to give to explain why certain fields somehow or another seem to lend themselves more readily to New Historicist approaches than others. I think it’s fair to say that in addition to the early modern period, the three fields that have been most influenced by the New Historicism are the eighteenth century, British Romanticism, and Americanist studies from the late colonial through the republican period. That age–the emergence of print culture, the emergence of the public sphere as a medium of influence, and the distribution of knowledge in the United States–has been very fruitfully studied from New Historicist points of view. So those are the fields that are most directly influenced by this approach. When we discuss Jerome McGann’s essay, you’ll see how it influences Romantic studies.

新历史主义——这或许可以解释其在七十年代末至九十年代初这段时期内为何如此盛行并产生如此巨大的影响——是对某些文学研究中所谓孤立文本的做法日益加剧的伦理失范的回应。从新批评到解构主义时期，再到拉康等人在精神分析领域的深奥论述，学者们，尤其是年轻学者，普遍感到，在某种程度上，尤其是在面对诸多紧迫问题——后越战时代、全球化问题、权力分配和全球资本问题——时，所有这些问题都引发了学术文学研究中一种可称之为“负罪感”的情绪，并导致了“回归历史”的趋势。人们感到，某种伦理转折点已经到来，那些曾经盛行的分析模式需要被一种新的分析模式所取代，在这种新模式中，历史以及研究的政治意义变得尤为突出和核心。

Now the New Historicism was–and this probably accounts for its remarkable popularity and influence in the period roughly from the late seventies through the early nineties–was a response to an increasing sense of ethical failure in the isolation of the text as it was allegedly practiced in certain forms of literary study. Beginning with the New Criticism through the period of deconstruction, and the recondite discourse of Lacan and others in psychoanalysis, there was a feeling widespread among scholars, especially younger scholars, that somehow or another, especially in response to pressing concerns–post-Vietnam, concerns with globalization, concerns with the distribution of power and global capital–all of these concerns inspired what one can only call a guilt complex in academic literary scholarship and led to a “return to history.” It was felt that a kind of ethical tipping point had been arrived at and that the modes of analysis that had been flourishing needed to be superseded by modes of analysis in which history and the political implications of what one was doing became prominent and central.

我必须指出，这类辩论中总是充斥着大量的空谈，或许双方都有。在很多方面，所谓孤立的研究方法并非真正孤立。例如，第二代解构主义者始终关注历史，并致力于将解构技巧应用于对历史的理解。另一方面，新历史主义则表现出对形式和文本完整性问题的关注，这无疑源于其之前的学科和研究方法。此外，在很大程度上——当然，我们即将探讨的许多其他研究方法，包括那些同样基于身份认同问题的研究方法，也存在这种情况——新历史主义在很大程度上挪用了解构主义者一代的语言，并在一定程度上借鉴了某些与自我与他者之间的二元关系以及社会实体（而非语言实体）之间的二元关系相关的结构主义思想；但正如我所说，它们本质上仍然继承了先前研究方法的思维结构。所以，正如我所说，新历史主义正是在一种争论不休的氛围中，在学术文学界普遍自我怀疑的时刻应运而生——正如我所说，它是对某些技巧和方法将文本孤立起来的一种回应。

I have to say that in debates of this kind there’s always a considerable amount of hot air, perhaps on both sides. In many ways it’s not the case that the so-called isolated approaches really were isolated. Deconstruction in its second generation wrote perpetually about history and undertook to orient the techniques of deconstruction to an understanding of history, just to give one example. The New Historicism, on the other hand, evinced a preoccupation with issues of form and textual integrity that certainly followed from the disciplines, the approaches, that preceded them. Also to a large degree–and this is, of course, true of a good many other approaches that we’re about to investigate, approaches based in questions of identity also–to a large degree, appropriated the language of the generation of the deconstructionists and, to a certain extent, certain underlying structuralist ideas having to do with the binary relationship between self and other, and binary relationships among social entities, as opposed to linguistic entities; but still, as I say, essentially inheriting the structure of thought of preceding approaches. So, as I say, it was in a polemical atmosphere and at a moment of widespread self-doubt in the academic literary profession that the New Historicism came into its own–a response, as I say, to the isolation of the text by certain techniques and approaches to it.

第二章 新历史主义方法与福柯

Chapter 2. The New Historicist Method and Foucault

现在快速概括一下：新历史主义的分析方法形成了一种模式，一种非常引人入胜的模式，格林布拉特的那篇简短引言就很好地体现了这一点，我请各位阅读了那篇引言：这种模式以轶事开篇，这些轶事往往与最终在文章论证中涉及的文学问题看似毫不相干。例如：一个满身尘土的磨坊主漫无目的地走在路上，突然遇到一个法警，然后一些法律问题浮出水面，不知不觉中，我们就开始讨论《李尔王》了。这种巧妙而迂回地切入文学主题的方式，尤其要归功于格林布拉特、路易斯·蒙特罗斯以及他的一些同事们的精湛技艺。这种技巧后来成为新历史主义的标志性特征之一。

Now very quickly: the method of New Historical analysis fell into a pattern, a very engaging one, one that’s wonderfully exemplified by the brief introduction of Greenblatt that I have asked you to read: a pattern of beginning with an anecdote, often rather far afield, at least apparently rather far afield, from the literary issues that are eventually turned to in the argument of a given essay. For example: a dusty miller was walking down the road, thinking about nothing in particular, when he encountered a bailiff, then certain legal issues arise, and somehow or another the next thing you know we’re talking about King Lear. This rather marvelous, oblique way into literary topics was owing to the brilliance in handling it of Greenblatt, in particular, and Louis Montrose and some of his colleagues. This technique became a kind of a hallmark of the New Historicism.

当然，从长远来看，戏仿它并非难​​事。它早已饱受戏仿之苦，某种程度上，戏仿的盛行也使其有所修正和反思；但即便如此，我认为，它仍然揭示了新历史主义思维的运作方式。新历史主义深受福柯的影响——而福柯正是新历史主义的主要思想来源。今天我不会过多赘述这一点，除非我很快会在性别研究的语境下再次探讨福柯，届时我们将共同探讨福柯和朱迪斯·巴特勒的思想——但我还是要简要指出，福柯的著作，尤其是他后期的著作，探讨的是他所谓的“权力”的普遍性和在社会秩序中的流通。权力并非仅仅是——或者说，在福柯的许多论述中，甚至并非主要指——既得利益者的权力、暴力的权力或自上而下的暴政权力。在福柯看来，权力——尽管它可以是那些东西，而且常常确实是——更普遍、更隐蔽地体现为知识在文化中流通的方式：也就是说，我们思考的内容，我们认为合适的思考方式——被社会网络或社会系统中那些大多不可见的力量——是如何传播的。换句话说，在福柯看来，权力在某种意义上就是知识，或者更确切地说，它解释了某些知识形式是如何产生的——顺便一提，这里所说的知识并不一定是指真理。某些知识形式在特定的场所中产生。

In the long run, of course, it was easy enough to parody it. It has been subjected to parody and, in a certain sense, has been modified and chastened by the prevalence of parody; but it nevertheless, I think, shows you something about the way New Historicist thinking works. The New Historicism is interested, following Foucault–and Foucault is the primary influence on the New Historicism. I won’t say as much about this today as I might feel obliged to say if I weren’t soon be going to return to Foucault in the context of gender studies, when we take up Foucault and Judith Butler together–but I will say briefly that Foucault’s writing, especially his later writing, is about the pervasiveness, the circulation through social orders, of what he calls “power.” Now power is not just–or, in many cases in Foucault, not even primarily– the power of vested authorities, the power of violence, or the power of tyranny from above. Power in Foucault–though it can be those things and frequently is–is much more pervasively and also insidiously the way in which knowledge circulates in a culture: that is to say, the way in which what we think, what we think that it is appropriate to think–acceptable thinking–is distributed by largely unseen forces in a social network or a social system. Power, in other words, in Foucault is in a certain sense knowledge, or to put it another way, it is the explanation of how certain forms of knowledge come to exist–knowledge, by the way, not necessarily of something that’s true. Certain forms of knowledge come to exist in certain places.

因此，所有这些都是福柯著作的核心，并被新历史主义者继承；这就是他们对这些轶事感兴趣的原因。尽可能从你最终要讨论的内容之外出发，而你最终要讨论的内容很可能是莎士比亚作品中的某个文本或主题问题，或者伊丽莎白时代的假面剧，或其他任何情况。尽可能从这个主题之外出发，正是为了展现某种思维方式的普遍性，某种社会约束或对自由的限制的普遍性。如果你能展现出这种普遍性，你就能强化并论证福柯的观点，即权力正如我所说，是一种潜移默化且无处不在的知识传播方式。所有这些都隐含在新历史主义者的研究方法中，有时甚至是明确地体现出来。

So all of this is central to the work of Foucault and is carried over by the New Historicists; hence the interest for them of the anecdotes. Start as far afield as you can imaginably start from what you will finally be talking about, which is probably some textual or thematic issue in Shakespeare or in the Elizabethan masque or whatever the case may be. Start as far afield as you possibly can from that, precisely in order to show the pervasiveness of a certain kind of thinking, the pervasiveness of a certain social constraint or limitation on freedom. If you can show how pervasive it is, you reinforce and justify the Foucauldian idea that power is, as I’ve said, an insidious and ubiquitous mode of circulating knowledge. All of this is implicit, sometimes explicit, in New Historicist approaches to what they do.

第三章 历史与话语的相互关系

Chapter 3. The Reciprocal Relationship Between History and Discourse

正如我所说，福柯是至关重要的先驱。当然，当涉及到福柯时，我们所理解的文学——或许是泛指的，或许是作为一种特殊的言语形式而非其他形式的——往往会回归到更广泛、更普遍的话语概念，因为权力正是通过话语来传播知识的。再次强调，尽管新历史主义试图让我们回归现实世界，但它仍然承认这种回归受制于语言。现实世界正是通过语言来塑造自身的。这就是为什么对于新历史主义者而言——稍后我会提到格林布拉特在我请大家阅读的那篇短文开头所讲述的精彩轶事——这就是为什么新历史主义者如此强调话语（如果你愿意，也可以称之为文学）与历史之间的关系是相互的。

So as I said, Foucault is the crucial antecedent and of course, when it’s a question of Foucault, literature as we want to conceive of it–perhaps generically or as a particular kind of utterance as opposed to other kinds–does tend to collapse back into the broader or more general notion of discourse, because it’s by means of discourse that power circulates knowledge. Once again, despite the fact that New Historicism wants to return us to the real world, it nevertheless acknowledges that that return is language bound. It is by means of language that the real world shapes itself. That’s why for the New Historicist–and by this means, I’ll turn in a moment to the marvelous anecdote with which Greenblatt begins the brief essay that I’ve asked you to read–that’s why the New Historicist lays such intense emphasis on the idea that the relationship between discourse–call it literature if you like, you might as well–and history is reciprocal.

是的，历史制约着文学在特定时代所能表达的内容。历史是理解特定时期某些话语价值的重要途径。换句话说，历史——正如旧历史主义的传统观点（我稍后会谈到这一点）——是话语或文学的背景。但与此同时，历史也具有一种能动性，或者说一种能力，可以在话语中反过来传递权力。不妨称之为“文学”：当伊丽莎白女王在埃塞克斯起义的威胁下得知莎士比亚的《理查二世》正在公共街道和私人住宅中上演时，她说道：“我就是理查二世，你们难道不知道吗？”换句话说，凡是有叛乱的地方，凡是有想要推翻她、拥立王位觊觎者埃塞克斯伯爵的人的地方，《理查二世》都在上演。这让伊丽莎白女王感到恐惧，因为她深知——她是一位戏剧爱好者——理查二世的故事讲述的是一位拥有诸多美德却也存在某种弱点的国王，这种弱点既体现在政治上，也体现在性情上——正是这种弱点让他常常坐在地上，讲述其他国王的悲惨遭遇。最终，他被博林布鲁克篡位，成为亨利四世，开启了英国王室的新篇章，也改变了王室的重心。伊丽莎白女王说：“他们上演这出戏，是想把我跟理查二世作比较，为废黜我做准备。谁知道他们还会对我做什么？”这确实令人担忧。

Yes, history conditions what literature can say in a given epoch. History is an important way of understanding the valency of certain kinds of utterance at certain times. In other words, history is–as it’s traditionally thought to be by the Old Historicism, and I’ll get to that in a minute–history is a background to discourse or literature. But by the same token there is an agency, that is to say a capacity, to circulate power in discourse in turn. Call it “literature”: “I am Richard II, know you not that?” says Queen Elizabeth when at the time of the threatened Essex Uprising she gets wind of the fact that Shakespeare’s Richard II is being performed, as she believes, in the public streets and in private houses. In other words, wherever there is sedition, wherever there are people who want to overthrow her and replace her with the Earl of Essex, the pretender to the throne, Richard II is being performed. Well, now this is terrifying to Queen Elizabeth because she knows–she’s a supporter of the theater–she knows that Richard II is about a king who has many virtues but a certain weakness, a political weakness and also a weakness of temperament–the kind of weakness that makes him sit upon the ground and tell sad tales about the death of kings, that kind of weakness, who is then usurped by Bolingbroke who became Henry IV, introducing a whole new dynasty and focus of the royal family in England. Queen Elizabeth says, “They’re staging this play because they’re trying to compare me with Richard II in preparation for deposing me, and who knows what else they might do to me?” This is a matter of great concern.

换句话说，文学——正如弗雷德里克·詹姆逊所说“历史会带来伤痛”——文学也会带来伤痛。[笑] 换句话说，文学具有话语权，它对历史的影响与历史对文学的影响同样深远：文学“存在于世”，戏剧——尤其是当它突破剧院的局限时，因为正如格林布拉特所论证的，剧院具有某种中介作用，可以化解煽动叛乱的可能性。人们或许会以某种客观的视角看待剧院中的文学作品，而当利益相关方为了煽动叛乱而改编并搬上舞台时，这种客观性就完全消失了。文学，尤其是当它突破了传统的束缚时，会成为一种非常非常危险或非常积极的影响，这取决于你对历史进程的看法。

In other words, literature–Fredric Jameson says “history hurts”–literature hurts, too. [laughs] Literature, in other words, has a discursive agency that affects history every bit as much as history affects literature: literature “out there,” and theater–especially if it escapes the confines of the playhouse because, as Greenblatt argues, the playhouse has a certain mediatory effect which defuses the possibilities of sedition. One views literary representation in the playhouse with a certain objectivity, perhaps, that is absent altogether when interested parties take up the same text and stage it precisely for the purpose of fomenting rebellion. Literature, especially when escaped from its conventional confines, becomes a very, very dangerous or positive influence, depending on your point of view on the course of history.

因此，历史与话语之间的关系是相互的。格林布拉特极力论证新历史主义与旧历史主义的区别，我认为他的论证非常有效。这一点在第1443页右侧栏有论述。约翰·多佛·威尔逊是一位传统的莎士比亚学者，也是一位非常重要的学者，在格林布拉特的论述中，他是旧历史主义的代表人物。我即将引用的观点正是约翰·多佛·威尔逊关于文学与历史关系的一种共识：

So the relationship between history and discourse is reciprocal. Greenblatt wants to argue with a tremendous amount of stress and, I think, effectiveness that the New Historicism differs from the Old Historicism. This is on page 1443 in the right-hand column. John Dover Wilson, a traditional Shakespeare scholar and a very important one, is the spokesperson in Greenblatt’s scenario for the Old Historicism. The view I’m about to quote is that of John Dover Wilson, a kind of consensus about the relationship between literature and history:

现代历史学（即旧历史主义）向伊丽莎白女王保证（笑），她（这是右侧栏大约三分之二的位置）（笑）完全不必担心：理查二世一点也不颠覆，反而是对都铎王朝秩序的颂歌。这部剧非但没有煽动叛乱，反而将废黜合法国王视为“亵渎神明”的行为，将国家拖入“混乱的深渊”；J·多佛·威尔逊宣称，“莎士比亚和他的观众都认为博林布鲁克是篡位者，这一点毋庸置疑。” 但在1601年，伊丽莎白女王和埃塞克斯伯爵都对此并不那么确信……格林布拉特胜出。这是一个绝妙的例子。格林布拉特的过人之处在于，他选择的例子如此具有启发性，又如此无可辩驳。我们知道伊丽莎白女王当时很害怕（笑），这足以证明约翰·多佛·威尔逊认为理查二世对她没有威胁的想法是错误的。重点在于，对理查二世的广义意识形态看法与威尔逊的说法并无二致；他的说法完全正确。博林布鲁克被认为是篡位者。理查二世被废黜被认为是悲剧；但这并不意味着文本不能被篡改、曲解和颠覆。

Modern historical scholarship [meaning Old Historicism] has assured Elizabeth [laughs] that she had [this is the right-hand column about two thirds of the way down] [laughs] nothing to worry about: Richard II is not at all subversive but rather a hymn to Tudor order. The play, far from encouraging thoughts of rebellion, regards the deposition of the legitimate king as a “sacrilegious” act that drags the country down into “the abyss of chaos”; “that Shakespeare and his audience regarded Bolingbroke as a usurper,” declares J. Dover Wilson, “is incontestable.” But in 1601 neither Queen Elizabeth nor the Earl of Essex were so sure… Greenblatt wins. It’s a wonderful example. It’s the genius of Greenblatt to choose examples that are so telling and so incontrovertible. We know Queen Elizabeth was scared [laughs] on this occasion, which makes it quite simply the case that John Dover Wilson was wrong to suppose that Richard II was no threat to her. It’s not at all the point that a broad, ideological view of Richard II was any different from what Wilson said; that was perfectly true. Bolingbroke wasconsidered a usurper. It was considered tragic that Richard II was deposed; but that doesn’t mean that the text can’t be taken over, commandeered and made subversive.

威尔逊不承认这一点，因为他认为历史与文学的关系仅仅是历史影响文学，而非这种影响可以相互影响。你看，这就是新历史主义试图以此来定义自身，并与旧历史主义划清界限的方式。如果在君主制的合法性、君权神授、英国国教认可的继承合法性等等方面存在政治或意识形态上的共识——当你思考这些历史剧时，所有这些都显得不合时宜——如果存在这种广泛的共识，那么按照旧历史主义的逻辑，这就是这部剧的意义所在。尽管很明显，你可以把剧中的情节完全颠覆这些价值观，而埃塞克斯派正是这样做的，他们在伊丽莎白女王怀疑的地方上演这部剧。

Wilson doesn’t acknowledge this because his view of the relationship between history and literature is only that history influences literature, not that the influence can be reciprocal. You see, that’s how it is that the New Historicism wants to define itself over and against the Old Historicism. If there is a political or ideological consensus about the legitimacy of monarchy, the divine right of kings, the legitimacy of succession under the sanction of the Church of England and all the rest of it–all of which is anachronistic when you’re thinking about these history plays–if there is this broad consensus, that’s it, that’s what the play means according to the Old Historicism, even though plainly you can take the plot of the play and completely invert those values, which is what the Essex faction does in staging it in those places where Queen Elizabeth suspects that it’s being staged.

第四章 历史学家与主观性

Chapter 4. The Historian and Subjectivity

好的。现在，旧历史主义和新历史主义的另一个区别——我认为这个区别很正确——格林布拉特认为，旧历史主义根本不考虑历史学家的主观性——我指的是第1444页，右侧栏大约三分之一处。“历史并非历史学家诠释的产物，”格林布拉特说，“历史就是历史本身。人们客观地看待它，仅此而已。”

Okay. Now another way in which the Old Historicism and the New Historicism differ–correctly, I think– according to Greenblatt is that in the Old Historicism there is no question–I’m looking at page 1444, the right-hand column about a third of the way down–of the role of the historian’s own subjectivity. “It is not thought,” says Greenblatt, “to be the product of the historian’s interpretation…” History is just what is. One views it objectively and that’s that.

现在请注意，我们又回到了伽达默尔的论述。请记住，伽达默尔曾对历史主义提出过这样的批判：历史主义——格林布拉特称之为“旧历史主义”——认为我们可以排除自身的历史视野，消除所有历史偏见，从而客观地理解过去本身。伽达默尔指出，事实并非如此。伽达默尔认为，诠释必然涉及不同视野的融合，即他者的视野和我作为诠释者的自身视野。我无法排除自身的主观性。

Now notice here that we’re back with Gadamer. Remember that this was Gadamer’s accusation of historicism, the belief of historicism–what Greenblatt calls the Old Historicism–that we can bracket out our own historical horizon and that we can eliminate all of our own historical prejudices in order to understand the past objectively in and for itself. This is not the case, said Gadamer, remember. Gadamer said that interpretation must necessarily involve the merger of horizons, the horizon of the other and my own horizon as an interpreter. I cannot bracket out my own subjectivity.

好的。如果真是这样，那么伽达默尔就预见到了格林布拉特的观点，即旧历史主义的幼稚之处在于它假定自己对所谈论的内容没有任何既得利益——也就是说，它假定自己希望历史以某种方式符合自身的先入之见，但却对此浑然不觉。约翰·多佛·威尔逊曾在1939年向德国一群学者发表过关于理查二世的言论，这个轶事——再次巧妙地融入了论战之中——确实颇为有趣。希特勒即将成为德国的博林布鲁克。约翰·多佛·威尔逊希望他的听众说：“嘿，等等。坚持既得利益。[笑]你们的民主制度虽然薄弱，但它毕竟是民主制度。别让它失控。”于是，他开始谈论德国政治，就像马已经从马厩里逃出来一样，以此来强化他对伊丽莎白时代英国政治的看法。

Okay. If that’s the case, then Gadamer anticipates Greenblatt in saying that the naïveté of the Old Historicism is its supposition that it has no vested interest in what it’s talking about–that is to say, its supposition that it wants history to accord in one way or another with its own preconceptions, but isn’t aware of it. The anecdote–again, wonderfully placed in the polemical argument–that after all, John Dover Wilson delivered himself of these opinions about Richard II before a group of scholars in Germany in 1939 is, after all, rather interesting. Hitler is about to be the Bolingbroke of Germany. John Dover Wilson wants his audience to say, “Hey, wait a minute. Stick with vested authority. [laughs] You have a weak democracy, but it is a democracy. Don’t let it get away from you.” And so he is speaking, the horse already having escaped from the barn, in this reassuring way about German politics as a means of sort of reinforcing his own view of the politics of Elizabethan England.

但格林布拉特认为，他对此几乎没有任何自觉意识。也就是说，他自身的利益（当然，在这种情况下理应如此）在于维护既得权威，而他的这种利益又反过来融入了他对伊丽莎白时代意识形态的理解，使其符合这一利益。换句话说，正如我们今天所说，他有一个隐藏的议程，但他对此却知之甚少。这与新历史主义者截然不同，后者在这方面追随伽达默尔，充分意识到主观投入如何影响人们对材料的选择、思考这些材料的方式，以及将这些材料赋予我们今天的生命力并使其清晰呈现的方法。换句话说，对格林布拉特而言，正如伽达默尔一样——这令E·D·赫希大为震惊——去探寻文本的意义而非文本的内容，是可以接受的。文本的意义在于它蕴含着某种特定的力量。这些权力类型在今天仍然引起我们的兴趣，仍然与我们自身所处的世界息息相关。新历史主义者以一种自觉的方式公开探讨了所有这些问题，而格林布拉特及其同事认为，这种自觉性在旧历史主义中是不存在的。

But this, Greenblatt supposes, is something about which he has very little self-consciousness. That is to say, his own interest, as of course it should be on this occasion, is in the preservation of vested authority, and his own interest then folds back into his understanding of Elizabethan ideology in such a way that it can conform to that interest. He has, in other words, as we say today, a hidden agenda and is very little aware of it, unlike the New Historicist who, following Gadamer in this respect, is fully cognizant of the subjective investment that leads to a choice of interest in materials, a way of thinking about those materials, and a means of bringing them to life for us today and into focus. In other words, it’s okay for Greenblatt, as it was for Gadamer–much to the horror of E. D. Hirsch–to find the significance of a text, as opposed to the meaning of a text. The significance of the text is that it has certain kinds of power invested in it. Those kinds of power are still of interest to us today, still of relevance to what’s going on in our own world. All of this is taken up openly as a matter of self-consciousness by the New Historicists in ways that, according to Greenblatt and his colleagues, were not available consciously in the older Historicism.

如今，新历史主义所看待的世界——说完这一点，我稍后会谈到麦克甘的观点——本质上是一个权力、权力网络和颠覆之间动态互动的过程：也就是说，即使在那些构建权力地位的权威文本内部，也存在着挑战这些权力网络的各种方式。例如，伊丽莎白时代的假面剧，以精妙绝伦的方式展现了宫廷与朝臣、访客和追随者之间的关系，它本身就是一种手段——因为它具有某种多声部的特点——在其结构中蕴含着颠覆的元素，正如关于这些事物的论点所言：宫廷仪式本身也是如此，早期现代英国每年一次的“一日女王”节也是如此，在这一天，人们称“恶作剧之王”，普通的权威被颠覆了一天。任何公民每年都有机会体验一次“一日女王”的滋味。这些都是为了淡化它们实际上带入人们视野和意识层面的东西——主要是颠覆权力结构和循环系统的存在，或许是不可避免的存在。

Now the world as the New Historicism sees it–and after I’ve said this, I’ll turn to McGann–is essentially a dynamic interplay of power, networks of power, and subversion: that is to say, modes of challenging those networks even within the authoritative texts that generate positions of power. The Elizabethan masque, for example, which stages the relation of court to courtier, to visitor, to hanger-on in wonderfully orchestrated ways, is a means–because it’s kind of poly-vocal–of containing within its structure elements of subversion, according to the argument that’s made about these things: the same with court ritual itself, the same with the happenstance that takes place once a year in early modern England, in which the Lord of Misrule is so denominated and ordinary authority is turned on its ear for one day. Queen for a day, as it were, is something that is available to any citizen once a year. These are all ways of defusing what they, in fact, bring into visibility and consciousness–mainly the existence, perhaps the inevitable existence, of subversion with respect to structures and circulatory systems of power. It’s t

第五章 杰罗姆·麦克甘和巴赫金

Chapter 5. Jerome McGann and Bakhtin

新历史主义，尤其是在研究早期现代时期的问题时，往往关注并专门研究权力与颠覆之间的关系。

his relationship between power and subversion that the New Historicism, especially in taking up issues of the Early Modern period, tends to focus on and to specialize in.

现在还不完全清楚杰罗姆·麦克甘是否真的认为自己是新历史主义者。虽然有人这样称呼他，但我认为至少在他与格林布拉特及其同事在早期现代时期的研究之间，存在一个相当重要的侧重点差异。麦克甘并不特别强调历史与话语的相互作用。他感兴趣的是历史的存在，即文本历史中直接的社会和个人环境的存在。他的主要关注点——至少在本文中——是文本研究。他本人是拜伦新标准作品集的编辑。他还编辑过斯温伯恩的标准作品集，并且在文本研究领域一些晦涩难懂的辩论中，他一直是一位直言不讳、观点鲜明的代言人：文本研究是否应该构建一个融合了各种现有手稿和印刷文本的文本；麦克甘在这篇文章中似乎持这种观点，即文本应当是作者最终且最精辟的构思，还是恰恰相反，应当是作者最初的灵感迸发。例如，所有偏爱华兹华斯《序曲》早期版本的人，都倾向于后一种观点。换言之，麦克甘在此做出的贡献，尤其体现在围绕编辑和权威学术文本制作的辩论中。

Now it’s not wholly clear that Jerome McGann has ever really thought of himself as a New Historicist. He has been so designated by others, but I think there is one rather important difference in emphasis, at least between what he’s doing and what Greenblatt and his colleagues do in the Early Modern period. McGann doesn’t really so much stress the reciprocity of history and discourse. He is interested in the presence of history, the presence of immediate social and also personal circumstances in the history of a text. His primary concern is with–at least in this essay–textual scholarship. He himself is the editor of the new standard works of Byron. He has also done a standard works of Swinburne, and he has been a vocal and colorful spokesperson of a certain point of view within the recondite debates of textual scholarship: whether textual scholarship ought to produce a text that’s an amalgam of a variety of available manuscripts and printed texts; whether the text it produces ought to be the last and best thoughts of the author–that’s the position that McGann seems to be taking in this essay–or whether the text, on the contrary, ought to be the first burst of inspiration of the author. All the people who prefer the earliest versions of Wordsworth’s Prelude, for example, would favor that last point of view. In other words, McGann is making a contribution here not least to the debates surrounding editing and the production of authoritative scholarly texts.

正是在这种背景下，我们才能理解他对济慈的评论。我认为，对麦克甘影响最大的并非福柯，而是巴赫金——他在第十八页和第十九页引用了巴赫金的观点；或者更确切地说，是他引用了巴赫金的影响。我认为，这种影响贯穿了他在第十八页末尾（复印中心读者手册中）的论述：

It’s in that context that the remarks he’s making about Keats have to be understood. I think the primary influence on McGann is not so much Foucault, then, with the sense of the circulation of power back and forth between history and literary discourse, as it is Bakhtin, whom he quotes on pages eighteen and nineteen; or whose influence he cites, I should say rather, in a way that, I think, does pervade what you encounter in reading what he then goes on to say at the bottom of page eighteen in the copy center reader:

麦克甘恩指出，接下来的内容是对所谓巴赫金批评学派提出的一些关键思想的总结和推论。巴赫金学派是由一小群来自苏联的马克思主义批评家组成，他们很早就对诗歌的形式主义方法进行了批判（正如麦克甘恩本人以及新历史主义者们所做的那样）。巴赫金学派的社会历史方法将所有语言表达——包括诗歌——都视为具有具体起源和历史特征的现象。也就是说，这些现象是由产生它们的物质环境所表达的；或者换句话说，浪漫主义孤独个体的声音实际上并非其本身，而是多种视角（包括意识形态视角）交织而成的多元语言，这些视角塑造了特定的表达，并且，就文本学者而言，也塑造了众多手稿中哪些将被选中出版，并在特定文本的接受传统中成为关注的焦点。所以麦克甘认为所有这些理论都源自巴赫金，而不是福柯。我认为这是两位作者之间的一个重要区别。

What follows [says McGann] is a summary and extrapolation of certain key ideas set forth by the so-called Bakhtin School of criticism, a small group of Marxist critics from the Soviet Union who made an early attack upon formalist approaches to poetry [just as he, McGann, is, and as the New Historicists are themselves, in their turn, doing]. The Bakhtin School’s socio-historical method approaches all language utterances–including poems–as phenomena marked with their concrete origins and history. That is to say, phenomena voiced by the material circumstances that produce them or phenomena, in other words, in which the voice of the Romantic solitary individual is not really that voice at all, but is rather the polyglossal infusion of a variety of perspectives, including ideological perspectives, shaping that particular utterance and also, in the case of the textual scholar, shaping which of a variety of manuscripts will be chosen for publication and for central attention in the tradition of the reception of a given text. So all of this McGann takes to be derived from Bakhtin rather than from Foucault. I do think that’s a significant difference between our two authors.

第六章 麦甘论济慈

Chapter 6. McGann on Keats

如今，麦克甘对七八十年代历史研究最重要的贡献是一本名为《浪漫主义意识形态》的小册子。这本书——嗯，说白了，就是对浪漫主义的批判。至少，它是对某些广为人知且被普遍接受的浪漫主义观念的批判——顺便说一句，我并不认同这些观念，但这门课不是在讨论我个人。 《浪漫主义意识形态》是由两个书名组合而成。其中一个是德国诗人、有时也算是浪漫主义者的海因里希·海涅早期对浪漫主义的重要批判著作《浪漫主义学派》（Die romantische Schule）。在这部著作中，浪漫主义诗人的主观性，甚至是唯我论，以及他们与社会关怀和历史进程的脱节，都得到了强调和批判。除此之外——这也是《浪漫主义意识形态》标题中“浪漫主义”一词的由来——它融合的另一个标题是马克思的著作《德意志意识形态》，该书涉及诸多方面，但尤其关注那些与黑格尔思想相符的流氓无产阶级知识分子——尽管他们自认为是进步的，但仍然追随黑格尔——他们与黑格尔一样认为思想创造物质条件，而不是相反：换句话说，简而言之，这些人是唯心主义者，因此，按照这种指责，他们也是浪漫主义者。

Now McGann’s most important contribution to the return to history of the seventies and eighties is a short book calledThe Romantic Ideology, and this book–well, what it is is an attack on Romanticism. At least it’s an attack on certain widely understood and received ideas about Romanticism–ideas with which, by the way, I don’t agree, but this course isn’t about me. The Romantic Ideology is an amalgam of two titles. One of them is the important early critique of Romanticism by the German poet and sometime Romantic Heinrich Heine called Die romantische Schule, or The Romantic School, in which the subjectivity, even solipsism, and the isolation from social concern and from unfolding historical processes of the Romantic poets is emphasized and criticized. In addition to that–that’s where the word “Romantic” comes from in the title The Romantic Ideology–the other title that it amalgamates is Marx’s book The German Ideology, which is about many things but is in particular about Lumpenproletariat intellectuals who think with Hegel– still following Hegel despite believing themselves to be progressive–who think with Hegel that thought produces material circumstances rather than the other way around: in other words people, in short, who are idealists and therefore, under this indictment, also Romantic.

正如我所说，麦克甘的书名巧妙地融合了另外两个书名，并为这本篇幅不长的书定下了基调。这本书不仅抨击浪漫主义，更抨击他认为我们仍然“身处”浪漫主义之中、仍然保持浪漫主义的倾向。他尤其抨击所谓的耶鲁学派，而你今天读到的文章中也对这一学派进行了批判。保罗·德曼和杰弗里·哈特曼关于济慈《致秋》的著名文章受到了特别的嘲讽和抨击，理由大致是：阅读浪漫主义、理解它、甚至为之着迷固然很好，但我们不能成为浪漫主义者。换句话说，如果我们想要成为社会性动物，积极参与政治，并融入社会共同体，那么我们对浪漫主义的解读必然是一种反浪漫主义的批判。正如我所说，这仍然是麦克甘所持的根本立场。

McGann’s title, as I say, cleverly amalgamates these two other titles and sets the agenda for this short book, which is an attack not just on Romanticism but on what he believes to be our continued tendency still to be “in” Romanticism, still to be Romantic. There his particular object of attack is the so-called Yale school, which is still under attack in the essay that you’ve read for today. Paul de Man and Geoffrey Hartman’s well-known essay on Keats’s “To Autumn” are singled out for particular scorn and dispraise, all sort of on the grounds that yes, it’s all very well to read Romanticism, to come to understand it, and even to be fascinated by it; but we can’t be Romantic. In other words, our reading of Romanticism–if we are to be social animals, politically engaged, and invested in the world as a social community–must necessarily be an anti-Romantic critique. This is, as I say, still essentially the position taken up by McGann.

好的。我已经解释了麦克甘与格林布拉特的不同之处，他更倾向于巴赫金而非福柯。我也解释了麦克甘在这篇文章中主要探讨的是文本研究问题，他捍卫了济慈最后的深思熟虑的选择，他认为1820年所谓的《无情的美人》“指示性”文本才是济慈最后的深思熟虑的选择，而不是蒙克顿·米尔恩斯于1848年出版的济慈诗集中的版本。

All right. So I’ve explained the ways in which he differs from Greenblatt in leaning more toward Bakhtin than toward Foucault. I have explained that McGann is engaged primarily in talking about issues of textual scholarship in this particular essay, that he defends Keats’s last deliberate choices, that he believes the so-called “indicator” text of 1820 of “La Belle Dame Sans Merci” is Keats’s last deliberate choice, as opposed to the 1848 text published by Monckton Milnes in the edition of Keats’s poems that he brought out at that time.

现在，我想在剩下的时间里，就麦克甘关于济慈的论述谈几点看法。我想强调的是，他关于文本历史性、关于文本如何受到其创作环境的影响、如何受到意识形态因素制约的总体论断，是无可辩驳的。在我看来，这至少是文学研究者应该考虑的必要方法，即便不一定非要强调这一点。认为文本只是从树上掉下来的想法——顺便说一句，如果有人真的有过这种想法的话[笑]——显然站不住脚，而相反的观点，即文本是从复杂的社会和历史环境的矩阵中产生的，则无疑是合理的。所以，如果要批评他，那也不是批评他的基本论断。在我看来，这些论断几乎无可指摘。问题在于，就麦克甘而言——他是一位杰出的浪漫主义研究学者，我想，人们很难不去反驳他的观点——他在这篇文章中对文本所做的所有解读，都完全错误，而且前后一致。他似乎出于某种本能，才会对这些文本做出错误的解读。我昨晚在邮件中请您抽空看一下这些文本，就是为了让我接下来要说的几点更有说服力。

Now I think that in the time remaining to sort of linger over McGann, I do want to say a few things about what he says about Keats. I want to emphasize that his general pronouncements about the historicity of texts, about the permeation of texts by the circumstances of their production, their conditioning by ideological factors, is unimpeachable. It seems to me that this is a necessary approach at least to have in mind if not, perhaps, necessarily to emphasize in one’s own work of literary scholarship. The idea that a text just falls from a tree–if anybody ever had that idea, by the way [laughs] –is plainly not a tenable one, and the opposite idea that a text emerges from a complex matrix of social and historical circumstances is certainly a good one. So if one is to criticize, again it’s not a question of criticizing his basic pronouncements. It seems to me nothing could be said really against them. The trouble is that in the case of McGann–who is a terrific, prominent Romantic scholar with whom one, I suppose, hesitates to disagree–everything he says about the text that he isolates for attention in this essay is simply, consistently, wrong. It’s almost as if by compulsion that he says things that are wrong about these texts, and the reason I asked you in my e-mail last night to take a look at them, if you get a chance, is so that these few remarks that I make now might have some substance.

以《无情的美人》为例。首先，谁说我们只能读1848年的版本？学术版本——他主要抨击的对象是杰克·斯蒂林格的济慈学术版本——基本上提供的是校勘本。没错，它可能用粗体字标出某个特定版本，但也会用脚注以较小的字体提供异文。它不会对你隐瞒异文。它会说：“不，你看，还有这个版本。你自己选择吧。” 校勘本学术版本的真正氛围是“任你选择”，而不是以某种专断的方式将特定版本强加于公众。每个人都知道1820年的指示文本。“你这可怜的家伙，究竟有什么难处？”至少对我这个浪漫主义者来说，和1848年版本开头的“你这身武士，究竟有什么难处？”一样熟悉。坦白说，除了浪漫主义学者之外，又有多少人了解这两部作品呢？我们到底在讨论什么？[笑声][大笑]

Take for example “La Belle Dame Sans Merci.” In the first place, who says we only read the 1848 text? A scholarly edition–and his main object of attack is Jack Stillinger’s scholarly edition of Keats–gives you basically a variorum apparatus. Yeah, maybe it gives you a particular text in bold print, but it gives you the variant text in smaller print in a footnote. It doesn’t withhold the variant text from you. It says, “No, look, there’s this too. Take your choice.” Really the atmosphere of a variorum scholarly edition is an atmosphere of take your choice, not a kind of tyrannical imposition on the public of a particular version of the text. Everybody knows the 1820 Indicator text. “What can ail thee, wretched wight?” is at least as familiar to me, as a Romanticist, as “What can ail thee, knight at arms?” the way in which the 1848 text begins; and frankly how many people who aren’t Romanticists know anything about either text? What are we talking about here? [laughter] [laughs]

浪漫主义者们心知肚明。他们丝毫不会被针对1820年版文本的历史阴谋所蒙蔽，而非浪漫主义者们也对此漠不关心。归根结底就是这样；但是，如果仅仅这样说还不够，那么就来探讨哪个版本更好——嗯，这很难说。麦克甘的论点是，1820年的版本更好，因为它讲述的是一对男女相遇的故事，接下来他们就发生了性关系，但结局并不美好。换句话说，它反映的是现实世界。这些事情确实会发生。它不是一部浪漫小说，而“你这可怜的骑士，究竟有什么事？”在1848年版——以及它的所有其他变体，例如“四吻”等等——中，麦克甘认为，1848年版是一种不加掩饰的浪漫小说，它秉持着某些中世纪关于女性的观念，一方面将女性奉为神明，另一方面又恐惧她们被某种黑魔法所笼罩，这种魔法会摧毁灵魂，耗尽那些值得拥有她们的年轻绅士的精力：麦克甘认为，所有这些都是1848年版中预设的意识形态。为什么呢？因为查尔斯·布朗对待女性的行为令人不齿，他不喜欢范妮·布朗，而且1848年版的实际编辑蒙克顿·米尔恩斯酷爱色情作品，并且是一位情色作品的收藏家。因此，与1820年版相比，1848年版因其对女性的恐惧和贬低而显得逊色。

The Romanticists know what’s going on. They’re not in any way hornswoggled by this historical conspiracy against the 1820 indicator text, and people who aren’t Romanticists don’t care. That’s what it comes down to; but, if it’s not enough simply to say that, turning to the question of which text is better–well, it’s hard to say which text is better. McGann’s argument is that the 1820 version is better because it’s a poem about a guy and a girl who sort of meet, and the next thing you know they’re having sex and that doesn’t turn out so well. In other words, it’s about the real world. These things happen. It’s not a romance, whereas the “What can ail thee, wretched knight?” in the 1848 version–and all of its other variants, the “kisses four” and so on–the 1848 version is a kind of unselfconscious–in McGann’s view–romance subscribing to certain medieval ideas about women, simultaneously putting them on a pedestal and fearing, at the same time, that they’re invested with a kind of black magic which destroys the souls and dissipates the sap of deserving young gentlemen: all of this is ideologically programmed, according to McGann, in the 1848 version. Why? Because Charles Brown behaved despicably toward women, he didn’t like Fanny Brawne, and because Monckton Milnes, the actual editor of the 1848 edition, loved pornography and was a big collector of erotica. So that’s why the 1848 text with its fear of and denigration of women, in contrast to the 1820 text, is inferior.

嗯，有两点：首先，谁又能断言1848年的文本不是济慈的遗作呢？换句话说，没错，1820年《指示者》文本出版时，他已经病重了。那时他清晰思考自己作品的能力已接近极限，也无暇顾及作品的出版形式。但与此同时，我们也不知道布朗何时收到了他的版本。我们不能像麦克甘暗示的那样，认为布朗只是坐下来重写了一遍。[笑] 从来没有人这么说过，如果他没有重写，那么济慈一定是把原稿交给他的。谁又能断言那不是他最后也是最好的想法呢？谁又能断言济慈并非真的想写这样一首诗呢？毕竟，标题取自阿兰·夏蒂埃的中世​​纪民谣《无情的美人》（La Belle Dame Sans Merci），印证了“骑士，你为何如此？”的版本。故事的主角是一位摩根勒菲式的人物。无论我们从意识形态上如何看待这种形象，如果标题准确的话，它所描绘的正是1848年版本中展现的那种女性形象，而非1820年版本中展现的那种女性形象。

Well, two things: first of all, who’s to say the 1848 text wasn’t Keats’s last thoughts? In other words, yes, he was already ill when the Indicator text was published in 1820. It is pretty close to the end of his ability to think clearly about his own work and to worry very much about the forms in which it was published, but at the same time we don’t know when Brown received his version of the text. We can’t suppose, as McGann more than half implies, that Brown just sort of sat down and rewrote it. [laughs] Nobody has ever really said that, and if he didn’t rewrite it, then Keats must have given it to him in that form. Who’s to say that wasn’t his last and best thoughts? Who’s to say Keats didn’t really want to write a poem of this kind? After all, the title, taken from a medieval ballad by Alain Chartier, “La Belle Dame Sans Merci,” bears out the “What can ail thee, knight at arms?” version. It’s about a Morgan Le Fay-type. For better or worse, whatever we think of that ideologically, it is about, if the title is right, the kind of woman who is evoked in the 1848 version, as opposed to the kind of woman who is evoked in the 1820 version.

所以，1848 年的版本与标题更为契合。这是其中一点，但另一点是，麦克甘利用新历史主义的观点——即个人的主观性和历史视野在思考这些问题时发挥着重要作用——从而得以将一种令人愉悦的政治正确性注入济慈的文本，进而也注入济慈的意图。也就是说，济慈不可能以那种贬低女性的方式思考。顺便说一句，我喜欢济慈，但他书信中的一切都表明他确实如此——回到麦克甘的论点：济慈不可能以那种贬低女性的方式思考。因此，1820 年的文本才是他真正想要表达和偏爱的文本。

So the 1848 version is simply more consistent with the title. That’s one point to be made, but the additional point to be made is that taking advantage of the New Historicist acknowledgement that one’s own subjectivity, one’s own historical horizon, is properly in play in thinking about these things, McGann is then able to infuse Keats’s text and therefore Keats’s intentions with a pleasing political correctness. That is to say, Keats can’t possibly have thought in that demeaning way about women. By the way, everything– I like Keats, but everything in his letters suggests that he did–but back to McGann: Keats can’t possibly have thought in that demeaning way about women. Therefore, the 1820 text is the text that he intended and preferred.

好的。当然，这让济慈的形象更符合我们自身的标准和对两性关系的看法，但换句话说，这是否符合我们所熟知的、尽管他有缺点和不足却依然深爱的济慈呢？换句话说，对于麦克甘关于文本问题的论断，有很多话要说，并非一定要为1848年版辩护，而是对这两个版本持一种不可知论的态度，认为“是的，我们最好两个版本都保留。最好把它们放在一起比较。最好一起阅读；但如果后来有人强行推崇1820年版而贬低1848年版，那将和历史上对1848年版或1820年版的偏爱一样，都是历史的遗憾。”我认为这才是我们应该采取的视角。

Okay. That, of course, makes Keats more consistent with our own standards and our own view of the relations between the sexes, but does it, in other words, make sense vis-à-vis the Keats whom we know and, despite his weaknesses and shortcomings, love? There is a great deal, in other words, to be said over against McGann’s assertions about this textual issue, not necessarily in defense of the 1848 text but agnostically with respect to the two of them, saying, “Yeah, we’d better have both of them. We’d better put them side-by-side. We’d better read them together; but if by some fiat the 1820 were somehow subsequently preferred to the 1848, that would be every bit as much of an historical misfortune as the preference, insofar as it has actually existed, of the 1848 or the 1820.” I think that’s the perspective one wants to take.

我本来想谈谈《致秋》。关于麦克甘对《致秋》的解读，我只想说，他似乎不太喜欢这首诗——他喜欢《无情的美人》，所以他把《致秋》解读得政治正确。他不喜欢《致秋》，是因为他认为这首诗是济慈的保守派朋友与济慈合谋，收录在1820年出版的《诗集》中的，而《诗集》删改了济慈所有进步的政治观点。换句话说，他认为《致秋》是对济慈思想的彻底背叛。他认为，1819年恰好是丰收之年，所以济慈把那一年的丰收变成了永恒，变成了一个虚幻的乐园，在那里，水果落入篮子，鱼儿跃入渔网，一切都完美无瑕。

Now I was going to talk about “To Autumn.” I’ll only say about his reading of “To Autumn” that McGann, who doesn’t seem to like the poem very much–he likes “La Belle Dame Sans Merci,” so he makes it politically correct. He doesn’t like “To Autumn” because he thinks that “Autumn” was published in collusion with Keats’s conservative friends in the Poemsof 1820, which bowdlerized everything he had to say of a progressive political nature. He thinks that “To Autumn” is a big sellout, in other words, and that yes, 1819 happened to be a year of good harvest, and so Keats turns that year of good harvest into something permanent, into a kind of cloud cuckoo-land in which the fruit falls into your basket and the fish jump into your net and everything is just perfect.

你觉得这首诗真的是那样吗？你读了第三节，麦克甘除了“春天的歌声在哪里？啊，它们在哪里？”之外，完全忽略了后面的内容。换句话说，他只给了你开头，却没有让你对后面的诗节有任何了解，因为对他来说，《致秋》的全部意义就在于第一节。在他看来，济慈似乎认同那些认为温暖的日子永不结束的蜜蜂，“因为夏天已经灌满了它们潮湿的蜂巢”。济慈就像一只蜜蜂，他完全沉浸于感官享受之中。

Well, do you think the poem is really like that? You’ve read the third stanza, which McGann totally ignores apart from “Where are the songs of Spring? Ay, where are they?” In other words, he gives you the opening but he doesn’t give you any sense of the rest of the stanza, because for him “To Autumn” is all about the first stanza. For him, Keats seems to identify with the bees who think warm days will never cease, “for Summer has o’er-brimmed their clammy cells.” Keats is like a bee. He’s all into the sensuous.

嗯，就历史证据而言，如果我们查阅济慈的信件，就会发现这种说法至少已经过时十八个月了。他早年的确如此，但他对某种观点深感不安，这在他早期的一封信中有所体现：“哦，我多么渴望一种感官而非思想的生活……”这已不再是济慈创作《致秋》时的立场。济慈创作《致秋》时的立场，是一个像他患有肺结核的哥哥一样喉咙疼痛的人，他越来越害怕自己即将离世，并试图通过写作来直面死亡——事实上，我特意强调“事实上”——这首诗是英语世界有史以来最完美的抒情诗，它绝非是对漫无目的的游荡的歌颂，并非认为秋天完美无瑕，认为秋天永远完美，认为温暖的日子永不消逝，认为花园里的一切都如此美好。它并非那种类型的诗，仅仅因为它在济慈的保守派朋友的建议下，于 1820 年出版的《诗集》中被当作向当权派出的作品而认为它是那种类型的诗，这真是对它的歪曲。

Well, again just in terms of historical evidence, this is outmoded by at least eighteen months if we consult Keats’s letters. He was like that early in his career, but he has had severe misgivings about a point of view which is represented in what he said in an early letter: “Oh, for a life of sensations rather than thoughts…” That’s no longer Keats’s position when writing “To Autumn.” Keats’s position when writing “To Autumn” is the position of a guy who has a sore throat just as his tubercular brother did, who is increasingly afraid that he’s going to die soon and is trying to confront mortality in writing what is in fact–and I say “in fact” advisedly–the most perfect lyric ever written in the English language, and which is most certainly not a celebration of sort of wandering around like an aimless bee, thinking that the autumn is perfect but that autumn is always perfect, that warm days will never cease, and that everything is just lovely in the garden. It is not that kind of poem, and it’s really a travesty of it to suppose that it is simply on the grounds that it was published in the Poemsof 1820 as a kind of sellout to the establishment under the advice of Keats’s conservative friends.

第七章 拖车托尼再度登场

Chapter 7. Tony the Tow Truck Revisited

好了。关于麦克甘对济慈的评论就说到这里。我想再次声明，这绝非质疑或否定他关于考虑历史背景的论点的普遍有效性。恰恰相反，我们需要考虑历史背景，而且必须准确把握。这当然是研究历史背景的挑战所在。你必须确保理解正确。

All right. So much then for McGann’s remarks on Keats, which I want to say again in no way impugn or undermine the general validity of the claims that he’s making about taking historical circumstances into account. Precisely, we need to take them into account and we need to get them right. That’s the challenge, of course, of working with historical circumstances. You have to get it right.

说到这里，我想快速地回顾一下从巴赫金到新历史主义对《拖车托尼》的解读。我可能会略过詹姆逊对《拖车托尼》的解读，因为我们在上一讲结尾已经讨论过了，所以还是回到巴赫金的论述吧。你可以看到，《拖车托尼》这首诗的结构中，第一部分完全充斥着第一人称单数：我做这个，我做那个，我喜欢我的工作，我被困住了——我，我，我，我。然后，随着你继续阅读，你会发现“我”消失了，或者即使它仍然存在，也出现在行中而不是行首。换句话说，“我”，这种主观性，这种第一人称单数，这种拥有独特声音的感觉——随着故事的展开，逐渐被社会性所吞噬。我不再是浪漫主义意义上的个体“我”。我，更确切地说，是朋友——也就是说，是一个与“他者”的关系构成其身份认同的人，在这种友谊的互惠关系中，第一人称单数消失了。换句话说，《拖车托尼》最终表达的并非个体主观性的声音，而是社会联结的声音，是“他者”的声音。

With that said, let me turn quickly to a review of Tony from Bakhtin to the New Historicism. I may glide over Tonyaccording to Jameson, because we did that at the end of the last lecture, so let me go back to Bakhtin. You can see the way in which in the structure of Tony the Tow Truck the first part of the poem is absolutely saturated with the first person singular: I do this, I do that, I like my job, I am stuck–I, I, I, I. Then as you read along through the text you see that the “I” disappears, or if it still appears, it’s in the middle of a line rather than at the beginning of a line. In other words, the “I,” the subjectivity, the first person singular, the sense of having a unique voice–this is gradually subsumed by the sociality of the story as it unfolds. I am no longer “I” defined as a Romantic individual. I am “I,” rather defined as a friend–that is to say, as a person whose relation with otherness is what constitutes his identity, and in that mutuality of friendship, the first person singular disappears. What is spoken in Tony the Tow Truck, in other words, in the long run is not the voice of individual subjectivity but the voice of social togetherness, the voice of otherness.

在雅斯看来，《拖车托尼》的关键在于它与《小火车头的故事》并非同一故事。换言之，每一代人的接受过程中，特定时期盛行的审美标准都会被重新审视、重新思考、重新组合。新的审美视野由此出现，文本的构成方式也随之改变，这与俄国形式主义者的观点颇为相似，只是在雅斯看来，这其中蕴含着历史的必然性。《小火车头的故事》讲述的是弱者与强者之间权力关系的颠倒，弱者帮助强者，这一点毋庸置疑，正如《圣经》中的以赛亚书所言，山谷被填平，高山被夷平。而《拖车托尼》则不然。弱者自身也需要帮助。他需要另一个弱者的帮助。小与大之间并非辩证的互惠关系，而是一点一点相互加强的关系，这就是《小火车头》和《拖车托尼》之间审美视野的变化。

According to Jauss, the important thing about Tony the Tow Truck is that it is not the same story as The Little Engine that Could. In other words, in each generation of reception, the aesthetic standards that prevail at a given time are reconsidered and rethought, reshuffled. A new aesthetic horizon emerges, and texts are constituted in a different way, much also as the Russian formalists have said, only with the sense in Jauss of the historical imperative. The Little Engine that Could is all about the inversion of power between the little guy and the big guy, so that the little guy helps the big guy and that is unequivocal, showing, as in Isaiah in the Bible, that the valleys have been raised and the mountains have been made low. That’s not the way Tony the Tow Truck works. The little guy himself needs help. He needs the help of another little guy. There is a reciprocity not dialectically between little and big, but a mutual reinforcement of little-by-little, and that is the change in aesthetic horizon that one can witness between The Little Engine that Could and Tony the Tow Truck.

正如我们之前所说，本雅明作品中最重要的是叙述者即机器这一概念。通过我们对机械世界的认同，我们得以赋予它人性，这正是《拖车托尼》的精髓所在。换句话说，所有这些汽车和卡车，所有这些或笑或皱眉的房子，它们的共同点当然是它们都缺乏人性，但对汽车、卡车和房子的拟人化赋予了它们人性。它们本身就是人。换句话说，我们是从机器的视角来看待事物的。正如电影观众是从摄影机的视角来看待事物一样，我们也是从拖车的视角来看待《拖车托尼》，对吧？那么接下来会发生什么呢？正如本雅明所说，摄像机的视角使所见之物“摆脱了设备”——同样地，如果我们从设备的角度看待事物，我们所看到的恰恰是故事的寓意：换句话说，是故事的人性。也就是说，在所有这些设备环绕下，我们看到的恰恰是现实中摆脱了设备的人性层面。因此，拖车托尼的运作方式与本雅明的机械复制理论相符。然而，在阿多诺看来，这个形象——机械复制的装置，一遍又一遍地拖拽——对阶级关系不平等的默许，恰恰证明了本雅明理论中认为独立于文化工业运作的装置，反过来又可以被文化工业收买和利用，为自身所用。

In Benjamin the important thing, as I think we’ve said, is the idea that the narrator is the apparatus. The humanization of a mechanized world, through our identification with it, is what takes place in Tony the Tow Truck. In other words, all these cars and trucks, all these smiling and frowning houses, of course, have as their common denominator their non-humanity, but the anthropomorphization of the cars and trucks and of the houses constitutes them as the human. They are precisely the human. We see things, in other words, from the point of view of the apparatus. Just as the filmgoer sees things from the point of view of the camera, so we see Tony the Tow Truck from the point of view of the tow truck, right? And what happens? Just as the camera eye point of view leaves that which is seen, as Benjamin puts it, “equipment-free”–so, oddly enough, if we see things from the standpoint of equipment, what we look at is the moral of the story: in other words, the humanity of the story. What we see, in other words, surrounded by all of this equipment, is precisely the equipment-free human aspect of reality. So Tony the Tow Truck works in a way that is consistent with Benjamin’s theory of mechanical reproduction. For Adorno, however, the acquiescence of this very figure–the apparatus of mechanical reproduction, of towing again and again and again–in the inequity of class relations, rejected as always by Neato and Speedy, proves that the apparatus which Benjamin’s theory takes to be independent of the machinations of the culture industry, that the apparatus in turn can be suborned and commandeered by the culture industry for its own purposes.

好吧。詹姆逊的观点我就略过不谈了。旧历史主义对托尼的解读只是重申了一种现状：美德清晰，恶行清晰，二者毋庸置疑，一切都一成不变——换句话说，这种现状反映了一种停滞不前、亘古不变的社会动态。新历史主义在很多方面也体现了这一点，但我想最后指出，如果文学能够影响历史，那么《拖车托尼》或许可以解释为什么我们今天如此推崇节能汽车，为什么对油老虎、SUV或小型货车（还记得那辆会说“我太忙了”的车吗？）的抨击在故事中如此普遍，以及为什么如果我们看看今天的头条新闻，就会发现通用汽车要想繁荣发展就必须淘汰悍马，并且需要缩小现有车型的尺寸并简化设计。托尼和邦比这两个小家伙重申了对节能小型车辆的必要性，由此可见，《拖车托尼》本身就是一种创造历史的话语。根据托尼的说法，这一切都正在发生。

All right. I will skip over Jameson. The Old Historicist reading of Tony simply reconfirms a status quo in which virtue is clear, vice is clear, both are uncontested, and nothing changes–in other words, a status quo which reflects a stagnant, existent, unchanging social dynamic. The New Historicism in a lot of ways is doing this, but let me just conclude by suggesting that if literature influences history, Tony the Tow Truck might well explain why today we’re promoting fuel-efficient cars, why the attack on the gas guzzler and the SUV or minivan–remember the car that says “I am too busy”–is so prevalent in the story, and why if we read today’s headlines we need to get rid of the Humvee if GM is to prosper, and we need to downsize and streamline the available models. The little guys, Tony and Bumpy, reaffirm the need for fuel-efficient smaller vehicles and you can plainly see that Tony the Tow Truck is therefore a discourse that produces history. All of this, according to the prescription of Tony, is actually happening.

好的，非常感谢。关于拖车托尼，有一点需要说明，那就是车里没有女性，而这正是我们周四要讨论的问题。

All right. Thank you very much. One thing that needs to be said about Tony the Tow Truck is it has no women in it, and that is the issue that we’ll be taking up on Thursday.

第20讲——古典女权主义传统

Lecture 20 - The Classical Feminist Tradition

第一章 向女权主义理论过渡：拖车托尼

Chapter 1. Transition into Feminist Theory: Tony the Tow Truck

保罗·弗莱教授：我认为，本次讲座以一系列预备内容开篇。在文学研究中，这类预备内容的专业术语是“预示”（prolepsis）——也就是说，它是一种预先设定的形式，在某种意义上涵盖了之后将要讨论的内容。这些就是这类预示。首先，我想说的是，在进入本课程的这一阶段，即探讨一系列特定身份作为视角和出发点时，我们仍然在思考文学文本；当然，在思考身份本身时，我们会遇到一种批评方法，这种方法在实践层面上极其丰富且富有成效。正如乔纳森·库勒曾经说过的那样，“以女性的视角阅读”，或者以非裔美国人的视角阅读，或者以我们即将讨论的任何其他身份进行阅读——如果运用得当，这种阅读方式能够彻底改变一切，其效果令人惊叹。也就是说，它具有巨大的实践价值。

Professor Paul Fry: This lecture, I think, starts with a series of preliminaries. The technical term for preliminaries of this kind in literary study is “prolepsis”–that is to say, the form of anticipation which, in a certain sense, covers what will be talked about later. They are prolepses of this kind. First, I wanted to say that in entering upon the phase of this course which concerns a series of particular identities as perspectives, as points of departure, we’re still thinking about the literary text; and, of course, in thinking about identity itself, we come upon a form of critical endeavor which is, in practical terms, incredibly rich and productive. It is simply amazing how, as Jonathan Culler once put it, “reading as a woman,” or reading as an African-American, or reading as any of the other sort of identity that we’re going to be talking about–it’s simply amazing how this kind of reading, if it’s done alertly, transforms everything. That is to say, it has an incredible practical payoff.

上次在新历史主义的语境下，斯蒂芬·格林布拉特（Stephen Greenblatt）精彩的轶事以伊丽莎白女王的一句“我是理查二世，你们难道不知道吗？”开篇。斯蒂芬·格林布拉特并非意在从女性主义批评的角度，或者从我们稍后将要探讨的性别理论的角度来审视这种说法；但即便如此，伊丽莎白女王说出这样的话仍然令人惊叹，不是吗？这实际上表明，她作为一名女性，竟然会发现自己身处一个特殊的位置，这本身就非同寻常：她无需承受传统上女性所承受的苦难和危险，反而有可能承受男性所面临的苦难和危险。更耐人寻味的是，伊丽莎白非常清楚，尽管她是理查二世的情况极为罕见，但这并非她独有的处境。她就曾让苏格兰女王玛丽（Mary Queen of Scots）也处于同样的境地。（笑）她最终废黜并斩首了她，正如她所担心的埃塞克斯伯爵会废黜并斩首她一样。因此，这句“我是理查二世，你难道不知道吗？”——从新历史主义的视角来看，它很容易被挪用和利用——但当我们把它视为一种性别经验时，它便会呈现出截然不同的意义，我认为这本身就非常引人入胜。

Last time in the context of the New Historicism, Stephen Greenblatt’s brilliant anecdote begins with Queen Elizabeth saying, “I am Richard II, know you not that?” Well, Stephen Greenblatt isn’t concerned with investigating a pronouncement of that sort from the standpoint of feminist criticism, or indeed from the standpoint of something we’ll be taking up later on–gender theory; but still, it’s rather an amazing thing for Queen Elizabeth to say, isn’t it? It suggests really that it’s, after all, remarkable that she, a woman, would find herself in a position not so much needing to endure the kind of suffering and peril that her own sex has traditionally endured but rather potentially enduring the suffering and peril that one would experience in the masculine gender position, made perhaps even more interesting and complicated by the fact that Elizabeth knows perfectly well that despite the rarity of her being Richard II, it’s nevertheless not a unique position. She has subjected [laughs] Mary Queen of Scots to precisely that position. She has deposed and beheaded her, ultimately, in just the way that she fears the Earl of Essex will depose and behead her. So the way in which this remark, “I am Richard II, know you not that?”–so easily commandeered and made use of from the standpoint of the New Historicism–can come to life in a completely different way when we think about it as a question of a gendered experience is, I think, in itself a fascinating one.

在上一节课的结尾，作为进一步的铺垫，我撒了个小谎。我说《拖车托尼》里没有女性角色，当然，在你那本你整个学期都紧紧抱着的文本里——也就是你读的那本——确实没有女性角色。里面只有几个男人在聊天。但是，如果你把这些插图——我之前跟你说过——添加到文本里，比如这幅（指着黑板）——大致来说，就是其中一幅，我是凭记忆画的——你就会明白，不仅仅是汽车。你看，那些房子脸上都带着微笑：不仅仅是汽车在邦比终于出现推托尼的时候感到高兴，背景里那些对尼托和斯皮迪的反应表示不满的房子也露出了笑容。插图中的那些房子脸上都带着愁容，而现在，当人们做道德上正确的事情时，这些房子却都露出了灿烂的笑容，表示赞许。

Now at the end of the last lecture, by way of further preliminary, I told a little fib. I said that there were no women in Tony the Tow Truck, and of course in your prose text of it–the one that you’ve been clutching to your bosom feverishly for the entire semester–there are no women. There are just guys talking. However, if to the prose text, and I’ve told you about these, you add the illustrations–this [gestures to board] is one of them, roughly speaking, and I did it from memory–if you add the illustrations, you’ll have to realize that it’s not just the cars. You see the little smiles on the faces of the houses there: it’s not just the cars that are happy about what’s going on when Bumpy finally comes along and pushes Tony, but it’s the houses in the background which have been expressing disapproval at the reactions of Neato and Speedy to the predicament. There are big frowns on the faces of those houses in those illustrations, houses that now express beaming approval when the morally correct thing is done.

维多利亚时代——从某种意义上说，我认为“拖车托尼”这个形象也与维多利亚时代有着某种联系——有一位名叫考文垂·帕特莫尔的诗人，他其实是一位相当优秀的诗人，却因为写了一首长诗而臭名昭著，诗中他将女性描述为“家中的天使”。你可能熟悉这个表达，而我认为，安·道格拉斯大约二十五年前出版的巨著《美国文化的女性化》也体现了这种观点。其核心思想是，道德、审美和文化价值在某种程度上掌握在客厅里、茶桌旁的女性手中，她们向社会机构——所有这些机构都严格属于男性特权——发号施令，决定着何为恰当的伦理观念。换句话说，“家中的天使”的角色不仅仅是洗碗和照顾孩子，尽管这确实是其重要组成部分。天使在屋子里的角色也在于评判家庭生活中的道德层面，而这些房子——显然住着天使——正是如此——它们时而微笑，时而皱眉。所以，托尼拖车里确实有女人。

Now in the Victorian period–and in a certain sense I think Tony the Tow Truck in this regard harkens back to the Victorian period–there was a poet named Coventry Patmore who, actually a rather good poet, became notorious, however, in the feminist tradition for having written a long poem in which he describes woman as “the angel in the house.” You’re probably familiar with that expression, and it’s an idea which is also, I think, embodied in a monumental book of some twenty-five years ago by Ann Douglas called The Feminization of American Culture. The idea is that moral and aesthetic and cultural values are somehow or another in the hands of women in the drawing room, at the tea table, dictating to the agencies of society–all of which are strictly male prerogatives–what a proper ethical sense of things ought to be. In other words, the role of the angel in the house is not just to wash the dishes and take care of the kids, although that’s a big part of it. The role of the angel in the house is also to adjudicate the moral aspect of life at the domestic level, and that’s exactly what these houses, obviously inhabited by angels–how else could they be smiling and frowning?–that’s what these houses are doing. So it is the case after all that there are women in Tony the Tow Truck.

第二章 重叠身份

Chapter 2. Overlapping Identities

好的。正如我所说，此刻并非我们课程的十字路口。这并非从语言转向心理再转向社会，因为显然我们仍然深陷于社会之中。事实上，我们并非从未接触过视角这一概念。显然，我们以各种方式接触过它，尤其是在巴赫金或詹姆逊的著作中，我们了解到阶级冲突——也就是说，属于某个阶级，因而拥有某种身份——是如何以对话的形式在文学作品中表达出来的，它既可以表现为阶级之间冲突的表达，也可以表现为一种更为嘈杂却又常常和谐的合唱，这种合唱在巴赫金的“狂欢化”等概念中有所体现。换言之，文本语言——无论是叙事语言、诗歌语言还是戏剧语言——的表达方式，正如我们所见，本身就是一个视角问题。也就是说，要理解文本语言，就必须结合身份认同的概念，在本例中指的是阶级身份认同的概念。

All right. Now, as I say, this moment is not exactly a crossroads in our syllabus. It’s not like moving from language to the psyche to the social, because obviously we’re still very much in the social. In fact, it’s not even as though we haven’t hitherto encountered the notion of perspective. Obviously, we have in all sorts of ways, but particularly in the work of Bakhtin or Jameson, we’re introduced to the way in which class conflict–that is to say, being of a certain class, therefore having an identity–gets itself expressed in literary form dialogically and gets itself expressed either as the expression of conflict between or among classes or as a more cacophonous and yet, at the same time, very frequently harmonious chorus of voices of the sort that–in notions of “carnivalization” and other such notions–one finds in Bakhtin. In other words, the way in which the language of a text, the language of a narrative or of a poem or of a play gets itself expressed, is already, as we have encountered it, a question of perspective. That is to say, it needs to be read with notions of identity, in this case notions of class identity, in mind if it’s to be understood.

不过，探讨身份认同问题还有一点很有意思，那就是，或许现在这种现象比以往任何时候都更加明显——尽管我一直在课程大纲中强调，在某些时刻，人们确实会走到十字路口，无法同时选择两条路——然而，在以文学理论的方式思考身份认同问题时，我们开始感受到不同视角之间日益激烈的竞争。在接下来的系列讲座中，我会不时地指出这一点，但从一开始就存在一种竞争，这种竞争在某种程度上至今仍未得到解决——例如，女权主义视角和马克思主义视角之间的竞争。也就是说：身份认同和意识的根本决定因素是什么？例如，是阶级还是性别？这并非一个新话题。这也不是我们今天才因为某种迟来的深刻理解而偶然发现的话题。请听弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫在《一间自己的房间》第600页左侧栏顶部的文字：

Well, what’s also interesting, though, about turning to questions of identity is that perhaps more sharply now than hitherto–although I have been at pains to point out certain moments in the syllabus in which one really does arrive at a crossroads, and you simply can’t take both paths–nevertheless, within the context of thinking about identity in these ways as literary theory, we begin to feel an increased competitiveness among perspectives. I’m going to be pointing this out from time to time in the sequence of lectures that we now undertake, but from the very beginning there is a sense of actually a competition which is in some ways unresolved to this day–for example, between the feminist and the Marxist perspective. That is to say: what is the underlying determination of identity and consciousness? Is it class or gender, just for example? This is not a new topic. This isn’t a topic that we stumble on today as a result of some belated sophistication we have achieved. Listen to Virginia Woolf on page 600 of A Room of One’s Own where she says, top of the left-hand column:

像莎士比亚那样的天才并非诞生于劳作的、未受教育的、卑微的人民之中。它并非诞生于英国的撒克逊人和不列颠人之中。它也不是诞生于当今的工人阶级之中。那么，这种天才又怎能诞生于那些女性之中呢？正如特里维廉教授所言，她们几乎在离开育婴室之前就开始工作，被父母强迫，并被法律和习俗的强大力量束缚。然而，某种天才必然存在于女性之中，正如它必然存在于工人阶级之中一样。某种程度上，伍尔夫在这里有所保留。如果我们想要理解女性受压迫的历史或女性表达形式受限的历史，她既没有说阶级优先于性别，也没有说性别优先于阶级。她有所保留，但与此同时，我认为我们仍然可以从伍尔夫的《自己的房间》中看到一个相当令人惊讶的观点。想想这个书名吧。想想伍尔夫后来一篇与此有些相似的文章的标题——《三枚金币》，这篇文章探讨了当代女性活动的可能性。这些标题都根植于物质条件。伍尔夫站在她的听众面前，她的牛津剑桥女学生听众面前，说她真正想说的只有一件事：如果你想在写作或其他任何真正独立于父权制限制的活动中有所作为，你每年必须有500英镑，并且拥有一间属于自己的房间。

For genius like Shakespeare’s is not born among labouring, uneducated, servile people. It was not born in England among the Saxons and the Britons. It is not born today among the working classes. How, then, could it have been born among women whose work began, according to Professor Trevelyan, almost before they were out of the nursery, who were forced to it by their parents and held to it by all the power of law and custom? Yet genius of a sort must have existed among women as it must have existed among the working classes. Now in a way, Woolf is pulling her punches here. She is not saying class has priority over gender, nor is she saying gender has priority over class, if we’re to understand the history of the oppression of women or the history of the limits on the forms of women’s expression. She’s pulling her punches, and yet at the same time I think we can see a point of view in Woolf’s Room of One’s Own which is, after all, rather surprising. Think of the title. Think of the later title of a tract in some ways similar about the possible scope for contemporary activity for women, Three Guineas. These titles are grounded in material circumstances. Woolf stands before her audience, her Oxbridge audience of women, and says all she really has to say is just this one thing: if you’re going to expect to get anything done in the way of writing or in the way of any other activity that’s genuinely independent of patriarchal limitation, you’ve really got to have 500 pounds a year and a room of your own.

这就是她真正想说的全部。事实上，当你通读《一间自己的房间》的六个章节时，你会发现，仿佛被一根橡皮筋牵引着，在每一章所展现的非凡的印象派思维之后，她最终还是回到了她认为必不可少的实践前提，一个物质前提。如果你想有所作为——你不是简·奥斯汀，你不是那种坐在客厅里，每次有仆人进屋就赶紧用吸墨纸盖住正在创作的小说的天才，你不是那种人——你现在真的需要拥有500英镑和一间属于自己的房间。换句话说，我认为即使在《一间自己的房间》——即便不是最伟大的，也绝对是迄今为止最雄辩的关于女性写作状况的女权主义论著——中，我们也能看出，阶级视角而非性别视角仍然占据着一定的优先地位。如果实际上不采取措施——让我们面对现实吧——重新分配金钱和权力，那么性别将继续受到金钱和权力的影响。顺便一提，《三枚金币》更清晰地展现了这种观点，并表明尽管该片的主要目的是女权主义，但其背后仍然隐藏着阶级优先的观念。

That’s all she really says she has to say. In fact, as you read through the six chapters of A Room of One’s Own, you find that, as if on an elastic band after the extraordinary range of impressionist thinking that each chapter manifests, she is pulled back to this one particular–as she sees it–necessary practical precondition, a material precondition. If you want to get anything done–you’re not Jane Austen, you’re not a genius sitting in your parlor whisking your novel-in-progress under a piece of blotting paper every time a servant comes in to the room, you’re not like that–you really do need today the independence of having 500 pounds and a room of your own. In other words, I think one could show that even in A Room of One’s Own–which is, if not the greatest, certainly the most eloquent feminist treatise on the conditions of women’s writing ever written–one could show that even in that, there is a certain priority given to the perspective of class, as opposed to the perspective of gender. Gender will continue to be conditioned by the effects of money and power if in fact something isn’t done–let’s face it–to redistribute money and power. This is a perspective which, by the way, is even clearer in Three Guineas and suggests that despite its main agenda, which is a feminist one–that underlying that there is a sense of the priority of class.

这类紧张关系不仅持续困扰着女权主义批评，也困扰着其他涉及身份认同的批评，直到今天依然如此。各种身份认同视角的会议往往会演变成围绕这一问题的辩论，而这类会议中那些“高人一等”的人总是能抢占先机，说：“你们都太天真了。你们以为这是根本问题，但其实还有一个更深层次的问题才是根本问题，而我要证明，这个问题必须占据绝对优势。” 在这种情况下，打出的牌不一定总是马克思主义，尽管它经常出现。也可能是其他什么牌，但总有人会打出这张牌。会议结束时，总是有人会说：“哦，我还以为这是关于女性的会议呢。哎呀，看来是别的什么。”我们之后还会再谈到这一点，因为从某种意义上说，我们今天讨论的材料以及我们能够讨论它的方式，本身就需要另一次讲座来阐述，而我们也确实会进行一次这样的讲座。正如我希望在讲座结束时阐明的那样，传统的——我称之为“古典女性主义批评”——需要补充，或许可以借鉴德里达的理论，补充一些其他的东西，那就是性别理论。正如我所说，在讲座结束时，我会尝试解释这可能意味着什么，然后在几节课后讨论朱迪斯·巴特勒和米歇尔·福柯时，我们会再次回到这个问题。

These sorts of tensions continue to haunt not just feminist criticism, but other forms of criticism having to do with other forms of identity really to this day. Conferences featuring a variety of identity perspectives very typically develop into debates on precisely this issue, and the one-ups-persons of conferences of this kind are always the ones who somehow get in the last word and say, “You’re all naïve. You suppose that this is the basic issue, but there’s an underlying issue which is the basic issue, and that’s the one that, I’m going to demonstrate, must absolutely prevail.” It’s not necessarily always the Marxist card which is played in this context, although it frequently is. It could be some other card, but it’s always a card played. It’s always the last word at the conference which makes everybody go away and say, “Oh. I thought this was about women. Oh, dear. It must be about something else.” We will have to come back to that because in a way, the material we cover today and the way that we’re enabled to discuss it by its own nature is something that calls for another lecture and a lecture that we will actually provide. There’s a very real sense, as I hope to show by the end of the lecture, in which traditional–I call this “classical feminist criticism”–in which traditional or classical feminist criticism needs to be supplemented, perhaps in the Derridean sense, by something more, which is gender theory. As I say, at the end of the lecture I’ll try to explain what that might entail, and then come back to it when we discuss Judith Butler and Michel Foucault a few lectures from now.

第三章 《一间自己的房间》的结构

Chapter 3. The Structure of A Room of One’s Own

好的。所以，《一间自己的房间》绝对是一部令人惊叹的杰作。它实际上是我最喜欢的书之一。我把它当作小说来读，而且在很多方面它确实是一部小说。我立刻想到，这可能会让我们停下来思考，因为如果夏洛蒂·勃朗特因为带有倾向性而被指责——也就是说，因为她从抱怨、从感知到的压迫的角度来写作；如果夏洛蒂·勃朗特的倾向性妨碍了她想要表达的内容的充分表达——也就是说，妨碍了一部小说的展开；如果正如弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫（我认为她确实正确地指出，至少从美学的角度来看）所说，我们会疑惑，为什么在简·爱滔滔不绝地表达了她希望能够旅行、希望自己的视野更加开阔之后，格蕾丝·普尔会突然出现。弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫认为，格蕾丝·普尔的出现显得格格不入，叙事结构出现了裂痕。如果这种对夏洛蒂·勃朗特的批评是公正的（我们将在其他语境中再次讨论这一点），那么当然，这种批评也可以反过来用来批评《一间自己的房间》本身的叙事风格和叙事手法。

All right. So A Room of One’s Own is an absolutely amazing tour de force. It’s actually one of my favorite books. I read it like a novel, and in many ways it is a novel. I think immediately that that might give us pause because if Charlotte Brontë is to be called to task for tendentiousness–that is to say, for writing from the standpoint of complaint, of perceived oppression; and if Charlotte Brontë’s tendentiousness gets in the way of the full expression of what she has to say–which is to say, the unfolding of a novel; and if as Virginia Woolf, I think, actually rightly remarks, at least from an aesthetic point of view, we wonder why on earth Grace Pool suddenly appears after Jane’s diatribe about wishing that she could travel and wishing that her horizons had been broadened, that somehow, Virginia Woolf says, Grace Pool is out of place and there’s been a rift in the narrative fabric: if this criticism of Charlotte Brontë is fair, and we’ll be coming back to it in other contexts, then of course it could be turned against the choice of narrative style, of narrative approach, in A Room of One’s Own itself.

我想，只有读完《一间自己的房间》的全部六章，你才能真正体会到这一点。我强烈建议你读完，因为它真的很有趣。如果你读完了《一间自己的房间》，你会说：“哎呀，这其实也是一部小说。” 说话者说：“哦，你想怎么称呼我都行。” 这与梅尔维尔笔下的说话者说“叫我以实玛利”颇为相似。你可以叫我玛丽·贝顿，你可以叫我玛丽·塞顿，也可以叫我玛丽·卡迈克尔。这其实并不重要，但我确实经历过一些冒险。至少说话者本人经历过一些虚构的冒险，或者至少我保留让你认为这些冒险是虚构的权利。换句话说，这是一个在虚构世界中精心设计的叙事。

This, I suppose, could only strike you forcefully if you read the whole of A Room of One’s Own, all six chapters, which I urge you to do because it’s so much fun. If you read the whole of A Room of One’s Own, you’d say, “Well, gee. This is sort of a novel, too.” The speaker says, “Oh, call me anybody you like,” not unlike Melville’s speaker saying, “Call me Ishmael.” You can call me Mary Beton. You can call me Mary Seton, call me Mary Carmichael. It doesn’t really matter, but I’ve had certain adventures. At least that person speaking has had certain adventures which are fictitious, or at least I reserve the right to have you suppose that they are fictitious. In other words, this is a narrative that moves quite by design in the world of fiction.

换句话说，弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫的意思是，这并非事实。正如她在第一章中所述，她，玛丽·贝顿，坐在河边沉思，琢磨着究竟该如何向这些年轻女士们讲述女性与小说之间的关系——就在她苦思冥想之际，一个想法突然涌现。这感觉就像从河里捞出一小块鱼肉，那鱼肉在她脑海中游来游去。她兴奋不已，径直穿过草地走去。这时，一位身着牛津大学长袍、气宇轩昂的执事走了过来，指着碎石小路，告诉她，作为一名未经许可的女性，她应该走这条路，因为草地是大学男生的专属领地；之后，她又多次遭遇类似的场景。她漫不经心地走进图书馆，却被一位老态龙钟、形如幽灵般的绅士告知，因为她是女性，所以需要一封介绍信才能进入。于是，她虚构的一天——思考着究竟该如何向这些年轻女性讲述女性与文学——就这样以一种略显不快的虚构形式开始了，这对她而言无疑是件苦差事。换句话说，《一间自己的房间》在某种意义上是一部小说。

In other words, Virginia Woolf is saying it really isn’t true, as she tells us in the first chapter, that she, Mary Beton, after sitting at the river thinking, wondering what on earth she’s going to tell these young ladies about women and fiction–as she’s been thinking about that, finally she gets a little idea. It’s like pulling a bit of a fish out of the river, and the fish starts swimming around in her head. She becomes quite excited and she walks away across the grass. At that point up arises a beadle, a formidable person wearing Oxonian gowns and pointing at the gravel path where she, as an unauthorized woman, should be walking, as the grass is the province only for the men enrolled in the university; and then she has repeated encounters of that kind. She goes to the library unthinkingly, only to be told by an elderly wraithlike gentleman that since she’s a woman she needs a letter of introduction to get in. And so her day, her fictitious day of thinking about what on earth she should say to these young women about women and fiction, begins, somewhat unpleasantly for her character, as a presented fiction. In other words, A Room of One’s Own is, in a sense, a novel.

故事接着讲述她享用了一顿非常愉快的午餐。她受邀来到校园，担任一位杰出作家。只要不惹是生非，身为小说家的女性也无妨。从这个角度来看，她之所以能受邀参加这样的午餐，并且吃得如此愉快，是因为午餐是由男性提供的，而且用餐环境也是为男性设计的。之后，她去拜访一位在这所虚构的大学任教的朋友。她和朋友在大学食堂共进晚餐，晚餐极其简陋，毫无特色。晚餐后，她们回到她的房间，开始谈论这所大学的建造条件。一群十九世纪的女性竭尽全力筹集了三万英镑，没有任何花哨的装饰。她们当时身无分文。由于没有收到任何大额捐款，所以草坪无人修剪，砖墙朴素无华，这就是这所女子学院的真实写照。

It continues with a very pleasant lunch that she has. She’s been invited to the campus as a distinguished writer. It’s okay to be a woman who is a novelist as long as you don’t rock the boat too much. In that regard, she can have been invited to such a lunch and has a very pleasant lunch because it’s provided by men in an atmosphere which is designed for men. Then she goes to visit a friend who is teaching at this fictitious college. She has dinner with the friend in that college’s dining hall, and the dinner is extremely inferior and plain, and then they go to her rooms and they start talking about the conditions in which this college was built. A bunch of women in the nineteenth century did all they could do to raise 30,000 pounds, no frills, thank you very much. None of them had any money. There were no major donations and so the grass never gets cut, the brick is plain and unadorned, and that’s the way life is in this particular women’s college.

第二天，她去了图书馆，因为她决定一定要弄清楚人们对女性的看法；那么，女人究竟是什么呢？我不知道，所以最好去图书馆查一下，她心想。她发现成百上千的男人写过关于女性的书：关于女性的低劣、女性的道德敏感、女性缺乏体力等等，不胜枚举。她把这些书都列在了图书馆的目录里，而这些书居然真的都在目录里（笑）——当然，所有这些观点都通过成百上千本男性写的关于女性的书表达了出来。这真是令人沮丧，但正如你所想，这为精彩的讽刺提供了绝佳的素材——应该说是带有倾向性的讽刺，因为很明显，这是在抨击男性。我的意思是，她不会让夏洛蒂·勃朗特就这么算了。夏洛蒂·勃朗特必须克制自己的愤怒，弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫想表达的是，如果她想把所有想法都表达出来的话。弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫本人，听起来似乎并不怎么生气，但你很可能误解了——她只是用喜剧的方式来发泄愤怒——弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫允许自己，因为事实的确如此，怀有一丝愤怒。

The next day she goes to the library because she decides she’s really got to find out something about what people think of women; and so, what is a woman? I don’t know so I’d better look it up in the library, she thinks. She finds out that hundreds and hundreds and hundreds of men have written books about women: on the inferiority of women, the moral sensitivity of women, the lack of physical strength of women, on and on and on. She lists them as items in the library catalog which actually are there [laughs] in the library catalog–all of them, of course, getting themselves expressed in these hundreds and hundreds of books about women by men. Well, this is very frustrating but, as you can imagine, it’s an occasion for wonderful satire–one has to say tendentious satire, because obviously it’s male-bashing. My point is that she wouldn’t let Charlotte Brontë get away with that. Charlotte Brontë has to suspend her anger, Virginia Woolf wants to say, if she’s going to get the whole of what’s on her mind expressed. Well, Virginia Woolf, who sort of doesn’t sound very angry, but you could well be mistaken about that–she’s venting her anger in comic effects–Virginia Woolf allows herself, because that really is the case, a measure of anger.

故事就发生在这一章里。之后她回到家，《一间自己的房间》的其余部分都发生在她家中。她在书房里从书架上取书，这部分大致按时间顺序展开。故事从她看着书架上本该摆放女性作家作品的地方，却发现一本也没有开始；后来，是的，出现了女性作家，而且有不少小说家。到了二十世纪后期，女性作家的活动空间逐渐扩大，随着她回顾这一切，我们也得以继续看到她对女性在文学史上的文学可能性的思考。

So it is in that chapter. Then she goes home and the rest of A Room of One’s Own takes place in her home. She’s in her study pulling books off the shelf of her library, and this is more or less chronological. It starts with a time when she looks on the shelf where the women writers ought to be and there aren’t any women writers, and then later, yes, there are women writers, there are quite a few novelists. Then later in the twentieth century, women writers get a little bit more scope for their activity, and as she passes all of this in review, we continue to get her reflections on the state of literary possibility for women in literary history.

第四章 女性主义批评与《一间自己的房间》

Chapter 4. Feminist Criticism and A Room of One’s Own

这就是《一间自己的房间》的整体结构，而这种印象派叙事结构，无疑是小说式的结构——并非没有先例。奥斯卡·王尔德的《威廉·惠特曼先生的画像》就是其中之一，某种程度上，它本身就是《一间自己的房间》所探讨的对象：这是一部中篇小说，正如我所说，在中篇小说的语境下，作者一方面允许自己持有带有倾向性的观点，另一方面又否认她的前辈有权持有此类观点，这其中存在着某种张力或矛盾。可想而知，她对夏洛蒂·勃朗特的评价在后来的女性主义批评中引发了争议。女性主义批评家认为弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫的观点存在诸多误区或需要补充，而这只是其中之一。总的来说，女性主义批评家认为夏洛蒂·勃朗特，或者任何其他作家，都有权持有自己的观点。关于弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫的雌雄同体标准，我们稍后会详细讨论，该标准部分指的是不以任何性别的方式思考。我们稍后会再谈到这一点，但大多数女性主义批评家出于各种原因认为，雌雄同体未必是女性散文应该追求的理想状态，因此他们对弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫持有这种看待夏洛蒂·勃朗特的观点提出了批评。

That’s the structure of A Room of One’s Own overall and it is within this structure, which is an impressionistic and narrative, undoubtedly novelistic structure–there are precedents for it. Oscar Wilde’s Portrait of Mr. W. H. is one in particular–and which is, in a way, itself what it’s talking about: It is a novella, and in the context of the novella, as I say, there’s a certain tension or contradiction in an author who is allowing herself tendentious opinions while denying the right to have such opinions on the part of one of her predecessors. As you can imagine, what she says about Charlotte Brontë has been controversial in subsequent feminist criticism. There are a number of ways in which feminist critics feel that Virginia Woolf is misguided or needs to be supplemented, and this is one of them. By and large, feminist critics feel that Charlotte Brontë, or any other writer, has the right to be tendentious. We’ll have more to say about Virginia Woolf’s criterion of androgyny, which is not thinking like either sex, in part. We’ll come back to that, but most feminist criticism has felt for a variety of reasons that androgyny isn’t necessarily the ideal toward which women’s prose ought to be aspiring and takes Virginia Woolf to task therefore for having taken this view of Charlotte Brontë.

没错，女性主义批评从各个方面对《一间自己的房间》进行了批判，但与此同时——我认为女性主义批评界对此也毫不掩饰地承认——当你通读全文，甚至仅仅阅读你选集中收录的节选时，你会惊叹于弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫的论点竟如此完整地预示了女性主义批评史的后续发展。我只想指出其中的几个方面。正如肖瓦尔特所指出的，现代女性主义批评的第一阶段主要关注男性在小说中对女性的描写。玛丽·埃尔曼1968年出版的《思考女性》和凯特·米利特1970年出版的《性政治》这两本书都主要聚焦于那些性别歧视的男性小说家，他们认为女性贬低女性的描写正是女性主义视角需要揭露的。在伊莱恩·肖瓦尔特的论述中，这种批评被她称之为（也更倾向于称之为）“女性批评”或“女性批评家”的理论所取代。女性批评与其说是关注男性在小说中对女性的描写，不如说是关注女性作为作家在文学史上的地位，以及作为人物——无论她们本身是男性作品还是女性作品中的人物——在小说史上的地位。换言之，女性批评将六十年代末七十年代初女性主义批评的主题从男性压迫的历史转向了女性传统的历史。

Now yes, feminist criticism has taken A Room of One’s Own to task in a variety of ways, but at the same time–and I think this is freely and handsomely acknowledged by feminist criticism–it is amazing–when you read the whole text, and even when you read the excerpts that you have in your anthology–it is amazing how completely Virginia Woolf’s arguments anticipate the subsequent course of the history of feminist criticism. I just want to point out a few of the ways in which it does. As Showalter points out, the first phase of modern feminist criticism was the kind of work that primarily paid attention to men’s treatment of women in fiction. Mary Ellmann’s book of 1968 called Thinking about Women, Kate Millett’s Sexual Politics in 1970 are both books which focus primarily on sexist male novelists whose demeaning treatment of women is something that the feminist perspective needed to bring out. This criticism is superseded in Elaine Showalter’s account by what she calls, and prefers, “gynocriticism” or “the gynocritics.” Gynocriticism is not so much concerned with men’s treatment of women in fiction as with the place of women as writers in literary history and as characters–regardless of whether they are characters in men’s or women’s books in their own right–in the history of fiction. In other words, gynocriticism turns the topic of feminist criticism in the late sixties and early seventies from the history of oppression by men to the history of a women’s tradition.

在我看来，这种对事物发展进程的感知在伍尔夫身上已经完全显现。她也想探讨女性作家的可能性，探讨女性作家需要感受到她们并不孤单。然而，更重要的是，她以尖锐而又常常带有讽刺意味的观察来强调女性视角，这些观察揭露了男性对待女性的方式，以及男性贬低女性、将她们束缚在“位置”上的方法——例如，正如她在大英图书馆发现的那样，所有那些撰写关于女性书籍的男性，其中大多数是教授，都是如此。所有这些都与肖瓦尔特所认为的埃尔曼、米勒以及其他同代女性主义批评家所代表的第一阶段女性主义批评传统非常契合。因此，伍尔夫方法的包容性在某种意义上可以理解为她能够将两种现代传统联系起来——不再像肖瓦尔特正确地认为的那样是按时间顺序排列的——而是一种同时性，在这种同时性中，对男性边缘化女性的强调和对女性意识和传统的强调可以同时提出。

Now this sense of the unfolding of things, it seems to me, is already fully present in Woolf. She, too, wants to talk about the possibilities for women writers, about the need for women writers to feel that they’re not alone. Above all at the same time, however, she frames this emphasis on the woman’s perspective with the sort of trenchant, frequently satirical observations about men’s treatment of women and men’s way of demeaning women and keeping them in their place–as, for example, all the men, most of them professors, who wrote books about women, as she discovered in the British library, do. All of this is very much in the tradition of that first phase of feminist criticism that Showalter identifies with Ellmann and Millett and others of that generation. So the capaciousness of Woolf’s approach in one sense can be understood as precisely her ability to bridge both sorts of modern tradition–no longer chronological as Showalter presents them as being, correctly–but rather as a kind of simultaneity in which the emphasis on men’s marginalization of women and the emphasis on women’s consciousness and traditions can be set forth at the same time.

第五章 女性语言与男性句式

Chapter 5. Women’s Language and the Male Sentence

现在，在弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫的作品中也出现了类似的现象——自从桑德拉·吉尔伯特和苏珊·古巴尔出版了那本引人入胜的著作《阁楼上的疯女人》（The Madwoman in the Attic）之后——这本书也暗指《简·爱》，你还记得《简·爱》中阁楼里的疯女人伯莎吗？——自《阁楼上的疯女人》出版以来，女性主义批评界一直在讨论“疯女人”这一主题：换句话说，由于女性无法公开地以作家或其他艺术家的身份进行创作，她们被迫将自己的创造力引导到颠覆性的、狡猾的，甚至可能是心理上自我毁灭的形式中，例如夏洛特·珀金斯·吉尔曼的《黄色壁纸》。早在第600页——实际上就在我之前读到的关于阶级和性别的段落下方——伍尔夫就已经触及了“疯女人”这一主题，远早于吉尔伯特和古巴尔。她说：
