Now also in Virginia Woolf there is what–Since the publication of the fascinating book by Sandra Gilbert and Susan Gubar called The Madwoman in the Attic–this is also an allusion to Jane Eyre, you remember Bertha, the madwoman in the attic of Jane Eyre–since the publication of The Madwoman in the Attic, feminist criticism has talked about the madwoman thesis: the idea, in other words, that because they could not openly express themselves creatively as writers or as artists of other kinds, women were forced to channel their creativity into subversive, devious and perhaps psychologically self-destructive forms, as in, for example, Charlotte Perkins Gilman’s The Yellow Wallpaper. You find Woolf already on page 600–just actually below the passage about class and gender that I read before–you find her touching on this madwoman theme long before Gilbert and Gubar. She says:

然而，当读到女巫被浸入水中、女人被魔鬼附身、智者贩卖草药的故事时（当然，她还补充道），甚至读到一位非常杰出的男子拥有一位母亲的故事……换句话说，人们会强烈怀疑，这个人的创造力受到了压制，不幸的是，这种压制被引导到了不合群或反社会的方向。正如我所说，这是一个延续至今的传统。它仍然存在于肖瓦尔特的作品中。在她女性主义批判的视角下——也就是说，她坚持要求我们作为学者记录、编纂并熟悉女性的历史以及女性写作的历史——我们必须认识到诸如巫术、疯狂、草药学等等各种形式的压迫。

When, however, one reads of a witch being ducked, of a woman possessed by devils, of a wise woman selling herbs, [and then of course she adds] and even of a very remarkable man who had a mother… There, in other words, one strongly suspects that there is a person whose creativity has been oppressed and unfortunately channeled in unsocial or antisocial directions. This, as I say, is a tradition that’s sustained. It still exists in Showalter. In her gynocritical perspective–that is to say, her insistence on our registering, chronicling, and becoming familiar as scholars with the history of women as well as the history of women’s writing–the recognition of such forms of repression as witchcraft, as madness, as herbalism, as whatever it might be, need to be taken into account.

伍尔夫当时就非常关注这一点，这一点对肖瓦尔特来说尤其重要，因为这是肖瓦尔特对女性批评任务的理解。伍尔夫认为，女性作家需要一种传统，她们面临的一大困难和缺陷在于，虽然有一些伟大的作家——总是那几位老面孔：简·奥斯汀、勃朗特姐妹、乔治·艾略特——但她们缺乏一种可以延续发展的传统，一种可以依托进行写作的传统。因此，伍尔夫在第606页右栏谈到了“男性的句式”，谈到了女性作家难以接受自己不仅没有属于自己的空间，也没有属于自己的语言这一事实​​。右栏开头写道：“也许她提笔写作时首先会发现，根本没有现成的句式可供她使用。”所有文学范式，所有小说散文的范式——无论如何，它们中的大多数都是男性创造的。因为写作的氛围——这一点我们很快就会谈到——写作本身就带有男性的印记，我们必须理解这一点。

Also very much on the mind of Woolf already, as it still is particularly for Showalter because this is Showalter’s understanding of the task of gynocriticism, is the notion that one needs a tradition, that one of the great difficulties and shortcomings facing the woman’s writer is that, yes, there are a few greats–the same ones always named, Austen, the Brontës, George Eliot–but there is not a sense of an ongoing tradition, of a developing tradition within which one could write; so that Woolf on page 606, the right-hand column, talks about “the man’s sentence,” the difficulty of coming to terms with not having, not just a room of one’s own, but a language of one’s own. This is toward the top of the right-hand column: “Perhaps the first thing she would find, setting pen to paper, was that there was no common sentence ready for her use.” All the literary models, all the models of novelistic prose–most of them, in any case, are engendered male; because the atmosphere of writing–and this is a point that we’ll be getting to soon–the very fact of writing is something that we have to understand as having a male stamp on it.

右侧栏下方：

Further down in the right-hand column:

“那是一个人的判决（她刚才引用了一句很长的句子）；从这句话背后，我们可以看到约翰逊、吉本和其他人。”那句话并不适合女性使用。夏洛蒂·勃朗特，这位文笔精湛的散文家，也曾因这句笨拙的句子而失手。乔治·艾略特用这句形容词更是糟蹋了它。简·奥斯汀看着它，一笑置之，构思出一个自然流畅、优美动人的句子，完全符合她自己的风格，并且始终坚持使用。因此，尽管她的写作天赋不及夏洛蒂·勃朗特，却表达得更加丰富。顺便一提，这种说法是有争议的，因为我们完全可以理解简·奥斯汀的散文风格深受塞缪尔·约翰逊和塞缪尔·理查森的影响，所以这种说法值得商榷。与此同时，伍尔夫的观点是，奥斯汀能够摆脱这种可怕的困境：她想表达一些东西，却发现自己没有属于自己的语言，一种能够表达这种想法的语言——一种能够被自己所接受、为自己服务、并成为自己身份象征的语言。“所以我想以女性的身份写作，我想……” “我想表达一个女人想说的话，但我只能用男人的语言来表达。”这就是伍尔夫的观点，当然，它有很多深远的影响。

That is a man’s sentence [she’s just quoted a long sentence]; behind it one can see Johnson, Gibbon and the rest.” It was a sentence that was unsuited for a woman’s use. Charlotte Brontë, with all her splendid gift for prose, stumbled and fell with that clumsy weapon in her hands. George Eliot committed atrocities with it that beggar description. Jane Austen looked at it and laughed at it and devised a perfectly natural, shapely sentence proper for her own use and never departed from it. Thus, with less genius for writing than Charlotte Brontë, she got infinitely more said. By the way, this is disputable because certainly it’s possible to understand Jane Austen’s prose style as emerging from the work of Samuel Johnson and Samuel Richardson, in particular, so it is disputable. At the same time, Woolf’s point is that Austen was able to shake herself free from this terrible problem of wanting to say something but finding that one doesn’t have one’s own language, a language suitable to– appropriated by and for and as one’s identity–for saying it. “So I want to write as a woman, I want to say the things that a woman wants to say, but all I’ve got to say it with is a man’s sentence.” That’s Woolf’s point, and of course it has many and long ramifications.

我一直试图压制住自1980年以来女性主义批评和性别理论对这方面的诸多批评，但与此同时，其影响也颇为有趣，并得到了我们称之为法国女性主义的、理论上非常精深的女性主义批评分支的强化。你们当中有些人可能了解露西·伊里加雷和海伦·西苏的作品。这类作家坚持认为，存在一种女性语言。女性写作并非仅仅依靠头脑和性器官，而是依靠整个身体。女性不写精心构建的周期性句子。她们写的是持续不断的并列句、印象派的、离题的、即兴的句子：没有自我意识的句子——没有结构，或多或少地对应着没有自我意识的状态。我们稍后会在 Showalter 的著作中再谈到这一点，但与此同时，法国女权主义愿意接受并追求一种关于女性写作的理念，并且，在这种理念背后，隐含着一种关于女性是什么的理念，这种理念很容易被认定为某种本质主义的。

I’m holding at bay the criticism of a great deal of this that has to be leveled at it by feminist criticism and gender theory roughly since 1980, but in the meantime the ramifications are interesting and they are reinforced by the theoretically very sophisticated wing of feminist criticism that we call French feminism. Some of you may know the work of Luce Irigaray and Helene Cixous. Writers of this kind insist that there is such a thing as women’s language. Women write not just with their heads and their phalluses but with their whole bodies. Women don’t write carefully constructed periodic sentences. Women write ongoing paratactic, impressionist, digressive, ad hoc sentences: sentences without ego–being without structure more or less corresponding to being without ego. We’ll come back to this in a minute in Showalter, but in the meantime French feminism was willing to settle on and for an idea of women’s writing and, implicitly behind this idea, an idea of what a woman is that is very easy to identify as somehow or another essentializing.

为什么女性就不能写出严谨的句式？毕竟，简·奥斯汀实际上就写过这种句式。从各种角度来看，如果女性有权自由地成为她想成为的人，为什么她就不能写出不一定带有这种性别刻板印象的女性式句子呢？换句话说，为什么女性的写作就必须是女性的写作呢？

Why can’t a woman write a rigorous periodic sentence? After all, that’s the kind of sentence that Jane Austen did, in fact, write. In a whole variety of ways that one might think of, why can’t a woman, if she is to be free to be whatever she wants to be, write a sentence which isn’t necessarily of this gendered feminine sort? Why does women’s writing, in other words, have to be women’s writing?

在我看来，弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫在探讨雌雄同体这一危险的理念时，似乎预示着法国女权主义及其可能的批判。她设想了一种既需要具备男性特质又需要具备女性特质的思维方式，这种思维方式需要以一种弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫所说的“非常性感”的方式进行写作，而这种性感恰恰来自于人们不再思考自身性别的时刻——换句话说，就是不再区分男性和女性的话语的时刻。我认为必须指出的是，尽管我们可以在《一间自己的房间》中强调这种对法国女权主义的先进批判，以及对我们称之为“女性”的本质概念的批判——我对此话题的讨论尚未结束——但我认为必须指出的是，尽管我们可以这样解读《一间自己的房间》，但与此同时，我们也必须承认弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫在这个问题上存在着矛盾的态度。她坚持认为简·奥斯汀的写作风格像个女人，她摆脱了男性句子的束缚，写出了属于她自己的句子，一个女性的句子——无论这在文学史上是否属实——这两者之间存在着区别。一方面，像女人一样写作很重要；另一方面，以雌雄同体的方式写作也很重要。

It seems to me that it is French feminism and the possible critique of French feminism that Virginia Woolf is anticipating when she embarks on this perilous idea of androgyny, of the kind of mind that needs to be both male and female and that needs to write in a way that Virginia Woolf says is actually very sexy, precisely in the moment when one is not thinking about one’s sex–the moment, in other words, when there is no longer a question of the man’s sentence and the woman’s sentence. I think it has to be said that although one could emphasize in A Room of One’s Own this sort of advanced criticism of French feminism, and also of the idea that there is essentially something that we call woman–and I’m not through with that topic–I think it has to be said that although we could read A Room of One’s Own in this way, at the same time we have to recognize an ambivalence on Virginia Woolf’s part on this subject. There is a difference between her insistence that Jane Austen wrote like a woman, that she shrugged off the tyranny of the man’s sentence and wrote her own kind of sentence, a woman’s sentence–regardless of whether or not that is actually in literary historical terms true–between the idea, on the one hand, that it’s important to write like a woman and the idea, on the other hand, that it’s important to write androgynously.

我认为，我们必须承认她这些讲座带有印象派的风格。我们必须承认，她在这一点上摇摆不定；无论如何，在伍尔夫的作品中，很难明确界定是否存在某种可以称之为“女性写作”的东西；正如其背后的问题，是否存在某种可以称之为“女性”的东西，或者反过来——所有写作的理想是否在于尽可能彻底地摆脱其性别特征。或许，在这一点上存在某种富有创造性或丰富的矛盾，应该指出的是，我们在阅读《一间自己的房间》时也会发现这种矛盾，并且需要将其考虑在内。

We have to concede, I think, the impressionistic form of these lectures that she’s giving. We have to concede that she wavers on this point; that somehow or another it’s very difficult to pin down in Woolf the question of whether there is essentially something to be called “women’s writing”; just as the question behind that, whether there is essentially something to be called “woman,” or the question on the contrary–whether the ideal of all writing is to shed as fully as it can precisely its gendered aspects. There is perhaps a kind of creative or rich inconsistency on this point that, it should be said, one also finds and needs to take into account in reading A Room of One’s Own.

第六章 古典女权主义的复杂性和影响

Chapter 6. Complications and Implications of Classical Feminism

好的。现在我们更接近于超越女性主义批评的整个问题——例如，肖瓦尔特在谈到小说史时，提到了三个阶段：首先是“女性化”阶段，在这个阶段，女性作家竭力模仿男性写作，在各个方面完全顺从男性价值观；她们或许会引入一种“天使般的”文化仁慈和温和，以融入男性视角——而男性视角有时可能相当军事化和严酷。然而，她们却常常躲在柯勒·贝尔、阿克顿·贝尔、乔治·艾略特等男性化的名字背后，并没有真正深入探讨女性在社会中的地位。肖瓦尔特接着指出，这一阶段被小说史上的女权主义时刻所取代，在这个时刻，像盖斯凯尔夫人晚期作品等小说开始带有倾向性，女性的地位和角色成为这类小说的主导主题。顺便说一句，这使得伍尔夫对夏洛蒂·勃朗特的批评在时间顺序上有些脱节，因为夏洛蒂·勃朗特大概属于肖沃尔特所说的小说史上的“女性阶段”，因此，伍尔夫在夏洛蒂·勃朗特的小说中发现了一种原始女权主义，这种女权主义破坏了《简·爱》的质感，这很有意思。

All right. Now getting a little closer to this whole question of beyond the gynocritical–because Showalter, for example, in talking about the history of the novel talks about those three phases: first the “feminine,” the phase in which women try very much to write as though they were men by deferring completely to male values in all the ways that they can; perhaps introducing a kind of, again, “angel in the house” cultural benevolence and benignity into perspectives of men that can be sometimes rather militaristic and harsh. but nevertheless hiding behind frequently male names like Currer Bell, Acton Bell, George Eliot, and so on, and not really entering into questions of the place of women in society. Showalter then says this is a phase supplanted by a feminist moment in the history of the novel in which novels like the late work of Mrs. Gaskell, for example, and other such novels become tendentious, and the place and role of women becomes the dominant theme of novels of this kind. By the way, this takes Woolf’s critique of Charlotte Brontë a little bit out of chronology, because presumably Charlotte Brontë belongs to what Showalter is calling “the feminine phase” in the history of the novel, and so it’s interesting that Woolf finds a kind of proto-feminism, damaging to the texture of Jane Eyre, already in Charlotte Brontë’s novel.

最后，伊莱恩·肖瓦尔特最欣赏的是：用她所谓的“女性小说”取代女权主义小说——因为她也对小说的倾向性感到不安。这种“女性小说”理所当然地承认女性视角的真实性和合法性，并从女性视角出发进行写作，但如同弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫的作品一样，它摒弃了早期小说中常见的愤怒或对抗意识。这种小说史的解读与肖瓦尔特对近期女权主义批评史的解读非常相似。她将这一批评史分为两个阶段：首先是她所谓的“女权主义”阶段，主要关注男性在小说中对女性的刻画；其次是“女性主义批评”阶段，即女性对文学传统的挪用。肖瓦尔特不遗余力地指出，近期女性主义学术研究，尤其是20世纪70年代的女性主义学术研究，其最重要的工作在于发掘和拓展女性写作的经典范畴，而这一经典并非仅限于小说。因为曾几何时，小说被视为女性写作的一种可能出口，但这种认可却伴随着一种不容置疑的断言：她们不能写诗或戏剧。因此，拓展女性写作的经典范畴至关重要，它应涵盖所有形式的写作，使之得以呈现，并被认可为一种真实存在的传统——正如肖瓦尔特所言，这样我们才能追溯女性写作的历程，跨越数十年，而非仅仅关注某部经典著作。如此一来，女性写作便拥有了与男性写作传统相媲美的、可供创作者思考、借鉴和汲取灵感的真正传统。因此，无论是肖瓦尔特的小说史，还是她的现代女权主义批评史（或者更确切地说是现代女性批评史），都止步于女性视角的问题。

Then finally what Elaine Showalter likes best: the supplanting of the feminist novel–because Elaine Showalter, too, is nervous about the tendentiousness of fiction–the supplanting of that by what she calls “the female novel,” which is the novel that simply takes for granted the authenticity and legitimacy of the woman’s point of view, writes from that point of view but, as in Virginia Woolf, having shed or shaken off the elements of anger or adversary consciousness that earlier novels had typically manifested. This history of the novel is very similar to what Showalter is doing with her sense of the history of recent feminist criticism. That’s in two phases: first the feminist, as she calls it, when the treatment of women by men in fiction is the main focus; and then the gynocritical, which is the appropriation for women of a literary tradition. Showalter is at pains to point out that much of the most important work of recent feminist scholarship, the feminist scholarship of the 1970s, is in simply the unearthing of and expanding of a canon of women’s writing not exclusively novelistic, because there had been a time when the novel was sort of half conceded to women as a possible outlet for their writing. But this concession was accompanied by the sovereign assertion that they couldn’t write poetry and plays, and so an expansion of the canon such that all forms of writing are available and made visible and recognized as actually existing in a tradition–so that we can trace women’s writing, as Showalter puts it, from decade to decade and not from great book to great book, so that there really is a tradition comparable to the male tradition that one can think about, think within, and draw on as a creative writer oneself, is necessary. So both Showalter’s history of the novel and her history of modern feminist criticism–or modern women’s criticism, one had better say–end at the point when it is still a question of the woman’s perspective.

但这引出了一个问题——我曾以各种方式探讨过这个问题——但它确实提出了一个必须萦绕于此类思考之上的问题。当我们从批评和理论的角度探讨其他身份认同视角时，我们会一次又一次地遇到这个问题。它引出这样一个问题：如果我说一位女性或女性的写作属于某种类型，如果我以某种我认为可识别的方式来定义一位女性——比如说，我将一位女性定义为直觉敏锐、富有想象力、印象派、敏感、不合逻辑、反对理性、拒绝我们通常与男性写作联系在一起的那种周期性的主谓句——我是否可以将这种定义挪用给像法国女权主义者这样的女性，并以此来定义女性——但这难道不只是颠倒了弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫在《一间自己的房间》第二章中对大英博物馆发现的男性的描述吗？这难道不只是颠倒了男性一直以来强加给女性的所有负面价值吗？归根结底，这难道不是接受男性对女性的看法吗？接受男性认为女性是理性、科学、逻辑等等的化身——这难道不是在说“头脑高于心灵”，换句话说，接受了头脑相对于心灵的低劣地位吗？即便人们自认为已经提升了女性的价值，并在提升女性意识的过程中坚持认为“心灵高于头脑”？换句话说，人们并没有改变父权制思想自始至终所支配的那些本质身份。正是这种对女性的刻板印象，才使得父权制得以存在并滋生。这正是理论问题所在。在我看来，这似乎要求人们意识到，无论如何，都必须提出这样一种可能性——而且真的没有其他说法了，这也是朱迪斯·巴特勒经常说的，以及那些效仿朱迪斯·巴特勒风格的人经常说的——必须提出这样一种观点：也许作为一名女权主义者，你能说的最好的话就是：根本不存在女人这种东西；没有女人。

But this raises a question–and I’ve been touching on it in a variety of ways–but it really raises the question that has to haunt thinking of this kind. We’re going to be encountering it again and again and again as we move through other forms of identity perspective in criticism and theory. It raises the question whether if I say that a woman’s or women’s writing is of a certain sort, if I identify a woman in a way that I take somehow to be recognizable–let’s say I identify a woman as intuitive, imaginative, impressionistic, sensitive, illogical, opposed to reason, a refuser of that periodic sort of subject-predicate sentence that we associate with men’s writing–I can appropriate that for women like the French feminists and I can identify women in so doing as such people–but isn’t that simply inverting what men say in Virginia Woolf’s discoveries in the British museum in the second chapter of A Room of One’s Own–isn’t that just inverting all the negative values that men have attached to women all along? Isn’t it ultimately to accept men’s opinions of women, men’s ways of saying that because they are avatars of reason, science, logic and all the rest of it–isn’t a way of saying that the head is higher than the heart and accepting, in other words, the lower or inferior status of this organ to this organ even though one supposes oneself to have transvalued them and insisted, in promoting women’s consciousness, that the heart is higher than the head? One hasn’t done anything, in other words, to the essential identities that have governed patriarchal thought from the beginning. It is precisely this characterization of women that has enabled and engendered patriarchy. This is where the theoretical problem arises. It calls for, it seems to me, a sense that somehow or another one has to put the possibility–and there’s really no other way to say it, and this is something that Judith Butler frequently says and people who work in the mode of Judith Butler say–one has to put the suggestion that perhaps the best thing one can say as a feminist is there is no such thing as a woman; there is no woman.

当然，这种观点很危险，也正是这种危险性在女权主义思想中造成了不幸的分裂。在现实生活中，在真实的物质存在中，女性确实存在。她们受到法律的压迫，受到男性的压迫，她们的权利和生命需要时刻受到保护。换句话说，那种认为“女性不存在”的理论观点，在现实生活中是站不住脚的。然而与此同时，身份政治的语言总是称之为“本质主义”的含义，即说“女人”是某种特定的东西的含义——如果我们说“女人”是某种特定的东西，但又不同于男性一直以来所说的那样，或许会更好——但更糟糕的是，说“女人”是某种特定的东西，恰恰是男性一直以来所说的那样——尽管这种立场对于实践女权主义和现实世界的女权主义来说绝对必要，但以这种方式采取这种立场却是一件好事，对吧？——然而，这却不利于对性别及其可能性的更敏锐的理论理解。

Now of course this is perilous, and this is what drives such an unfortunate wedge in the midst of feminist thought. In real life, in real material existence, there certainly are women. They are oppressed by laws, they are oppressed by men, and their rights and their very lives need to be protected with perpetual vigilance. The theoretical idea, in other words, that there’s no such thing as a woman is not an idea that can be sustained in life. Yet at the same time, the implications of what the language of identity politics is always calling “essentialism,” the implications of saying “woman” is one particular thing–and it might be better if we said “woman” was one particular thing, but something other than what men have been saying she was all along–but making the problem worse, saying that “woman” is one particular thing, which is just what men have always said she was–only it’s a good thing, right, that positions of this kind are taken up in this way, despite the fact that they’re absolutely necessary for practical feminism and for real-world feminism–is nevertheless detrimental to a more sensitive theoretical understanding of gender and of the possibilities of gender.

凭直觉、感性、印象派固然很好，但关于这一点，我想说两点。首先，男人想怎样都可以，对吧？（笑）其次，女人为什么就一定要怎样呢？很明显，这两种情况下都存在例外，而且这些例外远远超出了证明规则的例外。很明显，在这两种情况下，都存在着跨越性别界限的感受，这些感受完全混淆并否定了这些分类，因此，基于以上种种原因，这确实是一个问题。

It’s all very well to be intuitive and emotional and impressionistic, but one wants to say two things about that. In the first place, a guy gets to be that if he wants to, right? [laughs] In the second place, why does a woman have to be that, right? It’s perfectly clear in both cases that there are exceptions which go vastly beyond the exception that proves the rule. It’s perfectly clear that in both cases there are sensibilities across gender that completely mix up and discredit these categories, and so for all of those reasons there is a problem.

我想快速指出一点，就肖瓦尔特的文章而言，这是1980年前后批评界一直未能真正克服的困境。时间到了。我不打算引用原文，但请注意她对马克思主义和结构主义的敌意——某种程度上，我们又回到了最初的问题——理由是——当然，我们自己也说过——它们都自诩为“科学”。啊哈！它们带有男性性别色彩！马克思主义和结构主义是我们不想与之有任何瓜葛的，因为这不过是弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫笔下那个丑陋的教士再次抬头，并试图通过其优越的理性将自己的意志强加于女性。所以我们不想要这些。我们想要的是一种批评形式，而这正是她在文章结尾（第1385页和1386页）所表达的，一种能够规避科学性的批评形式；这种批评形式关注文本及其传统的现实意义，却不纠缠于理论问题。换言之，它不拘泥于逻辑、不拘泥于宏大结构、不拘泥于科学性。

Just very quickly I want to point out, looking at Showalter’s essay, that this is a bind that criticism around 1980 really hasn’t gotten past. Time’s up. I’m not going to take the time to quote passages, but notice her animus–and here, in a way, we go back to the beginning–her animus against Marxism and structuralism on the grounds–and of course we’ve said this ourselves–on the grounds that both of them present themselves as “sciences.” Aha! They’re gendered male! Marxism and structuralism aren’t anything we want to have to do with because this is just Virginia Woolf’s beadle raising its ugly head again and imposing its will–through its superior rationality–on women. So we don’t want any of that. What we want instead is a form of criticism, and this is what she says in effect at the end of the essay on pages 1385 and 1386, that evades scientificity; a form of criticism that engages with the reality of texts and of the textual tradition but doesn’t trouble its head with theoretical matters. In other words, a form that dissociates itself from the logical, from overarching structure, from scientificity.

肖瓦尔特让自己陷入了这种境地，也让女权主义批评陷入了这种境地——该如何形容呢？——它就像一个被殖民的事业，只要不合情理，就可以为所欲为。如果真是如此，那么它当然会对女权主义批评的可能性施加本质主义的限制，正如它对男性批评的描述方式一样，毋庸置疑，也对女性批评施加了限制。至于这些限制是否公平合理，或者是否过于夸张，则值得商榷。但这远不如提醒我们女权主义批评的可能性被边缘化来得重要，因为这种边缘化意味着女权主义批评必须不同于马克思主义和结构主义范式所提供的那些东西。

Showalter leaves herself in this position, and she leaves feminist criticism in this position as–how might one put it?–a colonized enterprise that can do anything it likes as long as it’s not reasonable. If that’s the case, then of course it imposes an essentializing limit on the possibilities of feminist criticism, just as of course the characterization of men’s criticism in the way that it’s characterized, needless to say, also imposes limits on that. Whether fair and legitimate limits, or perhaps exaggerated limits, is open to question. That’s not nearly as important a point as the reminder that there is a kind of marginalization of the possibilities for feminist criticism involved in saying that it has to be something other than the sort of thing that Marxist and structuralist paradigms make available.

好的。我认为，受巴赫金影响的亨利·路易斯·盖茨，对于边缘化少数群体批评在规避或成功规避主流批评的框架后，其可利用的资源这一问题，会有一个非常有趣的见解。我希望你们带着这种想法去阅读盖茨的文章。之后，我们将回到自1980年以来，特别是性别理论家，特别是朱迪斯·巴特勒的著作，探讨女性主义批评的未来走向。

Okay. Now I think that Henry Louis Gates, influenced by Bakhtin, will have a very interesting way of coming to terms with this question of what’s available for a marginalized minority criticism once it avoids or has succeeded in avoiding the terms of the mainstream criticism. I want you to read Gates’ essay with that particularly in mind. Then we’ll come back with the question of, as it were, the future of feminist criticism, in a way since 1980, when we turn to the work of the gender theorists, in particular Judith Butler.

第21讲——非裔美国人批评

Lecture 21 - African-American Criticism

第一章 非裔美国文学批评的起源

Chapter 1. Origins of African-American Literary Criticism

保罗·弗莱教授：我不确定这次讲座会持续多久。也许十分钟就能结束，但我对此表示怀疑。如果五十分钟后还没讲完，我还有一些内容留到最后讲，这些内容我一定要讲清楚。不知道你们有没有注意到，有时候我明明准备讲最后一点，最后却没讲到。但这次我想确保把这些要点都讲清楚，这样如果今天没讲完，或者还有一两点要讲，我肯定会在周四的讲座开始时再讲。

Professor Paul Fry: So I’m not sure how long this lecture is going to be. We could be finished in ten minutes, though I doubt that, and if we’re not finished at the end of the fifty, there are some things that I’ve reserved for the end of the lecture that I definitely do want to get said. I don’t know if you’ve noticed that there are times when the last point or two that I appeared to have been preparing to make never get made, but in this case I want to make sure that they are made so that if I don’t finish today, or if I still have a point or two to make, I’ll definitely be taking up those points at the beginning of Thursday’s lecture.

好的。非裔美国人的文学创作传统源远流长，底蕴深厚。正如亨利·路易斯·盖茨所说，这一传统中真正意义上的第一位重要诗人菲利斯·惠特利是一位美国殖民时期的作家。奴隶叙事文学的兴盛始于十八世纪，并延续到十九世纪。十九世纪涌现出许多杰出的文学作品，而二十世纪最引人注目的当然是哈莱姆文艺复兴时期。但纵观整个二十世纪，非裔美国人的文学传统都取得了卓越的成就。这是一个非常丰富的传统——换句话说，它与同样丰富但又非常年轻的非裔美国人文学理论和批评传统形成了鲜明的对比。

All right. Now the African-American tradition of literary production is rich and long standing. As Henry Louis Gates tells you, the first really rather important poet in the tradition, Phillis Wheatley, is an American colonial writer. The flourishing of the slave narrative form begins in the eighteenth century, continues into the nineteenth, the nineteenth century witnesses extraordinary works of fiction, and in the twentieth century, of course most conspicuously in the Harlem Renaissance, but throughout the century there has been extraordinary work done in the African-American literary tradition. It’s a very rich tradition–in other words, somewhat in contrast with the very rich but also very recent tradition of African-American literary theory and criticism.

可以说，这一传统中理论和批评的发展在某种程度上受到了阻碍，因为它最初就存在内部矛盾。黑人批评和黑人女性主义批评从一开始就意识到，它们的关注点并不完全相同。这一点或许会在我们稍后讨论其他话题时有所体现，但与此同时，像芭芭拉·克里斯蒂安、芭芭拉·史密斯、黑兹尔·卡比和贝尔·胡克斯这样的批评家，以她们各自的方式，强调着其他非裔美国男性批评家不太认同的方面。因此，尽管相关研究成果，尤其是在八十年代之后，数量激增，但正如我所说，存在着一种内部分歧，这种分歧一直以来都是一个难以调和的复杂问题，而我认为，现在这种分歧已经基本得到缓解，非裔美国文学理论正在摆脱这些顾虑的束缚，或者至少不再受这些顾虑的过度影响，向前发展。但与此同时，鉴于文学传统的悠久丰富性，这或许可以部分解释理论和批评的出现为何有所延迟。

It’s possible to argue that the development of theory and criticism in this tradition was somewhat balked by a preliminary way in which it found itself at odds with itself. Black criticism and black feminist criticism from the beginning saw that they didn’t have quite the same agenda. This is something that can resonate, perhaps, later in this lecture when we move to other topics, but in the meantime critics like Barbara Christian, Barbara Smith, Hazel Carby, and Bell Hooks were in their variety of ways working with emphases that other, male African-American critics weren’t quite comfortable with. So while work, especially beginning in the eighties, proliferated, there was, as I say, a kind of internal divide which has been a complex matter to negotiate and which is, I think, now largely sort of–well, détente has been achieved, and African-American literary theory is moving forward unfettered any longer by these concerns, or at least by any excess of these concerns. But in the meantime that may partly account for a certain delay in the emergence of theory and criticism given the long-standing richness of the literary tradition.

第二章 亨利·路易斯·盖茨与本质主义问题

Chapter 2. Henry Louis Gates and the Problem of Essentialism

在我看来，亨利·路易斯·盖茨在非裔美国人批评领域的地位堪称典范。尽管本文中有些地方略显尖锐，而我也想就此展开讨论，这些地方似乎暗示着盖茨的思想中存在某种——该怎么说呢？——极端或矫枉过正的成分。但这实际上与他展现出的形象截然不同。盖茨的非凡之处在于他卓越的行政能力和卓越的项目构建能力。他离开耶鲁前往哈佛后，成功地将安东尼·阿皮亚、康奈尔·韦斯特以及其他一些后来离开哈佛的学者聚集到哈佛。从某种意义上说，盖茨本身就是一个庞大的学术帝国，他是一位非凡的人物。你今天读到的正是他最早的作品之一，实际上也是非裔美国人批评领域最早的作品之一。正是这部作品奠定了他的声誉，同时，他还出版了哈丽雅特·威尔逊的一份手稿——与其说是发现，不如说是鉴定——这份手稿极大地丰富了我们对十九世纪非裔美国文学的认识。

Now the role of Henry Louis Gates in African-American criticism is, it seems to me, exemplary, although there are some rather harsh moments in this essay, moments that I wish to take up, that would suggest an element of–what shall I say?–extremism or overkill in Gates’s thinking. This is actually not at all the persona that he has projected. Indeed what’s extraordinary about Gates, whose administrative power and whose abilities as a program builder are remarkable. After he left Yale to go to Harvard, he was able to gather to Harvard Anthony Appiah, Cornel West, and others who have since departed from Harvard, but Gates is in a way an empire unto himself and he has been an extraordinary figure. The earliest work, which is actually among the earliest work in African-American criticism, is what you’ve been reading for today, and it established his reputation together with–not so much discovery of, but authentication of–a manuscript by Harriet Wilson which he published, an important contribution to our knowledge of nineteenth-century African-American literature.

总之，后来发生的事情是，盖茨——他原本就是一位相当不错的作家，但后来逐渐成长为一位杰出的作家——奇迹般地开始为《纽约客》撰稿。在他职业生涯的这一阶段，他创作了一部关于在西弗吉尼亚州成长经历的杰出自传，并真正成为了种族和种族派别之间缓和的代言人。换句话说，他是一位温和派，却丝毫没有被指责为“汤姆叔叔”之类的种族主义者。在他为《纽约客》撰稿，并由蒂娜·布朗担任编辑期间，他展现出的那种优雅风度和杰出的写作才能，本身就是一项了不起的成就，而他的写作生涯至今依然蓬勃发展。

In any case, what happened then was that Gates who by some miracle or other–he was a perfectly good writer in the first place but gradually became a marvelous writer–began writing for The New Yorker, and during this phase of his career, when among other things he produced a remarkable autobiography about growing up in West Virginia, during this phase Gates really became a spokesperson for a détente among races and racial factions. In other words, he was a voice of moderation without incurring any imputation of Uncle Tom-ism or anything of the sort. His sheer urbanity as the remarkable writer that he is in those years when he wrote under Tina Brown for The New Yorker was just a remarkable achievement, and his career is still going strong.

对于盖茨而言，正如上周的伊莱恩·肖沃尔特以及更早的伍尔夫一样，围绕身份认同概念的问题依然存在。身份认同——当然，对于那些渴望发出声音、渴望在文学和文化领域占有一席之地的人来说，它是思想的重要锚点——然而，正如我们已经开始注意到的，它至少在某种程度上是一种流沙。实际上，有两个问题一直困扰着身份认同问题。其一是“本质化”问题，我接下来会讨论这个问题；其二是所谓的身份队列问题，我接下来会讨论这个问题。换句话说，我是一个来自巴勒斯坦的下层阶级黑人女同性恋女权主义者。毋庸置疑，我有很多身份选择，但结果是我必须弄清楚哪一个优先。换句话说，我认为这些身份中，哪一个具有内在的完整性和本质性，能够激励我的其他身份的特征，从而使其他身份在某种程度上被排在后面呢？

Now for Gates, as for Elaine Showalter last week and for Woolf before her, the problems surrounding the concept of identity persist. Identity–which of course is an important anchor for the thinking of people who feel the need for voices, for a place in the literary and cultural horizon–is nevertheless at least potentially, as we’ve begun to notice already, a kind of quicksand. There are two problems really that dog the issue of identity. One of them is the problem of “essentializing” which I’ll take up now, and then, as I’ll take it up next, also the problem of what might be called the identity queue. In other words, I am a lower-class black lesbian feminist whose nation is Palestine. Needless to say, I have a variety of identity options to choose from, but the result is I’ve got to figure out which of them has priority. In other words, which of those identities do I suppose has the underlying integrity and essence, essentiality, that can motivate, as it were, the characteristics of my other identities, which are therefore somehow or another placed further down in the queue?

所以，我稍后会再谈到这个话题，但与此同时，我们称之为本质化的问题：例如，正如盖茨在第1893页右栏中所描述的那样，他非常清楚地指出，将属性（无论是正面的还是负面的）归于任何被构成或被认为是某个群体的群体都是危险的——因为当然，根据盖茨的说法，种族的概念以及是否存在种族本身就是一个问题——即使是出于荣誉，将属性归于某个种族也是有问题的，正如他在第1893页所描述的那样：

So this is a topic that I’ll come back to in a minute, but in the meantime the problem of essentializing, as we call it: for example, as Gates describes it on page 1893 in the right-hand column, where he’s very clear on the dangers of ascribing, whether positively or negatively, attributes to any group that is constituted as or thought of–because of course, the notion of race and whether there is race is in itself according to Gates problematic–the problem of ascribing attributes even honorifically to a race is, as he describes it on page 1893:

在通俗用法中，“种族”一词所定义的差异意义[我的声音终于变了][笑声][大笑]既被用来描述语言、信仰体系、艺术传统、“基因库”的差异，也被用来刻板地定义各种所谓的“自然”属性，例如节奏感、运动能力、思维能力、放高利贷和忠诚度。换句话说，显然，将刻板印象强加给可能被视为种族的不同群体——他指出，所有这些刻板印象对任何人都没有好处。

The sense of difference defined in popular usages [finally my voice is changing] [laughter] [laughs] of the termrace has been used both to describe and inscribe differences of language, belief system, artistic tradition, “gene pool,” and all sorts of supposedly “natural” attributes such as rhythm, athletic ability, cerebration, usury, and fidelity. In other words, obviously, apportioning out stereotypes to the various groups that may come forward as candidates to be races–he’s pointing out that all of these stereotypes do nobody very much good.

因此，本质化的问题——它支撑着人们想要彰显种族存在的愿望——令人深思。仔细想想。另一方面，盖茨在文章开头似乎对种族问题持一种矛盾的态度：一方面，他坦诚地谈论种族问题，就像他所描述的伊波利特·泰纳的作品那样，认为“种族”、“环境”和“文化时刻”是任何艺术或文化作品的关键决定因素。他实际上是在说：“好吧，至少现在有人在谈论种族问题了。”但与此同时，他又明显地回避种族问题的含义，以及种族存在本身的信念——这种信念可以追溯到孟德斯鸠以及泰纳等人。不过，正如我所说，他很高兴至少种族问题现在得到了讨论，这与二十世纪截然不同，当时整个种族问题都被掩盖起来，一种虚假的礼貌阻止任何人谈论这些范畴，并导致了一种观念，即我们都存在于同一个伟大的传统中，作品要么属于这个传统，要么，如果它由于某种原因显得离谱或超出了传统，就可以被推到一边，被忽视。

So the problem of essentializing, which undergirds the wish to make manifest the existence of race gives pause. Think about it. On the other hand, Gates seems to be divided at the beginning of his essay between a certain candor about race, as in the work of Hippolyte Taine that he describes, in which “race,” “milieu” and “cultural moment” are considered the key determining issues of any kind of artistic or cultural production. He says of that in effect, “Well, at least race is being talked about,” while at the same time obviously wincing away from the implications of race and from the belief that there is such a thing as race, which goes all the way back to Montesquieu and others from Taine. Nevertheless, as I say, he’s rather cheerful about the fact that at least race is being discussed, unlike the twentieth century when the whole thing is swept under the rug and a kind of ersatz and hypocritical politeness prevents anybody from talking about such categories at all, and gives rise to the idea that we all exist in the same Great Tradition, that work either belongs to that tradition or, if it for some reason seems egregious or outside the tradition, it just can be shoved aside and neglected.

这就是二十世纪人们不愿谈论种族问题的假设。因此，种族是否构成问题本身就是这个问题的一部分，而这个问题又受到更为复杂的本质化问题的困扰。例如，假设——当然，你也在肖瓦尔特的著作中读到过这一点——你赋予了别人眼中的刻板印象以积极的意义。正如盖茨在第1901页右栏顶部所言，重要的法语非洲诗人桑戈尔就是这么做的。盖茨写道：

That’s the supposition of the twentieth century when folks don’t talk about race. So the very question whether it is an issue is part of this problem that is dogged by the more complicated issue of essentializing. For example, suppose–and of course, you’ve been reading about this in Showalter as well–you ascribe positive value to what another person might call a stereotype. This is what the important Francophone African poet Senghor does, as Gates says at the top of page 1901, the right hand-column. Gates says:

当我们试图通过颠倒概念来挪用“种族”一词来指代某种本质时，例如像黑人文化运动那样（桑戈尔曾论证非洲人“我们感受，故我们存在”），我们就放弃了太多东西，例如人类共同性的基础。正如安东尼·阿皮亚所观察到的，这种做法是徒劳且危险的，因为它会进一步强化新的、怪诞的刻板印象。由此可见，在探讨种族问题时，有很多需要避开的陷阱，而盖茨显然也意识到了这一点。

When we attempt to appropriate, by inversion, race as a term for an essence, as did the Negritude movement, for example (“We feel, therefore we are,” as Senghor argued of the African), we yield too much, such as the basis of a shared humanity. Such gestures, as Anthony Appiah has observed, are futile and dangerous because of their further inscription of new and bizarre stereotypes. So you can see there are a lot of landmines to be avoided in negotiating the discourse of race, and certainly Gates is aware of them.

第三章 “身份线索”问题

Chapter 3. The Problem of the “Identity Cue”

正如我所说，现在还存在身份认同问题，盖茨本人可能偶尔也会遇到这个问题，因为正如我开头所说，他与非裔美国批评传统中的女权主义之间存在着一种不安的缓和关系。例如，在第1894页，有一段似乎与身份认同问题相关的段落，大约在左侧栏的三分之一处，他写道：

Now there’s also the problem, as I say, of the identity queue, and Gates himself may have a little difficulty with this, at least from time to time, because as I said at the beginning, he does have this sort of uneasy détente with feminism in the African-American critical tradition still to work within. So for example, on page 1894, a somewhat problematic passage in which the identity queue seems to be at issue, about a third of the way down, the left-hand column, he says:

简而言之，性别差异所蕴含的生物学意义，在谈论“种族差异”时既不存在也不可能存在。然而，我们却常常不加思索地使用语言，将这种自然差异的概念强加于我们的表述之中。因此，他实际上是在说，从生物学的角度来看，两性之间确实存在差异，但从生物学的角度来看，所谓的原始种族之间未必存在差异。结果是，至少在女权主义传统中谈论男女时，我们必须直面实际差异的问题；而在种族话语的传统中谈论黑人和白人时，我们实际上根本没有在谈论真正的差异。因此，两者之间更具完整性的论述，是那些讨论绝对短暂的差异的论述，而不是那些无论人们如何看待、如何解读，都不可或缺的差异的论述。

The sanction of biology contained in sexual difference, simply put, does not and can never obtain when one is speaking of “racial difference.” Yet we carelessly use language in such a way as to will this sense of naturaldifference into our formulations. So what he’s saying is in biological terms there’s definitely a difference between the sexes, but in biological terms there is not necessarily a difference among the so-called primary races. The result is that at least when one speaks of women and men in the feminist tradition, one has to come face to face with the problem of actual difference; whereas when one speaks of black and white in the traditions of discourse about race, one isn’t actually talking about a genuine difference at all. Therefore the discourse with the greater integrity of the two is the one which is about differences that are absolutely ephemeral, as opposed to the one which is about differences, which, whatever one thinks of them and whatever one wants to make out of them, are nevertheless essential.

显然，当我们回到女性主义批评，特别是朱迪斯·巴特勒的性别理论时，我们会发现，关于性别的生物学基础，即两性之间的生物学差异——这正是我们接下来要讨论的核心——的整个问题，当然是一个备受质疑的问题。这不仅是因为所谓的跨性别议题，同时也是因为，根据巴特勒的观点，我们的性身份本身就是一种……

Now plainly when we go back to feminist criticism, particularly the gender theory of Judith Butler, we’ll see of course that the whole question of the biological basis of sex, the biological difference between the sexes which essentializes what we will be wanting to talk about, is of course something that is profoundly in question, and not just because of so-called trans-gender issues but also, at the same time, because of the way in which our very sexual identity is something which, according to Bu

第四章 托尼·莫里森与非裔美国人身份认同

Chapter 4. Tony Morrison and African-American Identity

我们构建的，远不止于此。因此，这里强调的是这两种身份认同讨论方式之间的生物学差异，而这种差异在我们看来或许是有问题的，或许没有问题。

tler, we construct. So there is an insistence here on a biological difference between these two forms of discussing identity which may or may not seem to us to be problematic.

现在，我认为我们终于可以理解我请大家阅读的托妮·莫里森那篇非凡文章的重要性了。我们当然最熟悉的是她作为小说家的身份，但她也是一位杰出的评论家，正如她曾担任其他重要作品的杰出编辑一样。在我看来，她的思考在某种程度上为我们提供了一个摆脱我之前一直在谈论的困境——本质主义问题和身份认同问题——的途径。因为莫里森想要表达的是——我认为她在这里尤其借鉴了黑格尔《精神现象学》中关于主奴辩证法的著名论述——身份认同与其说是“是什么”的问题，不如说是“不是什么”的问题。她认为，我们不应过分关注身为黑人的意义，而应思考黑人身份如何被铭刻于白人传统之中——当我们思考这个问题时，我们需要思考白人不是什么：换句话说，正如她反复强调的，黑人并非缺席、否定或消极的象征。我们必须理解——而这正是她从主奴辩证法出发展开论证的出发点——在构建白人身份的过程中，非裔美国人的存在，尤其是美国文化传统中大部分时期奴隶的存在，作为一种缺席和缺失，是绝对必要的。

Now I think this is the point at which we can see the importance of the extraordinary essay that I’ve also asked you to read, by Toni Morrison. We know her best, of course, as a novelist, but she’s also a distinguished critic, as she has been a distinguished editor of other important work. Here it seems to me that her reflections in some ways give us a sideways exit from the predicaments that I have been talking about, the problem of essentialism and the problem of the identity queue, because what Morrison wants to say–and I think she borrows here particularly from the famous discussion of the master-slave dialectic in Hegel’s Phenomenology of Mind–what Morrison wants to say is that identity isn’t so much a question of what something is but rather a question of what it is not. She says not that we should be so much preoccupied with what it is to be black, but rather that, as we think about the way in which being black is inscribed within the white tradition–as we think about that, we need to think about what white is not: in other words, as she says repeatedly, about black as absence, as negation, as negativity. We have to understand the absolute–and this is where she drives her argument from the master-slave dialectic–the absolute necessity in the construction of white identity for there to be, as an absence and as a lack over against white identity, the existence of the African American and, more particularly, for the better part of the American cultural tradition, of the slave.

那么，让我引用她在第1795页左侧栏的文章中的一段话：

Let me quote then from her essay on page 1795, the left-hand column, where she says:

在对“黑人”身份的建构中（此处已深入三分之一），奴役不仅体现了“不自由”，也体现了“非我”的投射。其结果为想象力提供了一个游乐场。为了缓解内心的恐惧并为外部剥削辩护，集体需求催生了一种独特的美国式非洲主义——一种由黑暗、他者性、警觉和欲望交织而成的虚构产物。她指出，尽管她的研究对象是美国传统，但欧洲也存在一种非洲主义，其对应物存在于欧洲自身的殖民文学中。为了佐证这一点，她举了一个非凡的例子，这个例子想必会让熟悉福克纳的人想起托马斯·萨特本，或者至少在某些方面想起托马斯·萨特本——邓巴这个人物，他实际上并非从沼泽中崛起，而是从苏格兰启蒙运动中崛起，来到美国，并且——根据她引用的历史学家伯纳德·贝林的说法——彻底改变了自己的性格。我不会引用贝林原文中阐明莫里森想要从中得出什么结论的长篇段落，而是引用莫里森在第 1796 页（右栏顶部）的总结：

In that construction of blackness [this is a third of the way down] and enslavement could be found not only the not-free but also the projection of the not-me. The result was a playground for the imagination. And what rose up out of collective needs to allay internal fears and rationalize external exploitation was an Africanism–a fabricated brew of darkness, otherness, alarm and desire–that is uniquely American. Then she points out that although her subject is the American tradition, there also exists a European Africanism with its counterpart in its own colonial literature. To reinforce this, she takes a remarkable example which must have reminded you, those of you who know Faulkner, of Thomas Sutpen or at least reminded you in some ways of Thomas Sutpen–the example of this character Dunbar, who actually rose up not so much out of the swamp as out of the Scottish Enlightenment and came to the United States and–according to Bernard Bailyn, the historian from whom she cites her information–became a completely transformed character. I won’t quote to you the long passage from Bailyn’s text which makes what Morrison wants to take from it clear, but rather from what Morrison summarizes of it on page 1796, the top of the right-hand column:

我认为威廉·邓巴的故事简洁地描绘了美国人作为新兴的、白人的、男性的形象是如何形成的。这种形成带来了诸多诱人的结果，贝林在对邓巴性格的总结中都提到了这些结果，并指出这些结果都源于邓巴“内心”的感受——“一种力量，一种他以前从未体验过的自由感”。顺便一提，这与古希腊文化中对奴隶制度的合理化有着惊人的相似之处。古希腊人总是说，他们拥有奴隶是为了获得自由：换句话说，在古希腊人看来，奴隶制是为了让统治阶级从维持生命、维系社会运转的日常劳作中解放出来。也就是说，在古希腊城邦的公民看来，自由意味着摆脱劳动。

I take this [William Dunbar] to be a succinct portrait of the process by which the American as new, white, and male was constituted. It is a formation that has several attractive consequences, all of which are referred to in Bailyn’s summation of Dunbar’s character and located in how Dunbar feels “within himself”–“a power, a sense of freedom he had not known before.” This is uncannily parallel by the way to the rationalization for slaves in Greek culture. The Greeks always said that the reason they had slaves was so they could be free: in other words so that the home or ruling population was liberated in the case of the Greeks from performing the daily necessities that are life sustaining and keep us going. In other words, to be free according to the citizen of the Greek polis is to be free from work.

从某种意义上说，这仍然是托尼·莫里森在美国奴隶制传统中看到的合理化，但在邓巴的例子中，这并非摆脱劳动的自由。这是一种更广泛、更隐蔽的自由观念：摆脱责任的自由，摆脱承认“他者”也是人的自由——换句话说，摆脱苏格兰和伦敦旧世界文明所施加的种种约束的自由；在这片边疆、这片荒野、这片沼泽中，可以随心所欲地做任何你想做的事。而这种自由，却是建立在黑奴的血汗之上的。正如我所说，它在某些方面与古希腊奴隶制的合理化相似，但在某种程度上，它更加隐蔽，而且——用莫里森的话来说——也更具辩证性。也就是说，问题在于，如果没有黑色的缺失，一个人是否能够变成白人；如果没有某种可以被压迫的东西——就像弹簧盒里的弹簧一样——那么，白色的弹簧盒里的玩具是否能够因为下方被压制的东西而跳出来。

Now in a certain way, this is still a rationalization that Tony Morrison sees in the American slave-owning tradition, but it’s not so much in the case of this Dunbar a freedom from work. It’s a more broad and insidious idea of freedom: freedom from responsibility, freedom from the need to acknowledge otherness as human–freedom, in other words, from the sorts of constraint imposed by old world civility in Scotland and in London; freedom on this frontier, in this wilderness, in this swamp, simply to be whatever one wants to be. That freedom is achieved on the backs of the black slaves. It is in some ways similar, as I say, to the rationalization for slavery in Greece, but it is in a way more insidious and certainly more–in the terms that Morrison’s giving it to us in–more dialectical. That is to say, it is the question of whether a person could become white without the availability of a black absence, of that which can be oppressed– like a kind of spring for the jack-in-the-box–which allows the white jack-in-the-box to leap out of the box because of that which has been suppressed down below.

第五章 莫里森对《哈克贝利·费恩历险记》的解读

Chapter 5. Morrison’s Reading of Huckleberry Finn

所有这些都是托妮·莫里森关注的焦点，也影响了她对《哈克贝利·费恩历险记》的解读——当然，这种解读无疑颇具争议性——但依我看来，它却蕴含着相当深刻的意义。每当有人指责《哈克贝利·费恩历险记》时，我的第一反应往往是感到不适，因为它是一部非凡的小说。它之所以在一些学区被禁，主要是因为其中使用了“N”字（我们稍后会再谈到），以及谁有权使用“N”字（正如我们将看到的，这并非一个容易回答的问题）。但这场争议虽然有其合理之处，但在文学层面和想象力方面，无疑显得相当局限。

All of that is part of Toni Morrison’s concern, and it colors her, well, certainly controversial reading of Huckleberry Finn–which nevertheless, it seems to me, has a quite profound interest. Now my own first instinct when people single outHuckleberry Finn for blame is to wince away, because it’s an extraordinary novel. The controversy about it in the school districts which made it a banished book had mainly to do with the “N-word,” to which we’ll return, and the question of who has the right to use the “N-word,” which is not an easy question to answer, as we’ll see. But that controversy, while it had an authentic basis, was nevertheless certainly in literary terms and in terms of the imagination perhaps rather limited.

莫里森提出了另一种同样深刻批判《哈克贝利·费恩历险记》的思考方式。她认为，解放吉姆——这当然是小说结尾处最大的失败，是汤姆·索亚想象力的匮乏，也是哈克自身意志或独立思考能力的缺失——这种解放吉姆的失败（这本是世上最容易的事，因为他们只需指出河流的正确岔路口）对于汤姆、哈克乃至马克·吐温本人持续不断地自我定义“白人身份”而言，都是绝对必要的。他不知道该如何结束这部小说。他写完之后，小说就一直放在他的桌子上，因为他实在想不出该如何处理它，最终他写出了这个——我们都认同的——令人震惊的结尾。托妮·莫里森认为这是唯一可行的结局，因为在她看来，小说的感伤主义，以及哈克和吉姆之间强烈的情感——这种情感如此强烈，以至于另一位评论家莱斯利·菲德勒（Leslie Fiedler）甚至谈到了他们之间的同性恋情愫——都掩盖了马克·吐温小说中基本的意识结构，而正是这种基本结构使得吉姆的自由成为绝对必要的。如果吉姆获得了自由，那么白人身份就无法与“他者”相对立来定义自身。这就是她运用美国文学传统这一普遍论点来解读《哈克贝利·费恩历险记》的方式。

Morrison gives rise to another equally and intensely critical way of thinking about Huckleberry Finn. She argues that to liberate Jim–which of course is the tremendous failure at the end of the novel, a failure of imagination on the part of Tom Sawyer and a failure of will or independence of mind on the part of Huck himself–that the failure to liberate Jim, which would have been the easiest thing in the world, because all they had to do was point out the right fork in the river, is an absolute necessity for the ongoing self-definition of whiteness as it’s available both to Tom and to Huck and, after all, by implication, to Mark Twain himself. He couldn’t figure out how to end the novel. He wrote it, then it lay on his desk for a long time because he just couldn’t figure out what to do with it, and he finally comes up with this–as we all agree–appalling ending. Toni Morrison says it’s the only ending available because in ways that the, as she sees it, sentimentality of the novel and the sentimentality of the relationship between Huck and Jim, which is so strong that it caused another critic named Leslie Fiedler to talk about a homoerotic relation between them–the title of Fiedler’s famous essay is “Come Up on the Raft, Huck, Honey”–with all of that in the background, Toni Morrison says the basic structure of consciousness in Twain’s novel is obscured, a basic structure which makes it absolutely imperative that Jim not be free. If Jim is free, then there is no Other over against which whiteness can define itself. That’s the way in which she makes use of the general argument about the traditions of American literature in culture in applying it to Huckleberry Finn.

第六章 盖茨与非裔美国批评家群体

Chapter 6. Gates and the Community of African-American Critics

好的。咱们还是回到斯基普·盖茨（Skip Gates）——抱歉，这是亨利·路易斯·盖茨（Henry Louis Gates）的昵称——他也是耶鲁大学的校友，我跟他很熟。其实，“能指猴”（signifying monkey）这个概念的起源我略有参与；稍后我会再细说。芭芭拉·约翰逊（Barbara Johnson，她现在也在哈佛大学任教）和我当时跟斯基普就这个概念进行了很多次交流，所以这并不是说我独占了这个想法——毕竟这是斯基普的主意——但我参与其中，所以这并非是在炫耀人脉。我得用他朋友们对他的称呼来称呼他。不过，我还是尽量记住要说亨利·路易斯·盖茨，总之，现在我们还是回到他身上来吧。

All right. Let’s go back to Skip Gates–Henry Louis Gates’s nickname, sorry–another person who was at Yale and whom I knew very well. I actually had a little bit to do with the origin of the notion of the signifying monkey; I’ll come back to that later. Barbara Johnson, also now at Harvard, and I had a lot of conversations with Skip at that period about this, and so it’s not that I feel proprietary–it’s Skip’s idea–but I was in on that, and so it’s not just name dropping. I get to call him by what his friends call him. However, I’ll try to remember to say Henry Louis Gates, and in any case to return to him now.

在深入探讨这个至关重要的核心问题之前，我想先简单谈谈他对非裔美国文学传统的理解——包括批评传统和文学传统。首先，他对批评传统的理解基本上是一个两步或两阶段的演进，这一点与上次伊莱恩·肖瓦尔特的观点不谋而合。大家可能还记得，肖瓦尔特说过，女性主义介入文学批评的重要运动始于她所谓的“女性主义”时刻：也就是说，始于凯特·米利特和其他一些作家开始探讨男性作品中女性遭受的贬低和不公待遇的时刻。随后，肖瓦尔特认为更重要的“女性主义批评”——即女性对文学传统的挪用，以及她们对女性文学经典的档案研究工作。这些研究工作使得女性文学经典不再仅仅是从一个伟大作家跳到另一个伟大作家，而是如肖瓦尔特所说，是一个逐年展开、持续发展的过程。

Before moving on to this crucial central issue, I want to talk a little bit simply about his understanding and the understanding of others of the African-American tradition–both of the critical tradition and of the literary tradition. First of all, the grasp of the critical tradition as basically a two-step or two-part progression is something that he shares with Elaine Showalter from last time. You remember Showalter says that the important movement of feminist interventions in literary criticism begins with the moment that she calls “feminist”: that is to say, the moment of Kate Millett and other authors who talk about the degradation and unfair treatment of women in male books, and then what Showalter prefers and supposes to have supervened and to have become more important, “gynocritical criticism,” which is women’s appropriation of literary traditions for themselves, the archival work that makes the canon of women’s literature not just leaping from great name to great name, but an actual unfolding and continuous development from decade to decade, as Showalter puts it.

现在，盖茨在第1896页右侧空白处，对非裔美国人批评的发展也持类似观点。盖茨说，基本上可以做两件事。他没有按时间顺序排列，但你可以将同样的时间顺序与他在这里所说的对应起来。他说：

Now Gates on page 1896, the right-hand margin, sees it in much the same way for the development of African-American criticism. You can do two things basically, says Gates. He doesn’t put them chronologically, but you could map onto what he’s saying here the same chronological sequence. He says:

我引用这两个被用滥的词（他尤其指的是“他者”）的目的正是为了说明这一点：黑人在文学作品中是如何被塑造的（也就是说，他们在文学作品中是如何被描绘的，无论是贬低的还是或许带有荣誉感的），以及黑人如何塑造他们自己创作的文学作品。（换句话说，你可以看到他在思考这些问题时采取了同样的思路。）正如肖瓦尔特所论证的那样，文学传统的问题更为复杂，它包含更多阶段。换句话说，女性从创作之初所拥有的自我表达能力，经历了不止两个阶段，非裔美国文学也是如此。现在我认为，盖茨只是想当然地将我们另一位耶鲁同事迈克尔·库克（Michael Cooke）在《批判性探究》（Critical Inquiry）上发表的一篇文章的前提视为理所当然。库克在发表这篇文章的前一年，也就是他发表在《批判性探究》上的文章中，论述了非裔美国文学的历史基本上经历了四个阶段。库克称之为“自我遮蔽”的时期：换句话说，在这个时期，那些首次尝试写作的人——当然，盖茨也谈到了写作对于黑人而言实际上是将自己融入人类社群的过程——最初尝试写作的人都以白人为榜样。盖茨提到的诗人菲利斯·惠特利是一位杰出的诗人，也是一位非常有趣的诗人，但她的写作风格却深受亚历山大·蒲柏的影响，以至于她的许多作品几乎无法与蒲柏的作品区分开来——这当然是一种赞扬。她是库克所说的“自我掩饰”这一第一阶段的典型代表。

What I mean by citing these two overworked terms [he’s talking about “the other” in particular] is precisely this: how blacks are figures in literature [that is to say, how they’re represented in literature, demeaningly, even perhaps honorifically], and also how blacks figure, as it were, literature of their own making. [You can see, in other words, the same movement in his thinking about these issues.] As Showalter argued too, the question of the literary tradition is more complicated; it has more steps. In other words, the powers of self-expression available to women from the beginning of their creative expression passed through more than just two stages, and the same thing is true of African-American literature. Now I think that Gates simply takes for granted as an implicit premise of the work that was done the year before he published this essay in Critical Inquiry by another colleague of ours here at Yale–who died tragically not too long thereafter–named Michael Cooke, who in 1984 wrote a book called Afro-American Literature in the Twentieth Century: The Achievement of Intimacy. Cooke argued in this book that the history of African-American literature passes essentially through four stages. It begins with what Cooke calls “self-veiling”: the period, in other words, in which people attempting for the first time to write–and of course Gates talks about the way in which writing is really writing oneself into the human community for black people–the people who first attempted to write used white models. Phillis Wheatley, the poet whom Gates talks about, a remarkable poet and a very interesting one, nevertheless wrote in the manner of Alexander Pope, so much so that a great deal of her work is almost impossible–which is course a point of praise–to distinguish from that of Alexander Pope. She is an instance of the first phase, which Cooke calls “self-veiling.”

库克称之为“孤独”的第二阶段，指的是继续沿用白人模式、白人散文风格以及叙事方式——这种叙事方式显然源于白人教师和白人榜样，但其核心主题却是自我定义。在这里，我们可以联想到道格拉斯以及一般的奴隶叙事，这些叙事强调接受白人的教导，但其中仍然存在一种张力，这种张力奠定并支配着自我解放和自我自由的可能性。换言之，奴隶叙事作为一种持续发展的形式，参与了库克所理解的非裔美国文学发展的第二阶段。

The second phase, which Cooke calls “solitude,” involves continuing to use white models, a white prose style, a way of narrating which is obviously derived from white teachers and white models but which nevertheless involves, as its central theme, self-definition. Here you might want to think of Douglass and of slave narratives in general, where the emphasis is on being taught by white people, but nevertheless there is a tension which exists and which founds and governs the possibility of self-liberation and self-freedom. In other words, the slave narrative as an ongoing form partakes of this second phase in the development of African-American literature as Cooke understands it.

第三，库克称之为“亲缘关系”的文学，在这一阶段，非裔美国人彼此联结，将自己视为一个社群，而非为自由而奋斗的个体。库克认为，这一阶段的特点是方言的实验性运用，以及一种自觉强调语言差异的叙事和诗歌创作方式。例如，兰斯顿·休斯的许多诗歌，以及哈莱姆文艺复兴时期的许多其他作品，都体现了这一点；这就是第三阶段，亲缘关系。

Thirdly, there is what Cooke calls “kinship,” a literature in which African Americans reach out to each other, identify themselves as a community, not as individuals struggling to be free but rather as a community. Cooke identifies this phase with the experimentation with dialect and a way of narrating and poetizing which involves a self-conscious insistence on verbal and linguistic difference. You can think of many of the poems, for example, of Langston Hughes in this regard and of a great deal else that goes on in the Harlem Renaissance; so that’s the third phase, kinship.

最后阶段——我想说的是，盖茨认为我们还没有达到这个阶段。换句话说，库克和盖茨之间的分歧点恰恰在于此。库克称之为“亲密性”的最后一个阶段，指的是可以自由地挪用任何模式，也就是说，并非一定要坚持将自身的创作范式视为一种种族传统，而是可以挪用任何唾手可得的资源。例如，埃里森的《看不见的人》就是一部现代主义杰作。换句话说，它自由地借鉴了所有唾手可得、最容易获得的、适合埃里森创作类型的传统。库克或许过于乐观地将此与他所谓的“亲密性”联系起来：换句话说，这是一种融合，一种最终实现的传统融合，以至于——这显然也是弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫的理想——人们不再需要以代言人的身份写作。人们不再需要关注写作所源于的身份认同主题。人们可以随心所欲地写作——换句话说，这是一种乌托邦式的愿景，即“无论我是谁，我都可以自由地运用任何我感兴趣的形式和主题”。

Then the last phase–and what I’m going to want to say is that Gates doesn’t think we’ve reached this. In other words, the point of disagreement between Cooke and Gates is precisely about this. The last phase, which Cooke calls “intimacy,” is the freedom to expropriate any and all models, not in other words to insist necessarily on one’s own creative paradigms as a racial tradition but to expropriate anything that comes ready to hand. Ellison’s Invisible Man, for example, is a masterpiece of High Modernism. It takes freely, in other words, from whatever traditions come to hand and are most readily available for the kind of work that Ellison wants to do. Cooke identifies this perhaps rather optimistically with what he calls “intimacy”: in other words, a merger, a finally achieved merger of traditions such that–and this is plainly the ideal of Virginia Woolf as well–such that one no longer has to write as a spokesperson. One no longer needs to be concerned with thematizing the kinds of identity out of which one’s writing has arisen. One can write just anything one wants to–in other words, the utopian vision of “no matter who I am, I have access to absolutely any forms and themes I care to work with.”

这就是迈克尔·库克的愿景，我认为盖茨遗憾地认为我们尚未完全达到这一境界，这也是我特意在谈到库克第四阶段时使用“挪用”一词的原因。如果我使用自身传统之外的模式，我并非凭空捏造，而是经过深思熟虑的。我选择模式时总是有其目的。我们尚未真正达到亲密关系，因为自我定义仍然是一个问题。你可以尽情谈论《看不见的人》中的“高度现代主义”，但请思考一下《看不见的人》的本质。《看不见的人》仍然在探讨身为黑人的意义。“伪装”是什么？换句话说，拥有这种种族身份意味着什么？所以，是的：传统、礼仪、风格都被剥夺了，但与此同时，非裔美国人的写作事业仍在继续，而且，归根结底，这和以往一样，都是一个自我定义的问题。

That is the vision of Michael Cooke, which Gates, I think, unfortunately, rightly feels that we haven’t quite arrived at, and that’s why I deliberately used the word “expropriate” in talking about Cooke’s fourth phase. If I use models other than models made available by my own tradition, I’m not just kind of pulling them out of the air. I’m using them with a calculated purpose. I always have something in mind in choosing the model that I choose. We’re not really quite at intimacy because self-definition is still at issue. You can talk about the High Modernism of the Invisible Man all you like, but think of what the Invisible Man is about. The Invisible Man is still about what it means to be black. What is “passing”? What does it mean in other words to have this racial identity? So that, yes: traditions, manners, styles have been expropriated, but at the same time the business of writing as an African American continues, and it is as much, after all, a question of self-definition as it has been hitherto.

在盖茨看来，这仍然是个问题。我们借鉴了其他模式，但我们需要将它们内化为己用。否则，我们就会被它们所殖民，最终又回到了原点，对吧？我们又回到了自我遮蔽的状态，因为菲利斯·惠特利毕竟也借鉴了其他模式。菲利斯·惠特利实际上渴望成为一位诗人。她可以写任何她想写的东西——理查德·威尔逊画作中尼俄柏的眼泪——无论是什么，她都可以写，因为她只是一位诗人。这是她最大的愿望，她不想被视为一个了不起的人物，一个会写作的年轻黑人女奴。她对那不感兴趣。她只想成为一名诗人，所以从某种意义上说，问题就在这里。如果亲密关系在第四阶段得以实现，那么，这最终只是菲利斯·惠特利在第一阶段想要的东西的实现，[笑] 我们必须承认，由于这些评论家所阐述的所有复杂原因，这并不是一个可以说已经实现的时刻。

As Gates sees it, it continues to be the issue. We use other models. We need to make them our own. Otherwise we’re just colonized by them, and then after all we’re back in phase one, right? We’re back in self-veiling because, after all, Phillis Wheatley used other models. Phillis Wheatley actually aspired to the idea that she was just a poet. She could write about anything she wanted to write about–the tears of Niobe in the painting by Richard Wilson–whatever it might be, she could write about it because she was just a poet. That was her great aspiration, to be received not as that amazing thing, a young black slave woman who could write. She wasn’t interested in that. She wanted to be a poet, and so in a certain sense you can see the problem. If intimacy is achieved in the fourth phase, well, then that’s finally just the realization of what Phillis Wheatley wanted in the first phase, [laughs] and we have to admit, for all of the complicated reasons that these critics go into, that this is not a moment which can be said yet to have been achieved.

第七章 征用

Chapter 7. Expropriation

好的。现在我们来谈谈盖茨的关键概念：挪用他人的传统，尤其是白人的传统，意味着什么？这样做有什么好处？毕竟，盖茨主要思考的是批评。我们如何用白人的语言进行理论研究和批评？我们如何挪用或挪用白人的语言？第1891页那段引自巴赫金的精彩题词强调了为己所用的必要性。顺便说一句，在我看来，这段文字在巴赫金的著作中占据着核心地位，甚至超过了我们之前研读巴赫金时所学的任何内容。我希望你们记下这段文字，因为它确实能够阐明巴赫金著作中许多我们当时可能没有完全理解的内容。巴赫金是这样说的：

Okay. Now this brings us to Gates’s key concept: what does it mean to expropriate other people’s traditions, more particularly the white tradition, and what is the advantage of doing so? Here Gates is after all thinking primarily about criticism. How can we do theory and criticism in the white man’s language? How can we appropriate or expropriate for ourselves the white man’s language? The necessity of bending language to one’s own purposes is what is emphasized in the remarkable epigraph on page 1891 that Gates takes from Bakhtin. This is, it seems to me, as central a passage in Bakhtin, by the way, as anything that we studied when we were actually reading Bakhtin, and I’d like you to make note of it because I think it really can illuminate a great deal that’s going on in Bakhtin that we didn’t perhaps fully articulate at the time. This is what Bakhtin says:

……对于个体意识而言，语言处于自我与他者的边界。语言中的词语一半属于他人。只有当说话者赋予它自己的意图和语调（你可以听出盖茨想要强调“语调”这个词），当他挪用词语，使其符合自己的语义和表达意图时，它才成为“自己的”。在此挪用之前，词语并不存在于中立且客观的语言中（毕竟，说话者并非从字典中获取词语！）[多么精辟]，而是存在于他人的口中，存在于他人的语境中，服务于他人的意图：正是从那里，人们必须汲取词语，使其成为“自己的”。事实上，盖茨在他的文章中呼应了巴赫金的这种观点，他在第 1901 页右栏的最上方引用了德里达的话，他说：“我们必须掌握，正如德里达所写的那样，‘如何在不放弃（我们）自己语言的情况下说对方的语言’。”

… language, for the individual consciousness, lies on the borderline between oneself and the other. The word in language is half someone else’s. It becomes “one’s own” only when the speaker populates it with his own intention, his own accent [and you can hear Gates wanting to emphasize that word “accent”], when he appropriates the word, adapting it to his own semantic and expressive intention. Prior to this moment of appropriation, the word does not exist in a neutral and impersonal language (it is not, after all, out of a dictionary that the speaker gets his words!) [how true], but rather it exists in other people’s mouths, in other people’s contexts, serving other people’s intentions: it is from there that one must take the word, and make it “one’s own.” Now actually during the course of his essay, Gates echoes this sentiment of Bakhtin by quoting Derrida at the very top of the right-hand column on page 1901, where he says, “We must master, as Derrida wrote, ’how to speak the other’s language without renouncing (our) own.”

那么，该如何做到这一点呢？该如何运用你所掌握的语言呢？这当然不仅仅是种族差异的问题，而是我们彼此之间关系的问题。正如巴赫金在你已读过的文章中所说，大多数时候我们都在说别人的语言。我们很少能像创作作家那样，觉得自己已经将别人的语言从其惯常用法中解放出来，并将其转化为我们自己的语言，稍加改写，使其真正属于我们自己。更广义地说，这就是任何理论传统或理论事业所面临的挑战，它不想仅仅沦为他人理论的衍生品。

Now how do you do this? How do you set about talking the language you are given? This isn’t, of course, just a question of the difference between the races. It’s a question of all of us in relation to each other. As Bakhtin says in what you have already read, most of the time we’re speaking other people’s languages. It is rare indeed that we can say, feeling very much like creative writers when we do so, that we have somehow wrenched other people’s language out of its conventional usages and made it our own, slightly rewritten it so that it is truly our own. So more broadly speaking, this is the challenge that faces a theoretical tradition or a theoretical enterprise, I should say, that doesn’t want to be just derivative from what other folks have already said.

盖茨在此提出的概念，毕竟他（和肖沃尔特一样）都意识到，符号的概念很可能是白人男性文学理论的基石——他意识到，为了进行这种挪用行为，他必须对符号的概念进行某种处理，因此他探讨了人们如何对某事物进行符号化。他在第1900页，也就是右栏的顶部附近，非常平静地引入了这个概念，似乎只是顺带提及：

The concept that Gates brings to bear on this, because after all he recognizes, as does Showalter too, that the notion of the sign is probably the cornerstone of white male literary theory–he recognizes that in order to perform this expropriative act, he’s got to do something with the notion of the sign, and so he talks about the way in which one cansignify on something. He introduces it very quietly on page 1900, the right-hand column, just seemingly in passing, near the top of the right-hand column:

根据休谟的说法，书写是区分动物和人类的最终标志，因此这些作家实际上是在对锁链本身进行“指称”（signifyin(g)）……注意重音。你不一定要发“g”音：他们实际上是在对锁链进行“指称”（signifyin' on the chain）。当然，这条等级分明的伟大存在之链与锁链帮的垂直链条截然不同，不是吗？它与束缚奴隶的锁链也截然不同。这就是“指称”的含义之一。至少在白人男性理论传统中，“能指”仅仅是语言差异博弈中的一个占位符。至于这种博弈的潜在社会学和文化基础，以及这种博弈的形成方式，却被忽略了——再次强调，这只是“据称”——因为——嗯，从我们一直以来所说的内容来看，你可能已经明白，这有点过于简化了，但这确实是他们所持的立场。总之，因此你需要获取能指并对其表示意义。

Since writing, according to Hume, was the ultimate sign of difference between animal and human, these writers implicitly were Signifyin(g) upon the figure of the chain itself… Notice the accent. You don’t necessarily pronounce the g: they were signifyin’ on the chain. Of course, the great chain of being, which is hierarchical, is very different from the vertical chain of the chain gang, isn’t it? It’s very different from the chain that holds slaves together. That’s part of what it means to “signify on” something. At least allegedly, the “signifier” in the white male theoretical tradition is just a kind of placeholder in a play of linguistic differences. The question of the underlying sociological and cultural basis of this play and of the way in which this play takes shape isn’t taken into account–again, allegedly–because–well, in ways that you can probably grasp from what we’ve said all along, this is slightly to oversimplify, but this is the position taken up. In any case, you therefore need to take the signifier and signifyon it.

那么，究竟什么是“指点”呢？盖茨从非洲民间故事中汲取了“骗子”这一概念，在非洲的民间故事里，弱者往往更聪明。比如猴子或蜘蛛阿南西——你们有些人可能还记得小时候拉菲唱的关于阿南西的歌——猴子或蜘蛛戏弄那些强大的坏蛋，比如大象和狮子。所有坏蛋都被骗是因为他们愚蠢，而弱小的家伙总能用“指点”的方式欺骗​​他们，让他们在不知不觉中被蒙蔽。这种关于“指点”的说法非常符合非裔美国人的民间传说传统，它最早出现在奥斯卡·布朗二世（Oscar Brown Jr.）创作的歌曲《指点猴子》（The Signifyin' Monkey）中，这首歌由他本人创作。如果我会唱歌，我一定会唱给你们听。幸运的是，我不会唱歌，但这首歌却风靡一时，被各种爵士乐器乐队采用，成为五六十年代爵士乐传统中的经典曲目。无论如何，盖茨的文章标题正是源于奥斯卡·布朗二世的“能指猴”概念，他也正是从中汲取了灵感，将他人的话语从其原本的语境中抽离出来，并坚持将其融入非裔美国人的语境——换句话说，融入一个属于自己的语境，而不仅仅是别人赋予自己的语境。

Well, what is it to signify on something? This is an expression that Gates takes from the trickster tradition, the tradition of African storytelling in which the weaker is also the smarter, and the monkey or Anansi the Spider–some of you may remember the songs of Rafi from your childhood about Anansi the Spider–in which the monkey or the spider tricks the big, bad guys, the elephant, the lion. All of the bad guys get tricked because they are stupider, and the little guy is always able to signify on them, to trick them, and to lie to them without their realizing what’s going on. This way of talking about signifying is very much in the tradition of African-American folklore and first comes to public consciousness in a song by the scat singer Oscar Brown, Jr., written by Oscar Brown, Jr., called “The Signifyin’ Monkey.” If I could sing, I’d sing it to you. Fortunately, I can’t sing, but it became extremely popular and was picked up by various instrumental jazz groups and was a staple in the jazz tradition of the fifties and sixties. In any case, Oscar Brown Jr.’s notion of the signifying monkey is where Gates takes his essay’s title from and which is where also he gets this idea of taking somebody else’s discourse out of its context and insisting on bending it into an African-American context–in other words, a context which is one’s own and not just the context one is given.

盖茨举出的另一个“象征意义”的例子是《紫色》的结尾部分，以及关于“把男人从你的眼中抹去”的对话。这实际上是在反思一个即使在非裔美国人传统内部也存在的难题。正如盖茨所指出的，惠特利和后来的丽贝卡·杰克逊都从白人男性那里汲取了教育和自我发展的模式，这些白人男性教会了她们阅读。当然，在每种情况下，这都是有害的，因为白人男性的存在仍然深深地影响着她们。你必须把男人从你的眼中抹去，至少根据盖茨引用的《紫色》中的对话是这么说的。

Now the other example of “signifyin’ on” that Gates gives is the culminating example of The Color Purple, and the conversation about “gettin’ the man out of your eye,” which is a way of taking back a problem that exists even within the African-American tradition. As Gates has been pointing out, Wheatley and later Rebecca Jackson take their models of education and self-development from white male figures who have taught them how to read. In each case of course, this is pernicious because the existence of the white male figure is very much still in your eye. You got to get the man out of your eye, at least according to the dialogue Gates quotes from The Color Purple.

有趣的是，在某种程度上，女权主义批评的问题再次困扰着盖茨的论点，因为很明显，舒格说的“那个男人”指的并非仅仅是白人男性。当然，《紫色》的一个重要主题是，一种可能从并非仅仅由种族定义的社会建构中涌现出来的女权主义；因此，当盖茨说“那个男人”时，我们都知道这是“白人男性”的简称，它既可以被非裔美国人的传统所指代，成为一个带有贬义的词语，对吧？——“把那个男人从你的眼里赶走”——同时，它也可以被女权主义的传统所指代，成为一个带有贬义的词语，虽然并非完全不同，而是以一种重叠且部分不同的方式。盖茨强调其中一种含义而非另一种含义，或许再次倾向于某种特定的立场。

Well, the interesting thing there is that in a way the issue of feminist criticism comes back to haunt Gates’s argument because plainly Shug doesn’t just mean the white man when she says “the man.” A big issue in The Color Purple, of course, is the emergence of a possible feminism from social constructions that aren’t just defined by race; so that when Gates says “the man,” which all of us recognize as shorthand for “the white man,” can be signified on by an African-American tradition, making it a term of opprobrium, right?–“get the man out of your eye”–at the same time it can be signified on by the feminist tradition, making it a term of opprobrium not in a completely different way, but in an overlapping and partially different way. Gates, in emphasizing the one as opposed to the other, is perhaps tilting again toward a certain

第八章 罗伯特·佩恩·沃伦与新批评的问题

Chapter 8. Robert Penn Warren and Problems with New Criticism

最后，我想谈谈他文章中最具争议性的例子，也是大多数读者感到愤慨的例子，它位于1893页左侧栏的底部。他一直在谈论新农业运动，这场运动涌现出许多与新批评相关的代表人物，其中包括罗伯特·佩恩·沃伦。沃伦很早就否定了新农业运动，并在自己的作品中成为一位政治进步的代表人物。你们中的许多人可能都读过他的《国王的人马》，当然也读过他的诗歌。他是新批评思想发展中的一位代表人物，一位核心人物，而我们之前也简要地探讨过新批评。

Now finally I want to take up the example, the most controversial example in his essay, one which is a source of outrage for most readers, at the bottom of page 1893 in the left-hand column. He’s been talking about the New Agrarian moment out of which there emerged a number of figures associated with the New Criticism, including Robert Penn Warren, who very early on repudiated the New Agrarians and became a politically progressive figure in his own writing. Many of you have probably read All the King’s Men, certainly, and his poetry as well. He was an avatar, a central figure, in the development of the thinking of the New Criticism, which we have briefly studied.

沃伦写了一首诗，叫做《池塘森林》（Pondy Woods）。斯特林·布朗断章取义地引用了这首诗，而且在我不打算朗读的那段文字中，他的引用也明显带有不公平的断章取义，因为我觉得我没有资格说出那个“N字”；所以，你们自己去看吧——我稍后再谈。斯特林·布朗的回应也记录在那里。问题是，对于任何真正读过这首诗的人来说——但请记住，在某种程度上，这是新批评视角提出的问题，我稍后会解释我的意思——那句话是秃鹫说的，我忘了是田纳西州还是肯塔基州。故事发生在路易斯安那州北部，那只秃鹫正满怀期待地栖息在树上，等着一个被白人追赶到沼泽里的逃亡奴隶死去。秃鹫正盘旋在那里——如果可以的话，它肯定会这么做——它正搓着手，兴高采烈地等待着这一切的发生。诗中正是这只秃鹫说的：换句话说，这与诗歌的作者沃伦毫无关系。沃伦以充满同情的笔触，描绘了逃亡奴隶在这种可怕而又令人绝望的恐慌状态下的感受。

Now Warren wrote a poem called “Pondy Woods,” which is quoted completely out of context by Sterling Brown and unfairly out of context in the passage which I’m not going to read because I don’t think I have the right to speak the “N-word”; so I’ll just have you look at it–and I’ll come back to that in a minute. Sterling Brown’s response is also recorded there for you. Well, the problem is, from the standpoint of anybody who’s actually read the poem–but remember in some ways it’s a problem raised by a New Critical perspective, and I’ll explain what I mean in a minute–that expression is spoken by a buzzard or vulture from–I forget whether it’s Tennessee or Kentucky. The episode takes place in northern Louisiana, and the buzzard is sitting expectantly on a tree waiting for a fugitive slave who has been chased into the swamp by his white pursuers to die. The vulture is sitting there–well, if it could it would be–rubbing its hands with glee waiting for this to take place. It’s the vulture that says it in the poem: nothing to do in other words, as we say, with the author of the poem, Warren, who is writing a completely sympathetic evocation of what it’s like to be a fugitive slave in this state of terrible and overwhelmed panic.

所以这看起来完全不公平，而且我认为确实不公平，因为斯特林·布朗接受了这种观点，盖茨随后也在自己的论述中延续了这种观点。不过，我想补充一点，我们援引新批评的观点来论证这种做法的不公平性。正是新批评（罗伯特·佩恩·沃伦是其参与者之一）告诉我们，不应该将诗歌中的叙述者与作者混淆。换句话说，根据新批评的观点，作者是客观冷静的人，即使在抒情诗中，作者也会引入戏剧性的声音，如果我们把这些声音与作者联系起来，只会造成混淆。

So it seems completely unfair and it is, I think, unfair as Sterling Brown took it up and as Gates then perpetuates the idea in his own reference. The one thing I would add, however, is that it’s a New Critical idea that we invoke to say that it’s unfair. It’s the New Criticism, in which Robert Penn Warren was a participant, that tells us we shouldn’t confuse speakers in poems with authors. In other words, an author is someone, according to the New Criticism, who is dispassionate and who introduces dramatic voices even in lyric poems, voices with which we are merely confusing ourselves if we associate them with an author.

现在，我们在读诗时往往会想当然地认为所有诗歌在某种程度上都是戏剧独白，就像勃朗宁和其他十九世纪诗人的作品一样。我们现在就是这样解读诗歌的，但正如我所说，这是一种新批评的观点，它最终会回到“谁有权使用‘N字’？”这个问题上。正如你所知，在非裔美国人文化中，这是一个经常在街头使用的词语，几乎带有某种亲切感，被当作一种相互问候的方式。但与此同时，这个词仍然被严格禁止，只有非裔美国人才能使用。因此，这个问题一直存在。沃伦对这个词的使用存在疑问——因为他写作的时间远早于围绕这个词的争议出现之前——这场争议真正爆发的时间点，恰恰是《哈克贝利·费恩历险记》被公立学校禁读之后，也就是很久以后。因此，沃伦使用这个词或许带有一种天真的意味。然而，在批评传统中，这是一个“谁有权使用它？”的问题。

Now this is something that we just take for granted when we read poems. All poems for us are to some degree dramatic monologues on the model of Browning and others in the nineteenth century. We read them that way now, but it is, as I say, a New Critical idea, and it comes back to the question, “Who has the right to use the ‘N-word’?” It’s a frequent term used on the street, as you know, in African-American culture, used almost with a certain fondness as a form of mutual greeting, but at the same time it is a term that continues rigorously to be rejected as available to anyone other than someone who belongs within this community. And so that issue lingers. It’s an issue that Warren–because of course he wrote long before this controversy began to arise around the word–the controversy really boiled over precisely at the time of the banning of Huckleberry Finn from public schools, much later, and so there’s a kind of innocence perhaps in Warren’s use of the word. Nevertheless, in the critical tradition it’s a question, “Who has the right to use it?”

这或许暗示了新批评思想中某种程度的封闭性。你可以使用任何你喜欢的模型：弗洛伊德的无意识模型，或者政治无意识模型。换句话说，我们这门课一直在读到，我们永远无法完全表达我们真正想表达的意思，我们永远无法完全掌控自己的话语，因为它源于无意识，对吧？现在，如果你采用这样的模型，即使盖茨引用的那句话是来自肯塔基州的讨厌秃鹫说的，但仍然存在一个作者，这句话源于它的无意识。

This gives rise perhaps to the suggestion of a certain insularity in the thinking of the New Criticism. Use any model you like: the model of the Freudian unconscious, the model of the political unconscious. In other words, we’ve been reading a lot in this course about our never quite saying what we mean to say, of our never quite being fully in control of our discourse because it bubbles up from the unconscious, right? Now if you take a model like this, even though it’s a nasty buzzard from Kentucky that’s saying what Gates quotes, nevertheless there is an author, and it has bubbled up from the unconscious of that.

那么，你打算怎么处理这件事呢？这里存在一种僵局。我们对此感受强烈而深刻，甚至可以说是愤懑——因为我喜欢沃伦，我喜欢《池塘森林》，而且我也算是新批评派——所以我们对这种挪用，对沃伦以这种方式表达的“意义化”感到愤慨。与此同时，我们也曾设想过一位潜意识的作者，他并非权威，而是一位自下而上涌现的作者。如果是这样的话，那么我们就不得不思考，这样的表达究竟是如何出现在这首诗里的。我称之为挥之不去的问题，因为在我看来，这就像那种如果盖茨没有效仿斯特林·布朗会更好的时刻，那种论证热情过头的时刻，但同时，由于我前面提到的种种原因，我们也不能完全否定它。

Well, what are you going to do with that? There’s a kind of impasse there. We feel distinctly and vividly and even bitterly–because I love Warren, I love “Pondy Woods” and I also am something of a New Critic–so we feel a bitterness about the expropriation, the “signifying on” what Warren says in this fashion. At the same time, we have entertained these ideas of a subliminal author, not an authority but an author welling up from below. If that’s the case, then we have to worry a little bit about how an expression like that got into the poem after all. I call it a lingering problem because it strikes me as one of those moments when probably it would have been better if Gates hadn’t followed Sterling Brown, one of those moments when there is a kind of overkill in the zeal of argumentation, but which at the same time we can’t absolutely dismiss out of hand for the variety of reasons that I have mentioned.

好的。我就说到这里，周四我们阅读布置给你们的后殖民批评范例时，会用新的词汇和新的形式再来探讨这些问题。

Okay. I’ll leave it there, and we’ll return to many of these issues in a new vocabulary and in new forms when we read the examples of post-colonial criticism on Thursday that you’ve been assigned.

第22讲——后殖民批评

Lecture 22 - Post-Colonial Criticism

第一章 “后殖民”一词的问题

Chapter 1. Problems With the Term “Post-Colonial”

保罗·弗莱教授：嗯，后殖民研究无疑是我们在本课程这一部分回顾的身份认同领域中最丰富多样、最包罗万象的：当然，这种包罗万象是必然的，因为涵盖的材料极其广泛，也因为后殖民研究（或人们亲切地称之为“后殖民”）内部存在着诸多纷繁复杂的问题和争议，这些问题和争议从各个角度提出了许多问题，至少可以说，它们让整个研究始终充满活力。今天，我们只探讨后殖民研究中的一个分支，一个发展分支，即从萨义德到巴巴的某种演进。这种演进相对容易梳理，只需从他们各自的理论议程来看即可，但除此之外，还有很多其他内容值得探讨。

Professor Paul Fry: Well, post-colonial studies is really by far the most varied and eclectic of the identity fields that we’re passing in review in this portion of the course: eclectic really of necessity, of course, because of the immense variety of the materials covered, but also because of swirling issues and controversies within post-colonial studies or “po-co,” as it’s affectionately known, which kind of pose a number of questions from the side that keep things lively, to say the least. We are taking up only one strand, one developmental strand, in post-colonial studies today, a kind of progression from the work of Said to the work of Bhabha which is relatively easily mapped, simply in terms of the intellectual agendas of each of them, but there’s a great deal else going on.

我想我应该顺便提一下，有些话题我们不会深入讨论，至少不会只是略微提及。不过，如果您对这个领域感兴趣，或许可以考虑一下。首先，当然是谁来定义“后殖民”？谁又能断言我们已经彻底摆脱了殖民主义？仅仅因为当地的总督收拾行囊回家，并不意味着所谓的后殖民环境下的局势就发生了翻天覆地的变化。我们需要认真思考，是否仍然处于殖民主义或殖民研究的范畴之内，以及“后殖民”这个标签是否因此被滥用。此外，在研究所谓的“第三世界”时，也会出现一个问题。“第三世界”本身就是一个颇具争议的术语。它指的是那些不属于冷战时期两大超级大国既定路线的地区。冷战已经结束，至少表面上已经结束了，因此，第三世界的地位、性质和结构等问题显然仍悬而未决。

I suppose I should just mention in passing certain topics that we won’t be discussing, at least except possibly in passing and that, however, you might really be interested in considering if you do have an interest in this field. The first issue, of course, is who says “post-colonial,” and who says that we’re necessarily out of colonialism? Just because the local viceroy packs up and goes home doesn’t necessarily mean that things change all that significantly in the so-called postcolonial setting, and it needs to be taken into account, seriously considered, whether or not one isn’t still in colonial or colonial studies and that the moniker “post-colonial” might therefore be inappropriately applied. There’s also the question that arises in the study of the so-called third world, which is obviously in itself a controversial term. It arises as that which is not comprised as either of the great sort of trajectories of the superpowers during the Cold War. There is no Cold War, at least allegedly no Cold War any longer, and so the question of the status, nature, and structure of the third world is obviously wide open.

但就后殖民研究而言，我想探讨的问题是，关于第三世界的危机和问题是否必然总是要从殖民性的角度来理解？仅仅是因为地球上的某些地区曾被殖民，就决定了它们的现状并塑造了它们的身份认同吗？萨义德以一种非常有趣的方式探讨了这个问题，他试图弄清为什么德国东方主义与法国东方主义如此相似，尽管德国人在中东并没有殖民利益。在整个时期——尤其是在19世纪早期，德国东方主义几乎与法国东方主义无异，关注点相同，利益也相同——萨义德认为，法国人无疑在某种程度上受其殖民利益的制约，而德国人似乎在很大程度上反映了法国的态度，却没有殖民利益，至少在中东是如此，这究竟是为什么呢？

But the issue I mean to touch on in terms of post-colonial studies is whether, in fact, crises and concerns with respect to the third world are necessarily always to be understood in terms of coloniality. Is it just that certain parts of the globe have been colonized that constitutes them as they are and shapes their identity? Said in a very interesting way takes this up in trying to figure out how it is that German Orientalism so very closely resembles French Orientalism, even though the Germans had no colonial interests in the Middle East. During the whole period–the early nineteenth century in particular, when German Orientalism is practically indistinguishable from the French, takes up the same concerns, and has the same interests–how is it that the French are undoubtedly in some sense, in Said’s view, determined by their colonial interests, and the Germans, who seem so much to reflect French attitudes, have no colonial interests, at least in the Middle East?

萨伊德相当坦诚地试图理解这一点。他的回答是：“嗯，德国东方主义在学术上源于法国东方主义。它带有那种思想的烙印，也反映了那种思想。” 就是这样。然而，他也可以说，某种对待第三世界的思维模式——这正是我在这个问题上一直强调的——决定了人们构建对第三世界思考方式的某种特定模式，而这与是否存在殖民利益无关。这就是我提出这个问题的原因：“在类似情况下，殖民性总是关键因素吗？”

Said sort of quite honestly tries to come to terms with this. His answer is, “Well, German Orientalism is simply derived in scholarly terms from French Orientalism. It has the stamp of that thinking and reflects that thinking,” and so there you are. He could have said on the other hand, however, that a certain mindset toward the third world–and this is the point I have been making about this particular issue–dictates a certain way of structuring one’s thought about that world, irrespective of whether or not there are colonial interests involved. That’s what I mean by raising the question, “Is coloniality always at issue in cases of this kind?”

在思考这些问题时，存在一种困惑，这种困惑在英国东印度公司的历史中体现得淋漓尽致——该公司的历史既具有民族主义色彩，又带有全球化色彩——但在更近代的殖民历史中也同样存在这种困惑，那就是：究竟是什么驱动着殖民主义？是民族主义，还是像当今世界日益普遍的情况那样，是全球化中的跨国利益？换句话说，殖民者与被殖民者之间的关系，究竟是某种宗主国与地方帝国之间的关系，还是由全球化的经济利益所决定和塑造的关系？这是一个复杂的话题，在我们今天所探讨的领域引发了很多争论。但在某种程度上，我们不能简单地说，“民族主义不再重要了，现在是全球化”，因为实际上民族主义似乎在布什的外交政策中重新出现，甚至有可能在奥巴马的外交政策中延续下去。因此，民族主义和全球化之间仍然存在着复杂的关系，如果要清楚地理解这些社会关系，就需要考虑和思考这种关系。

There’s a kind of confusion in thinking about these things, a confusion which is distilled in the history of the British East India Company–which is both nationalist and, as it were, globalizing–but a confusion which comes out in more recent history of coloniality, and that is: well, what drives coloniality? Is it always nationalism or, as seems increasingly the case in the modern world, is it transnational interests in globalization? In other words, is the relationship between the colonist and the colonized a relation of some sort of metropolitan nation with respect to a provincial empire, or is it a relation which is dictated and generated by the economic interests of globalization?
