This is a complex subject which generates a great deal of debate in the field that we take up today, but in a way, we can’t just say, “Well, nationalism isn’t important anymore, now it’s globalization” because actually nationalism seems to have reappeared in the Bush foreign policy, even possibly to be continued in the Obama foreign policy, and so there’s a complex relationship still between nationalism and globalization that needs to be considered and thought about if these social relations are to be clearly understood.

最后，在后殖民研究领域——尤其是在那些代表世界各地被殖民者利益的学者中——存在着一个问题，借用盖亚特里·斯皮瓦克（Gayatri Spivak）的说法，“底层民众应该如何发声？”这个问题与“底层民众应该用哪种语言发声？”这个问题有着最生动的联系。斯皮瓦克本人提出的问题是，“底层民众究竟能否发声？”正如你所看到的，萨义德在他的分析过程中也提出了这个问题；但相关的问题是，假设底层民众能够发声——例如，假设恩古吉·瓦·提昂戈（Ngugi wa Thiong'o）能够写一部小说。那么，这部小说应该用哪种语言写成？恩古吉在晚年致力于反对用英语写作，并敦促其他非洲作家用母语而不是殖民者的语言进行写作。这是后殖民研究领域内经常听到的一种观点，但围绕它一直存在争议，因为文学影响的传播媒介当然是那些能够利用国际出版渠道的语言，而不是那些只能在本地理解、出版和传播的语言。所以，这同样是一个复杂的问题，双方都有各自的见解，值得探讨；但正如我所说，对我们今天而言，这仅仅是一个问题——或者更确切地说，是一个问题，因为当课程大纲里出现霍米·巴巴时，就不存在简单的问题了——所以我应该说，这是一个关于追溯萨义德和巴巴之间发展轨迹的问题。

Finally, there is within post-colonial studies–especially among those who represent the various colonized interests of the world–there is the question, to borrow an expression from Gayatri Spivak, “How should the subaltern speak?” It has to do most vividly with the very question, “Which language should the subaltern speak in?” Spivak’s own question is, “Can the subaltern speak at all?” and Said raises that question, as you notice, during the course of his analysis; but the related issue is, okay, suppose that the subaltern can speak–suppose Ngugi wa Thiong’o, for example, can write a novel. What language should it be written in? Ngugi campaigned in his more recent career not to write in English and also to urge other African writers to write in native languages and not in the language of the colonizer. This is a frequently heard opinion from within post-colonial studies, but debate swirls around it because, of course, the means of circulation of literary influence is languages that draw upon international publishing possibilities and not languages that can only be grasped and published and disseminated locally. So there, too, you have a complicated issue or controversy on both sides, of which there is much to say; but as I say, for us today it’s simply a question– or more simply a question, because when you’ve got Homi Bhabha on the syllabus there’s no such thing as simplicity–so I should say it’s a question of following the trajectory or development specifically between Said and Bhabha.

第二章 重访一间属于自己的房间

Chapter 2. A Room of One’s Own Revisited

开始思考萨义德的时候，我以为我们不会想到他。至少在那一刻，我们会再次想起弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫。在《一间自己的房间》第二章中，这位年轻女子，玛丽·贝顿、玛丽·塞顿、玛丽·卡迈克尔——不管她是谁，正坐在大英图书馆里。她打算花一上午时间，弄清楚学者们对女性的看法。毕竟，主题是女性与小说。我本该就此主题对本科生们说：“我对女性了解多少？我最好去图书馆查查。”所以她以为只要找到几本书就万事大吉了。

In beginning to think about Said, I thought we wouldn’t think about him. We’d think instead, for a moment at least, once again about Virginia Woolf. In the second chapter of A Room of One’s Own, this young woman, Mary Beton, Mary Seton, Mary Carmichael–whoever she is, is sitting in the British Library. She’s thought that she’d spend the morning trying to figure out what scholars think about women. After all, the subject is women and fiction. I’m supposed to be addressing these undergraduates on this subject: “what do I know about women? I’d better go to the library and find out.” So she expects just to find a couple of books and she’ll be all set.

她却感到不知所措，面对的是如雪崩般涌来的资料。她提交了十几二十份索书，然后就坐等资料送达。当然，关键在于，大英图书馆里所有关于女性的资料，而这个主题浩如烟海，竟然都是男性写的，对吧？全部都是。她开始留意这些资料在类似电脑出现之前的数据库中是如何被描述的。也就是说，如何对男性关于女性的各种言论进行分类？事情是这样的：“中世纪的状况；斐济群岛的习俗；被奉为女神；道德感较弱；的理想主义；更认真负责；南太平洋岛民的青春期年龄；吸引力；被献祭；大脑体积小；潜意识更深；体毛较少；精神、道德和身体上的劣势；对孩子的爱；寿命更长；肌肉较弱；情感强烈；虚荣；受过高等教育；莎士比亚对……的看法；伯肯黑德勋爵对……的看法；英格院长对……的看法；拉布吕耶尔对……的看法；约翰逊博士对……的看法；奥斯卡·勃朗宁先生对……的看法；等等等等——名单还可以继续列下去。换句话说，她坐在那里。她完全不知所措，而她当然是在告诉我们，关于女性的观点有很多很多很多很多，都记录在案。”所有这些都是由男性表达的。

Instead she is simply overwhelmed, and there’s this avalanche of material. She submits maybe a dozen or two call slips and then sits back waiting for the material to appear. Of course, the point of it is that everything in the British Library on what turns out to be the voluminous subject of women is written by men, right? Everything. She begins to take note of the way these things are described in the sort of pre-computer database. That is to say, how do you classify the various things that men have to say about women? This is the way it goes: “condition of Middle Ages of; habits in the Fiji Islands of; worshipped as goddesses by; weaker in moral sense than; idealism of; greater conscientious of; South Sea islanders age of puberty among; attractiveness of; offered as sacrifice to; small size of brain of; profounder sub-consciousness of; less hair on the body of; mental, moral and physical inferiority of; love of children of; greater length of life of; weaker muscles of; strength of affections of; vanity of; higher education of; Shakespeare’s opinion of; Lord Birkenhead’s opinion of; Dean Inge’s opinion of; La Bruyere’s opinion of; Dr. Johnson’s opinion of; Mr. Oscar Browning’s opinion of; and dot, dot, dot–the list can continue. In other words, she sits there. She’s simply overwhelmed, and what she of course is telling us is that there’s lots and lots and lots and lots of opinions on record about women, all of them expressed by men.

现在想想爱德华·萨义德，如果他接手了弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫的计划，如果他着手写《一间自己的房间》，那书名会是《女性主义》，对吧？这正是他所说的“东方主义”的含义，指的是大量关于被统称为“东方”民族的信息——其中一些是学术性的，一些则纯粹是赞颂性的——尤其是在十九世纪的传统中。萨义德主要关注的是中东民族，他阐述了为什么用“东方主义”这个词来描述十九世纪的学术和语言学传统是恰当的。

So now thinking about Edward Said, if Edward Said had taken up Virginia Woolf’s project, if Edward Said had undertaken to write A Room of One’s Own, the title of it would have been Female-ism, right? That’s precisely what he means by “Orientalism,” the vast body of information–some of it scholarly, some of it just sort of sheerly doxological–the vast body of information about peoples called “Oriental” by and large, especially in the nineteenth-century tradition. Said’s main concern is the peoples of the Middle East, and he shows how it is that there’s a certain reason why this is an appropriate term to use for that tradition of scholarship and philology in the nineteenth century.

总之，关于这些人的已出版资料浩如烟海——图书馆里确实有数不尽的书架专门摆放着关于这个主题的多卷本专著，而所有这些著作都是我们西方人——我们——所撰写的，关于这个始终存在于我们想象中、由我们以各种方式构建的“他者”，萨义德在第1811页右栏中对此进行了探讨。他在该栏末尾写道：

In any case, the vast body of material published about these people–and it’s perfectly true that there are the infinitely long shelves of the library devoted to multivolume treatises on this topic, all of them written by us in the West–us–about this other who is perpetually in our imagination and constructed by us in the variety of ways that Said discusses on page 1811, the right-hand column. He says toward the bottom of the column:

东方主义的前提是外在性，也就是说，东方学家、诗人或学者让东方发声，描述东方，将其奥秘向西方阐明。正如伍尔夫的作品一样，男性对女性在书中表达自我的看法，使得女性这一主题对男性读者而言变得清晰明了。

Orientalism is premised upon exteriority, that is, on the fact that the Orientalist, poet or scholar, makes the Orient speak, describes the Orient, renders its mysteries plain for and to the West. Just as in Woolf, men’s opinions about women getting themselves expressed in books make the subject of woman clear to an audience of men.

第三章 东方主义与肖瓦尔特的阶段划分

Chapter 3. Orientalism and Showalter’s Phases

好的。在更深入、更精确地探讨萨义德的文本之前，让我先简要解释一下我所说的萨义德和巴巴构成某种序列是什么意思。我特别指的是伊莱恩·肖瓦尔特对女性主义批评和女性主义批评的区分。顺便一提，盖茨的文章中也呼应了这一区分。这种区分是：首先，你会遇到一种批评，它关注的是男性在文学作品中对女性的描写；随后，你会遇到一种批评，它关注的是女性的传统，是女性自身的声音，正如肖瓦尔特所认为的，这才是更有成效的批评领域。你可以看出，通过这种区分，萨义德显然属于第一阶段，因为东方主义当然是关于西方如何看待中东“他者”的。它也可以归入这一阶段。

All right. So before moving in with some more depth and precision into Said’s text, let me quickly explain what I mean by saying that Said and Bhabha constitute a kind of sequence. I’m thinking in particular of Elaine Showalter’s distinction between feminist and gynocritical criticism. You remember the distinction which is echoed, by the way, in Gates’s essay. The distinction is: first you get criticism in which the treatment of women in literature by men is the focus of attention, and then subsequently you get criticism in which the women’s tradition, the voice of women themselves, is the focus and, as Showalter believes, the more fruitful terrain for criticism. You can see that in that context, by way of making that distinction, you can see that Said is decidedly phase one because, of course, Orientalism is about the treatment of the Middle Eastern other by the West. It can be slotted into that same moment.

显然，霍米·巴巴以多种方式占据了被殖民者、底层民众的主体位置。他并没有忽略殖民者的主体位置，因为他认为两者之间存在着根本性的关联，但他显然对探讨被殖民者的传统与探讨殖民化如何发生和表现自身同样感兴趣。因此，从这个意义上讲，我们可以将萨义德和巴巴视为属于肖瓦尔特划分的这两个阶段。正如我顺便提一下盖茨——很抱歉这个标题造成了混淆[指向黑板]——实际上，萨义德和巴巴还可以被理解为第一阶段和第二阶段，这更多地与文学理论的传统有关，而肖瓦尔特和盖茨都以各自的方式否定了这一传统，他们坚持认为，人们需要挪用白人男性文学理论来服务于自身的目的。

Then Homi Bhabha obviously in a variety of ways takes up the subject position of the colonized, of the subaltern. He doesn’t leave out the subject position of the colonizer because he sees them as being radically interrelated, but he plainly is as interested in a variety of ways of talking about the traditions of the colonized as he is of talking about the way in which colonization takes place and expresses itself. So in that sense, we can see Said and Bhabha as belonging to these two phases as mapped by Showalter. As I say also in passing by Gates–and I’m sorry for the confusion of this heading [gestures to board]–actually there’s another way in which Said and Bhabha can be understood as phase one and phase two. That has much more to do with the tradition of literary theory, which in their ways both Showalter and Gates have rejected, insisting that one needs to commandeer white male literary theory for one’s own purposes.

我想，问题在于萨义德和巴巴为何没有提及这个问题。或许可以这样回答：恰恰在殖民主义的语境下，知识分子——第三世界的知识分子，被殖民的知识分子——仍然在精英云集的都市学府接受教育，这里指的当然主要是牛津和剑桥。在某种意义上，他们开始认同——这其实与巴巴关于混杂性的论述并无二致——他们在某种程度上认同了殖民者的教育议程，并参与其中。

I suppose it’s a question of how this issue doesn’t come up in Said and Bhabha. It could perhaps be answered by saying that precisely in the situation of colonialism, the intellectuals–third world, colonized intellectuals–nevertheless are educated in high-octane male metropolitan institutions, by which of course one means primarily Oxford and Cambridge. In a certain sense, they come to identify–and this is not actually a thing apart from Bhabha’s argument about hybridity–they come to identify in some measure with the educational agenda of the colonizer and participate in it.

这只是推测。或许我们错过了萨义德和巴巴也曾探讨过如何挪用白人男性文学理论传统的那些时刻；但就目前而言，我想指出的是：萨义德的东方主义理论与我们所谓的结构主义的历史语境密切相关。也就是说，它主要关注的是二元对立，一种中心自我与去中心化他者之间相互依存的二元对立，包括（我们稍后会看到）对他者的他者性建构实际上同时也是一种建构、定义和界定自我本质（或者在这个例子中，是西方人本质）的手段。萨义德的观点中存在一种根本的二元论，这种观点经常受到批评，而且最常受到巴巴的批评——这不仅是因为他不断引用德里达关于马拉美的著名文章《双重会议》，还因为他大量挪用了德里达的语言和风格。

Now that’s speculative. It may simply be that we have missed out on those moments when Said and Bhabha, too, may be talking about the way in which the white male tradition of literary theory needs to be appropriated; but for the moment what I want to point out is this: Said’s Orientalism works very much in the historical moment of what we call structuralism. That is to say, it’s primary concern is with the binary opposition, a mutual and interdependent binary opposition of central self and decentralized other including, as we’ll see in a minute, the way in which the construction of the otherness of the other is actually covertly also at the same time a means of constructing, defining, and delimiting the nature of selfhood, or in this case of being Western. There is a fundamental binarism in Said’s point of view, which by the way has often been criticized, and it’s been criticized most often from the standpoint of Bhabha–if only because he’s constantly referring to Derrida’s famous essay, “The Double Session,” which is about Mallarmé, and also because he appropriates a great deal of the language and style of Derrida.

你可以看出，巴巴对结构主义的二元论采取了一种解构的态度。换句话说，他对这些关系的理解至少会分解成一种他所谓的“双重意识”的双重化，以至于人们无法将殖民者和被殖民者清晰地视为二元对立。情况远比这复杂，它涉及一系列问题，而这些问题又取决于德里达对“差异”含义的深刻理解。我只想说，从这个意义上讲，萨义德-巴巴的关系也处于第一阶段和第二阶段的过渡阶段。

You can see that Bhabha takes, with respect to the binarism of structuralism, a deconstructive attitude. In other words, his sense of these relations breaks down into, at the very least, a redoubling sense of what he calls “double consciousness” so that one can’t clearly identify colonizer and colonized as a binary opposition. It’s more complicated than that, and it’s a series of issues that turns on a highly Derridian sense of what one might mean by difference. All I want to say is that the relation, Said-Bhabha, is phase one-phase two in that regard as well.

顺便一提，这种倾向在其他与身份认同相关的理论中也能找到。我们迄今为止讨论的古典女性主义与我们将在周二讨论的性别理论（尤其是在朱迪斯·巴特勒的案例中）之间的关系，再次体现为结构主义与解构主义之间的关系。同样，从文学理论的角度来看，萨义德-巴巴这一理论体系也以一种并非完全重叠但又相当有趣的方式，以两种不同的方式呈现了第一阶段和第二阶段，我认为这两种方式是可以有效区分的。

By the way, this is a tendency that one can find in other forms of theory having to do with identity. The relationship between the classical feminism that we have been discussing so far and the gender theory that we will be discussing on Tuesday, especially in the case of Judith Butler, is once again a relation that could be understood as between structuralism and deconstruction. There, too, you have a not completely overlapping but, from the standpoint of our concerns in literary theory, nevertheless rather interesting way in which this succession, Said-Bhabha, is phase one-phase two in two different ways that can be identified, I think, usefully.

第四章 赛义德与巴巴的关系

Chapter 4. The Relationship Between Said and Bhabha

好的。那么，关于他们的关系就说到这里。那么萨义德呢？我们如何才能触及萨义德想要探讨的问题，并理解他认为这些问题具有完整性的方式？我想先谈谈真相，因为萨义德明确指出，在某种程度上，他所进行的对东方主义的妖魔化，并非因为东方主义本身必然是一堆谎言。或许他在这个问题上有些含糊其辞，但对他而言，东方主义是说谎还是说真话，最终并不是重点。他在第1802页右栏是这样写的：

All right. So that then about their relationship. So what about Said? How do we get at the issues that Said wants to talk about and understand the way in which he thinks they have integrity? I think I’d like actually to begin with a word or two about truth, because Said makes it clear that in a way, the demonization of Orientalism that his project undertakes isn’t really undertaken because Orientalism is necessarily a pack of lies. Maybe he waffles a little bit about this, but it’s not really ultimately the point for him whether Orientalism lies or tells the truth. This is the way he puts it on page 1802 in the right-hand column:

……第三个限定条件。我们绝不应假定东方主义的结构仅仅是谎言或神话的堆砌，一旦真相大白，这些谎言或神话就会不攻自破。我个人认为，东方主义作为欧洲-大西洋对东方权力的象征，其价值远大于它作为对东方真实论述的价值……然而，我们必须尊重并努力理解的是东方主义论述本身所蕴含的强大力量……换句话说，拿破仑征埃及期间的一位副官就写出了十卷本的《埃及东征记》。萨义德在其《东方主义导论》中顺带提及的许多文本也同样篇幅浩大。五十卷本的巨著，堪称学术巨著，你不得不承认，既然他们写了这么多，其中必然包含一些真理。毕竟，至少在思考这类问题时，人们已经积累了大量的特定知识，因此不能简单地说：“我的观点是，这一切都是错的。” 因此，萨义德竭力区分真理和价值。东方主义话语本身并非必然是真或假。然而，它却以一种隐蔽的方式贬低了其关注的对象——其中蕴含着一种欧洲中心主义，萨义德甚至认为东方主义本身就是一种种族主义，而这与许多东方主义者所做的细致研究最终得出的结论的真假程度无关。例如，在第1812页的左栏中，他写道：

… [A] third qualification. One ought never to assume that the structure of Orientalism is nothing more than a structure of lies or myths which, were the truth about them to be told, would simply blow away. I myself believe that Orientalism is more particularly valuable as a sign of European-Atlantic power over the Orient than it is as a veridic discourse about the Orient… Nevertheless, what we must respect and try to grasp is the sheer knitted-together strength of Orientalist discourse… In other words, one of Napoleon’s adjutants during Napoleon’s campaign through Egypt wrote a ten-volume Eastward de l’Egypt. Many of the texts which Said mentions in passing in his introduction to Orientalism are just as long. You’ve got fifty-volume, sort of gigantic scholarly undertakings, and you’ve got to admit, well, if they are saying that much, there’s got to be something in it that’s true. There is, after all, a great deal of knowledge of a certain kind, at least, that has gone into thinking of this kind, and so one can’t just say, “My point is that none of it’s true.” Said is at pains to make a distinction, therefore, between truth and value. It’s not that Orientalist discourse is necessarily true or false. It is the case though that it is insidiously devaluate of its object of attention–that there is an implicit euro-centrism which Said does go so far as to consider a form of racism in Orientalism, quite irrespective of any measure or degree of truth that what are, after all, the meticulous researches of a lot of these characters turn up. For example, on page 1812, the left-hand column, he says:

因此，我对东方主义文本的分析（这大约在文章三分之一处）着重强调了这些表述作为表述而非对东方“自然”描述的那些证据，而这些证据绝非隐形。现在，我们可以稍作停顿，探讨一下这一点，因为它可能是一个值得批判的对象。因为在萨义德的文章结尾，或者如你所见，在引言结尾，你会注意到他说：“你看，我在这里并不探讨如何才能正确地描写这些人（笑）。”例如，他没有探讨作为这些少数族裔或被殖民者的代表，在描写自身时会是什么感受。他也没有真正探讨这样一个问题：由他人描写我，一个男人描写一个女人，这种偏见是否比我自身对自身的成见和偏见更糟糕。他承认自己并没有一套成熟的理论能够确凿地证明某种表述是真实可靠的，而另一种表述则是带有偏见且不真实的。他说：“或许会有其他学者来探讨这个问题。我在书中就此打住。”而这个问题也确实没有被提及，问题在于，他仍然声称——正如许多其他研究过此主题的人所预见的那样——他确实质疑东方主义仅仅是表述：也就是说，因为东方主义是一种表述，所以它与自然地唤起某种精神或世界截然相反。

My analysis of the Orientalist text therefore places emphasis [this is about a third of the way down] on the evidence, which is by no means invisible, for such representations as representations, not as “natural” descriptions of the Orient. Now we might pause for a minute over that as a possible object of critique because at the end of his essay, or at the end of the introduction as you have it, you notice Said saying, “Look, I don’t take up here the question of how one might actually write correctly [laughs] about these people.” He doesn’t take up, for example, the question of what it might be like to be sort of a representative of these minorities or colonized figures and to write about oneself. He doesn’t really take up the question of whether the bias of somebody else writing about me, a man writing about a woman, is worse than the bias of my own preconceptions and prejudices about myself. He admits that he doesn’t really have an advanced theory that secures one kind of representation as true or authentic and secures another kind of representation as bias and inauthentic. He says, “Another scholar will perhaps take this up. I leave it alone in my book,” and it is left alone, the problem being that the claim remains that he does–anticipating many other people who have written on this subject–he does impugn Orientalism as mere representation: that is to say, as the opposite because it is a representation, the opposite of a natural evocation of an ethos or world.

所以，我们只想在页边打个问号，然后说：“好吧，既然这一切都是表象，那么文本在哪里？自然的文本又在哪里呢？”例如，是否存在某种自然的符号，就像我们整个学期一直在问自己的那样？符号是任意的，这实际上已经把我们牢牢地置于表象的范畴之内。所有这些问题都源于萨义德对东方学研究史中真理与价值关系的理解。

So we just do want to put a little question mark in the margin and then say, “Well, fine. Granted this is all representation, where is the text? Where could the text be that would be natural?” Is there, for example, any such thing, as we’ve asked ourselves over the course of the semester, as a natural sign? The sign being arbitrary, it does place us already pretty securely in the realm of representation. So all of these questions are then posed by Said’s sense of the relationship between truth and value in the history of Orientalist scholarship.

第五章 主奴辩证法

Chapter 5. The Master-Slave Dialectic

那么，他的出发点是什么呢？他对此毫不避讳，或许值得我们停下来思考一下对他影响最大的两位学者兼理论家——米歇尔·福柯和意大利马克思主义者安东尼奥·葛兰西——的共同观点。首先，让我们回顾一下他在第1803页左栏中对葛兰西的借鉴：

Now where is he coming from? He’s quite open about it, and it’s perhaps worth pausing over an idea common to the two scholar-theorists who matter most to him, Michel Foucault and the Italian Marxist Antonio Gramsci. First of all, just to pass in review the way in which he’s indebted to Gramsci on page 1803, the left-hand column, Said says:

当然，文化是在公民社会中运作的，在公民社会中，思想、制度和他人的影响力并非通过统治，而是通过葛兰西所说的“同意”来发挥作用。换句话说，这不仅仅是强迫人们接受某些观念、概念或法律，而是一种所谓的知识、对事物的感受、意识形态的流通，这种流通通过“同意”来确立某些偏见态度。葛兰西区分了两种方式：一种是人们被实际权力和权威所强加的方式，另一种是人们被过去接触到的、被称为“意识形态”的流通所强加的方式。

Culture, of course, is to be found operating within civil society, where the influence of ideas, of institutions and of other persons works not through domination but by what Gramsci calls consent. In other words, it’s not just a question of having forced down your throat certain ideas of concepts or laws, for that matter, but a circulation of knowledge, so called, of feeling about things, of ideology, which through consent establishes certain attitudes of bias. This is the distinction that Gramsci makes between the way in which one is imposed on by actual power and authority and the way in which one is imposed on by the circulations of what we’ve been exposed to in the past as being called “ideologemes.”

那么，接下来：

So to continue:

萨义德认为，在任何非极权社会中，某些文化形式都会凌驾于其他文化形式之上，正如某些思想比其他思想更具影响力一样；葛兰西将这种文化领导形式称为“霸权”（ashegemony）。你会经常遇到这个术语，尤其是在马克思主义批评中，但它也与大多数西方读者在米歇尔·福柯的著作中更为熟悉的“权力”（power）或有时是“权力/知识”（power/knowledge）密切相关。

In any society not totalitarian [says Said], then, certain cultural forms predominate over others, just as certain ideas are more influential than others; the form of this cultural leadership is what Gramsci has identified ashegemony. This is a term that you will frequently encounter, particularly in Marxist criticism, but it is also a term very closely related to what for most Western readers is more famous in the work of Michel Foucault, the term “power” or sometimes “power/knowledge.”

正如你将在周二阅读的福柯节选中了解到的，福柯和葛兰西一样，区分了两种权力：一种是仅仅指警察、社会法律机构、独裁者、政府所行使的权力；另一种是作为知识传播和霸权化（即权威化）的方式——通常是隐蔽的方式。福柯对这种知识传播的结构非常着迷。事实上，这正是他晚期所有著作的核心主题：我们如何自以为是自由的思考主体，实际上却被周围流传的各种舆论结构所左右，这些结构让我们误以为自己掌握了真理，而实际上，我们面对的只是某种形式的、带有动机的偏见。葛兰西和福柯都区分了绝对权力（葛兰西称之为霸权，福柯称之为权力/知识）。

As you will learn in the excerpt from Foucault that you’ll be reading on Tuesday, Foucault like Gramsci makes a distinction between power merely as that which is exercised by the police, by the legal arm of society, by the dictator, by the government, and by power as the ways, the frequently insidious ways, in which knowledge is circulated and made hegemonic–that is to say, made authoritative. Foucault is fascinated by the structure of this circulation of knowledge. That is, in fact the essential subject matter of all of his late work, the way in which we are thinking that we are sort of free contemplative agents in the world, in fact browbeaten by structures of opinion circulating around us that lull us into feeling that we are in the presence of the truth, whereas of course, we’re only in the presence of one form or another of motivated bias. Both Gramsci and Foucault make the distinction between absolute power and, as Gramsci calls it, hegemony and, as Foucault calls it, power/knowledge.

萨义德在这里谈论的是权力/知识。他并非在谈论通过武力或其他任何手段对被殖民世界强加法律，而是在谈论意见如何构建这个世界，并同时强化那些产生这些意见者的权威。我认为指出这个相对微妙的区别很重要：然而，他确实在某一方面与福柯持不同意见。在第1813页，他回顾了我们对福柯的已知认知，即福柯关注的是作者的功能而非作者本身。福柯认为，一般来说，作者并非权威，而仅仅是各种意见形式的载体。某些非常接近权威的作者，我们称之为话语的奠基人，但即便在他们的情况下，重要的是话语的性质，而非他们作为作者的存在。萨义德想表达的是，“我对作者的重视程度要高一些”，他在第1813页的右栏中这样写道：

Said is talking here about power/knowledge. He’s not talking about the imposition of law through force or any other means on a colonized world. He’s talking about the way in which opinions construct that world and simultaneously reinforce the authority of those who generate the opinions. I think it’s important to point this relatively subtle distinction out: he does, however, disagree from Foucault in one respect. On page 1813 he goes back to what we already know about Foucault, which is Foucault’s interest in the author function as opposed to the author. Authors, generally speaking, Foucault wants to say, are not authorities but simply vessels of forms of opinion. Certain authors who come very close to being authority we call founders of discursivity, but even in their cases it’s the nature of the discourse and not their existence as authors which is important. Said wants to say, “I take authors a little bit more seriously than that,” and he does on page 1813 in the right-hand column where he says:

福柯认为，一般来说，单个文本或作者的重要性微乎其微；就东方主义而言，就经验而言（也就是说，“通过我的经验”），或许在其他任何地方，我都未发现例外。换言之，作者才是核心的语文学家，而那些对世界这一地区进行过大量著述的社会历史学家、探险家和人口学家才是权威。他们是神谕，从中传播出普遍的、最终沦为陈词滥调的观点，并将其转化为权力/知识。因此，这并非某种观点不断重复表达的无声鼓点，而这正是福柯更感兴趣的。正如我所说，萨义德在这方面与福柯有着微妙的区别，但他同时也公开承认福柯和葛兰西都对他处理材料的方式产生了影响。

Foucault believes that in general the individual text or author counts for very little; empirically [that is to say, “through my experience”], in the case of Orientalism, and perhaps nowhere else I find this not to be so. In other words, the author is the central philologist, and social historians, explorers, and demographers who have written so extensively on this part of the world are authorities. They are the oracles from which generalized and ultimately commonplace opinions disseminate as power/knowledge. It’s not a question, therefore, of a kind of silent drumbeat of opinion expressing itself over and over again, which is more what interests Foucault. So Said, as I say, distinguishes himself subtly from Foucault in that regard while nevertheless confessing openly the influence both of Foucault and of Gramsci on his way of approaching his material.

因此，作为一种权力流通，东方主义的影响最终是萨义德所关注的。嗯，他这么说多少有些反问的意味，因为他显然确实关心东方主义对相关民族的影响，但萨义德最终关注的是东方主义对欧洲中心主义思维的影响，实际上，它在多大程度上能够构建欧洲中心主义思维，见第1806页右栏：

So as a circulation of power, the effect of Orientalism is something that ultimately concerns Said.Well, he says this somewhat rhetorically because it obviously does concern him that it has an effect on the peoples in question, but what ultimately concerns Said is the effect of Orientalism on the Euro-centric mind, indeed the degree to which it even can be said to construct the Euro-centric mind, page 1806, the right-hand column:

……我的真正论点是，东方主义是现代政治知识文化中一个相当重要的维度，而不仅仅是其代表，因此，它与东方本身的关系远不如与“我们”的世界的关系密切。现在，你可以看出萨义德的观点与托妮·莫里森在她的文章中的观点非常相似。例如，如果我们研究美国文学史，那么“黑人”作为一种缺席的存在需要被理解为构建“白人”身份的手段，是将“白人”身份从其长期以来所受的种种束缚中解放出来的手段。当然，莫里森对这一论点进行了精彩的阐述，她显然是从黑格尔《精神现象学》第四章中汲取灵感，以此来理解主奴辩证法。换句话说，在黑格尔的论述中，我们可以清楚地看到，在互惠的结构中，主人和奴隶是彼此绝对必要的。如果没有奴隶的存在，主人就不是主人，也无法将自己定义为自由或优越的。奴隶在从属地位中习得的种种技巧，包括发展各种复杂的技能，最终使奴隶反过来在技术上驱动主人，并最终控制主人。这就像一个阶级颠倒的寓言，而这种颠倒又在各种情况下不断循环往复。这既是一个寓言，也是一个阶级关系哲学，它构建了莫里森的论证，我认为，也构建了萨义德的论证。

… [M]y real argument is that Orientalism is–and does not simply represent–a considerable dimension of modern political-intellectual culture, and as such has less to do with the Orient than it does with “our” world. Now here you can see the degree to which Said is saying something very similar to what Toni Morrison said in her essay. The existence of black as absence needs to be understood–for example, if we are studying the history of American literature–as the means of constructing whiteness, of that which liberates whiteness from the forms of constraint under which it’s been chafing at the bit. Morrison, of course, develops this argument beautifully, and she quite clearly takes it from the fourth chapter of Hegel’s Phenomenology of Mind as a way of understanding the master-slave dialectic. In other words, in Hegel it’s clear as Hegel develops the idea that master and slave are absolutely necessary to each other in a structure of mutuality. The master isn’t the master, can’t define himself as free or superior without the existence of the slave. The trickiness that the slave learns being in the position of subordination involving the development of all sorts of complicated skills means ultimately that the slave becomes, as it were, that which drives the master technologically and ultimately controls the master in a kind of fable of class reversal, which continues to reverse itself again and again and again on various grounds. This is the fable, which at the same time is a philosophy of class relations that structures Morrison’s argument and which, I think, also structures Said’s.

第六章 巴巴：矛盾与混合性

Chapter 6. Bhabha: Ambivalence and Hybridity

我想过渡到巴巴的理论，因为这显然是一种二元论。这两个能指彼此需要，就像我们在讨论索绪尔和结构主义时所描述的那样。我不能简单地说红灯具有积极价值。你还记得整个论证吗：我必须在它所属的符号系统的语境中看待红灯。我必须把它看作是与其他事物不同或对立的，才能理解它。换句话说，我无法正面地认识它；我只能负面地认识它。

I want to make the transition to Bhabha because obviously this is a form of binarism. The two signifiers in relation to each other need each other in the way that we described when we were discussing Saussure and structuralism. I can’t simply say that a red light has positive value. You remember the whole argument: I have to see the red light in the context of the semiotic system to which it belongs. I have to see it as being different from, or opposed to, something else in order to grasp it. I cannot know it positively, in other words; I can only know it negatively.

索绪尔传统中的结构主义基本概念，正是萨义德式二元论证的根源所在。我们否定性地将自身认知为“非他者”，这是其基本原则，也是支撑论证的理论原则，而这些理论原则显然也包含萨义德所说的经验性层面。没错，我可以说这是一个结构主义思想，但我深信不疑，因为我亲眼见证了它的运作。换句话说，它不仅仅是结构主义。然而，它与结构主义确实存在着某种理论倾向。

This basic concept of structuralism in the Saussurian tradition is what creates, is what shapes binary arguments of the kind that one finds in Said. That we know ourselves negatively as the not-other is the basic principle, the theoretical principle which underlies obviously aspects of the argument which are also, as Said says, empirical. Yes, I can say it’s a structuralist idea, but I really believe it because I’ve seen it in operation. It’s not just structuralism in other words. It shares, however, with structuralism a theoretical predisposition.

如果你翻阅巴巴的著作第1879页，你会发现他公开批判了这种二元论的前提——并非任何一种二元论，而是直接追溯到黑格尔。换句话说，他在1879页右下角指出了这种思维方式的源头，他写道：

Bhabha, if you look at page 1879, openly criticizes the premise of binarism of this kind–not just any binarism, but he actually does go directly back to Hegel. In other words, he identifies the source of thinking of this kind, bottom of 1879, right-hand column, when he says:

正是这种矛盾性使得殖民“立场性”（自我/他者之分）的边界，以及殖民权力问题（殖民者/被殖民者之区分），既不同于黑格尔的主奴辩证法，也不同于现象学意义上的“他者性”投射。他接着提到了其他内容，但我只想聚焦于此，因为巴巴在此尽可能清晰地将自己与萨义德的理论体系区分开来。

It is this ambivalence that makes the boundaries of colonial “positionality”–the division of self/other–and the question of colonial power–the differentiation of colonizer/colonized–different from both the Hegelian master/slave dialectic or the phenomenological projection of Otherness. He goes on to mention other things, but I just want to focus on this as a moment in which Bhabha is distinguishing himself as clearly as he can from the project of Said.

我刚才读的这段文字以“矛盾心理”一词开头。巴巴所说的矛盾心理是什么意思呢？让我们从这里入手，看看能否通过理解矛盾心理的概念，来逐步了解巴巴关于这些问题的复杂思考。我将用一个历史例子来说明，希望这样能更清楚地解释这个问题。殖民者对被殖民者抱有矛盾心理。换句话说，驱动殖民的并非只有一种心态。以英国东印度公司的历史经验为例，可以分为两个截然不同的阶段，这两个阶段实际上在整个二十世纪都反复出现。第一个阶段是十八世纪沃伦·黑斯廷斯执掌东印度公司时期。从某种意义上说，黑斯廷斯对我们所谓的“融入当地文化”很感兴趣，并且鼓励他所有的省级官员也这样做。换句话说，用萨义德的话来说，黑斯廷斯对东方化的他者有着深刻的了解。他精通所有当地语言和方言，熟知所有风俗习惯。他几乎无所不知，某种程度上来说，他既融入了当地社会，又对被殖民者牢牢掌控着权威。他自身也体现了一种矛盾心理：一方面，他寸步不让地捍卫着权力；另一方面，他又似乎与他人融为一体。

Now the passage I just read begins with the word “ambivalence.” What does Bhabha mean by ambivalence? Let’s try to start there and see if we can work our way into Bhabha’s complex thinking on these matters, first by way of the notion of ambivalence. I’m going to put this in terms of an historical example because I hope that will make it a little clearer. There is the ambivalence of the colonizer toward the colonized. In other words, it’s not just one mindset that drives colonization. In the historical experience of England in the East India Company, there are two distinct phases, phases which actually repeat themselves recurrently even throughout the twentieth century. The first in the eighteenth century is the period of the government of the East India Company by Warren Hastings who in a certain sense was interested in what we call “going native” and also encouraged all of his provincial administrators to do likewise. Hastings, in other words, in Saidian terms knew a great deal about the Orientalized other. He knew all the local languages and dialects. He knew all the customs. He really knew everything there was to know and in a certain sense was a person who did go native while at the same time wielding with an iron grip of authority power over the colonized other. He himself then embodies a certain ambivalence in not giving an inch as to the actual control of authority, while at the same time seeming to become one with the other.

此外，还有一种历史性的矛盾心理，它体现在一种截然不同的态度上。这种态度在十九世纪初查尔斯·格兰特领导下的东印度公司中显露出来。当时，英国出现了原教旨主义宗教（主要是卫理公会）的复兴，这种福音派的热情也影响到了帝国的利益。查尔斯·格兰特及其同僚对融入当地文化毫无兴趣，相反，他们坚持要牢牢确立一种英国性标准，尤其是以英文圣经为准绳的标准——巴巴在其文章开头提到的“英文书籍的到来”——并将向被殖民者强加英国性作为殖民的目的。著名历史学家托马斯·巴宾顿·麦考利在其著作《教育备忘录》中阐述了这种态度。这份文件后来臭名昭著，它坚持认为，在东印度公司统治下，印度人民的教育必须严格按照英国模式进行：传教士不再试图将他们的思想与当地风俗习惯相融合，而是要将一切都严格英国化。这是一种截然不同的殖民态度，可以理解为一种历史上的矛盾心理。

Then there is the historical ambivalence which expresses itself in a completely different attitude, an attitude which surfaced in the East India Company early in the nineteenth century under the supervisorship of Charles Grant. There had been a tremendous revival of fundamentalist religion, mainly Methodism, in England, and this evangelical enthusiasm spread itself into the interests of the empire. Charles Grant and others like him no longer had any interest at all in going native but, on the contrary, insisted that a standard of Englishness and, in particular, the standard of the English Bible–the coming of the English book that Bhabha talks about at the beginning of his essay–be firmly implanted, and that the imposition of Englishness on the colonized other be the agenda of colonization. The famous historian Thomas Babington Macaulay codified this attitude in a famous, and soon to be infamous, document he wrote called “The Minute on Education,” which insisted that the education of the Indian people under the regime of the East India Company be conducted strictly according to English models: that missionaries no longer try to adapt their ideas to local customs and folk ways but that everything be strictly anglicized. This is a completely different attitude toward colonization, and it can be understood as a sort of historical ambivalence.

我想先举个例子，说说你们所谓的“沃伦·黑斯廷斯时刻”，一个虽然残酷却又引人入胜的例子，出自约翰·福特那部令人不安的杰作《搜索者》。我希望你们当中至少有人看过这部电影。约翰·韦恩饰演的角色是一个孤身一人的陌生人——这在西部片中当然很常见——他来到亲戚家，听说一个女儿被印第安人绑架了。约翰·韦恩在这部电影里扮演的是一个极其残暴的种族主义者，他恨透了印第安人，但他的残暴并非出于无知。事实上，在某种意义上，他已经融入了印第安人的生活。他精通所有印第安语言和方言，了解他们的所有习俗。他一生都在仔细研究他所憎恨的人，而这种混合体在电影中呈现会引发强烈的反感，因为我们更容易接受仇恨源于无知的观点，对吧？约翰·福特的《搜索者》最令人不安的地方在于，它描绘了极其恶毒的种族主义：萨义德再次说道，“嘿，这未必是事实，但我们必须承认其中存在某种地域性的、浓厚的描述。我们必须承认，这个人掌握了大量信息[笑]，而所有这些都在约翰·韦恩在这部电影中的角色塑造中得到了印证。”

I’d actually like to pause over an example of what you might call the Warren Hastings moment, a vicious example although an absolutely fascinating one in the disturbing masterpiece by John Ford called The Searchers. I hope some of you at least know that film. The John Wayne character is sort of a lone stranger–which is of course not infrequent in the western–who shows up at the house of some relatives and hears that a daughter has been abducted by native Americans, by Indians. Now the thing about John Wayne is that in this film is that he’s a vicious racist, that he absolutely hates the Indians, but he is not a vicious racist from the standpoint of ignorance. He is in fact a person who has himself, in a certain sense, gone native. He knows all the Indian languages and dialects. He knows all their customs. He has throughout a lifetime made a careful study of the people he hates, and this is a volatile mixture to be exposed to in a film because we are much more comfortable with the idea that hatred arises out of ignorance, right? What is so deeply disturbing about John Ford’s The Searchers is that it is a portrait of absolutely vicious racism: again Said says, “Hey, it’s not necessarily truth, but we do have to acknowledge a certain local, thick description. We have to acknowledge that there’s quite a bit of information [laughs] at this person’s disposal, and all of that is borne out in the characterization of John Wayne in this film.

沃伦·黑斯廷斯很像这种人。他对那些他最终并不真正尊重的人了如指掌，并坚持用铁腕统治他们。巴巴在思考殖民者的矛盾心理时，想到的正是这类事情，以及萨义德已经阐述过的知识与价值之间的关系，同时也考虑到殖民者存在多种思维模式。一种是关注本土知识的思维模式，另一种则是树立绝对、不容置疑的殖民者标准。这两种截然不同的态度，各自决定着不同的策略，尤其是在教育策略方面。

Warren Hastings was a lot like that. Warren Hastings knew everything about people whom he ultimately didn’t really respect and whom he insisted on ruling with the iron fist of authority. That’s the kind of thing that Bhabha is thinking about when he thinks about the ambivalence of the colonizer, the relationship between knowledge and value as it’s already been enunciated in Said but also the fact that there is more than one mindset for the colonizer. There is the local knowledge mindset, and there is the sort of raising the absolute unequivocal standard of the colonizer that these are two different attitudes, each of which dictate different strategies, particularly strategies of education.

这就是殖民者的矛盾心理。被殖民者的矛盾心理也同样存在，而这种矛盾心理也必须被理解为与收编之间存在着复杂的关系。我认为，巴巴开篇的那个轶事引人入胜，值得我们细细品读。故事的主角并非殖民者，而是一个被彻底收编的人——一位印度裔的福音派皈依基督教者。某种程度上，他代表着那些坐在树下读圣经的人眼中完全真实的群体，因为他相信，并且乐于相信，圣经，乃至基督教本身，都是英国人的馈赠。但他却遭到了一些人的抵制，他们说：“这很有意思。我们希望也能有地方权威来认可它。我们理解这本书是直接从上帝那里得到的，对吧？这就是我们的理解，我们也有自己的看法。当然，也许有一天我们会受洗，但在此之前，我们得回家收割庄稼，所以这件事以后再说吧。别担心。对了，如果我们受洗了，肯定不能领圣餐，因为那是吃肉。我们不吃肉。我们就是我们。”

So that’s the ambivalence of the colonizer. Then there is the ambivalence of the colonized, and that, too, has to be understood as a complex relation to co-optation. The anecdote with which Bhabha begins, I think, is fascinating and well worth attending to. You have not a colonizer but someone thoroughly co-opted, an evangelical converted Christian of Indian descent who represents, in a way, that the people he finds sitting under the trees reading the Bible consider to be completely authentic because he believes and is perfectly happy to believe that the Bible, and for that matter Christianity itself, is an English gift. But he’s met with the response of people who resist that, who say, “This is very interesting stuff. We wish we could have some local authority for it. Our understanding is we got this book directly from God, right? That’s our understanding and we have our own attitude toward it. Sure, maybe we’ll get baptized one of these days, but in the meantime we got to go home and take care of the harvest, so we’ll get around to that. Don’t worry about it. By the way, if we get baptized we certainly can’t take the Eucharist because that’s eating meat. We don’t eat meat. We are who we are.”

你可以看到，这些巧妙暗示的附加条件，实际上是在传教士试图灌输给他们的态度上设置了障碍，这完全破坏了他的目的。他们不把它当作英文圣经，也不会接受它作为英文圣经。他们只会把它当作一种权威，但这种权威是由他们自身的价值观所塑造的，从而改变了圣经的本质。你可以再次看到这一点——正如巴巴所指出的，这是1813年。这正是我们正经历的转变，权威体系正从沃伦·黑斯廷斯的模式转向查尔斯·格兰特的模式。我们再也不能像过去那样，根据当地的信仰和环境来调整圣经了。

You can see that these cunningly insinuated provisos to the attitude that the missionary wants to inculcate in them in a very real way completely undermines his purpose. They don’t think of it as the English Bible. They won’t accept it as the English Bible. They will only accept it as an authority that’s mediated by their own values, which transforms the document. You can see it again–this is1813, as Bhabha points out. This is precisely at the moment when we’re moving, when the regime of authority is moving from the Warren Hastings paradigm to the Charles Grant paradigm. It’s no longer possible to think in terms of adapting the Bible to local beliefs and circumstances.

此刻，被殖民者的态度之复杂性便显露出来。一方面是受人收买的传教士的态度，另一方面则是他遇到的那些坐在树下的人们更为复杂也更耐人寻味的态度。请翻到第1881页，左侧栏。这段文字非常难懂。巴巴的著作向来晦涩难懂。我想在此简要说明一下，他所谈论的是被殖民者内心的矛盾——我们不妨直接指出，他为这种矛盾专门创造了一个术语，那就是“混杂性”——这种矛盾体现在被殖民者的双重意识中：一方面是顺从，也就是说，顺从权威但又有所不同，是按照自己的方式顺从权威；另一方面则是默认权威的既定模式，这当然正是传教士的立场。接下来，我将朗读巴巴描述被殖民者双重意识中这种混杂性的段落：

This is a moment in which the complexity of the attitude of the colonized is brought up. There’s the attitude of the suborned missionary, and there’s the more complicated and interesting attitude of the people he encounters sitting under these trees. Turn to page 1881, the left-hand column. This is a very difficult passage. Everything in Bhabha is difficult. I think I want to gloss it by suggesting to you that what he’s talking about is that the ambivalence which–and we might as well say right out that he has a term for this ambivalence, and it’s “hybridity”–is the double consciousness of the colonized hovering between submission–that is to say, submission to authority but with a difference, submission to authority on one’s own terms, and on the other hand, acquiescence in authority as given, which of course is basically the position of the missionary. With that said, I’ll read the passage in which Bhabha describes this hybridity in the double consciousness of the colonized:

在我提出的这种“处置”体系中，差异和他者性的位置，或者说对抗的空间，绝非完全处于外部或毫不妥协的对立状态。[换句话说，并非仅仅是“我们”与“他们”的问题。]它是一种压力，一种存在，持续地、尽管不均衡地作用于授权（即权威）的整个边界，也就是说，它存在于我所谓的“处置即给予”（我将其理解为屈服——简单来说就是“好吧，行，我让步”）和“倾向即倾向”（即“嘿，我挺喜欢的，我同意，我自发地让步”）之间的表面上。## 第七章 “狡猾的礼貌”的意义 仅仅因为承认自己被打败而屈服，仅仅因为屈服是一种顺从，就使人处于巴巴所说的“狡猾的礼貌”的位置。我想再回到这个立场，因为它与盖茨所说的“符号化”（signifyin'）密切相关。巴巴在他的著作中列举了许多这种狡黠的礼貌的例子，当然，这一切也体现在他开篇轶事中那些坐在树下的人物身上，他们所展现的巧妙而丰富的反讽之中。让我举个例子来说明这种狡黠的礼貌是如何作为一种符号化形式，以及一种被殖民的抵抗姿态，一种对意志的恢复——或许带有后现代主义的意味——的运作。然而，这种恢复并非反叛，也并非意图推翻权威，而是一种在权威框架内生存的方式。

The place of difference and otherness, or the space of the adversarial, within such a system of “disposal” as I have proposed, is never entirely on the outside or implacably oppositional. [Not just, in other words, again as a question of us versus them.] It is a pressure, and a presence, that acts constantly, if unevenly, along the entire boundary of authorization [which is also authority], that is, on the surface between what I’ve called disposal-as-bestowal [I take that meaning submission–simply “okay, fine, I give in”] and disposition-as-inclination [which is “hey, I kind of like that, I go along with it, I give in spontaneously”]. ## Chapter 7. “Sly Civility” as Signifyin’ Now to give in simply as a form of recognizing that one’s beaten, as a form of submission, puts one in the position of what Bhabha calls “sly civility.” This is the position that I’d like to go back to for a moment as being very closely related to what Gates calls signifyin’. Bhabha gives a number of examples of this sly civility in his text, but of course it’s all present in the clever and wonderfully rich ironies of these figures sitting under the trees in his opening anecdote. Let me just give you an example of how sly civility works as a form of signifyin’ and as a stance of colonized resistance, a recuperation of the will, perhaps in a post-modern sense, which is nevertheless not rebellious, not in any way envisioning an overthrow of authority, but is a means of living in the framework of authority.

举个简单的例子，然后我就不打扰你了。两个非裔美国人和一个白人聊天，他们面带笑容地称呼这个白人为“比尔”。“比尔”这个词对白人带有贬义和嘲讽意味，而站在旁边的白人听到别人这么称呼自己，有两种选择：他可以生气地说：“你为什么这么叫我？我人很好，你不应该这么说我。”这样一来，这个词的挑衅作用就显现出来了；或者他可以装傻充愣，假装不知道别人在暗指他，假装觉得被叫“比尔”没什么大不了的。无论哪种方式，你看，这都是双赢的局面。这个叫比尔的家伙是奴隶主，对吧？他喜欢和人相处，所以他才会坐在那里和别人聊天，听到别人叫他“比尔”，对吧？因为他奴隶主的性格中还保留着一丝善良，所以他进退两难。他要么抱怨别人对他不公平——当然，就现有的权力结构而言，这种抱怨毫无意义——要么装傻充愣，假装没注意到自己被嘲笑。无论哪种方式，这都体现了他那种狡黠的礼貌，也表明虽然权力结构短期内无法被推翻，但至少在现有的权力结构下，人们仍然可以找到生存之道——至少可以保持幽默感——同时还能给这个奴隶主制造一些麻烦。

Just a quick example and then I’ll let you go. Two African-American people are having a conversation in the presence of a white person, and they cheerfully and with broad smiles on their face refer to this person in his presence as Bill. Now “Bill” is a derisive and derogatory term for white people, and the white person standing there has two choices in response to hearing himself referred to as “Bill”: he can either take umbrage and say, “Why are you saying that about me? I’m a nice guy. You don’t want to say that,” in which case the needling effect of the term has taken hold; or he can play the fool and pretend that he doesn’t know that he’s being signified on and pretend that, well, it’s perfectly okay to be called “Bill.” Either way you see it’s a win/win situation. This guy, Bill, is the slave owner, right? He likes to get along with people, so he’s sitting around having this conversation and he hears them calling him “Bill,” right? Because there is an element of good nature in his slave-owning personality, he’s stuck. He can either complain that people are treating him unfairly–which of course is neither here nor there in terms of the structure of power involved–or he can play the fool and pretend that he doesn’t even notice that he’s being made fun of. Either way, this is an example of that sly civility which signifies on the man and which makes it clear that while the structure of power can’t be overthrown anytime soon, there nevertheless is a way of living–at least of keeping one’s sense of humor within the existing structure of power–while giving the man a hard time.

这就是巴巴在其关于被殖民者混杂性的概念中所阐述的一系列态度，这种态度体现在表演中——我们周二会详细讨论表演——这种狡黠的礼貌的表演中。我认为他在第1889页给出了这个表达，我认为你应该记住它——我会把它与亨利·路易斯·盖茨所说的“signifyin'”非常相似。好的。周二见。

That is the set of attitudes that Bhabha is articulating in his notion of the hybridity of the colonized, which takes the form in performance–we’re going to have a lot more to say about performance on Tuesday–in performance of this sly civility. I think it’s on page 1889 that he gives us that expression, which I think you should keep hold of–which I would compare very closely with what Henry Louis Gates calls “signifyin’.” Okay. See you on Tuesday.

第23讲——酷儿理论与性别表演性

Lecture 23 - Queer Theory and Gender Performativity

第一章 朱迪斯·巴特勒导论：什么是性？

Chapter 1. Introduction to Judith Butler: What Is Sexuality?

保罗·弗莱教授：嗯，我想我以前从未遇到过这种情况——虽然可能遇到过，但我记不起来了——我竟然要就昨天在耶鲁大学讲过课的人做讲座，但这次就是发生了。你们今天早上在《每日新闻》上读到了那篇——姑且称之为——讽刺文章，内容是关于那场讲座的。你们当中有些人可能真的在现场。很遗憾我没能去，但碰巧那天晚上我碰到了她，并和她的一些同事聊了聊她讲的内容，所以我对当时的情况还是有所了解的。

Professor Paul Fry: Now, I don’t think it’s ever happened to me before–although it might have but I can’t recall its having happened–that I found myself lecturing on a person who had lectured yesterday here at Yale, but that’s what happened in this case. You read–let’s just call it–the facetious article on the lecture in The Daily News this morning. Some of you may actually have been in attendance. I unfortunately could not be, but as it happened I ran into her later in the evening and talked to some of her colleagues about what she’d said, so I do have a certain sense of what went on.

总之，关于今天发生的事情，我要谈的是她文章中最难以捉摸的智识现象，即她所谓的“精神过剩”，也就是来自无意识的能量或过剩，它在某种程度上甚至会扰乱那些可以被展现出来的东西。我们展现身份，我们展现主体性，我们以各种方式展现性别，这些都将在本次讲座中讨论，但超越我们所能展现的还有“性”，我稍后会谈到它。这与它所源自的无意识的真实领域有关。巴特勒在昨天的讲座中，重新回到了你们今天要读的文章的精神分析层面，特别强调了拉康的弟子让·拉普朗什的著作，并阐述了性如何属于一个超越且更难以触及的维度，而这些维度比我们通常认为的性别或身份等更为隐晦的概念更为复杂。所以很巧的是，对于昨天参加了她讲座的各位来说，在很多方面，她确实回到了她职业生涯中关注的问题，当时她写了《性别麻烦》一书，也写了你们今天读到的这篇文章。

In any case, as to what went on, I’m going to be talking today about the slipperiest intellectual phenomenon in her essay having to do with what she calls “psychic excess,” the charge or excess from the unconscious which in some measure unsettles even that which can be performed. We perform identity, we perform our subjectivity, we perform gender in all the ways that we’ll be discussing in this lecture, but beyond what we can perform there is “sexuality,” which I’m going to be turning to in a minute. This has something to do with the authentic realm of the unconscious from which it emerges. What Butler did in her lecture yesterday was to return to the psychoanalytic aspect of the essay that you read for today, emphasizing particularly the work of Lacan’s disciple, Jean Laplanche, and developing the ways in which sexuality is something that belongs in a dimension that exceeds and is less accessible than those more coded concepts that we think of as gender or as identity in general. So conveniently enough, for those of you who did attend her lecture yesterday, in many ways she really did return to the issues that concerned her at the period of her career when she wrote Gender Trouble and when she wrote the essay that you’ve read for today.

好的。现在我想先从一个看似简单的问题开始。我们当然有权知道这个问题的答案，那就是：什么是性？当然，你可能会犹豫——尤其如果你对术语比较敏感——你可能会对“性”这个词本身感到疑惑，因为它在语言中显然出现的时间相对较晚。人们过去不谈论性，他们谈论的是性，这似乎更直接一些，但“性”这个词不仅在文化思想中无处不在，而且在描述我们生活中这一方面时，它似乎也具有某种特殊的地位。换句话说，正如我刚才提到的，我们的性中存在着某种真实的东西，它比我们能够并且确实展现的那些自我特质更加真实。这是巴特勒的论点，也是一个有趣的出发点，但它还不是，或者说根本就不是“什么是性？”这个问题的答案。

All right. Now I do want to begin with what ought to be an innocent question. Surely we’re entitled to an answer to this question, and the question is: what is sexuality? Now of course you may be given pause– especially if you’ve got an ear fine-tuned to jargon–you may be given pause by the very word “sexuality,” which is obviously relatively recent in the language. People didn’t used to talk about sexuality. They talked about sex, which seems somehow more straightforward, but “sexuality” is a term which is not only pervasive in cultural thought but also has a certain privilege among other ways of describing that aspect of our lives. In other words, there is something authentic, as I’ve already begun to suggest, about our sexuality, something more authentic about that than the sorts of aspects of ourselves that we can and do perform. That’s Butler’s argument, and it’s an interesting starting point, but it’s not yet, or perhaps not at all, an answer to the question, “What is sexuality?”

第二章 福柯与联盟的部署

Chapter 2. Foucault and the Deployment of Alliance

在福柯看来，性欲可以说是渴望并体验到的身体愉悦，但福柯的问题在于，这种愉悦总是受到一系列复杂因素的制约，这些因素在他的著作第1634页右下角的章节中或许阐述得最为透彻。他探讨的是他所谓的“联盟部署”与“性欲部署”（我们用这个词）之间的区别和互动。我想读一下这段话，然后简要地做个评述：“总而言之（当然，这并非一言以蔽之，而是多言之语），联盟部署与社会机体的稳态相协调……”联盟部署指的是在特定文化中，核心生殖单元（通常指“家庭”）是如何被定义的，但家庭本身的性质和结构也在不断变化。家庭的呈现方式，家庭中应该发生和不应该发生的活动——因为福柯特别强调乱伦及其带来的氛围威胁——家庭中发生的种种事情以及围绕这些事情的特定知识话语——我们稍后会回到这句话的后半部分——所有这些都与联盟的运用有关。另一方面，我们理解的性欲的运用，是指我们试图定义的某种事物被谈论的方式——因此，这种谈论未必是由任何国家机器或实际的法律体系所主导——而仅仅是由各种知识警察的普遍性和力量所主导。

Now for Foucault sexuality is arguably something like desired and experienced bodily pleasure, but the problem in Foucault is that this pleasure is always orchestrated by a set of factors that surround it, a very complicated set of factors which is articulated perhaps best on page 1634 in his text, the lower right-hand column. He’s talking about the difference between and the interaction between what he calls the “deployment of alliance” and the “deployment of”–our word–“sexuality.” I want to read this passage and then comment on it briefly: “In a word [and it’s of course not in a word; it’s in several words], the deployment of alliance is attuned to a homeostasis of the social body…” The deployment of alliance is the way in which, in a given culture, the nuclear reproductive unit is defined, typically as the “family,” but the family in itself changes in its nature and its structure. The way in which the family is viewed, the sorts of activities that are supposed to take place and not take place in the family–because Foucault lays a certain amount of stress on incest and the atmospheric threat of incest–the sorts of things that go on in the family and are surrounded by certain kinds of discourse conveying knowledge–and we’ll come back to the latter part of that sentence–all have to do with the deployment of alliance. On the other hand, the deployment of sexuality we understand as the way in which whatever this thing is that we’re trying to define is talked about–and therefore not by any state apparatus or actual legal system necessarily–but nevertheless simply by the prevalence and force of various sorts of knowledge police.

好的。继续这段文字：

Okay. To continue the passage:

总之，联盟的部署与社会机体的稳态（或称规范化；他所说的“稳态”指的就是这个意思）相契合，其功能在于维持这种稳态；由此，联盟与法律有着特殊的联系（也就是说，法律告诉我们关于家庭的各种事情——包括同性婚姻是否合法，顺便提一下：我稍后会再谈到这一点）；也由此，联盟的重要阶段是“繁衍”。性行为的部署存在的理由并非在于自身的繁衍，而在于以日益精细的方式增殖、创新、吞并、创造和渗透各个群体，并以日益全面的方式控制人口。他想表达的是，性欲的运用（这本身并非坏事——这些运用并非意在建立恐怖主义政权）——例如，如果性欲的运用支持节育或同性恋等性行为形式，那么它无疑是控制生育的一种手段。仅就这一点而言，性欲的运用就可以被视为与联盟的运用存在微妙或明显的冲突。联盟的运用完全是为了生育，或者至少如福柯所言，其主要标志是生育在特定文化（或者说社会生物系统）中的重要性和核心地位。以上便是联盟的运用与性欲的运用在哪些方面趋同、不趋同以及相互冲突。但无论从哪个方面来看，我们都能看到性欲这个概念；然而，正如我所说，它究竟是什么，仍然有些难以捉摸。

In a word, the deployment of alliance is attuned to a homeostasis [or a regularization; that’s what he means by “homeostasis”] of the social body, which it has the function of maintaining; whence its privileged link with the law [that is to say, the law tells us all sorts of things about the family–including whether or not there can be gay marriage, just incidentally: I’ll come back to that in a minute]; whence too the fact that the important phase for it is “reproduction.” The deployment of sexuality has its reason for being, not in reproducing itself, but in proliferating, innovating, annexing, creating, and penetrating bodies in an increasingly detailed way, and in controlling populations in an increasingly comprehensive way. What he’s saying is, among other things, that a deployment of sexuality, which isn’t necessarily a bad thing–these deployments aren’t meant somehow or another to be terroristic regimes–a deployment of sexuality, which for example favored forms of sexuality such as birth control or homosexuality, would certainly be a means of controlling reproduction. Just in that degree, the deployment of sexuality could be seen as subtly or not so subtly at odds with the deployment of alliance, alliance which is all for the purpose of reproduction or at least takes as its primary sign, as Foucault suggests, the importance, the centrality, to a given culture–or sociobiological system, if you wil– of reproduction. These are the ways in which the deployment of alliance and the deployment of sexuality converge, don’t converge, and conflict with each other. But in all of these ways, we keep seeing this concept of sexuality; but, as I say, it continues to be somewhat elusive what precisely it is.

暂且搁置这一点，让我再就刚才读到的段落中的概念做几点补充。首先，我们不妨明确一点：福柯文本的核心思想——他在三卷本性史著作中不断阐述的核心思想——是“权力”的概念，它并非通过法律、警察或国家机器手段强制执行的权力。这种权力以知识的流通或传播的形式得以实施，本质上是话语性的，它对我们所有人强制执行着某种规范，无论好坏——因为话语既可以释放，也可以构成抵抗的场所，同时也可以压迫——这种权力在我们之间流通，在某种意义上支配着我们对任何相关事物的认知，就此而言，显然是性。福柯称之为“权力-知识”，有时也会加上连字符。

Just to bracket that for the moment, let me make another comment or two on the concepts in the passage that I have just read. Let’s say once and for all at the outset that the central idea in Foucault’s text, the idea which he continues to develop throughout the three volumes on the history of sexuality–the central idea is this idea of “power” as something other than that which is enforced through legal, policing or state apparatus means. This is power which is enforced as a circulation or distribution of knowledge, which is discursive in nature, and which enforces its norms for all of us, for betteror for worse–because discourse can release and can constitute sites of resistance as well as oppress–which, for better or worse, circulates among us ideas that are in a certain sense governing ideas about whatever it is that’s in question, in this case, obviously, sexuality. Foucault calls this, sometimes hyphenating it, “power-knowledge.”

这绝对是福柯晚期思想的核心。你还记得吗，上次在谈到萨义德的时候我就提到过它。现在我再回到这个话题，因为它真正主导并引导你理解福柯的整部著作：权力，其传统理解是权威性的——某种自上而下、来自上层、由法律、警察或任何类似机构强加于我们的权力——与这种权力的区别在于，权力仅仅是知识传播的方式——顺便说一句，“知识”这个词未必恰当，它未必是指真理的知识——知识传播的方式，以及知识对我们、我们的行为、我们的存在方式（或者至少是我们自认为的存在方式）——用巴特勒的话来说，就是我们“表演”的方式。在福柯看来，所有这些都应被理解为权力-知识的产物。

This is absolutely the central idea in late Foucault. I introduced it, you remember, last time in talking about Said. I come back to it now as that which really governs–and guides you through–the whole text of Foucault: the distinction between power as it’s traditionally understood as authoritative–as sort of top- down, coming from above, imposed on us by law, by the police, by whatever establishment of that kind there might be–the distinction between power of that kind and power which is simply the way in which knowledge–and knowledge is not, by the way, necessarily a good word, it’s not necessarily knowledge of the truth–the way in which knowledge circulates and imposes its effects on us, our behavior, the way we are or the way at least that we think we are–the way in which we “perform,” in Butler’s term. All of that in Foucault is to be understood as an effect of power-knowledge.

然而，就我们提出的问题——“什么是性？”——而言，请注意福柯的回答相当含糊。他谈论的是性，但并非谈论性本身，无论“性本身”究竟是什么。他谈论的是性如何被运用，也就是说，权力知识如何建构性，如何使性可见，如何使性为我们所用，并使其成为欲望表达的渠道。然而，这个渠道本身未必就是我们所寻求、渴望并不断追寻的自然之物：性的本质。因此，当福柯的讨论重点真正在于运用时，即联盟——家庭，无论核心社会结构如何——或性——无论它如何以欲望的形式表达——这些事物，我们生活的这些方面如何被运用时，我们仍然未必是在谈论事物本身。福柯并非人类学家。他谈论的也不是家庭本身。他谈论的是一种基本的联盟概念，这种联盟概念是繁衍的根源，并且能够被权力知识的流通所利用和操纵。

Now notice, however, in terms of our question–What is sexuality?–that Foucault is being quite coy. He’s talking about sexuality but he’s not talking about it in itself, whatever it “in itself” might be. He’s talking about the deployment of it, that is to say the way in which power-knowledge constructs it, makes it visible, makes it available to us, and makes it a channel through which desire can get itself expressed, but a channel which is still not necessarily in and of itself that natural thing that we look for and long for and continue to seek: the nature of sexuality. So when the emphasis in Foucault’s discussion is really on deployment, that is, the way in which alliance–the family, whatever the nuclear social structure might be–or sexuality–whatever it is that gets itself expressed as desire–the way in which these matters, these aspects of our lives, can be deployed, we still aren’t necessarily talking about the thing in itself. Foucault isn’t an anthropologist. He’s not talking about the family in itself either. He’s talking about the way in which a basic concept of alliance out of which reproduction arises and gets itself channeled can be deployed, and understood as manipulated by, the circulation of power-knowledge.

顺便一提，同性婚姻问题非常有趣，它介于联盟的构建和性取向的构建这两个概念之间，因为在某种程度上，性取向的构建与联盟的构建是相矛盾的。如果性取向仅仅是在寻找表达自身的方式，在合适的场合利用联盟，在感觉更像是监管的地方抵制联盟——如果它只是在寻找表达的方式，那么它对联盟并不特别感兴趣。它对涉及性取向的关系如何形成某种编码模式或规律体系并不感兴趣，因此，这种张力自然会在同性恋群体中表现出来，尤其是在人们强烈支持同性婚姻并将其视为当代同性恋生活政治化的核心时。或者，同性恋群体中的一些人，其中不乏理论思想较为成熟的人士，认为这根本不是问题，或者只是个次要问题，这恰恰忽略了福柯所说的“性欲的运用”，而只是试图扩展“联盟运用”的领域——可以说，这是一种专制的领域——换句话说，他们试图重新定义“联盟”的基本概念，但这种重新定义实际上并没有真正触及“性欲的运用”。因此，整个同性婚姻问题，这个高度政治化的问题，引发了一系列有趣且相当复杂的问题。这就是福柯眼中的“性欲”[笑声]。

The issue of gay marriage is very interestingly, by the way, between the concepts of the deployment of alliance and the deployment of sexuality, because there’s a certain sense in which the deployment of sexuality is at odds with the deployment of alliance. If sexuality is something that is really just looking around for ways to get itself expressed, taking advantage of deployment where that’s a good thing and trying to resist deployment where that seems more like policing–if it’s just looking around for a way to get expressed, it’s not particularly interested in alliance. It’s not interested in the way in which relationships involving sexuality could settle into any kind of a coded pattern or system of regularity, so that there is this tension which, of course, gets itself expressed whenever, within the gay community, people strongly support gay marriage and see that as the politicized center of contemporary gay life; or people also in the gay community, many of them theoretically advanced, think of it as a non-issue or a side issue which loses track precisely of what Foucault calls the deployment of sexuality, simply trying to extend the domain, arguably a tyrannical domain, of the deployment of alliance–in other words, to redefine the basic concept of alliance in such a way that doesn’t really touch very closely on the deployment of sexuality. So it’s an interesting and rather mixed set of issues that the whole question, the whole sort of profoundly politicized question, of gay marriage gives rise to. So that’s what sexuality is [laughter] in Foucault.

第三章 性别表演

Chapter 3. Performing Gender

在巴特勒的著作中，我们更清楚地看到，提出“什么是性？”这个问题——其实只是个错误的开始。我们最初以为这只是个无伤大雅的问题，但当你深入了解巴特勒的理论后，你会非常清楚地看到，你根本无法成为某种特定的性取向。正如我们将看到的，你可以通过重复、模仿和反串等方式来表演一种身份。你可以表演一种身份，但你无法完全表演性，正是因为这种精神上的过剩——而巴特勒的思考始终坦诚、公开且诚实地回归到这一层面。换句话说，巴特勒的作品不仅仅关乎“身份的建构”，也不仅仅关乎表演的领域。它承认，在表演之外，存在着一些难以把握和表达的东西。它的主要任务是解释表演的性质、范围和目的，但巴特勒在谈到无意识问题时，总是清楚地表明，表演的概念之外，或者说表演的概念无法完全涵盖某些东西。

In Butler it’s just clearer that to ask the question–What is sexuality?– is–well, it’s just been a false start. We thought it was an innocent question, but you get into Butler and you see very clearly that you simply can’t be a certain sexuality. You can perform an identity, as we’ll see, by repeating, by imitating, and by parodying in drag. You can perform an identity, but you can’t wholly perform sexuality precisely because of this element of psychic excess to which her thinking continues very candidly and openly and honestly to return. Butler’s work, in other words, is not just about “the construction of identity.” It’s not just about the domain of performance, as one might say. It acknowledges that there is something very difficult to grasp and articulate beyond performance. Its main business is to explain the nature and purview and purposes of performance, but it’s nevertheless always clear in Butler, as she returns to the question of the unconscious in particular, that there is something in excess of, or not fully to be encompassed by, ideas of performance.

所以，我们开了个错头。我们问了一个无法回答的问题，但与此同时，我们也学到了一些东西。我们确实学到，无论性欲是什么，它都更加灵活，而且在某种意义上也更加真实——也就是说，它更接近本能的真实本质。昨天，巴特勒区分了本能和本能，我在此不做赘述，因为这与她对无意识生活中哪些是文化因素、哪些是生物因素或非文化因素的思考有关。就我们的目的而言，无论性欲在无意识中扮演什么角色，无论它多么真实——也就是说，无论这个角色最终被证明多么非文化决定——它都更加灵活。这才是最重要的，比任何形式的社会编码都重要：例如，福柯在谈到联盟或部署的性欲时所指的那种编码，以及巴特勒反复提到的“性别化”的那种编码。

So we’ve made a false start. We’ve asked a question we can’t answer, but at the same time we have learned certain things. We’ve learned certainly that sexuality, whatever it is, is more flexible and also in some sense more authentic–that is to say, closest to the actual nature of the drives. Yesterday Butler made a distinction between instinct and drive which I won’t go into because it had to do with her reflections on what is cultural and what is biological or not cultural in the life of the unconscious. For our purposes, whatever role sexuality may play in the unconscious, and however authentic–that is to say, however not culturally determined that role may turn out to be–it’s more flexible. That’s the important thing, more than any kind of social coding: the sort of coding, for example, that Foucault would indicate in speaking of alliance or deployed sexuality and the sort of coding that Butler refers to repeatedly as “gendering.”

然而，对他们二人而言——这也是我们所学到的另一点——即使是通过部署，或者通过与性别和表演相关的表达方式来展现的性，也具有话语性。它关乎话语。它源于语言结构，福柯将其理解为流通的知识，而巴特勒则再次将其理解为表演。福柯将性视为权力知识的产物，权力即知识。巴特勒则将其视为表演的产物——就其可见性而言，就其被演绎而言。

Still, for both of them–and this is the other thing we’ve learned–even sexuality through deployment, or through the way in which it can get expressed in relation to gender and performance, is discursive. It’s a matter of discourse. It arises out of linguistic formations, formations that Foucault understands as circulated knowledge and that Butler understands, again, as performance. Foucault sees sexuality as the effect of power-knowledge, power as knowledge. Butler sees it as the effect–insofar as it’s visible, insofar as it is acted out–sees it as the effect of performance.

现在，让我们来看看巴特勒是如何构建这种关系的：一方面是人们可能认为的真实、现实的、关乎自我的一切，另一方面是表演出来的、人们为了成为自我而建构的东西。我们来看她文章中最具启发性的一句话，这句话在第1711页，大约三分之一处：“自从我十六岁起，我就一直是个女同性恋。” 她这样做——记住，在文章开头她就说过，她写作的全部目的在于反思——她实际上是想以某种方式，从哲学反思的角度，对性别研究进行一次政治化的介入，反思本体论，反思“存在”。换句话说，她问，成为某种东西究竟是什么？ 这句话——“我一直都是个女同性恋”——看似有些别扭，但她实际上是在向我们指出，“成为某种东西”与“成为”某种东西是截然不同的。

So now to take the way in which Butler makes this relationship between what one might suppose to be authentic, actual, all about one’s self, and that which is performed, that which is one’s constructs toward being a self, let’s take one of the most provocative sentences in her essay, which is on page 1711 about a third of the way down: “Since I was sixteen, being a lesbian is what I’ve been.” Now what she’s doing–remember at the very beginning of the essay she says that her whole purpose is to reflect, is somehow or another to register a politicized intervention in gender studies in terms of a philosophical reflection–on ontology, on “being.” What is it in other words, she says, to be something? Now what she’s doing in this sentence, which is an awkward-seeming sentence, “[B]eing a lesbian is what I’ve been,” is pointing out to us that to be something is very different from to be “being” something.

例如，我可以说我很忙。（顺便说一句，我的确很忙。）我可以这样说，并且希望你能理解我所说的“忙”本身就具有某种真诚和真实性。是的，我很忙，但假设你怀疑我其实并不忙，然后说：“哦，他是在装忙。”换句话说，他是在表演忙碌。他到处装忙，试图让我觉得这个懒人其实在做事。所以，这就是表演忙碌。但巴特勒提出的有趣观点是：本体论领域应该关注事物的简单存在，而哲学总是将其与能动性、行动、完成某事、表演事物等概念对立起来。但巴特勒想表达的是——这也是她为何对这个问题的本体论层面感兴趣的原因——她想表达的是，存在一种表演性的因素，这种因素实际上悄然渗入了本体论层面。她说，甚至“存在”本身，在某种程度上——或许并非完全如此，但确实在某种程度上——也是我们表演出来的。因此，在“自从我十六岁以来，我就一直是女同性恋”这句话中，“存在”一词被重复使用。

For example, I can say I’m busy. (By the way, I am.) I can say I’m busy and I expect you to take it that there’s a certain integrity, there’s a certain authenticity in the fact that I’m busy. Yes, I’m busy, but suppose you say, suspecting that I’m not really busy, “Oh, he’s being busy.” In other words, he’s performing busy-ness. He’s going around being busy, sort of imposing on me the idea that this lazy person is actually accomplishing something. So, the performance of being busy. But here’s the interesting point that Butler is making: the ontological realm is supposed to be about the simple being or existence of things, and it’s always in philosophy contrasted with agency, with the doing of things, with getting something done, with the performance of things. But what Butler is saying–and that’s why she says that she takes an interest in the ontological aspect of the question–what she’s saying is that there is an element of the performative which actually creeps into the ontological. Even being, she says, is something that in some measure–perhaps not altogether but in some measure–something we perform. Hence the doubling up of the word “being” in the sentence, “Since I was sixteen, being a lesbian is what I’ve been.”

从某种意义上说，是的，我就是——我就是这样的人，但从另一个意义上说，我一直在扮演这个角色。我一直在做我自己。[笑] 如果你愿意的话，我可以说是在“出柜”。我一直在扮演一个角色，就像所有角色一样，可以通过表演来理解。所以她才会那样写这句话，如果你在旁边做了个大标记，说：“啊哈，抓到她了！她在这里表明了她真正的身份。别再说什么建构主义、随心所欲地塑造自己了。她在这里表明了她真正的身份，”那你就错了。[笑] 她逃脱了你的批评，因为她说：“哦，不，不，不。我一直在扮演一个女同性恋：我一直在做我自己，这和成为女同性恋是两回事，虽然并非完全不同。”换句话说，她刻意地游走于本体论的真实性和她自身对本体论的创新理解——即本体论属于表演领域——之间。她不想离开这个中间地带。她真的不想完全站在任何一边，因为对她而言——这也是我最欣赏她作品的地方，尽管这或许也是最令人沮丧的地方——因为她所谈论的最终是神秘的。她对此有很多话要说，但她并不假装自己已经穷尽了关于这个“主题”的一切。正因如此，我认为她在这方面保持这种摇摆不定的态度是令人钦佩的，而不仅仅是让我们感到沮丧的原因。

In one sense, yeah, I am–that’s what I am, but in another sense I’ve been performing it. I’ve been being one. [laughs] I’ve been outing myself, if you will. I have been taking up a role that can be understood, as all roles can, intelligibly in terms of its performance. So that’s why she puts the sentence that way, and if you made a big mark in the margin and said, “Aha, got her! This is where she says she really is something. No more of this stuff about just constructivism, making oneself up as one goes along. This is where she says she really is something,” then you’re wrong. [laughs] She’s escaped your criticism because she says, “Oh, no, no, no. I have been being a lesbian: I’ve been being one, which is a different thing, although not altogether a different thing, from being one.” She is deliberately, in other words, on the fence between the sense of the ontological as authentic and her own innovative sense of the ontological as belonging within the realm of performance. She doesn’t want to get off the fence. She really doesn’t want to come down squarely on either side because for her–and this is what I like best about her work, even though it’s perhaps the most frustrating thing about it–because for her, what she is talking about is ultimately mysterious. She has a great deal to say about it, but she’s not pretending that in what she has to say about it she’s exhausted the “subject.” That’s why it seems to me to be admirable that she stays on the fence about this, and not simply an occasion for our frustration.

第四章 性别理论的政治议程

Chapter 4. The Political Agenda of Gender Theory

综上所述——暂且抛开故弄玄虚——显而易见，福柯和巴特勒确实有着共同的政治诉求。福柯是一位同性恋作家，在撰写《性史》后期，他正因艾滋病去世；巴特勒是一位女同性恋作家。他们都十分关注自身边缘化性别角色的政治意义，同时，他们对这些角色的理论探讨也十分精辟。他们共同的政治诉求在于，通过否定特权性别角色的真实性，或者用巴特勒的话来说，否定其“原创性”，来动摇异性恋规范。换句话说，谁说异性恋是先于一切存在的？谁说核心家庭是自然而然的？谁说性只能以权力知识所赋予的特定方式表达？这些正是他们共同提出的政治问题。

So with all of this said–and mystification aside, if you will, as well–with all of this said, it seems plain that Foucault and Butler do have a common political agenda. Foucault is a gay writer who was, in the later stages of writing The History of Sexuality, dying of AIDS; Butler is a lesbian writer. Both of them are very much concerned for the political implications of their marginalized gender roles, while at the same time–of course, being theoretically very sophisticated about them. Their common political agenda is to destabilize the hetero-normative by denying the authenticity, or in Butler’s parlance “originality,” of privileged gender roles. In other words, who says heterosexuality came first? Who says the nuclear family is natural? Who says sexuality can only get itself expressed in certain ways that power-knowledge deploys for it? These are the sorts of questions, the politicized questions, which these discourses raise in common.

所以在我看来，他们有着非常广泛的共同目标，而且他们的立场也高度一致。我之所以这么说，是为了稍作停顿，谈谈他们似乎存在分歧的地方。你可能已经注意到，在阅读过程中，有一段文字提到了另一段文字，那么我们就来看看：第1712页，右侧页边空白处。当然，这里的背景是巴特勒谈到杰西·赫尔姆斯在抨击罗伯特·梅普尔索普的摄影作品时谴责了男性同性恋，巴特勒认为，这实际上抹杀了女性同性恋的存在，因为他的抨击完全忽略了女性同性恋。巴特勒接着抱怨说，这其中存在某种不公，因为在某种程度上，被宣布不存在甚至比被宣布为异类更糟糕。至少男性同性恋者会被宣布为异类：而我们女性同性恋者却被彻底抹杀了。这就是她在这里所持的立场，然后，她接着说：

So it seems to me that they have a very broad agenda in common, and it also seems to me that they are very closely in agreement. I say that just in order to pause briefly on the moment in which they seem not to be. You’ve probably noticed that one text is referring to another at one point in your reading, and so let’s go there: page 1712, the right-hand margin. The context for this, of course, is Butler talking about Jesse Helms having deplored male homosexuality in attacking the photography of Robert Mapplethorpe, and by implication, Butler argues, simply erasing female homosexuality because his diatribe pays no attention to it. Butler then complains that there’s a certain injustice in that because, in a way, it’s even worse, she says, sort of to be declared nonexistent than it is to be declared deviant. At least the male homosexual gets to be declared deviant: we’re simply erased. That’s the position she’s taking here, and then at that point, what she says is:

被明确禁止意味着占据了一个话语场域，从中可以展开类似反向话语的内容；而被隐性禁止则甚至不构成被禁止的对象。在这里，她给我们提供了一个关于福柯的脚注，脚注十五（你知道我们喜欢脚注）：

To be prohibited explicitly is to occupy a discursive site from which something like a reverse-discourse can be articulated; to be implicitly proscribed is not even to qualify as an object of prohibition. Here’s where she gives us a footnote on Foucault, footnote fifteen (you know we love footnotes):

福柯在其权力分析中大多忽略了这种特殊的抹除伎俩。巴特勒的论点是，用福柯的话来说，身份的产生必须以话语为前提。赫尔姆斯拒绝“女同性恋”这一范畴——当然，我们都知道，这仅仅是拒绝——换句话说，赫尔姆斯对这一范畴的拒绝，实际上就是对话语的抹除。没有话语，就没有身份。换句话说，这就是巴特勒声称福柯的立场所蕴含的。话语创造权力知识。权力知识创造身份。因此，没有话语，就没有身份，既然赫尔姆斯通过拒绝关于女同性恋的话语抹去了这一概念，那么必然得出女同性恋者并不存在。这就是这条脚注的含义。待续：

It is this particular ruse of erasure which Foucault for the most part fails to take account of in his analysis of power. Butler’s argument is that in Foucauldian terms, there’s got to be discourse for there to be identity. Helms’s refusal of the category of “lesbian” simply by omission–and of course, we know, by the way, that this is a refusal only by omission–Helms’s refusal of this category is, in other words, an erasure of discourse. No discourse, no identity. That is, in other words, what Butler is claiming Foucault’s position entails. Discourse creates power-knowledge. Power-knowledge creates identity. Therefore, where there’s no discourse, there can be no identity, and since Helms has erased the lesbian by refusing discourse about it, it must follow that there is no such thing as a lesbian. That’s the implication of this footnote. To continue:

他几乎总是假定（我们必须尊重“几乎”这个词），权力是通过话语作为其工具而产生的，压迫与臣服和主体化紧密相连，也就是说，它被确立为主体身份的形成原则。现在，为了捍卫福柯的观点，让我们翻到第1632页右上角的专栏，这段文字在很多方面都引人入胜。它相当长，但我还是会读一读，就是右上角那一栏。福柯说：

He almost always presumes [and we must do honor to that word “almost”] that power takes place through discourse as its instrument, and that oppression is linked with subjection and subjectivization, that is, that it is installed as the formative principle of the identity of subjects. Now in defense of Foucault, let’s go to page 1632, the upper right-hand column, a passage that’s fascinating on a number of grounds. It’s rather long but I think I will read it, upper right-hand column. Foucault says:

例如，想想曾经被视为“最大的”反自然罪行——鸡奸的历史。关于鸡奸——这个极其混乱的范畴——的文本极其谨慎，以及人们几乎普遍对此讳莫如深，这使得双重作用成为可能。福柯指出，鸡奸是一个范畴。从鸡奸的角度理解的同性恋身份是一个范畴。他接下来会说，鸡奸在法律上是要受到严厉惩罚的，但与此同时，他又说，关于鸡奸的讨论几乎一片空白。人们对这个话题几乎保持沉默。当然，你肯定知道，但丁的作品中并没有沉默，但在那个时期的大多数情况下，没有人谈论鸡奸。鸡奸是要受到惩罚的，而且是要受到严厉惩罚的，然而却没有人谈论它。这似乎违背了福柯自己关于话语构成身份的前提，也显然与巴特勒关于福柯认为话语总是构成身份的说法相矛盾。

Consider for example the history of what was once “the” great sin against nature. The extreme discretion of the texts dealing with sodomy–that utterly confused category–and the nearly universal reticence in talking about it made possible a twofold operation. Okay. Here’s Foucault saying that this is a category. The homosexual identity, as understood in terms of sodomy, is a category. He’s going to go on to say that it’s punishable in the extreme by law, but in the meantime he’s saying there’s no discourse. There’s a kind of almost universal silence on the subject. You don’t get silence in Dante, as I’m sure you know, but in most cases in this period nobody talks about it. It’s punishable, severely punishable by law, and yet nobody talks about it. This would seem to violate Foucault’s own premise that discourse constitutes identity but also plainly doescontradict Butler’s claim that Foucault supposes that discourse always constitutes identity.

我们继续：

Let’s continue:

……人们几乎普遍对此保持沉默，这使得双重作用成为可能：一方面，刑罚极其严厉（火刑一直持续到十八世纪，直到十八世纪中叶才出现实质性的抗议）[话语在这里也失效了，因为它没有构成抵抗的场所，没有人抱怨这些严厉的刑罚，正如另一方面，也没有人经常谈论它们一样：换句话说，话语被抹杀了]，另一方面，[他继续说道]一种普遍存在的宽容（我们可以从司法判决的罕见性间接推断出来，也可以从一些关于军队或法庭中存在的男性群体的陈述中更直接地窥见一斑）——换句话说，他认为存在一种身份认同，而这种身份认同并非——至少在很大程度上——由话语构成。当你继续阅读这篇文章时，你会发现他接下来会说，在某种程度上，同性恋者的困境在人们开始谈论它之后反而恶化了。没错，对同性恋的惩罚确实减轻了，但对同性恋的监视——这种监视可能受到心理治疗、神职人员以及所有可能对此发表意见的人的左右——变得比以前更加普遍和确定，也更加根深蒂固。在某种程度上，福柯甚至认为，沉默虽然对少数人来说是危险的，但对大多数人来说却是一件好事；而话语或许能让少数人摆脱极度的恐惧，但却会对所有留下来的人施加一种霸权权威，并将他们塑造成权力知识所认为的样子，而不是他们基于自身性取向而自然而然形成的样子。在我看来，巴特勒提出的与福柯的尖锐分歧，福柯本人早已预先回应。即便在这一点上，仔细想想，他们其实也意见一致。福柯的立场比她自己认为的要灵活得多，但这仅仅意味着它与她自己的立场相似。正如我所说，这一点，再加上他们广泛的共同政治诉求，在我看来，都表明他们的写作非常协调一致，彼此的观点也高度契合。

… [T]he nearly universal reticence in talking about it made possible a twofold operation: on the one hand, there was an extreme severity (punishment by fire was meted out well into the eighteenth century, without there being any substantial protest expressed before the middle of the century) [Discourse is here failing also in that it’s not constituting a site of resistance, and nobody’s complaining about these severe punishments just as on the other hand nobody’s talking very much about them: there is, in other words, an erasure of discourse], and [he continues] on the other hand, a tolerance that must have been widespread (which one can deduce indirectly from the infrequency of judicial sentences, and which one glimpses more directly through certain statements concerning societies of men that were thought to exist in the army or in the courts)– In other words, he’s saying there was an identity and that identity was not–at least not very much– constituted by discourse. As you read down the column, he’s going to go on to say that in a way, the plight of the homosexual got worse when it started being talked about. Yes, penalties for being homosexual were less severe, but the surveillance of homosexuality–the way in which it could be sort of dictated to by therapy and by the clergy and by everyone else who might have something to say about it–became far more pervasive and determinate than it was when there was no discourse about it. In a certain way, Foucault is going so far as to say silence was, while perilous to the few, a good thing for the many; whereas discourse which perhaps relieves the few of extreme fear nevertheless sort of imposes a kind of hegemonic authority on all that remain and constitutes them as something that power-knowledge believes them to be, rather than something that in any sense according to their sexuality they spontaneously are. It seems to me that this pointed disagreement with Foucault, raised by Butler, is answered in advance by Foucault and that even there, when you think about it, they’re really in agreement with each other. Foucault’s position is more flexible than she takes it to be, but that just means that it’s similar to her own and, as I say, that fact together with the broad shared political agenda that they have seems to me to suggest that they’re writing very much in concert and in keeping with each other’s views.

第五章 福柯的方法，巴特勒的方法

Chapter 5. Foucault’s Method, Butler’s Method

在方法论上，他们略有不同。福柯是一位更注重历史的作家，尽管历史学家经常批评他缺乏历史性。历史学家认为他缺乏历史性的原因在于，他从未真正解释过历史中各个时刻是如何衔接的。他谈论历史时刻，但他是从知识体系的角度来谈论这些时刻——他有时称之为“认知时刻”。然后，这些时刻以某种神秘的方式转化为其他时刻，并发生转变。从历史学家的角度来看，能够解释这种现象的因果关系，在福柯的论证中往往被忽略了。

Now in method they are somewhat different. Foucault is a more historical writer, although historians often criticize him for not being historical. The reason historians don’t think he’s historical is that he never really explains how you get from one moment in history to the next. He talks about moments in history, but he talks about them in terms of bodies of knowledge–“epistemic moments,” as he sometimes says. Then these moments somehow mysteriously become other moments and are transformed. The kind of causality that might explain such a thing from an historian’s point of view tends in Foucault’s arguments to be left out.

然而，他仍然关注事物观念随时间推移而发生的变化，而他在《性史》中的论述也主要集中于这种观念的转变；因此，他认为从十九世纪至今，权力知识主要围绕着四个群体展开。他将它们描述为歇斯底里的女性、手淫的儿童以及马尔萨斯夫妇——即被要求不要过度生育的夫妇，因为经济不允许这种情况发生。这是一种利用联盟来操纵和控制生育的方式。顺便一提，在这一点上，联盟的运用和性行为的运用可能是相互关联的，因为显然，节育和同性恋行为也能控制生育。由此可见，这两种运用方式并非总是相互冲突的。总之，这里存在马尔萨斯式的夫妇，以及性变态的成年人，也就是各种形式的同性恋者。他在第1634页左栏中谈到这一点时说，你会遇到这四种类型，并且他认为，心理治疗、神职人员、家庭、父母的建议以及此类知识传播的各种途径，主要都与人们对这四种类型的关注、紧张和焦虑有关。一旦人们开始认为歇斯底里的女性的全部存在就是她的性欲，她就被认定为歇斯底里。手淫的儿童违背了儿童生来纯洁且必须保持纯洁的观念——因为它暗示了始于19世纪的“纯洁儿童崇拜”存在着某种可怕的错误——因此，这种行为会受到极其严密的监视。“谁知道这会带来什么后果呢？”关于手淫的科学观点主要集中在它会导致阳痿的观念上，认为等你真正开始谈恋爱的时候，可能什么都没有了。这些想法非常可怕——甚至有人认为手淫会阻碍发育，导致早逝——总之，关于手淫的种种可怕想法一直存在。这些观点在20世纪的大部分时间里都主导着科学文献。

He nevertheless is concerned, however, with the way in which views of things change over time, and it’s the change in those views that his argument in The History of Sexuality tends to concentrate on; so that he can say that starting in the nineteenth century and continuing to the present, there are essentially four cathected beings around which power-knowledge deploys itself. He describes them as the hysterical woman, the masturbating child, the Malthusian couple–meaning the couple that is enjoined not to reproduce too much because the economy won’t stand for it, which is a way of, you see, of deploying alliance in such a way as to manipulate and control reproduction. That’s a moment, by the way, in which the deployment of alliance and the deployment of sexuality may be in league with each other, because obviously birth control and homosexual practices can also control reproduction. As you see, it’s not always a question of conflict between these two forms of deployment. So in any case, there’s the Malthusian couple and then the perverse adult, meaning the queer person in whatever form. He says about this–on page 1634 in the left-hand column–that you get these four types, and he says that therapy, the clergy, family, parental advice, and the various ways in which knowledge of this kind circulates have to do primarily with the preoccupation with, tension about, anxiety about these four types. The hysterical woman is determined to be hysterical once it begins to be thought that her whole being is her sexuality. The masturbating child violates the idea that children are born innocent and must be–because it suggests something terribly wrong about the cult of the innocent child that begins in the nineteenth century–it’s something that is subject to extreme and severe surveillance. “Who knows what will come of this?” Scientific thinking about masturbation had to do with the notion that it led to impotence, that by the time you got around to being in a relationship, there wouldn’t be anything there anymore. Just terrible thoughts–also it stunted your growth and you died sooner–just terrible, terrible thoughts about masturbation existed.
