All of this dominated the scientific literature until well into the twentieth century.

然后是马尔萨斯夫妇，这主要是十九世纪早期所谓“政治经济学”领域的一种现象，但顺便一提，它也存在于我们认为的、实际上也确实是我们在全球范围内推广节育的进步技术中。“我们必须控制人口”仍然是马尔萨斯原则，我们以此为基础认为，人们确实需要认识到生育并非无限的可能性。由此可见，福柯的假设仍然是正确的，马尔萨斯夫妇的观念在我们当中仍然盛行。最后是变态的成年人，正如我前面读到的段落所暗示的那样，这个概念最早出现在十九世纪，当然，它至今仍然是人们广泛讨论的话题。当然，它现在有了自己的声音和话语体系：文学、新闻等等，换句话说，它已经非常接近主流话语，并且仍然充满争议，正是因为依附于它的话语体系。

Then the Malthusian couple, which was primarily a phenomenon of what’s called “political economy” in the earlier nineteenth century but has prevailed, by the way, in what we suppose to be, and indeed what is, our progressive technology of the promotion of birth control around the world. “We must control population” is still the Malthusian principle on which we base the idea that people really need to be enlightened about the possibility of not just having an infinite number of children. Again you see that Foucault is right still to suppose that the notion of the Malthusian couple prevails among us. Then finally the perverse adult, who is first discoursed about in the nineteenth century, as the earlier passage that I read suggested, and is still, of course, widely discoursed about. Of course it now has a voice and discourses in its own right: a literature, a journalism and all the rest of it, and is in other words very much in the mainstream of discourse and still has controversy swirling around it, precisely because of the discursive formations that attach to it.

福柯认为这一切都属于历史观察的范畴。而巴特勒的风格则截然不同，正如你从她的文风中可以感受到的——我相信，就像阅读巴巴的作品一样，你会在巴特勒的风格中发现许多德里达的影子——巴特勒关注的是将这些相同的问题更多地引向哲学领域。我已经指出，她将这篇文章理解为对“本体论”（存在哲学）这一哲学分支的贡献。总的来说，她对本体论抱有特别而敏锐的兴趣。我希望到目前为止，你已经熟悉、理解甚至可能已经预料到她的基本思路。

All of this Foucault takes to be in the nature of historical observation. For Butler on the other hand, as you can tell from her style–I am sure that, as in the case of reading Bhabha, you recognize a lot of Derrida in Butler’s style–in Butler it’s a question of taking these same issues and orienting them more in the direction of philosophy. I’ve already suggested the way in which she understands this particular essay as a contribution to that branch of philosophy called “ontology,” the philosophy of being. In general she takes a particular and acute interest in that. Her basic move is something that I hope by this time you’ve become familiar with and recognize and perhaps even anticipate.

对我们而言，或许这类研究的开端是列维-斯特劳斯提出的各种区分。我特别提到的一个区分——我认为它通俗易懂，而且能直接解释这一研究方法的运作方式——是“生”与“熟”。我试图表明，从直觉上讲，生显然先于熟。先是生的，然后是熟的。然而，如果我们把生与熟之间的关系理解为一种话语建构，我们就必须认识到，如果没有熟，也就不存在生。如果你说吃生胡萝卜，那你肯定吃过熟胡萝卜。你不可能拿起一根从未见过的胡萝卜，然后说：“这是生的。” 你只有知道它可以被煮熟，而且已经被煮熟，才能知道它是生的。

For us, perhaps, the inaugural moves of this kind were the various distinctions made by Levi-Strauss. The one that I mentioned in particular–as accessible and I think immediately explanatory of how the move works–is “the raw” and “the cooked.” I tried to show that intuitively, obviously, the raw precedes the cooked. First it’s raw, then it’s cooked, and yet at the same time if we understand the relationship between the raw and the cooked to be a discursive formation, we have to recognize that there would be no such thing as the raw if there weren’t the cooked. If you talk about eating a raw carrot, you have to have had a cooked carrot. You don’t just pick up a carrot, which you’ve never seen before, and say, “This is raw.” The only way you know it’s raw is to know that it can be and has been cooked.

嗯，这就是巴特勒惯用的伎俩，她一遍又一遍地重复着这套说辞。什么意思？异性恋先于同性恋？什么意思？异性恋是原创，同性恋只是它的复制品？谁会想到异性恋这个概念？你是地球上唯一一个站在那里说“我是异性恋”的人。[笑] 你不会这么做。你只会说“我有性取向”。你可以这么说。如果你有足够的术语，你可以这么说，但你不能说“我是异性恋”。没有同性恋的概念，就不可能有异性恋的概念。它们完全相互依存，这与先有鸡还是先有蛋的自然法则毫无关系。在性取向问题上，巴特勒的强烈假设是，两者都不是先出现的。它们总是同时存在于我们用来定义性的那种精神过剩之中，但在社会层面上，认为异性恋是自然的，而同性恋是不自然的、次要的、衍生的、模仿异性恋的，这种想法被一个简单的事实所否定：在概念上，两者是不可分割的。

Well, this is the Butler move, the move that she makes again and again and again. What do you mean, the heterosexual precedes the homosexual? What do you mean, the heterosexual is an original and the homosexual is just a copy of it? Who would ever think of the concept of the heterosexual? You’re the only person on earth. You stand there and you say, “I’m heterosexual.” [laughs] You don’t do that. You just say, “Well, I have sexuality.” You could say that. If you had enough jargon at your disposal, you could say that, but you can’t say, “I am heterosexual.” You can’t have the concept heterosexual without having the concept homosexual. They are absolutely mutually dependent, and it has nothing to do with any possible truth of a chicken and egg nature as to which came first. In sexuality, the very strong supposition is for Butler that neither came first. They’re always already there together in that psychic excess with which we identify sexuality, but in social terms the idea that what’s natural is the heterosexual and what’s unnatural, secondary, derivative, and imitative of the heterosexual is the homosexual is belied simply by the fact that you can’t have one conceptually without the other.

性别和变装也是如此。变装表演是对性别的戏仿、模仿和模仿，但它所指出的是，性别本身始终是一种表演。当然，这或许可以算作一种批判，但我们在表演方面都堪称行家。瞧，我就站在你们面前，表演着专业精神，表演着白人身份，表演着男性气质。我同时在做着所有这些事情。我真是个表演高手：多么精彩的表演啊！[笑声] 也许很难想象我站在这里，除了表演其他所有东西之外，仅仅是在表演男性气质，但好吧，我当然也在表演男性气质。巴特勒认为，我对所有这些都感到不安，因为我一直在表演它们。换句话说，我一直在重复我自认为的样子。我大概是不自在，也无法自然而然地融入我所认为的自己。我是在表演。换句话说，这是一种持续不断的自我构建，它同时起到两个作用：一方面，它稳定了我的身份认同（这正是它的初衷）；另一方面，它也暴露了我对自身身份的焦虑，因为我必须不断重复这种自我构建才能维持下去。

It’s the same thing with gender and drag. Drag comes along and parodies, mimics, and imitates gender, but what it points out is that gender is always in and of itself precisely performance. This could, of course, take the form of a critique, I suppose, but we’re all quite virtuoso when it comes to performing. Here I am. I’m standing in front of you performing professionalism. I’m performing whiteness. I’m performing masculinity. I’m doing all of those things. I’m quite a virtuoso: what a performance! [laughter] Perhaps it’s kind of hard to imagine my standing here sort of exclusively performing masculinity as opposed to all the other things that I am performing, but okay, I’m certainly doing that too. I’m insecure about all of these things, Butler argues, because I keep performing them. In other words, I keep repeating what I suppose myself to be. I’m not comfortable in my skin, presumably, and I don’t just relax into what I suppose myself to be. I perform it. It is, in other words, a perpetual self-construction which does two things at once. It stabilizes my identity, which is its intention, but at the same time it betrays my anxiety about my identity in that I must perpetually repeat it to keep it going.

所有这一切都发生在“表演”的概念之中，而变装恰恰将这一切呈现在我们面前。它一劳永逸地向我们揭示了，在我们自以为是地将自己融入的、看似自然的性别范畴（就像一套舒适的旧衣服）中，真正岌岌可危的是什么。变装，完全不是舒适的旧衣服，它提醒我们（笑），我们称之为身份的这身装束实际上有多么尴尬，因此它扮演着这样的角色。身份与表演之间的关系也是如此。这种表演身份的概念应该让你想起亨利·路易斯·盖茨思想中的“符号化”（signifyin'）。换句话说，它应该让你想起，通过戏仿、嘲讽、自我疏离，以及一种“自身之所以存在，恰恰是因为它并非仅仅占据他人的主体位置”的意识，他人的身份是如何被挪用的。

All of this is going on in this notion of performance, so what drag does is precisely bring all this to our attention. It shows us once and for all that that’s what’s at stake in the seemingly natural categories of gender that we imagine ourselves to inhabit like a set of comfortable old clothes. Drag, which is not at all comfortable old clothes, reminds [laughs] us how awkward the apparel of ourselves that we can call our identity actually is, and so it plays that role. The relationship between identity and performance is just the same. This notion of performing identity should recall for you “signifyin’” in the thinking of Henry Louis Gates. It should recall for you, in other words, the way in which the identity of another is appropriated through parody, through derision, through self-distancing, and through a sense of the way in which one issomething precisely insofar as one is not simply inhabiting the subject position of another.

这还应该让你想起霍米·巴巴思想中底层民众的“狡黠礼貌”：双重意识既处于他者的主体位置，又处于自身的主体位置，从而使人摆脱了“他人才是真实的，而自己是某种衍生的、从属的、依赖的”这种观念。所有这些关系都应该在你心中融会贯通，因为它们都属于同一个思想领域。正如你不能只吃生的而不吃熟的一样，一般来说，自我与他者以及身份本身这些范畴，都不能被独立地、稳定地思考，而只能在关系中思考。

It should also recall for you the “sly civility” of the subaltern in Homi Bhabha’s thinking: the way in which double consciousness is partly in the subject position of another, partly in one’s own in such a way that one liberates oneself from the sense that it’s the other person who is authentic and that one is oneself somehow derivative, subordinate, and dependent. All of these relations ought to gel in your minds as belonging very much to the same sphere of thought. The way in which you can’t have the raw without the cooked is the way in which, generally speaking, categories of self and other and of identity per se simply can’t be thought in stable terms in and for themselves, but only relationally.

第六章 阅读的性别化

Chapter 6. The Gendering of Reading

现在你可能会问自己，“为什么这是文学理论？”或者你一直在问自己这个问题。当然，巴特勒在文章结尾给出了一个最好的例子，她说：“假设艾瑞莎在为我唱歌。”“你让我感觉”不是一个自然的女人，因为根本不存在所谓的自然。“你让我感觉像个自然的女人”，这里的“你”大概指的是某个异性恋规范的“他者”，向我展示了真正做女人是什么感觉。然而，假设“艾瑞莎在为我唱歌”，或者假设她是在为一个变装皇后唱歌。这就是阅读。这就是以一种，确切地说，是文学理论的方式来解读歌词。

Now “why is this literary theory?” you ask yourself, or you have been asking yourself. Of course, Butler gives the greatest example at the end of her essay when she says, “Suppose Aretha is singing to me.” “You make me feel,” not a naturalwoman, because there’s no such thing as natural. “You make me feel like a natural woman,” “you” presumably being some hetero-normative other who shows me what it is really to be a woman. Suppose, however, “Aretha is singing to me,” or suppose she is singing to a drag queen. That is reading. That’s reading a song text in a way that is, precisely, literary theory.

显然，我写这句话时想到了弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫笔下的拉姆齐先生[指着黑板上的句子：“这位哲学家心情阴郁地在他的东方地毯上踱步。”]。这句话写得很糟糕，我为此道歉。弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫绝不会写出这样的句子；但为了回顾一下我们一直在进行的文学理论研究：马克思主义批评家当然会关注“他”，因为在马克思主义批评家看来，这句话的核心在于占有——也就是说，资本的运用使得占有策略得以实施。非裔美国批评家则会关注以白色为代表的隐喻，换句话说，他们会坚持认为，解读文学作品的一种方式是通过解构隐喻化的过程，在这个过程中，白色代表着明亮、阳光和中心，而黑色，正如托妮·莫里森在她的文章中所指出的，代表着缺失、否定和消极。这很糟糕，气氛阴郁。对后殖民主义批评家而言，问题显然在于一种被剥夺却又无差别化的商品。“东方”指的并非真正的东方，而是哈萨克、布哈拉或基里姆地毯。换言之，概念本身缺乏具体性，暗示着话语的想象或意识中存在着物化或客体化的他者。

Now obviously I’m thinking of Virginia Woolf’s Mr. Ramsay in writing this sentence [gestures to sentence on chalkboard: “The philosopher in a dark mood paced on his oriental rug.”]. It’s a terrible sentence for which I apologize. Virginia Woolf never would have written it; but just to pass in review the way in which what we’ve been doing is literary theory: the Marxist critic would, of course, focus on “his” because the nexus for the Marxist critic in this sentence would be possession–that is to say, the deployment of capital such that a strategy of possession can be enacted. The African American critic would call attention to white color-coded metaphors, insisting, in other words, that one of the ways in which literature needs to be read is through a demystification of processes of metaphorization whereby white is bright and sunlit and central, and black, as Toni Morrison suggests in her essay, is an absence, is a negation, and is a negativity. This is bad, a dark mood. For the postcolonialist critic, obviously the problem is an expropriated but also undifferentiated commodity. By “Oriental” you don’t mean Oriental. You mean Kazakh or Bukhara or Kilim. In other words, the very lack of specificity in the concept suggests the reified or objectified other in the imagination or consciousness of the discourse.

最后，就性别理论而言，哲学家拉姆齐先生的男性化愤怒——你还记得他为何如此沮丧，因为他无法突破“r”这个音节；他想达到“s”的境界，却被“r”挡住了——这种哲学家男性化的愤怒掩盖了拥有东方地毯之人的审美主义的软弱无力。反过来，这又可能掩盖了软弱无力的教授形象，而教授形象又可能掩盖了过于异性恋规范的性掠夺，如此循环往复，辩证地展开——如果你把这句话解读为性别理论的一个方面或要素的话。

Finally, for gender theory the masculine anger of the philosopher, Mr. Ramsay–you remember he is so frustrated because he can’t get past r; he wants to get to s, but he can’t get past r–the masculinized anger of the philosopher masks the effeteness of the aestheticism of somebody who has an Oriental rug. That in turn might mask the effete professorial type, that might mask an altogether too hetero-normative sexual predation and on and on and on dialectically if you read this sentence as an aspect or element of gender theory.

好的。我今天就先讲到这里，下次我们会继续探讨我们几节课以来一直在讨论的内容——身份和事物的建构，这显然是本课程的共同特点之一——如何在更抽象的层面上进行理论化，并得出一些结论。

Okay. I will certainly end there, and next time we’ll take up the way in which what we’ve been talking about for a few lectures, the construction of identity and of things, which has obviously been one of the common features of this course, is theorized at an even more abstract level, with certain conclusions.

第24讲——文学研究的制度建构

Lecture 24 - The Institutional Construction of Literary Study

第一章 理论中的身份认同

Chapter 1. Identity in Theory

保罗·弗莱教授：我们一直在探讨关于身份本质、身份建构方式的各种论述——顺便一提，这些论述对文学中身份建构方式的侧重点也各不相同。我稍后会再谈到文学这个或许缺失的环节。与此同时，我想指出一点，我相信你们自己也已经有所领悟：那就是，每一种身份研究方法都有其历史渊源，而这段历史最终会形成一个类似于解构时刻的近期篇章，它标志着理论本身发生了转变，即理论作为主流话语所宣称的某些观点，从颠覆性的视角来看，本身就需要被解构和瓦解。后殖民研究中有一种观点认为，混杂性是对文化二元对立的瓦解——也就是说，它体现了一种双重意识，在这种意识中，人们既认同国家机器，又渴望颠覆它。

Professor Paul Fry: We’ve been passing through a variety of discourses concerning the nature of identity, the way in which identity is constructed–incidentally with varying degrees of emphasis, the way in which identity is constructed in literature. I’m going to come back to this perhaps missing link, literature, in a minute. In the meantime, I just wanted to point out something that I’m sure you’ve inferred for yourselves: namely that each one of these approaches to identity has a history, and that the history results in a recent chapter which is something like what you might call a deconstructive moment, signifying on theory itself such that the claim of theory as a mainstream discourse to hold certain views is something that in and of itself, from a subversive perspective, needs to be deconstructed and undermined. There is the idea in postcolonial studies of hybridity as the undermining of cultural binaries–that is, the double consciousness in which one experiences simultaneously a kind of identification with a state apparatus and a will to subvert it.

顺便说一句，我想再举个例子说明一下，因为这跟我自己的经历很贴切。我其实不常看脱口秀，但如果我真的要看的话，他们经常会邀请一些被称为“教授”的人上节目。我只是想指出，这种称呼“教授”时所带有的那种狡黠的礼貌，或者说那种混合着狡黠和礼貌的语气，对真正的教授来说，是最令人沮丧的声音之一，因为他们非常清楚，当脱口秀主持人称呼某人为“教授”时，其含义就是：你是个书呆子。你连自行车都停不好。你对现实世界一无所知。我也不知道我当初为什么要邀请你上这个节目，[笑] 大概是因为有人告诉我你是专家吧。这就是在公共领域里“教授”的含义。

By the way, I thought I’d give you another example of how that works because it applies to me. I don’t actually watch talk shows very often, but should I be watching a talk show, they often invite people on to these shows whom they call professors. I just wanted to point out to you the degree to which the sly civility, the hybrid sly civility with which people are called “professors,” is for a professor one of the most discouraging sounds in the language, because they know very well when someone is addressed by a talk show host as “professor” what they mean is you are a pedant. You don’t know how to park a bicycle straight. You have no understanding of the real world. I don’t know why I’ve invited you on this show in the first place, [laughter] except somebody told me you were an expert. That’s what it means in the public sphere to be a professor.

巴巴或许有些夸张，他说混合性话语带有恐怖主义的成分。巴巴写作的时间远早于9/11事件等等，他使用这个词可能有些随意，但我不得不说，当我听到有人称呼我时——尤其是非学术界人士——因为当然，学术界人士也鄙视我，但这更复杂。他们可能不会鄙视其他教授，你明白我的意思，所以情况更复杂。但当非学术界人士称呼我为“教授”时，我想我不能说我感到恐惧，但我确实感到沮丧。[笑声] 正如巴巴所阐述的，这是底层民众双重意识的重要组成部分。最后，无论如何，性别理论的解构时刻到来了，性别不再被理解为本质的东西，而是被理解为一种表演——它不仅通过言语话语而产生，而且通过所有符号系统而产生，包括手势、服装以及构成性别产生方式的所有其他方面。

Bhabha perhaps exaggerates a little bit when he says the discourse of hybridity has an element of terrorism about it. Bhabha is writing long ago before 9/11 and so on and perhaps uses the term a little loosely, but I have to say when I hear somebody addressing me, someone not in the academy–because of course, people have contempt for me in the academy, too, but it’s a more complicated thing. They may not have contempt for other professors, if you see what I mean, so that’s more complicated. But when someone not in the academy addresses me as “professor,” I suppose I can’t say that I feel terrorized exactly, but I do feel depressed. [laughter] That’s an important part of the double consciousness of the subaltern, as Bhabha expatiates on it. Then in any case, finally there is the deconstructive moment of gender theory in which gender is understood not as something essential but as something performed–something brought into existence not just by verbal discourse but by all the semiotic systems, including gesture, dress, and all the rest of it that constitutes the way in which gender comes into being.

现在，在每一种情况下，你都能看到知识作为否定性的体现。我只是想把这些重新拉回到我们或许更容易理解的文学理论视角。我所说的“知识作为否定性”指的是符号学知识，这正是我在本课程中一直强调的核心主题。“我是——嗯，我不知道我是什么，但我可以告诉你：我不是那样的人。”换句话说，我是如何理解自己并非那样的人的——当然，我拥有霸权话语权，所以我第一次在托妮·莫里森、爱德华·萨义德，或者在某种意义上，朱迪斯·巴特勒的论证中看到自己、理解自己。某种程度上，我第一次真正理解了自己，是在反思“我不是什么”的时候——也就是说，当我试图客观化或归类我“不是”的东西时，这当然不是我真正不是的东西，而是我自以为不是的东西。由此可见，根据我们近几周来探讨的各种思维方式，人们理解自身的方式恰恰是符号学和形式主义语言理解传统中的否定式的。我并非必然是我所是的。我恰恰是我所理解的，而非我所理解的，也非他者；而我或许正是通过这种否定式的过程，加深了我对自身的所谓理解。

Now in each case you have instances of knowledge as negation. I’m just trying to pull this back into the perspective of what we recognize perhaps more readily as literary theory. By “knowledge as negation” I mean semiotic knowledge, something that I’ve been trying to stress really as a central theme throughout this course. “I am–well, I don’t know what I am, but I’ll tell you this: I’m not that.” In other words, the way in which I come to understand myself as not that–and I, of course, am the person who possesses hegemonic discourse, so I see myself, I come to understand myself for the first time in the argument of a Toni Morrison or an Edward Said or, in a certain sense, of a Judith Butler. I come to understand, in a way, for the first time when I reflect on what I’m not–that is to say, when I try to objectify or to pigeonhole that which I’m not, which is of course not what I’m really not but what I suppose myself not to be. In all of these ways then, you can see that the way in which, according to the sorts of thinking we have been reviewing in recent weeks, one comes to understand oneself is precisely negative in the tradition of semiotic and formalist understandings of language. I am not at all necessarily what I am. I am precisely as I understand it not that, not the other; and I grasp myself perhaps in ways that deepen my alleged understanding of myself as a result of this negative process.

好的。我再次强调这些，是为了让你们放心，我们仍然在讨论文学理论，我们最近遇到的这些思考方式，确实源于符号学和形式主义传统中解构和否定所提出的问题。我们可以从课程的整体结构角度来理解，这本质上并非是我们之前探讨的思维结构发生了改变——当我们把语言作为理解的主要决定因素时，我们考察的思维结构发生了改变——而是语言（社会理解的决定因素）转变为我们所谓的“社会文本”；因此，我们的大脑不再是索绪尔所说的“语言”的容器，不再是独立存在、自成体系的东西，而是充满了其他人的语言。这是一个社会本身作为话语而争夺关注、并以某种方式努力塑造自身、使其可理解的空间。这就是根本性的变化。

All right. So I say all these things again to reassure you that we still are talking about literary theory, that the ways of thinking about things that we’ve encountered recently really do arise out of issues given to us by deconstruction and by negation in the semiotic and formalist tradition. We can understand what has happened basically–this in terms of the overall structure of the course–not as a change in the structure of thought we examined when we took up language as the primary determinant of understanding, but as a transformation of language–the determinant of social understanding–into what we call “a social text”; so that our head now is not the repository of Saussure’s langue, that is something that just sits there in and of itself as a system, but rather it’s full of other people’s language. It is a space in which society itself understood as discourse jostles for attention and struggles somehow or another to shape itself into intelligibility. That’s the fundamental change.

语言在我们以往的思维方式中仍然占据着至高无上的地位。我们并没有真正摆脱语言，只是改变了我们对语言的理解。语言如今已成为一种社会文本。用巴赫金的话来说，它现在是“他人的语言”，因此我们无法理解它——当然，符号学和解构主义也无法将其理解为我们自己的语言，因为语言总是先于我们而存在；但我们更清晰地认识到，语言作为一种社会建构被赋予我们，而这种建构反过来又塑造了我们。

Language is still preeminent in the kinds of thinking that we’ve been doing. We haven’t really gotten away from language, but we have altered our understanding of language. Language is now a social text. It is now, in Bakhtin’s words, other people’s language, and we understand it therefore not–and of course, semiotics and deconstruction don’t understand it as our own either, because language always precedes us; but we understand it more clearly as something that is given to us as a social formation that in turn forms us.

某种程度上，这确实引出了我们今天的主题，因为这个主题——几乎是本课程的最后一个主题——与诠释的前提条件有关。是什么让我们能够思考某些事情？我们是如何形成对某件事的看法而不是对另一件事的看法的？我们之间是如何达成共识的？同样，我们之间又是如何产生分歧的，而且这些分歧似乎总是那么不容置疑的？（笑）我们有时会发现自己在某些事情上无法达成一致，就像我们有时会意识到我们在某些方面对其他事情有着深刻的共识一样。这一切究竟是如何发生的呢？

In a way that does bring us to our topic today because this topic, almost the last topic of the course, has to do with the preconditions of interpretation. What makes it possible for us to think something? How is it that we come to think one thing as opposed to another thing? How is it that there are areas of agreement among us? How is it, for that matter, that there are areas of disagreement among us and indeed that these areas characteristically seem to be so nonnegotiable? [laughs] The point arises at which we just can’t find ourselves in agreement on things just as the point arises when we realize that we are in some profound way in agreement about other things. How is it that all of this comes to be?

第二章 拖车托尼的身份认同

Chapter 2. Identity in Tony the Tow Truck

为了做到这一点，我们先回到《拖车托尼》这部作品。因为我们一直强调，它与我们讨论的任何话题都息息相关，所以让我们再次思考一下，托尼与我们最近讨论的内容有何关联。例如，我们可以说，托尼以马克思主义的视角，对身份的社会决定论提出了质疑。它是一部现实主义作品，因为正如我们之前所说，故事中什么也没发生。故事中既定的社会结构没有任何改变，但它仍然以一种独特的方式展现了社会规范之间的关系，表明生活即便在社会不平等的情况下依然继续，即便——当然，在这里我要提出一个你之前可能没有过多考虑过的关于托尼的观点——即便存在种族和性别差异。

In order to do that, let’s first go back to Tony the Tow Truck. Because we’ve said all along that it’s about whatever it is that we happen to be talking about, let’s think about Tony once again as being about the things we’ve been discussing recently. We can say, for example, that Tony is a Marxist contestation of the social determinacy of identity in other forms. It’s a realist text because, as we’ve said before, nothing happens. There is no change in the social formations that are the givens of the story, but it nevertheless does lay out the relationship among social norms in ways that show that life goes on despite social inequality, despite–of course here I’m going to throw something at you that you perhaps hadn’t thought of so much in terms of Tony before–despite ethnic and gender difference.

现在，让我们换个角度来看待托尼的故事。我们可以看到，这其实是一个全球性的故事，它被伪装成美国大熔炉中文化融合的故事。其实，你们应该早就看出来了，托尼是一个意大利裔美国人，有着底层民众特有的复杂人格。一方面，他相信美国梦，喜欢自己的工作，换句话说，他认同这个体制；但另一方面，他也意识到自己在这个世界上拥有属于自己的一席之地——那间黄色的小修车铺。那是他在世界上的专属空间，也是他身份认同的来源之一。

Now what happens then in Tony, to move to a slightly different way of thinking about it, is we can see that it’s a global story masked as a story of hybridity in the American melting pot. It should have been perfectly plain to you all along that Tony is an Italian American with the complex personality of the subaltern. On the one hand, he believes in the American dream. He likes his job. He buys into the system, in other words, but on the other hand he recognizes that he has his own place in the world, the little yellow garage. It’s his niche in the world and it’s something that is partly what affords him his identity.

另一方面，尼托（Neato）则是庄园里那个神经质的盎格鲁-撒克逊新教徒（WASP），某种程度上代表了这类阶层。而斯皮迪（Speedy）则非常有趣地属于约翰·吉洛里（John Guillory）所说的“专业/管理阶层”。斯皮迪的有趣之处在于，我们突然意识到，他的种族出身、阶级出身，甚至性别——因为他可能是女性——或许并不像人们想象的那样重要。因为专业/管理阶层本身就很有趣——正如吉洛里的资料来源阿尔文·古尔德纳（Alvin Gouldner）详尽指出的那样——它代表着一群拥有共同利益的人的出现，这些人至少不能说源自于某个特定的阶层，或者说在某种程度上甚至不能说他们属于某个特定的阶层。在《拖车托尼》（Tony the Tow Truck）这部影片中，斯皮迪无疑是这个新兴阶层的代表。或许，尼托先出现并非偶然。我记得没错的话，在民间传说中的三部曲里，Neato排在第一位，因为Neato代表着一个较老的阶层，这个阶层在某种意义上正在被专业/管理阶层所取代。所以，先出现Neato，然后出现Speedy，这很合理。

Neato, of course, on the other hand is the neurotic WASP in the manor house, sort of representing that sort of class, and Speedy very interestingly is a member of what John Guillory calls “the professional/managerial class.” What’s interesting about Speedy is that suddenly we realize that his ethnic origins, his class origins, and even his gender–because he may be a woman–are not perhaps as relevant as one might have imagined them to be because the professional/managerial class is interesting–as Guillory’s source, Alvin Gouldner, points out at length–precisely as the emergence of a body of people with common interests who really can’t be said, at least, to derive from, or perhaps in a way even to belong to, a common class. Speedy is certainly in Tony the Tow Truck a representative of this new emerging class. Perhaps it’s no accident that Neato comes first. I think memory serves me in saying that Neato comes first in the sort of folkloric triad because Neato represents an older class, a class which in a certain sense is giving way to the professional/managerial class. It makes sense that first you get Neato and then you would get Speedy.

所以，我们当然也可以从性别的角度来思考拖车托尼。我们说过里面没有女性角色，但同时，那些皱着眉头或面带微笑的房子似乎象征着房子里的天使，但这还不是全部。显然，尼托——我从来没画过尼托的画像，但他那小领结和矫揉造作的“哦，我不想弄脏自己”的样子，简直就是一堆同性恋刻板印象的集合体。[笑声] 然后还有邦比，他总是推来推去——你甚至都不想去想他。[笑声] 总之，这显然是一个关于性别的故事，所以你可以看出它涉及到所有这些方面。

So then we can also think of Tony the Tow Truck, of course, in terms of gender. We’ve said there are no women in it, and yet at the same time you do have those frowning and smiling houses sort of embodying the angel in the house, but it’s not just that. Obviously, Neato–I’ve never drawn a picture of Neato but with his little bow tie and his prissy “Oh, I don’t want to get dirty” he’s just a bundle of gay stereotypes. [laughter] Then obviously with Bumpy, he pushes and pushes–you don’t even want to go there. [laughter] In any case, this is plainly a story about gender, and so you can see that it’s about all these things.

第三章 阐释共同体导论

Chapter 3. Introduction to Interpretive Communities

那么问题来了，这个问题也确实为我们今天的讨论做好了铺垫：我这些年来和托尼·托奇（Tony the Tow Truck）一起做了些什么？正如你们现在看到的，我所做的，正是菲什（Fish）对雅各布斯（Jacobs）、罗森鲍姆（Rosenbaum）、莱文（Levin）、索恩（Thorne）、海耶斯（Hayes）和奥曼（Ohmann）所做的。我一直在表明，如果你带着某种预设去阅读，你就会进行某种诠释行为，这种行为并非刻意为之，而是或多或少自发的，因为你已经被训练成这样做。

So then here is the question, and it really does provide us with our transition to today’s materials: what have I been doing all this time with Tony the Tow Truck? I’ve been doing exactly, as you can see now, what Fish does with Jacobs, Rosenbaum, Levin, Thorne, Hayes, and Ohmann. I’ve been showing that if you bring a certain supposition to what you’re reading, you’re going to perform a certain kind of hermeneutic act, not with any particular strain but more or less spontaneously because that’s what you are conditioned to do.

菲什的学生们毫不费力地就把上一节课的作业解读成了一首诗，当然，你也能看出，这首诗本身就很容易被这样解读。菲什也承认这一点，但他在凯尼恩学院给一些人讲课时，只是随意地扫了一眼教职工名单，然后说：“看看我能用这些名字做什么。” 我觉得他的确达到了目的，因为你可以用任何名字来做这件事。当然，我们也能看到，他的学生们实际上漏掉了一些要点。他们忘记提及“莱文”（Levin）这个词古老而重要的含义是闪电，因此，任何对这首诗的宗教解读都包含着启示的闪光。几乎无法理解为什么他的学生们会被“海耶斯”（Hayes）这个词难住，因为“海耶斯”——嗯，我们透过镜子看东西总是模糊不清的。我们透过迷雾看待它们，而这恰恰是我们对十七世纪虔诚诗歌中所描述的宗教启示的反应方式。

Now Fish’s class had no trouble construing the assignment for his previous class as a poem, and you can see, of course, that it was sort of ready to hand to be construed that way. Fish admits that, but he’s lecturing some people in Kenyon College and he just sort of runs his finger down the list of faculty names and says, “Look what I could do with these names.” I think he does make his point because you can do it with absolutely anything. We can see, of course, that his class actually missed a few points. It forgot to mention that an ancient and important meaning of the word “Levin” is lightning, so that a flash of revelation is entailed in any religious understanding of the poem. It’s almost impossible to understand why his class was stumped by the word “Hayes” because “Hayes”–well, we see things through a glass darkly. We see them in a haze, and that’s exactly the way in which we’re likely to respond to instances of religious revelation as they are given in the devotional poetry of the seventeenth century.

总之，我们一直在做的“拖车托尼”的故事就是这个意思。我们选取了一篇文本——顺便一提，你可能想知道我是否认为托尼的故事真正表达的是某个主题，而不是包罗万象。嗯，我的确这么认为，我之前也顺带提过，但这只是我的直觉，并非源于我对精神分析的任何特殊偏好。不过，在我看来，一个写给那个年龄段读者的故事，如果结尾的台词是“他推啊推，我终于要走了”，那么它显然只表达了一个主题，而不是其他很多东西。如果你真的追问我《拖车托尼》讲的是什么，我会说：“嗯，我觉得这是一个关于肛门期的寓言故事，罗伯特·克劳斯很可能就是为此而写的。换句话说，这个故事能吸引听故事的幼儿的注意力，它的意义或许会以比其他任何方式都更明显的方式传递给幼儿——当然，这肯定比我们之前讨论的大多数解读方式都要明显得多。”

In any case, what we’ve been doing with Tony the Tow Truck is of this kind. We’ve taken a text with a–by the way, you may want to know whether I think Tony is really about something as opposed to about all those things. Well, I actually do, and I mentioned it in passing, but it’s only an intuition and it really doesn’t arise out of any particular predilections I have for psychoanalysis. It does seem to me, however, that a story written to that age group in which the climactic line is “He pushed and he pushed and I’m on my way” is pretty obviously about one thing as opposed to a lot of other things. If you really pushed me about what Tony the Tow Truck is about, I would say, “Well, I think it’s an anal phase parable and that Robert Kraus very possibly wrote it for that purpose. In other words, this would engage the attention of the toddler who is having the story read to him or her, and its meaningfulness probably is going to come across to the toddler in that way perhaps in more pronounced fashion than in any other–certainly and obviously in a more pronounced fashion than most of the ways in which we’ve been talking about the text.

这就是我的想法。当然，我否认自己与精神分析有任何关联，但我确实了解一些这方面的知识，所以它也算是我诠释社群的一部分。我们稍后再谈。总之，我们一直以这种方式解读“拖车托尼”，我们一边点头一边说：“对，对，它也跟这个有关。”“好像是这样。挺有意思的，不是吗？不知道周四那部会讲什么。”我们这样做是因为我们属于一个诠释社群。

So that’s what I think. Of course, I’ve disclaimed any connection with psychoanalysis but nevertheless I know something about it, and so that’s part of my interpretive community. We’ll get back to that. In any case, we’ve been treating Tony the Tow Truck in this way and we have been, well, nodding our heads and saying, “Yeah, yeah, it’s about that, too,” and “Guess so, yeah. Interesting, isn’t it? Wonder what it’s going to be about on Thursday.” We’ve been doing this because we belong to an interpretive community.

现在我想立即补充两点。我想说，在座各位都是对诠释感兴趣的诠释界人士，你们或许一直都觉得诠释是个徒劳无功的活儿，所以才想来上这门课，看看它到底有多糟糕。至少我们都对诠释所涉及的各种复杂情况感到担忧。我们是一个对诠释感兴趣的诠释界人士，所以我们参与其中。然而，我敢说，在这个诠释界内部可能存在两个子群体，他们或许在某种程度上看到了这次实践的意义，但仍然想要抵制它。

Now I want immediately to add here two caveats. I would say that within the interpretive community that makes up this room, a community of people who are interested in interpretation, you probably have suspected all along that interpretation was a mug’s game and therefore wanted to take a course of this kind to find out just how bad it was. All of us at least have in common a concern with the potential complexity of those circumstances that surround interpretation. We are an interpretive community that’s interested in interpretation, so we play the game. However, I would hazard that within this interpretive community there are two sub-communities which probably, in a certain sense, while they see the significance of the exercise, nevertheless want to hold out against it.

其中一类人，要么一直以来都对本课程中探讨过的某个观点抱有非常强烈的认同，要么现在才开始认同。因此，他们认为，如果仅仅以概览的形式，将这个重要的观点与其他各种可能取代或与之冲突的观点并列呈现，是对这个观点的贬低。这就回到了我一开始提到的，人们或许会承认概览课程的实用性，但同时又会对概览课程本身感到反感，毕竟，在他们看来，唯一重要的只有马克思的思想。我们为什么要花时间去了解其他各种方法等等——只要某种思想形式对你来说才是最重要的就行了。这或许会让你觉得，与其说托尼只关注这一件事，不如说“哦，这真是一个肤浅且无关紧要的练习，因为重要的是认真对待这一件事。”这意味着，如果你在复习时考虑了很多其他因素，你就没有认真对待这一件事。

One of them is the community which either always has or has now come to have a very, very strong commitment to one or another point of view that’s been passed in review in this course and who therefore finds it demeaning of the important point of view that it would be treated simply in a survey in a serial way with all sorts of other points of view that may or may not supplant or jostle with it. Now this takes us back to the remarks I was making at the beginning about the way in which one can perhaps acknowledge the usefulness of a survey course but nevertheless bridle at the very idea of a survey course when, after all, the only thing that matters is Marx’s thought. Why do we spend any time with all of these other approaches to things and so on–just sort of whichever form of thought is the only thing that matters to you. This would probably lead you to say not so much that Tony is only about this one thing but “Oh, this is a really facile and irrelevant exercise because the important thing is to take this one thing seriously.” The implication is that if you take a lot of other things in review, you’re not taking this one thing seriously.

所以，这或许是我们诠释社群中的一个子社群。另一个子社群可能仍然坚持（正如人们可能会说的那样）高雅文化，他们会说：“我认为我们应该用《利西达斯》或《古舟子咏》。用拖车托尼来诠释是对高雅文化的侮辱，而且，”这个子社群很可能会说，“如果我们用了《利西达斯》或《古舟子咏》，那么某种特定的解读方法，某种特定的解读方式，就会显得不言而喻——这意味着所有其他的解读方法都显得无关紧要。”如果你所坚持的并非某种特定的观点，而是某种高雅文化的理念，那么你不会预先表明你采取的是哪种方法，但你会假定高雅文化的价值和本质在于，它能够使人们对其中某种产物的内涵达成某种共识。吉洛里在其对西方文明、西方文化等的辩护评论中，至少部分地谈到了这一点。它们具有意义，具有延续性，具有值得维护的稳定性，而这种稳定性应当成为各学派的核心任务。

So that might be one sub-community within our interpretive community. Another one might be a sub-community that is still committed, as one’s tempted to say, to high culture and says, “I think we should have used ‘Lycidas’ or ‘The Rhyme of the Ancient Mariner.’ It was demeaning to high culture to use Tony the Tow Truck and furthermore,” this sub-community might very well say, “if we had used ‘Lycidas’ or ‘The Rhyme of the Ancient Mariner,’ a certain approach, a certain way of reading either of those poems, would have made sense self-evidently–meaning that all of the other approaches are trivial.” If your commitment is not so much to one point of view as to some idea of high culture, you’re not going to say in advance which approach it is, but you’re going to suppose that somehow or another such is the value and nature of high culture that it will be possible to arrive at a sort of consensus view of what’s going on in one of its products. This is what Guillory is talking about at least in part in his review of defenses of Western civilization, Western culture and so on. They have a meaning. They have a continuity. They have a stability which is worth preserving and which ought to be the central business of the schools to promulgate.

所以，这些都是我们诠释社群内部可能存在的子社群，但我们都共同认识到，文本可以以这种方式进行即兴发挥。如果有人这样做，我们就会意识到，无论我们是否喜欢，我们自己也可能这样做——这从斯坦利·菲什和约翰·吉洛里的角度来看都是一种证明，因为我们同属一个有很多共同之处的学派。正是这些共同之处，使得文本以我们诠释的各种方式呈现出来。

So those are possible sub-communities within our interpretative community, but we all do have in common the recognition that it’s possible to riff on a text in this way. If somebody does it, we recognize that whether we like it or not, we ourselves could probably do it ,too–which is proof, from Stanley Fish’s point of view and also from John Guillory’s point of view, because we’re in a school that we have a great deal in common. It’s what we have in common that brings the text into visibility in the variety of ways that we’ve performed on it.

第四章 斯坦利·菲什：对诠释共同体的初步探讨

Chapter 4. Stanley Fish: First Take on Interpretive Communities

现在，综上所述，我们先来详细探讨一下斯坦利·菲什对阐释共同体的定义，然后再探讨我们可能想要对这一观点提出的各种批评意见。我们先来看菲什在第1023页左上角的第一句话。这是一系列讲座，所以他开篇就说：

Now with all of this said, let’s talk a little bit more about what an interpretive community is first, according to Stanley Fish, and then move to the point where we may wish to suggest one form or another of criticism of this idea. Let’s begin with Fish’s first sentence, which is on page 1023, the upper left-hand column. This is a series of lectures, and so he begins by saying:

上次我简要阐述了一个论点：意义既非固定不变的文本所独有，也非自由独立的读者所独有，而是阐释社群的属性。这些社群既塑造了读者的阅读活动，也影响了这些活动所产生的文本。我不确定他在这次讲座中是否进一步推进了这一论点，因此我认为有必要以这句话作为开篇，因为它在某种程度上预示了他接下来在讲座中再次提出的观点。

Last time I sketched out an argument by which meanings are the property neither of fixed and stable texts nor of free and independent readers but of interpretative communities that are responsible both for the shape of a reader’s activities and for the texts those activities produce. I don’t know that he really carries his argument all that much farther forward in this lecture, which is why I think it’s worthwhile to begin with this sentence because in some ways it does anticipate what he then lays out once more in this lecture.

斯坦利·菲什的职业生涯中有一件趣事，那就是在他那颇为引人注目的职业生涯中，他竟然两次改变了自己的想法。他的想法转变其实隐约记录在他那篇题为《我们如何辨认一首诗？》的文章中。顺便说一句，这个标题完全是误导性的，因为我们根本看不到诗。[笑] 这正是问题的关键。那里根本没有诗。如果它在那里，那是因为你把它放在那里。无论如何，这些想法的转变仍然隐约存在于这篇文章中。它们实际上体现在他早期一篇名为《解读校勘本》的文章中，这篇文章收录在[笑]里希特诗选第二版中，也是我以前教的那本。但我认为回顾这些想法的转变仍然很有意义。当我还是他在加州大学的学生时，他持有最初的观点。这正值他出版《罪的惊愕：〈失乐园〉中的读者》一书之前不久，我当时参加的一个研讨会就成了这本书的试验品。为了举例说明他所说的“稳定的文本会产生读者”（这是他最初的信念），我举个例子，他引用了弥尔顿关于撒旦精神的描述。撒旦站在火湖边，刚刚挺直身子，手里拿着长矛，弥尔顿这样写道（指着黑板）：

Now an interesting thing about the career of Stanley Fish is that he actually, in the course of that quite high-visibility career, changed his mind twice. His changes of mind are actually recorded residually in this essay that you read, “How Do We Recognize a Poem when We See One?” which, by the way, is a completely disingenuous title because we don’t see poems. [laughs] That’s the whole point. There is no poem there. If it’s there, it’s because you put it there. In any case, these changes of mind are residually present in this text. They are actually manifest in the peculiar vagary of the argument of an earlier essay he wrote called “Interpreting the Variorum,” which is what was in the second edition of [laughs] the Richter anthology and the one that I used to teach, but I think it’s still worth harkening back to those changes of mind. When I was his student at the University of California, he held his first opinion. This was just before he publishedSurprised by Sin: The Reader in Paradise Lost, a book for which a seminar that I was in was a kind of guinea pig. To give you an example of what he meant by saying that a stable text produces a reader, which was his first belief, I give you an example that he uses from Milton about Satan’s spirit. This is Satan standing by the fiery lake. He’s just pulled himself up to his full height, he has a spear, and Milton writes about it [points to board]:

他的长矛，与最高的松树相当[好吧：长矛，松树大小差不多]

His Spear, to equal which the tallest Pine [okay: spear, pine about the same size]

凿成……桅杆

Hewn… to be the Mast

某些伟大的海军上将（嗯，让我想想，桅杆-松树-长矛）只不过是一根魔杖……

of some great Ammiral [well, let’s see, mast-pine-spear] were but a wand…

然后你意识到，大小的顺序完全颠倒了，你之前所认为的，你脑海中早已充斥的——最高的松树——与撒旦的长矛相比，简直就像一根魔杖。所以他想表达什么呢？他是在说，你以为你的思维能够理解撒旦的强大，你以为你知道撒旦有多大，但《失乐园》的语言会教导你，会让你明白，你不应该招惹撒旦，因为撒旦远比你想象的要强大得多。

Then you realize that the sequence of sizes is completely reversed and what you thought, what you’d already filled your consciousness with–the tallest pine–is just a wand compared with the size of Satan’s spear. So what’s he saying? He’s saying you think that your mind can grasp the magnitude of Satan, you think you know how big Satan is, but the language of Paradise Lost is going to teach you, is going to educate you into realizing that you shouldn’t mess with Satan because Satan is much bigger than you think he is.

我在这里没写的内容，以及接下来的段落，都表明即使在这里，撒旦也处于他最虚弱的状态。这段文字继续写道（指着黑板）：“他扶着摇摇晃晃的脚步走着……”换句话说，他刚刚从火湖中复活。他此刻的虚弱程度达到了前所未有的程度（笑），然而他已经远超你的掌控。这就是《失乐园》的句法教导我们的方式：每当我们自以为理解了文本的要旨，就证明我们是堕落的读者，我们过早地理解了文本的内容，只有从长远来看，才能使我们真正认识到堕落的境况——而这显然正是文本所要探讨的主题。

What I didn’t write here, and what continues the passage, shows that even here Satan is absolutely at his weakest. The passage continues [points to board]: “He walkt with to support uneasy steps…” In other words, he’s just risen from the fiery lake. He’s as weak as he’s ever going to be right now [laughs] and yet he’s already a lot more than you can handle. That is the way the syntax of Paradise Lost educates us into realizing that every time we think we grasp the point of a text, we prove that we are fallen readers, that we have prematurely understood what’s there, and that only understanding it in the long run can prevail upon us to realize the fallen condition, which the text is obviously after all about.

第五章 斯坦利·菲什：对诠释共同体的再思考

Chapter 5. Stanley Fish: Second Take on Interpretive Communities

这是菲什最初的观点。不久之后，在撰写《自我消耗的艺术品》一书的过程中，他的观点发生了转变，几乎完全推翻了之前的观点。他认为，并非文本使读者存在——也就是说，并非文本使我意识到自己在《失乐园》中堕落的存在。并非文本使读者存在，而是读者使文本存在。毕竟，是读者完成了阅读这一行为，也是读者在文本中揭示了弥尔顿的意图。因此，他虽然改变了研究方向，但仍然保留了相同的论证结构和对文本思考的相同洞见。

That was Fish’s first opinion. Not too long after that, in the course of writing a book called Self-Consuming Artifacts, he began to have a different opinion which more or less reversed the first one. He decided it isn’t the text that brings the reader into being–that is to say, brings about the self-realization on my part that I’m a fallen being in the case of Paradise Lost. It isn’t the text that brings the reader into existence. It’s the reader that brings the text into existence. It’s the reader, after all, who performed this act of reading, and it’s the reader who made visible in the text the possibility that this is what Milton is doing. So he reverses his field while retaining the same structure of argument and the same range of insight about what one can think about a text.

嗯，这本来没什么问题，直到他意识到读者必须来自某个地方。读者并非一个独立的个体。正是在这里，他意识到自己思想发展的第三步，也就是他的第二次转变，意味着：不是文本造就了读者，也不是读者造就了文本，而是社群造就了读者，而读者反过来又造就了文本。换句话说，这三点勾勒出了他在这些问题上的思考进程。请快速浏览第1025页右侧栏。他在该段末尾写道：“阐释不是解读的艺术，而是建构的艺术。阐释者不是解码诗歌，而是创造诗歌。”

Well, that was fine until he realized that a reader has to come from someplace. A reader isn’t just an autonomous being. This is where he realized that the third step in his development, his second change of mind, means this: it’s not the text that produces the reader, it’s not the reader that produces the text, but it’s the community that produces the reader who in turn produces the text. Those three points in other words map the progress of his thinking on these issues. Take a quick look at page 1025, the right-hand column. He says, bottom of the paragraph: “Interpretation is not the art of construing but the art of constructing. Interpreters do not decode poems; they make them.”

当他这样说的时候，他仅仅处于思考的第二阶段，因为读者仍然可以认为阐释者是一个自主的个体，其思想、阐释能力和阅读策略都源于其内在。然后在第1027页，他在右栏底部澄清道：“但这并不意味着我必然具有主观性……”换句话说，这不仅仅是“我认为文本中包含的内容就是文本本身”的问题。文本是由我创作的，也是由你创作的，其他人也创作的。我们创作的文本各不相同，因为我们都拥有不同的主观性——这并非他想表达的意思。

When he says that, he’s only at phase two of his thinking, because there is still the possibility open to the reader of thinking that the interpreter is an autonomous being whose thoughts, whose interpretive powers, and whose strategies of reading emanate from something from within. Then on page 1027 he clarifies, toward the bottom of the right-hand column: “This does not, however, commit me to subjectivity…” In other words, it’s not just a question of whatever I think is in a text is in a text. I’m the one who makes the text, and you make the text, and the other person makes the text. We all make different texts because we all have different subjectivities–that’s not what he’s saying.

但这并不意味着我必须保持主观性，因为主观性的产生方式是社会性的、约定俗成的。换句话说，如果其他人听到我的解读，我就无法做出天马行空的解读。是啊，如果我只是（笑）待在房间里，周围都是黄色壁纸之类的东西，我想我或许可以对某些事物做出天马行空的解读，但如果我试图发表它，那就别想了。当我试图发表，当我试图表达自己，当我将自己暴露于公共领域的任何方面时，我的解读——如果它要被评判为一种解读，如果它要算作一种解读，如果它要算作一种观点——就必须已经融入到它所指向的解读社群之中。它必须与该社群存在某种联系。它必须包含某种成员身份或与该社群的关系，因此，菲什得出的结论是，既不存在主体，也不存在客体。

This does not, however, commit me to subjectivity because the means by which they are made are social and conventional. In other words, I can’t have an off-the-wall interpretation of anything if anyone else ever hears it. Yeah, if I’m [laughs] just in my room, surrounded by yellow wallpaper or something like that, I suppose I can have an off-the-wall interpretation of something, but if I try to publish it, forget it. When I try to publish, when I try to express myself, when I expose myself to any aspect of the public sphere, my interpretation–if it’s to be judged as an interpretation at all, if it’s to count as an interpretation, and if it’s to count as an opinion–must already be enmeshed in the interpretative community to which it’s addressed. It must have some sort of link with that community. It must involve some sort of membership or relationship with that community, so that what Fish concludes is that there are neither subjects nor objects.

换句话说，这是菲什追随德里达和解构主义，攻击西方形而上学传统的途径。只要我们认为理解就是解析或理解主客体关系，我们就走错了理解的正确道路。我们必须先理解主体和客体都无法拥有稳定的存在，无法拥有任何形式的完整性，才能更接近于理解阐释是如何产生和实现的。早在学期初，我们讨论海德格尔和伽达默尔的“先在”概念时，就已见识过这一点，即我们总是将事物视为某种事物：我们从未将其视为客体，也从未将其视为自在之物。我们之前已经见过这种观点，但这里略有不同，因为海德格尔和伽达默尔将客体视为检验自身观点的标准。换句话说，诠释循环是解释与被解释对象之间的往复运动，因此被解释对象不断地检验解释过程，正如解释随着深入而对对象的本质进行越来越精细的勾勒一样。

In other words, this is Fish’s way, following Derrida and deconstruction, of attacking the Western metaphysical tradition. As long as we suppose that understanding is a matter of parsing or coming to terms with subject-object relations, we’re on the wrong track to understanding. We have to understand the way in which neither the subject nor the object can be said to have a stable existence, to have integrity of any kind, before we can come closer to grasping how it is that interpretation is made and achieved. We’ve seen this before all the way back at the beginning of the semester when we talked about fore-having in Heidegger and Gadamer, about the way in which we always see something as something: we never see it as an object, we never see it in and of itself. We’ve seen this before, but there is a slight difference because Heidegger and Gadamer hold out the object as a standard against which one’s opinions about it can be tested. In other words, the hermeneutic circle is a movement back and forth between interpretation and what’s being interpreted, so that what’s being interpreted is a constant check on the process of interpretation just as interpretation, as it deepens, is a finer and finer outlining of the nature of the object.

因此，这种与菲什的思想相似（或者说预示了菲什的思想，因为它坚持所有解释都始于先入之见）的诠释循环，也蕴含着一个微妙的区别，即客体确实存在。这并非菲什否认客体的存在——尽管他的某些修辞有时会让人产生这种错觉。他只是否认我们能够在任何时刻将它们认知为客体。我们创造了它们，并且在创造它们的过程中，我们以我们构建它们的方式构建了它们。

So the hermeneutic circle which resembles, which anticipates the thinking of Fish in that it insists on the way in which all interpretation begins as preconception, nevertheless does also entail that subtle difference in that the object is there. It’s not that Fish denies the existence of objects–although sometimes his rhetoric makes it seem that way. He simply denies that we can know them as objects at any point. We bring them into being, and in bringing them into being we construct them in whatever way it is that we construct them.

第六章 阐释共同体的局限性

Chapter 6. The Limits of Interpretive Community

好的。阐释共同体。我们该如何理解阐释共同体这个概念呢？我刚才说过，我们都属于一个阐释共同体。我们今天在座的各位都属于一个阐释共同体。这里可能存在一些子共同体，但本质上我们是一个阐释共同体。我们彼此理解，但同时，我相信你们也都在思考，我们每个人的观点都不尽相同。我们说我们属于一个阐释共同体。事实上，根据某种较弱的论证形式，我们可以理解，是的，我们的确会根据某些习惯来创造事物，而这些习惯正是我们在这样一个共同体中逐渐形成的；但与此同时，我们又会说：“猜猜怎么着？我对雅各布斯、罗森鲍姆和其他人的作品的解读，和菲什班上的学生不太一样（笑）。我至今仍然不认同弗莱教授对他们解读的补充。我的解读略有不同，而且我一直都知道那不是一首诗。别想骗我。”等等。我们每个人都会对自己说：“好吧。没错，我们有一些共同点，但也存在差异。”

Okay. Interpretive community. What do we make of this idea of interpretive community? I have just said we all belong to an interpretive community. We sitting here all belong to an interpretive community. There may be a couple of sub-communities here, but basically we’re an interpretive community. We understand each other, and yet at the same time it’s equally the case, as I’m sure all of you are thinking to yourselves, that no one of us has exactly the same set of opinions as anyone else. We say we belong to an interpretive community. We can in fact, according to a certain weak form of the argument, understand the way in which yes, we do bring things into being according to certain habits that have evolved through our membership in such a community; but at the same time we say, “Guess what? I don’t quite interpret [laughs] Jacobs, Rosenbaum and the rest of them in the way Fish’s class did. I still don’t interpret it in the way that Professor Fry supplemented their interpretation. I interpret it a little differently, and furthermore I knew all along it wasn’t a poem. You can’t fool me,” and so on. Each of us says to ourselves, “Okay. Yeah, we have certain things in common, but there are also ways in which we differ.”

菲什会怎么回应呢？我想他会这么说，而且我认为这一点必须承认：这削弱了他的立场。他会说：“好吧，我承认：粗略地说，我们都属于这里——就像约翰·吉洛里说的，粗略地说，我们都在同一所学校里——我们属于一个阐释共同体；但还有另一种意义，我们每个人都是所有阐释共同体的总和，是所有我们如今以某种方式与之相关的阐释共同体的复合体，而我们正是从这些共同体中以各种方式演化而来。是的，我们每个人都不同，因为我们所属的阐释共同体的总和，构成了我们最终的阐释共同体，而这个共同体总是会与其他人所属的共同体的总和略有不同。这把阐释共同体的概念简化成了一种原子论，在这种原子论中，我们都承认并说：‘是的，没错。在某种意义上，我是一个共同体。’”

What would Fish say to that? I think what he would say is this, and I do think this needs to be acknowledged: it weakens his position. He would say, “All right, granted: in a rough sense, we belong here–just as John Guillory says in a rough sense we’re all in a school–we belong to an interpretive community; but there’s another sense in which we are each of us the sum total, the composite, of all the interpretive communities to which we now in some way or another have an affinity and from which, in all the variety of ways one can mention, we have emerged. Yes, we’re each different because the sum of the interpretive communities to which we belong, constituting the ultimate interpretive community that indeed we are, is always going to be a little different from the sum of the communities to which other people belong. This reduces the idea of interpretive community to a kind of atomism whereby we all concede and all say,”Yes, it’s true. I am in a certain sense a community.”

巴赫金说的就只有这些：“我是一个共同体。我是一个共同体，当然，共同体思考时所做的就是诠释。”思考即诠释。但与此同时，我们又会问：“如果我实际上与其他人略有不同，那么说我是一个共同体又有什么意义呢？”为什么不保留某种主观性，或者至少保留那种源于个体性的意识呢？这种个体性源于这样一个事实：我们每个人最终都不会在所有具体问题上都与他人完全一致——原因在于，构成我们声称自己所属的那个基本共同体的各个诠释共同体的总和，总是略有不同。

That’s all Bakhtin said: “I am a community. I am a community and, of course, what communities do when they think is interpret.” Thinking is interpretation. But at the same time “What’s the point,” we then say, “of saying I’m a community if, in fact I’m a little different from everybody else?” Why not retain a certain sense of subjectivity, or why not at least retain that sense of individuality which results from the fact that none of us ultimately or completely on every particular agree with anybody else–the reason being that the sum of our interpretative communities that makes up that fundamental community to which we say we belong is always a little bit different?”

现在还有另一种反对这种观点的论据，可以称之为激进建构主义。我们经常听到像爱德华·威尔逊这样的社会生物学家指出，意识天生就具备识别和执行各种事物的能力。实验室研究表明，审美偏好——当然，它一直被视为一种客观标准而遭到嘲笑——“品味无可争议”，我们总是这样说——但即使是审美偏好，实验室研究也表明，它包含着我们所有人都有的某些共同倾向。我们都偏爱所谓的黄金分割，我们都喜欢拱形，而这可以用各种各样的方式来解释。最常见的解释与所谓的庇护理论有关。我们喜欢那些能够以某种方式提供庇护或保护的形状。无论如何，相当确凿的证据表明，我们天生就具备识别事物的能力。达尔文的最后一本书通篇都在讲述我们如何识别彼此的表情，如何识别与我们有很多共同之处的动物的表情，以及我们从婴儿时期就开始这样做——换句话说，书中提供了各种各样的证据来证明这一点。

Now there is another argument against this position which might be called radical constructivism. We hear very frequently from sociobiological thinkers like Edward O. Wilson, for example, who point out that consciousness is hard wired to do and to recognize all sorts of things. It has been shown in the lab that aesthetic preference, which of course was always held up to derision as anything like an objective standard–“There is no disputing tastes,” we always say–but even aesthetic preference, it’s been shown in the lab, involves certain predilections we all do have in common. We all prefer the so-called golden section, we love arches, and this can explained in all sorts of ways. The most common explanation has to do with what’s called shelter theory. We like shapes that somehow or another offer shelter or protection. In any case, the fairly conclusive evidence is that in a variety of ways, we are hard wired to recognize things. Darwin’s last book is all about how we recognize each other’s expressions, we recognize the expressions of animals with which we have a great deal in common, and that we do this from infancy–in other words, all sorts of evidence to this effect.

我不确定菲什的论点是否容易被这种立场驳倒，毕竟，先天性思维本身就是社群性的。[笑] 关键就在于我们每个人都拥有这种思维，它并非个体特有的，也并非任何个体所独有的。因此，在我看来，尽管反对所谓激进建构主义的论证通常采取这种形式，但它实际上并非一个强有力的论证，而反对阐释共同体概念最终走向原子化的论证则更有力；因为如果我仍然是一个人的共同体，那么我是否属于阐释共同体又有什么意义呢？在某种程度上，一旦这样表述，这个问题似乎就不那么值得讨论了。

I’m not sure Fish’s argument is vulnerable to that position because, after all, hard wiring is communitarian. [laughs] The point is precisely that we all have it and that it’s not something that we can call individual, not something that we can call autonomous to any one of us as individuals. So it seems to me that although the argument against so-called radical constructivism usually does take this form, it actually is not a very good argument, and that the argument objecting to the mere weakness of the way in which interpretive community as a concept ultimately becomes atomistic is a stronger argument; because what does it matter if I’m an interpretive community if I’m still a community of one? In some measure, it’s something that seems less worth talking about once one’s put it in those terms.

第七章 吉洛里：学校和其他诠释社群

Chapter 7. Guillory: The School and Other Interpretive Communities

接下来很快就谈到了吉洛里，他的论点实际上终结了一场他认为会愈演愈烈的争论。换句话说，他认为未来二十五年甚至更长时间内，学术界最热门的话题将是经典之争：经典、非经典、文化和多元文化——他认为这将是学术界争论的根本焦点。然而，事实并非如此，原因在于他的论点如此精辟，以至于所有人都幡然醒悟，意识到（笑）他们完全搞错了方向。他的著作《文化资本》并没有让公众噤声（因为没有什么能让公众噤声，笑），而是平息了学术界关于文化战争的争论。在某种程度上，吉洛里以一种有趣的方式否定了他自己的预言，顺便一提，如果你有兴趣，可以在第1477页右上角找到相关内容。

Very quickly then on Guillory whose argument actually ended the very debate that he thinks is going to intensify and get worse. In other words, he thought that the big, hot-button topic in the academic world for the next twenty-five years or more would be the canon wars: canonical, non-canonical, cultural, and multicultural–he thought this would be the fundamental point of contention in the academic world. Well, it wasn’t, and the reason it wasn’t is that his argument was so brilliant everybody came to their senses and realized [laughs] that they were barking up the wrong tree, literally. His book, Cultural Capital, simply silenced not the public, because nothing ever silences the public, [laughter] but simply silenced the debate about the culture wars in the academy. In some ways Guillory amusingly undermines his own prophecy, which by the way is on page 1477 in the upper right-hand column if you care to read it.

吉洛里的主要关注点——这很大程度上源于皮埃尔·布尔迪厄，但也如他在一段颇具建设性的论述中所指出的，源于安东尼奥·葛兰西——在于学校如何成为建立和传播葛兰西所谓的“霸权”的手段。换句话说，按照这种论点，学校通常不会——我们稍后会讨论吉洛里本人提出的例外——向世界输送具备特定知识体系或理解力的人才。学校向世界输送的，尤其是在人文领域——吉洛里认为人文领域正因其愚钝而陷入困境——学校输送的是拥有一定文化资本的人。换句话说，它重复——用布迪厄的话来说，就是“再生产”——一种阶级结构，但这种阶级结构实际上是一种上层建筑意义上的阶级：一种阶级优越感，无论一个人自认为掌握了何种具体内容，它都只是复制了一种对统治阶级的取向，而这种取向，正如吉洛里所说，在西方文化中，学校一直都具有这种取向。学校再生产的与其说是知识，不如说是它自身，是它所体现的态度，是它存在的理由，是它延续的理由，以及它与权力和国家机器的关系。这就是吉洛里的基本立场，也是他为何认为文化战争恰恰正中学校单一意识形态的下怀。

Now Guillory’s main preoccupation–which he takes largely from Pierre Bourdieu but also, as he argues in a long constructive digression, from Antonio Gramsci–his main preoccupation is with the school as a means of establishing and proliferating what Gramsci called “hegemony.” The school, in other words, on this argument doesn’t typically–and we’ll come back to the exception that Guillory himself does make–doesn’t typically send out into the world minds armed with specific bodies of knowledge or understanding. It sends out into the world, especially when it’s a question of the humanities–which Guillory thinks are painting themselves into the corner in their obtuseness–the school sends out into the world people endowed with a certain quantum of cultural capital. It repeats, in other words–in Bourdieu’s term it “reproduces”–a structure of class, but really class in the sort of super-structural sense: class superiority that regardless of the specific content that a person supposes himself to have been mastering, simply replicates an orientation to the ruling class that the school in Western culture, according to Guillory, has always had. What the school reproduces is not knowledge so much as itself, the attitude that it embodies, its reason for being, its reason for continuation, and its relation to power and state apparatus. That’s Guillory’s basic position and it’s why he says that the culture wars simply play into the hands of the monolithic ideology of the school.

当你把多元文化主义奉为灌输吉洛里所谓的“进步教育学”的唯一途径时——吉洛里认为，当你拥抱多元文化主义时，你就会像西方文明的伟大丰碑早已脱离其历史文化语境那样，将你的目标对象从它们所属的文化中剥离出来。你将西方文明和其他经典都简化为一种脱离语境、无根的文化资本。“我读过这个。读过这个，我就拥有了某种地位和话语权。”就西方文明而言，这体现在引用诗人名言和餐后演讲中。就多元文化课程而言，这体现在几乎相同的场合以完全相同的方式提及这些内容。而无论哪种情况，吉洛里都认为，这与学习任何文化产品赖以存在的历史和社会语境毫无关系。

What happens when you embrace multiculturalism as the only means of inculcating what Guillory calls “progressive pedagogy”–what happens when you embrace multiculturalism, according to Guillory, is that you deracinate the objects of your intention from the culture to which they belong in precisely the way that the great monuments of Western civilization have long since been deracinated from their historical and cultural circumstances. You reduce both Western Civ and alternative canons to the same deracinated, rootless sort of nature as cultural capital. “I have read this. I have a certain status and negotiability in the world as having read this.” In the case of Western Civ, it’s quotations from the poets and after-dinner speeches. In the case of multicultural curricula, it’s the opportunity to allude in precisely the same way on largely the same occasions, and in either case it has nothing to do with learning anything, according to Guillory, about the historical and social circumstances in which any kind of cultural production are grounded.

当然，这种论证的前提是，伟大作品的教学方式仿佛体现了某些理念或原则。也就是说，在吉洛里看来，无论信息的形式如何，它们都被当作信息来教授。西方经典传递着关于身为美国人的重要性的信息。多元文化经典则传递着关于作为说话者本身的重要性的挑战性信息，但无论如何，它们都仅仅是信息，而非文化产物。它们并非源于其写作时的真实历史和生活环境，而这，从广义上讲，不过是一种方法论上的诉求，一种新的教学方式。

Now the argument depends, of course, on supposing that the way in which the great works are taught is as though they embody certain ideas of principles. That is to say, they’re taught as messages, in Guillory’s view, whatever form of message it might be. The Western canon has a message about the importance of being an American. The multicultural canon has a contestatory message about the importance of being whoever happens to be speaking, but in each case they’re merely messages. They’re not cultural artifacts. They don’t emerge from the real sort of historical and living circumstances in which they are written, which of course is, most broadly speaking, simply an appeal to method, a new way of teaching.

事实上，吉洛里本人最深切的追求在于对伟大作品的热爱。吉洛里最初是一位早期现代文学学者，他撰写了一部关于斯宾塞和弥尔顿的非常优秀的著作。他后来的文学社会学研究丝毫没有否定或削弱他早期对文化经典的关注。实际上，《文化资本》一书中或许最精彩的章节并非这篇理论导论，而是他阐述托马斯·格雷的《乡村教堂墓园挽歌》如何在英语课程中占据主导地位的精彩章节，尽管这首诗是用白话英语写成的。换句话说，他指出，《乡村教堂墓园挽歌》在当时的文化语境中，实际上削弱了古典文学和拉丁语的至高地位，并促进了白话英语国家课程的兴起。这是一个极其精辟的论证，其中《乡村教堂墓园挽歌》本身被不断地、持续地、引人入胜地引用。

Guillory’s own deepest commitment is, in fact, to the great works. Guillory began as an early modern scholar. He wrote a very, very fine first book on Spenser and Milton. His later work in literary sociology in no ways discredits or undermines the fact that earlier in his career he was interested in a cultural canon. In fact, probably the most interesting chapter inCultural Capital is maybe not this introductory theoretical one but an amazing chapter in which he shows how Thomas Gray’s “Elegy in a Country Churchyard” came to predominate in English curricula even though it was written in the vernacular, in English. He shows in other words how “Elegy in a Country Churchyard,” in the way in which it situated itself in culture at that time, actually undermined the premium place on the classics, on Latinity, and helped the emergence of a vernacular national curriculum. It’s an absolutely brilliant argument in which “Elegy in a Country Churchyard” is itself constantly and steadily and fascinatingly invoked.

换句话说，吉洛里本人也喜欢古典文学。或许这个论点中最有趣的部分在于，西方文明研究的权威们对“经典”的理解完全被蒙蔽了，因为历史总是在不断地改变着经典。书籍越多，可读之物就越少，任何课程体系（包括西方文明课程）中被剔除的书籍也就越多。如今，我们以拥护伟大著作为荣。我们以阅读柏拉图和亚里士多德为荣。但在古代，人们的阅读范围远不止于柏拉图和亚里士多德。他们阅读希腊和拉丁文化中所有可读之物，然后还会阅读一些可能以英文出版的书籍。然而，自那时以来，世界发生了翻天覆地的变化，现代语言和文学必然会不断改变经典，最终导致经典的精简。越来越多的作品被排除在外。即使在所谓的“经典”中，这也是不可避免的，因此，经典本身也需要承认历史变迁的核心地位。

In other words, Guillory himself likes the classics. Perhaps the most interesting part of this argument is the way in which the Western Civ mavens are simply fooled about their own understanding of what a canon is because perpetually, history changes canons. The more books you get, the fewer you can read, and the more gets dropped out of any curriculum, including the Western Civ curriculum. Today we’re proud if we’re proponents of great books. We’re proud of reading Plato and Aristotle. In the old days, people didn’t stop with Plato and Aristotle. They read everything there was to read in Greek and Latin culture and then they read such few books as may have been published in English. Well, a great deal has happened since then, and perforce modern languages and literatures have altered the canon always to the end of thinning it out. More and more gets left out. This is an inevitability even in the so-called “canonical” and therefore itself needs to acknowledge the centrality of historical change.

吉洛里的论点显然基于这样一个前提：参与这些辩论的人都未能区分这两种文化形式。[笑] 一种文化，是那种完全没有受过教育的人和新兴的专业人士/管理阶层都能共通的文化，在这种文化中，文学根本无关紧要。谁需要文学？“我可是惠普公司的老板，我需要文学吗？”与此同时，还有一种文化，我们称之为“大写的文化”，它关乎伟大的书籍、高雅的文化、文明的丰碑等等。吉洛里认为，我们对这两种文化形式之间关系的理解完全脱节，正是导致他所抱怨的教学中那种脱离根基现象的根源所在。他最终认为，任何事物都可以被教授，只要将其置于社会和历史语境中进行教授，就可以循序渐进地进行。他指出，一本伟大的书——我引用这句话，然后就此打住——之所以伟大，部分原因在于它不可能被简化成西方文明拥护者们强加给它的那些荒谬之事。他在第1482页右栏写道：

Guillory’s argument obviously hinges on the failure of anybody involved in these debates to distinguish between the two forms of culture. [laughs] There is culture, the kind of culture on which a person without any education at all and the new professional/managerial class can meet, the kind of culture in which precisely literature doesn’t matter. Who needs literature? “I’m running Hewlett-Packard. Do I need literature?” At the same time, there is the kind of culture with a capitalK, as we say, which is all about the great books, high culture, the monuments of civilization, and so on. Guillory says the total disconnect in the way in which we understand the relations between these two forms of culture is what leads to the kinds of deracination in teaching that he complains about. He himself finally thinks that anything is fair game to be taught, and it can be taught progressively as long as it is taught in terms of its social and historical circumstances. He points out that a great book–I will quote this and then I’ll leave you–is great in part because it can’t possibly be reduced to the silliness that the advocates of Western Civ attach to it. He says, page 1482, right-hand column:

任何真正有价值的文化作品都不可能简单到足以用这种方式进行可信的寓言化解读，因为任何文化作品都会在其形式和内容上客观化那些社会冲突，而经典之争正是通过分裂的课程体系来寓言化这些冲突。《奥德赛》充满了谎言、诡计和阶级背叛。在《伊利亚特》中，或许最有趣的角色（我相信大家都会同意）是忒耳西忒斯，他几乎不认同我们通常认为的西方文化价值观。总之，这就是吉洛里所说的，如果你足够仔细认真地阅读，就无法以这种方式将任何作品奉为圭臬。所以归根结底，这仅仅是一个阅读指南而已。

No cultural work of any interest at all is simple enough to be credibly allegorized in this way, because any cultural work will objectify in its very form and content the same social conflicts that the canon debate allegorizes by means of a divided curriculum. The Odyssey is full of lying, trickery, class betrayal. In The Iliad, perhaps the most interesting character, as I’m sure you’ll all agree, is Thersites who is scarcely an advocate of the values that we associate with Western culture. In any case, this is what Guillory means by saying that you cannot monumentalize anything in this way if you read it carefully and attentively enough. So ultimately it’s simply a program for reading.

好的。下次我们来讨论一下我们根本就不应该有理论这种观点。

Okay. Next time we’ll talk about the idea that we shouldn’t have theory at all.

第25讲——理论的终结？；新实用主义

Lecture 25 - The End of Theory?; Neo-Pragmatism

第一章 克纳普和迈克尔斯的背景

Chapter 1. Knapp and Michaels in Context

保罗·弗莱教授：好的，我谨代表耶鲁大学欢迎各位准学生。我不会过早地提及“耶鲁人”，但我当然希望你们都能来。我希望有机会能先为我今天要讲的内容提供一些背景信息，但或许你们会在我们进行的过程中逐渐理解。本次讲座的主题是一篇论文，这篇论文由两位当时还很年轻、影响力不大且尚未获得终身教职的学者撰写，他们当时正努力在学术界闯出一片天地。这篇发表在《批判性探究》（Critical Inquiry）上的文章无疑取得​​了成功，该期刊当时无疑是传播创新理论思想的权威刊物，而他们也对结果感到满意。几乎就在文章发表后，《批判性探究》的编辑们决定将一系列对《反理论》的回应与《反理论》一起出版成书，这些回应都措辞委婉、深思熟虑，最终汇集成一本非常有趣的小册子，至今仍有售。我认为这本书仍然有印刷版，如果你对这篇文章引发的争议感兴趣，那么它非常值得拥有。当然，我希望在剩下的时间里，能让你对这些争议产生兴趣。

Professor Paul Fry: Well, I’d like to welcome the prospective students. I won’t say the word “Yalie” prematurely, but of course I hope you all come. I wish I had a chance to provide a little context for what I’m going to say today, but maybe you’ll scramble into some sense of things as we go along. This lecture concerns an essay written to immediate widespread acclaim and controversy by two young, at the time quite uninfluential and untenured scholars trying to make their way in the world. They certainly succeeded with this essay, which was published in Critical Inquiry, then certainly the leading organ for the dissemination of innovative theoretical ideas, and they were, generally speaking, gratified by the results. Almost immediately the editors of Critical Inquiry decided to publish, together with “Against Theory,” in book form a series of responses to “Against Theory,” all of them sort of polite, carefully thought-through responses which made a very interesting thin book, which is still available. I think it’s still in print and well worth having if you take an interest in the controversies that the article generated, and of course, I’m hoping in the time remaining to get you to take an interest in them.

克纳普和迈克尔斯当时是，现在仍然是所谓的“新实用主义者”，也就是说，他们最直接的影响来自哲学家理查德·罗蒂在20世纪70年代撰写的一本重要著作《哲学与自然之镜》；但罗蒂的写作传统可以追溯到20世纪30年代和40年代约翰·杜威的重要著作，甚至更早，不仅包括亨利·詹姆斯的兄弟威廉·詹姆斯的伟大哲学论述，还包括查尔斯·桑德斯·皮尔斯的符号理论——这一理论在当时并未引起太多关注或争议。它被以I.A.理查兹为首的所谓剑桥学派文学批评家所采纳。他和奥格登（CK Ogden）曾就皮尔斯的符号学撰写过一些反思文章，但如今，随着实用主义和新实用主义——学术理论和文学思考中一个相当重要的思潮——的兴起，皮尔斯的符号学在某种程度上受到了更多关注，也在某种程度上挑战了索绪尔符号学在文学理论领域的主导地位。这种对符号的理解与索绪尔的阐释有所不同，将是本次讲座第二部分（也是核心部分）的潜在主题。

Knapp and Michaels were then, still are, what’s called “neo-pragmatists,” which is to say they are influenced most immediately by an important book written in the 1970s by the philosopher Richard Rorty called Philosophy and the Mirror of Nature; but Rorty was writing in a tradition that goes back through the important work of John Dewey in the 1930s and ’40s, and before then not only to the great philosophical interventions of William James, Henry James’s brother, but also a theory of signs by Charles Sanders Peirce, a theory which at the time didn’t generate too much recognition or controversy. It was taken up by the so-called Cambridge School of literary critics headed by I. A. Richards. He and C. K. Ogden wrote some reflections on Peirce’s semiotics, but today with pragmatism, neo-pragmatism–a fairly important strain in academic theoretical and literary thinking–Peirce’s semiotics is in a way receiving more attention, in a way also challenging the hegemony in the field of literary theory of Saussure’s semiotics. This sense of the sign as something different from what Saussure said it was is going to be the underlying theme of the second and central part of this lecture.

1982年或许是美国文学理论既令人着迷又令人沮丧的巅峰时期。它曾是一个热门话题——我们之前也讨论过——而如今已不再如此，因此可以说，我们对文学理论的兴趣至少在某种程度上是历史性的。然而，在1982年，你对这些问题持何种立场至关重要，而克纳普和迈克尔斯的《反对理论》正是在这种氛围下出版的。

Nineteen eighty-two was probably the high-water mark both of the fascination and the frustration with literary theory in this country. It was a hot-button topic–we’ve gone into this before–in ways that it is not really today, so that our interest in literary theory is at least in part historical, one might want to say. In 1982, though, where you stood on these matters just made all the difference, and it was in that atmosphere that Knapp and Michaels’s “Against Theory” was published.

正如我所说，他们是新实用主义者，这基本上意味着，人知道某些事物（这等同于相信某些事物），因此能够毫不犹豫地作为行动者在世间行事。一切关乎人性的重要因素都与人的行动能力有关，但我们的信念和行为并没有任何客观可知的基础。换句话说，这是一种被称为反基础主义或反基础论的立场，但并非如这类立场可能暗示的那样，必然包含虚无主义或某种令人窒息的极端怀疑论。恰恰相反，这种立场坚持认为，我们只需做我们正在做的事情，我们始终都在行动、思考、相信和表达；我们作为社会人，始终在对周围环境施加影响；而关于我们的能动性，唯一无需担忧的是，我们或许并没有一个完整、充分的客观解释，来说明我们为何以及如何以我们的方式行事、说话、相信和影响事物。克纳普和迈克尔斯的观点本质上正是如此。

Now as I say, they were neo-pragmatists, and what that means basically is that one knows things, which is the same thing as to say that one believes things, such that one acts in the world unhesitatingly as an agent. Everything that matters in being human has to do with one’s powers of agency, but there are no actual foundations in what we can know objectively for our beliefs and actions. In other words, it’s a position which is called anti-foundational or anti-foundationalist but not a position that, as such a position might imply, somehow entails nihilism or a kind of crippling radical skepticism. On the contrary, it’s a position that insists that we just do what we do, that we are always doing, thinking, believing, and saying something; that we are always exerting an influence as social beings in our surroundings, and that the only thing that needn’t concern us about our powers of agency is that perhaps we don’t really have a full, adequate objective account of how and why it is that we do and say and believe and influence things in the way that we do. That position is essentially the position taken up in Knapp and Michaels.

第二章 斯坦利·菲什

Chapter 2. Stanley Fish

上次你在斯坦利·菲什的文章中已经看到过这种观点——菲什认为，我们很大程度上是由我们所属的阐释社群塑造的。你可能还记得，他对这个社群的理解是，它构成了我们的价值观——换句话说，我们自身并没有什么内在的东西，我们自身的感知模式也并非独一无二，而仅仅是我们的教育环境引导我们相信和理解事物的方式。这也是一种新实用主义的立场。

Now you saw it last time already in the essay of Stanley Fish–Stanley Fish, who takes it that we are largely produced by the interpretive community to which we belong. You’ll recall his understanding of this community as that which constitutes our values–in other words, there’s nothing intrinsic to ourselves, nothing unique in our own modes of perception, but rather only the ways in which our educational circumstances bring us to believe and understand things. This, too, is a neo-pragmatist position.

现在你会注意到，在克纳普和迈克尔斯的文章第三部分，他们对菲什进行了某种礼貌性的反驳。他们表面上与菲什的观点大体上是一致的，但请记住，在文章的第三部分，他们讨论的是知识和信念的同义性或同一性，并指出菲什论证中的一段话，菲什似乎无意间表达了这样一种观点：一方面，你拥有知识；另一方面，你拥有与知识相关的信念。他们反驳道：“不，不，不，不。知识和信念是不可分割的。”仅凭这一点，他们就与菲什的观点相左。菲什在后来出版的《反对理论》一书中也写了一篇回应文章，但这完全是一场关于无关紧要、流于表面问题的友好争论。事实上，虽然我会重点关注前两个论点——这篇文章基本上有三个论点——但我对第三个论点（即菲什关于知识与信念之间关系的论述）关注甚少，部分原因在于它属于哲学范畴。它是罗蒂在《哲学与自然之镜》一书中论证的基石，或许与我们进行文学理论思考的内容没有直接关联。

Now you notice that in the third part of the Knapp and Michaels essay, they engage in a kind of polite disagreement with Fish. There is an underlying, very broad agreement with him, but remember in the third part of the essay they’re talking about the synonymity, the identity, of knowledge and belief, and they point to a particular passage in one of Fish’s arguments where he kind of slips into the idea that, on the one hand, you have knowledge and then, on the other hand, you have, in relation to that, belief. They say, “No, no, no, no. You can’t separate knowledge and belief,” and just on those grounds they disagree with Fish. Fish writes one of the responses in the book that’s then subsequently published concerning “Against Theory,” but it’s a completely friendly controversy about a transitory and superficial matter. As a matter of fact, while I’m going to pay a lot of attention to the first two arguments–there are basically three arguments in this essay–I’m going to pay very little attention to the third argument in which Fish is challenged about the relationship between knowledge and belief, in part at least because it’s an argument that belongs to philosophy. It is the cornerstone of Rorty’s argument in Philosophy and the Mirror of Nature and perhaps not so immediately relevant to the kinds of things that we think about in doing literary theory.

那么，让我们来看看他们就我所说的这场运动究竟说了些什么。你会注意到，例如，他们的作品在语气上与斯坦利·菲什的作品非常相似。这是一种直截了当、毫不含糊、直奔主题的语气，读过德里达和其他类似作家的作品之后，你或许会感到有些措手不及。某种程度上，这令人耳目一新。在经历了早期作家们那些拐弯抹角、摇摆不定的论述之后，这种直截了当的态度想必会让人感到如释重负。某种程度上，这种语气是与生俱来的。你接受这些观点，某种程度上，这种语气似乎就由此而来，因为他们实际上是在说：你只需做你该做的，你想什么就想什么。作为一名文学阐释者，你必然会对你所研究的内容持有某种观点，所以就继续下去吧。表达你的观点，这就是你的工作。在这种观点和语气下，你唯一可能犯错的地方就是试图为你的行为寻找某种理论依据。你这样做完全没问题，别担心，继续做下去。但不要像克纳普和迈克尔斯所论证的那样，指望能找到任何潜在的或广泛的理论依据来支持你的行为。显然，这种颇具挑战性和启发性的观点，恰恰适合我所说的这种直截了当的语气。

So to turn then to what they actually do say in relation to this movement that I’m talking about, you notice for example that in tone, their work is very similar to that of Stanley Fish. It’s a kind of a downright, no-nonsense, let’s-get-on-with-it kind of tone that, after reading Derrida and other writers of that kind, you’re perhaps not quite ready for. In a way it’s bracing. It must be kind of a relief to get this sort of no-nonsense attitude toward these issues after all the tacking and veering that we’re likely to have experienced in earlier writers. In a way, the tone comes with the territory. You take these views and in a way, the tone seems to follow from it, because what they’re saying in effect is, You just do what you do. You think what you think. As a literary interpreter, you’re bound to have some opinion about what you’re looking at, so just get on with it. Express that opinion, that’s your job of work. On this view and in this tone, the only way you can go wrong is to grope around for some theoretical justification for what you’re doing. It’s just fine that you’re doing it. Don’t worry about it. Get on with it, but don’t think, according to the argument of Knapp and Michaels, that you can hope to find anything like an underlying or broad theoretical justification for what you’re doing. Obviously, that rather challenging and provocative notion is something that lends itself readily to the sort of no-nonsense tone that I’m talking about.

第三章 克纳普和迈克尔斯的三个论点

Chapter 3. Knapp and Michaels’s Three Arguments

那么，回到他们的论点，他们认为，人们之所以会陷入理论问题的泥潭，是因为犯了两个——好吧，其实是三个，但正如我所说，我们暂且把“知识和信念”放在一边——根本性的错误。第一个错误是假定意义和意图之间存在区别：换句话说，例如，他们认为要了解一个意义，一方面就必须能够援引一个意图；另一方面，如果没有意图，我们就不可能谈论意义。这就是他们的第一个论点：人们一旦犯了这两个错误中的任何一个，就会陷入理论的泥潭。我们稍后再来讨论这一点。

So turning then to their argument, they argue that people become entangled with issues of theory, all of which in their view should be avoided, when they do two–well, three but, as I say, we’re going to set “knowledge and belief” aside–when they make three fundamental mistakes. The first is to suppose that there is a difference between meaning and intention: in other words, for example, that to know a meaning you have to be able to invoke an intention, on the one hand, or in the absence of an intention, we cannot possibly speak of a meaning, on the other hand. That’s their first argument: people become embroiled in theory when they make one of those two mistakes. We’ll come back to that in a minute.

第二个论点是他们坚持认为语言和言语之间没有区别：换句话说，索绪尔的观点——即我们头脑中以某种形式存在着语言，它以词汇和语法规则的形式呈现，语言（或称“langue”）产生言语，也就是我一句一句地说的话（或称“parole”）——这种观点完全错误，因为语言和言语之间根本没有区别。这是他们的第二个前提。

The second argument is their insistence that there is no such thing as a difference between language and speech: in other words, the Saussurian idea that we have language somehow or another virtually present in our heads as a lexicon and a set of rules of grammar and syntax, that language or langue produces speech, what I say from sentence to sentence, or parole–this notion is simply false because there is no difference between language and speech. That’s their second premise.

在我展开论述这些论点之前，我想再谈谈他们对理论的态度。请大家注意第一段，也就是你们资料包第79页上的那段。这是“反对理论”一章的第一段，有趣的是，他们把某些文学思考方式，尤其是那些准科学的文学思考方式，排除在了他们对理论的批判之外。他们说：

Now before I launch into those arguments, let me say one more thing about their attitude toward theory. Let me call your attention to the very first paragraph, which in your copy center packet is on page 079. This is the very first paragraph of “Against Theory,” where interestingly they exempt certain ways of thinking about literature, certainly quasi-scientific ways of thinking about literature, from their charge against theory. They say:

“理论”一词有时被用来指代一些与具体作品解读并无直接关联的文学主题，例如叙事学、文体学和韵律学。然而，尽管这些主题具有普遍性，但在我们看来，它们本质上是经验性的，因此我们反对理论的论点并不适用于它们。嗯，这有点令人惊讶，因为首先，在这门理应致力于理论的课程中，我们已经讨论过其中一些内容——尤其是叙事学；文体学——它是研究风格的科学，探讨如何从句法、统计等各种角度分析风格；以及诗学——它探讨构成诗歌或其他体裁文本的一般性观点。所有这些都让我们不禁联想到俄国形式主义者。我们所学习的叙事学很大程度上源于结构主义，甚至也源于弗洛伊德的某些思想，而这一切听起来都与理论颇为相似。

The term [“theory”] is sometimes applied to literary subjects with no direct bearing on the interpretation of individual works, such as narratology, stylistics, and prosody. Despite their generality, however, these subjects seem to us essentially empirical, and our arguments against theory will not apply to them. Well, now this is a little surprising because for one thing, in this course, which is presumably devoted to theory, we’ve talked about some of these things–especially about narratology: stylistics–which is the science of style and how one can approach style syntactically, statistically and in the variety of ways in which that’s done–and poetics, which is general ideas about what constitutes a poem, or a text written in some other genre. All of these, for example, must remind us very much of the Russian formalists. Narratology, as we studied it, is largely derived from structuralism, indeed also from certain ideas of Freud, and all of this sounds suspiciously like theory.

他们想表达什么观点呢？简而言之，他们想表达的是，那些被他们排除在对文学理论的抨击之外的文学思考方式，正是他们所谓的“经验主义”的，是基于观察的文学思考方式——当然，在我看来，这肯定适用于俄国形式主义者，或者至少适用于俄国形式主义者自认为正在做的事情——这些思考方式之所以被称为经验主义，是因为它们观察数据，建立某种数据库，并从观察结果中进行概括。换句话说，它们从研究对象出发，然后从中得出结论。因此，这些经验主义的文学研究方法，即通过简单的数据观察进行概括——被他们排除在对文学理论的普遍指责之外。

What point are they making about it? Well, simply, the point that those ways of thinking about literature, which they exempt from their diatribe against theory. are the ways that they call “empirical,” ways of thinking about literature that are based on observation–and that, of course, would certainly, it seems to me, apply to the Russian formalists or at least to what the Russian formalists think they’re doing–ways that are empirical in the sense that they observe data, they build up a kind of database, and they generalize from what they have observed. They begin, in other words, with the object in question and then draw conclusions from it. So empirical approaches to literature, the simple observation of data from which one can generalize–they exempt these from the general charge against literary theory.

接下来，我们来探讨意图和意义必然是同一回事，以及语言和言语必然是同一回事。在此，我想请大家思考一下斯坦利·卡维尔（Stanley Cavell）的这句话（他指着黑板说：“我能知道一个词的意义，但我能知道一个词的意图吗？”）。这句话出自《反理论》（Against Theory）一书中对本文的另一篇回应文章。我现在不想深入探讨这句话，但我觉得它以一种非常生动的方式挑战了克纳普（Knapp）和迈克尔斯（Michaels）的观点，而我们之后会以各种方式（即便只是间接地）触及到这一点。

Turning then to the idea that intention and meaning just must be the same thing, and then subsequently the idea that language and speech just must be the same thing: in the background I’d like you to be thinking about some of the implications of this sentence [points to board: “I can know the meaning of a word, but can I know the intention of a word?”] by Stanley Cavell which was written in another one of the responses to this essay that was published in the book, Against Theory. I don’t want to reflect on it now, but it seems to me a strikingly vivid way of posing a challenge to the Knapp and Michaels position which in a variety of ways, if only by implication, we’ll be touching on.

那么，克纳普和迈克尔斯究竟是如何说服我们的呢？——接下来我会和他们一起深入探讨，几乎是全程参与，尽管在最后我会急转弯，希望这能挽救理论。毕竟，在你们面前站了二十六次，每次一个小时，最后却不得不承认我们一直在讨论的东西应该从我们的词汇中彻底清除，这简直令人难以接受。[笑声] 不用说，我有责任拯救我们的主题。我会做到，但你们还得等一段时间，因为正如我所说，我会和克纳普和迈克尔斯一起深入探讨。

So what do Knapp and Michaels do in order to convince us?–and I’m going to be going a long way with them here, indeed almost all the way, even though I’m going to be taking a sharp turning toward the end of the road which, I hope, saves theory. After all, it’s scarcely conscionable to stand here twenty-six times in front of you for an hour each and then finally to confess at the end that the thing we have been talking about should be banished from our vocabulary. [laughter] Needless to say, it’s incumbent on me to save our subject matter. I will, but you’re going to have to wait a while because, as I say, I am going to be going a long way down the road with Knapp and Michaels.

第四章 意图与意义：华兹华斯的《沉睡封印了我的灵魂》

Chapter 4. Intention and Meaning: Wordsworth’s “A Slumber Did My Spirit Seal”

克纳普和迈克尔斯实际上是在说：你知道吗？我们对待任何文本、任何话语、任何出现在我们面前的语言实例的方式，就是想当然地认为它们都带有某种意图。作为理论家和批评家，我们总是纠结于如何才能了解意图，而这一切都是一个危险的错误，因为事实上，在日常实践中，我们遇到的任何语言片段，我们都会默认它们都带有某种意图。

Knapp and Michaels say in effect, Well, you know what?
